{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hey there, I guess I just needed to talk today.
supporter: Of course, Emily. I'm here for you. What's on your mind?
seeker: Well, I got an unexpected compliment from my boss today about my recent performance at work.
supporter: That sounds like a positive development! How does that make you feel?
seeker: Relieved, to some extent. It's been a while since I've felt good about my work.
supporter: It's understandable given the increased workload and stress you've faced. It's great to hear some recognition is coming your way. What do you think brought about the compliment?
seeker: I think I've finally adapted a bit to the changes after the acquisition, and I've been trying really hard to stay focused, even though it's tough with everything else going on.
supporter: You've been putting in a lot of effort, and it shows. It's not easy to balance work stress with personal struggles. How have things been at home?
seeker: Things with Bob are still stressful, with the financial strains and all. His part-time job has helped some, but there's still tension.
supporter: Relationships can be challenging, especially under financial pressure. Have you two had any discussions about how to move forward?
seeker: We talk... but it's mostly arguments. I feel like we're both just at our wits' end sometimes.
supporter: It sounds really tough. Disagreements are hard, but it can be helpful to approach it as a team, looking for solutions together. Do you think that's possible?
seeker: I hope so. It's just hard to communicate when we're both stressed and upset.
supporter: Stress can definitely make communication harder. Your therapist might have some strategies that could help when you're feeling overwhelmed.
seeker: Yeah, I'll mention it next time I see her. It could be helpful to have some new approaches.
supporter: That's a great idea. How is everything going with your son and his situation at school?
seeker: 's still having a tough time. He's grounded after the incident at school, and that's affecting us too. I just wish things could be simpler.
supporter: That sounds really tough on all of you. It's okay to feel overwhelmed by everything. You mentioned Jerry left home after a disagreement too—how are you handling that?
seeker: Honestly, I feel a mix of anger, sadness, and worry. I know he's an adult, but I wish he hadn't left like that.
supporter: It's completely natural to have those feelings, Emily. You're a caring mother, and wanting your child close is understandable. Have you been able to reach out to him since then?
seeker: Not much. He needs space, I think. It's just hard to not be able to help him when he needs it.
supporter: That must be really tough. Giving him space while being there if he needs support is a good balance. Try to focus on being ready for when he's ready to reconnect.
seeker: Thanks for saying that. It's been a lot to handle, but I'm trying to stay hopeful.
supporter: Hope is important. Taking things one step at a time can make it more manageable. Is there anything specific that's helped you manage your stress lately?
seeker: I've started walking in the mornings to clear my head. It’s not much, but I think it helps.
supporter: That sounds like a healthy habit. Small steps forward are definitely progress. Remember, I'm always here when you need to talk. You don't have to face things alone.
seeker: Thank you. It's nice to know I have your support.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-01-10","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hey, can we talk? I could really use someone to listen right now.
supporter: Of course, Emily. I'm here for you. What's going on?
seeker: Well, Bob finally got a part-time job, which should be a good thing, right?
supporter: It's a step forward, but it sounds like you're feeling a lot more than just relief. What's on your mind?
seeker: I thought I'd feel better, but instead, I just feel overwhelmed. Like things are barely holding together.
supporter: That makes sense, considering everything you've been dealing with lately. It's a lot to carry.
seeker: Exactly. It's just this constant stress. Bob's part-time gig helps a bit with money, but I can't help feeling frustrated that it took so long.
supporter: It's understandable to feel that way. It's been a tough road for you, especially with the financial stress.
seeker: Yeah, and it doesn't help that my job feels so unstable. I worry all the time about whether I'll be able to keep it.
supporter: The job uncertainty adds another layer of stress. It's okay to have those concerns.
seeker: Sometimes I feel like I'm just waiting for the next thing to go wrong. It's exhausting.
supporter: Feeling trapped in that cycle is really tough. Have you been able to talk about this with your therapist?
seeker: I have. We've been working on it. I think I just struggle with knowing where to even start making changes.
supporter: Taking those first steps can be daunting. It's great that you're seeking help and trying to navigate through this.
seeker: Thanks. It's just hard when the people around me feel like they're adding to the weight instead of helping.
supporter: That sounds isolating. It’s important to have support from those around you. Have there been any positive moments between you and Bob lately?
seeker: Well, we did have a decent conversation about budgeting yesterday. It felt productive.
supporter: That's great to hear. Even small constructive talks can help rebuild some connection.
seeker: You're right. I guess I need to focus on those moments more and not get swallowed by the bigger picture.
supporter: Exactly. Celebrating small victories can help lighten the load a bit. You’re doing the best you can.
seeker: Thanks for saying that. It helps to hear it out loud. I forget sometimes.
supporter: I’m happy to remind you anytime. You're strong and capable, Emily.
seeker: Thank you. I appreciate you being here for me.
supporter: Always here to lend an ear whenever you need it. Take care, Emily.
seeker: I will. Talk to you soon.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-12-20","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hi I am seeking support to assist me with better sleep patterns.
supporter: Hi there, let me get a deeper understanding of your existing sleep pattern. Do you suffer from insomnia or another type of sleep disorder? 
seeker: No, it is not insomnia.  
supporter: Okay, are you drinking enough water and eating a healthy diet? 
seeker: I could improve my water intake and eat more vegatables.
supporter: I like to analyze my own habits every now and then, it helps me stay in check. You can definitely benefit from meditating and self reflecting. 
seeker: Thanks!  What other ideas do you have?
supporter: Of course! I always knock right out after a workout. But if you aren't able to, just simple things like turning all the lights off at the same time every night and laying in bed will help. It will align your circadian rhythm! 
seeker: Great, but I wake up frequently thinking about the recent events surrounding police and how they treat black people.
supporter: It definitely is a valid reason to be kept awake. The only good part about something so horrible, is that you have the power to make sure you will continue to be a good person. If everyone was as empathetic as you, the world would be a better place. Thank you for caring so deeply about such a brutal matter. 
seeker: I wish there were more caring people in the world. 
supporter: Kindness is contagious, and you definitely have a kind heart. As long as you remain soft in a hard world, people will recognize that and follow suit. The world is becoming more aware, and we have the power to raise future generations with more knowledge and love for one another. Caring doesn't come naturally to many unfortunately, but the ways of inspiring the people that don't care, are endless. We as a society can definitely think of more ways to care for one another. 
seeker: Correct, but having a kind heart does not keep me from waking up & worrying about my son and other black men in my family. 
supporter: I worry about my sons and husband and father all the time... I shift my focus on loving them and cherishing every moment we have together. Police or not, the time we have is not promised.. 
seeker: That's good advice.
seeker: Are you still there?
supporter: A hot cup of tea never hurt too! But in all seriousness, I can completely understand your sleep troubles. It is much deeper than just that. Perspective is the key to life. You are a strong and empathetic soul. 
seeker: okay
seeker: Love conquers all
supporter: That is so beautifully true 
seeker: I'm looking forward to a fulls night rest. 
supporter: That is good, lavender baths or showers will also ease and relax the troubled mind. 
seeker: Relaxing is good therapy. 
supporter: I like to relax with a book and a blanket sometimes too. 
seeker: Self care is needed.
supporter: Self care is definitely something we can overlook accidentally. Being self aware is a daily practice.
seeker: I agree.  Loving ourselves & the ones we care about too.  
supporter: It is good that we spoke today, I am going to hug my sons a little harder when I see them tonight. ","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-09-06","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hello
seeker: Hello, I am looking for help in managing some depression.
supporter: You've come to a good place to start.
supporter: Is there something in particular that is leaving you feeling depressed?
seeker: I am feeling resentful towards my husband for quitting his job, and my son for being the reason that he quit his job.
seeker: My son's behavior is causing a lot of conflict in our house and my husband not working is putting a lot of financial stress on us
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. Feeling resentment for both your husband's loss of work and your son's loss of his job is entirely understandable. 
seeker: I have a hard time not dwelling on the negative things going on.  It's hard to see anything positive or feel hopeful for the future.
supporter: I have an adult son who also lost his job recently, and I understand the added stress that can cause in your household. 
supporter: That is a really difficult position to be in. 
seeker: My son is very defiant and argues with us about everything we try and get him to do, but he expects us to give him money for fun things that he wants to do when he isn't willing to work or even help out around the house
supporter: Regardless of what your husband's actions are and your son's, could you possibly make the time to do things to support yourself, that even momentarily would provide you with some positive feelings? 
seeker: I try to go for a run every night, that does help.  
supporter: That is very hard emotionally, so I am sorry you have to deal with your son's behavior.
seeker: It is hard to keep my emotions separate from what is going on with him
supporter: That is very understandable! Setting boundaries for yourself may help. Even when it's difficult, being clear with your son that you will not be giving him money could help. 
supporter: Sometimes being clear with your own expectations can help him to see what won't be accepted from him as long as he is living in your home.
seeker: Yes, I could do better at that.  I want him to have fun and do things with friends, but I want him to be willing to work for what he wants, too.  
seeker: I do struggle with expectations.  I want him to be someone that he is not willing to be, I need to let go of that and just let him be himself and not base my emotions on his choices.
supporter: I completely understand that. Especially when it comes to people we are close to, it can be hard to separate our expectations from theirs. 
seeker: I feel guilty sometimes taking time to do things that I like and that are away from my family.  I can see that I need to do that more, though.
supporter: I've had to learn this lesson many times with my own children. It's difficult, but ultimately will give you some relief from your resentment. 
seeker: Thank you, it is helpful to know that other people have felt the same way.
supporter: Absolutely! Being a parent is difficult. Remembering to support yourself helps. Making the time to do things to support your wellbeing doesn't make you selfish at all
seeker: Thank you!
supporter: You are certainly not alone.
supporter: Has any of this been helpful? Is there more I can do for you?","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-07-14","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hey, are you around? I could really use someone to talk to.
supporter: Of course, Emily. I'm here for you. What's going on?
seeker: Bob and I had a big argument last night. I haven't been able to stop thinking about it.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. Arguments can be really tough. Do you want to share what happened?
seeker: Yeah, it just spiraled out of control. We started talking about our finances, and it just got heated.
supporter: Financial pressures can put so much strain on relationships. It's completely understandable to feel overwhelmed. How are you feeling now?
seeker: Exhausted, honestly. It's like we're stuck in this cycle of stress, and I don't see a way out.
supporter: It sounds really challenging, Emily. It's okay to feel this way. Have you two been able to talk it out since it happened?
seeker: Not yet. We both needed some space. Bob went for a drive, and I've just been trying to calm down.
supporter: Taking some space can be helpful to gather thoughts. Do you think you’ll be ready to talk soon?
seeker: I hope so. I don't want to keep ignoring it, but I'm also scared it'll turn into another argument.
supporter: That's understandable. Talking during a calm moment might help. Maybe planning a time to chat could prevent it from escalating?
seeker: That's a good idea. Maybe after dinner tonight. I just wish he would understand how stressed I am too.
supporter: Your feelings are very valid, Emily. It's important for both of you to feel heard. Do you feel like you can express how you’re both feeling?
seeker: I want to, but sometimes I don’t know how to start without sounding like I’m blaming him.
supporter: Starting with 'I feel' statements can help focus on your emotions rather than assigning blame. It's okay to express vulnerability.
seeker: That's true. I'll try that. Thanks for reminding me. I just want us to be okay.
supporter: You’re doing your best, and that is important. Figuring it out together might bring you closer. How are you taking care of yourself today?
seeker: I haven’t really done much for myself yet. Maybe I should go for a walk or listen to some music.
supporter: That sounds like a wonderful idea. Taking a little time for self-care can help clear your mind and give you strength.
seeker: Thanks for listening. It really helps just having someone to talk to about all this.
supporter: I'm always here for you, Emily. Take it one step at a time, and keep me updated if you need anything.
seeker: I will. Thanks again.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-10-10","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hey, I just need someone to talk to right now.
supporter: Of course, Emily. I'm here for you. What's been going on?
seeker: It's about George. He had this really scary allergic reaction and ended up in the hospital.
supporter: Oh no, that sounds terrifying! Is he alright now?
seeker: Yeah, he's okay now, but I just can't seem to shake the anxiety after everything that happened.
supporter: It's totally understandable to feel anxious after something like that. You must have been so worried.
seeker: I really was. I kept thinking about what could have happened if we hadn't gotten to the hospital in time.
supporter: It's frightening to think about those 'what ifs.' But you did get him there in time, and he's safe now.
seeker: I know, but having to stay strong through it all is exhausting. And it brings back all those feelings from when he was bullied.
supporter: It sounds like there's been so much on your plate lately. It's okay to feel overwhelmed.
seeker: I thought things were getting better with Bob's new job and the positive feedback from my boss. But now it feels like I'm back at square one with worry.
supporter: Progress isn't always a straight line, although it feels like a setback now, you've managed so much already. You're very strong.
seeker: Thank you for saying that. It's just hard to see my kids go through this. I want to protect them, but sometimes I feel helpless.
supporter: Wanting to protect your children is natural. It doesn't make you helpless; it shows how deeply you care.
seeker: That makes sense. I've been trying to focus on the positives, like Bob's new job and how George is feeling better now.
supporter: That's a great approach, Emily. Focusing on those positives can help ground you during tough times.
seeker: I miss having Jerry around, though. Him leaving just added to everything.
supporter: It's tough when a family member moves away unexpectedly. Have you had any chance to reconnect with him since he left?
seeker: We've exchanged a couple of texts, but it's not the same. I'm hoping he'll come around eventually.
supporter: I hope so too. It's hard, but giving it time and keeping the door open for when he's ready to reconnect is a loving way to handle it.
seeker: Yeah, I'm trying to keep that in mind. It's comforting to at least talk this out.
supporter: Anytime, Emily. You're doing your best, and it shows. Remember, you're never alone in this.
seeker: Thanks for being here for me. It does make things feel a bit easier.
supporter: I'm really glad to hear that. Take care of yourself, and remember to reach out whenever you need.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-04-01","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hey Emily, it's been a little while. How are you doing?
seeker: Hi, it's been... a tough week.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. Do you want to talk about what's been going on?
seeker: Yeah, actually. My son Jerry got in trouble at school. They caught him using his phone inappropriately.
supporter: That sounds really stressful. How did you find out about it?
seeker: We had a meeting with the school's principal. It was embarrassing, especially after telling him so many times to focus on his studies.
supporter: I can imagine how difficult that must have been for you. How did the meeting go?
seeker: It was tense. The principal was understanding but firm. I just felt so disappointed and a bit like I've failed him.
supporter: It's understandable to feel that way, but you haven't failed him. You're a caring mother who's trying her best.
seeker: Thank you. I've been trying to figure out how to handle this. The financial strain with Bob, and now Jerry acting out... it's just a lot.
supporter: That does sound overwhelming. How have you been managing everything?
seeker: Therapy helps, but outside of that, I just try to keep my head above water.
supporter: I'm glad you've found some support in therapy. What strategies have been helping you there?
seeker: The therapist has been teaching me breathing techniques and we've been working on expressing my feelings more constructively.
supporter: That sounds really valuable. Do you think any of those techniques could help with how you're feeling about Jerry?
seeker: Perhaps. I think I need to communicate better with him and find out what's really going on beneath the surface.
supporter: It sounds like you have a great approach. Being able to talk openly with him might really help both of you.
seeker: I hope so. I just want to make sure he understands that I care about him, even when I’m upset.
supporter: He’s fortunate to have you watching out for him. If you ever need to talk more about any of this, I’m here for you.
seeker: Thank you. It means a lot to have someone to lean on right now.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-10-25","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

seeker: Hi, honestly I'm feeling pretty overwhelmed today.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. Is it what's happening at work that's on your mind?

seeker: I'm trying to just keep everything together. It’s hard when I’ve got stuff going on with Bob and with Jerry too.

seeker: We’re both stressed with money issues, and we've been arguing more. It's tough on both of us.
supporter: That sounds really challenging. Have you been able to talk about these concerns in therapy?
seeker: Yes, my therapist is great, but sometimes I feel like there's so much to unpack that it's overwhelming.
supporter: It's good to have that support though. It’s okay to take things one step at a time, even if it feels slow.

seeker: Thanks. It’s just hard when it feels like I'm not doing enough at work, and then things at home aren’t great either.
supporter: You're doing your best, and that counts for a lot. Have you had any moments recently where you found some peace or relief?
seeker: I guess there's been small moments, like when I take a walk or read a book before bed.
supporter: That's wonderful. Those small moments are so valuable. It's important to keep finding those times for yourself.
seeker: I should focus more on that, even if it's hard sometimes. Thank you for listening.

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hey, I really need to talk. Things have been so overwhelming lately.
supporter: I'm here for you, Emily. What's been going on?
seeker: Jerry left us. It was so sudden after a huge argument, and I feel lost.
supporter: I'm so sorry to hear that. It must be incredibly hard for you. Do you want to talk about what led to the disagreement?
seeker: We were arguing about his lack of responsibility and how he's ignoring his future. Maybe I was too harsh.
supporter: It sounds like you're worried about his well-being and future, which is completely understandable. How are you feeling about the situation now?
seeker: I'm torn. Part of me feels guilty, but another part feels exhausted from all the stress we've been through.
supporter: It's okay to feel mixed emotions. You're dealing with a lot on your plate—work, family, and financial pressures. It's understandable to feel overwhelmed.
seeker: Yeah, with Bob's job, Jerry's incident at school, and all... it feels never-ending. I just want a break.
supporter: You've been through an extraordinary amount. Can your therapy sessions provide a space to process these feelings?
seeker: They're helpful, but it's hard to shake the constant anxiety. I just wish Jerry was back home so we could work things out.
supporter: It sounds like you really value the connection with your family. Have you tried reaching out to Jerry since he left?
seeker: I have, but he hasn't responded. It breaks my heart knowing he's out there, upset and alone.
supporter: Feeling powerless in this situation can be stressful. Is there anyone else you can lean on for support during this time?
seeker: Bob's trying his best, but we both feel so drained. It's tough to even find time for us to talk deeply anymore.
supporter: Finding moments to connect amidst the chaos sounds challenging. Maybe even small shared moments with Bob could provide some comfort?
seeker: That's true. Even just sitting together, watching something light, might ease the tension.
supporter: That sounds like a good start. Remember, you're doing your best in a tough situation. It's okay to take small steps and be kind to yourself.
seeker: Thank you, that really helps. I guess I just have to keep trying and hope things will get better.
supporter: Absolutely, Emily. Keep holding on to that hope, and I'm here for you whenever you need to talk.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-12-30","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hello
seeker: Hello, I am looking for help in managing some depression.
supporter: You've come to a good place to start.
supporter: Is there something in particular that is leaving you feeling depressed?
seeker: I am feeling resentful towards my husband for quitting his job, and my son for being the reason that he quit his job.
seeker: My son's behavior is causing a lot of conflict in our house and my husband not working is putting a lot of financial stress on us
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. Feeling resentment for both your husband's loss of work and your son's loss of his job is entirely understandable. 
seeker: I have a hard time not dwelling on the negative things going on.  It's hard to see anything positive or feel hopeful for the future.
supporter: I have an adult son who also lost his job recently, and I understand the added stress that can cause in your household. 
supporter: That is a really difficult position to be in. 
seeker: My son is very defiant and argues with us about everything we try and get him to do, but he expects us to give him money for fun things that he wants to do when he isn't willing to work or even help out around the house
supporter: Regardless of what your husband's actions are and your son's, could you possibly make the time to do things to support yourself, that even momentarily would provide you with some positive feelings? 
seeker: I try to go for a run every night, that does help.  
supporter: That is very hard emotionally, so I am sorry you have to deal with your son's behavior.
seeker: It is hard to keep my emotions separate from what is going on with him
supporter: That is very understandable! Setting boundaries for yourself may help. Even when it's difficult, being clear with your son that you will not be giving him money could help. 
supporter: Sometimes being clear with your own expectations can help him to see what won't be accepted from him as long as he is living in your home.
seeker: Yes, I could do better at that.  I want him to have fun and do things with friends, but I want him to be willing to work for what he wants, too.  
seeker: I do struggle with expectations.  I want him to be someone that he is not willing to be, I need to let go of that and just let him be himself and not base my emotions on his choices.
supporter: I completely understand that. Especially when it comes to people we are close to, it can be hard to separate our expectations from theirs. 
seeker: I feel guilty sometimes taking time to do things that I like and that are away from my family.  I can see that I need to do that more, though.
supporter: I've had to learn this lesson many times with my own children. It's difficult, but ultimately will give you some relief from your resentment. 
seeker: Thank you, it is helpful to know that other people have felt the same way.
supporter: Absolutely! Being a parent is difficult. Remembering to support yourself helps. Making the time to do things to support your wellbeing doesn't make you selfish at all
seeker: Thank you!
supporter: You are certainly not alone.
supporter: Has any of this been helpful? Is there more I can do for you?","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-07-14","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hey there, I guess I just needed to talk today.
supporter: Of course, Emily. I'm here for you. What's on your mind?
seeker: Well, I got an unexpected compliment from my boss today about my recent performance at work.
supporter: That sounds like a positive development! How does that make you feel?
seeker: Relieved, to some extent. It's been a while since I've felt good about my work.
supporter: It's understandable given the increased workload and stress you've faced. It's great to hear some recognition is coming your way. What do you think brought about the compliment?
seeker: I think I've finally adapted a bit to the changes after the acquisition, and I've been trying really hard to stay focused, even though it's tough with everything else going on.
supporter: You've been putting in a lot of effort, and it shows. It's not easy to balance work stress with personal struggles. How have things been at home?
seeker: Things with Bob are still stressful, with the financial strains and all. His part-time job has helped some, but there's still tension.
supporter: Relationships can be challenging, especially under financial pressure. Have you two had any discussions about how to move forward?
seeker: We talk... but it's mostly arguments. I feel like we're both just at our wits' end sometimes.
supporter: It sounds really tough. Disagreements are hard, but it can be helpful to approach it as a team, looking for solutions together. Do you think that's possible?
seeker: I hope so. It's just hard to communicate when we're both stressed and upset.
supporter: Stress can definitely make communication harder. Your therapist might have some strategies that could help when you're feeling overwhelmed.
seeker: Yeah, I'll mention it next time I see her. It could be helpful to have some new approaches.
supporter: That's a great idea. How is everything going with your son and his situation at school?
seeker: 's still having a tough time. He's grounded after the incident at school, and that's affecting us too. I just wish things could be simpler.
supporter: That sounds really tough on all of you. It's okay to feel overwhelmed by everything. You mentioned Jerry left home after a disagreement too—how are you handling that?
seeker: Honestly, I feel a mix of anger, sadness, and worry. I know he's an adult, but I wish he hadn't left like that.
supporter: It's completely natural to have those feelings, Emily. You're a caring mother, and wanting your child close is understandable. Have you been able to reach out to him since then?
seeker: Not much. He needs space, I think. It's just hard to not be able to help him when he needs it.
supporter: That must be really tough. Giving him space while being there if he needs support is a good balance. Try to focus on being ready for when he's ready to reconnect.
seeker: Thanks for saying that. It's been a lot to handle, but I'm trying to stay hopeful.
supporter: Hope is important. Taking things one step at a time can make it more manageable. Is there anything specific that's helped you manage your stress lately?
seeker: I've started walking in the mornings to clear my head. It’s not much, but I think it helps.
supporter: That sounds like a healthy habit. Small steps forward are definitely progress. Remember, I'm always here when you need to talk. You don't have to face things alone.
seeker: Thank you. It's nice to know I have your support.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-01-10","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hi I am seeking support to assist me with better sleep patterns.
supporter: Hi there, let me get a deeper understanding of your existing sleep pattern. Do you suffer from insomnia or another type of sleep disorder? 
seeker: No, it is not insomnia.  
supporter: Okay, are you drinking enough water and eating a healthy diet? 
seeker: I could improve my water intake and eat more vegatables.
supporter: I like to analyze my own habits every now and then, it helps me stay in check. You can definitely benefit from meditating and self reflecting. 
seeker: Thanks!  What other ideas do you have?
supporter: Of course! I always knock right out after a workout. But if you aren't able to, just simple things like turning all the lights off at the same time every night and laying in bed will help. It will align your circadian rhythm! 
seeker: Great, but I wake up frequently thinking about the recent events surrounding police and how they treat black people.
supporter: It definitely is a valid reason to be kept awake. The only good part about something so horrible, is that you have the power to make sure you will continue to be a good person. If everyone was as empathetic as you, the world would be a better place. Thank you for caring so deeply about such a brutal matter. 
seeker: I wish there were more caring people in the world. 
supporter: Kindness is contagious, and you definitely have a kind heart. As long as you remain soft in a hard world, people will recognize that and follow suit. The world is becoming more aware, and we have the power to raise future generations with more knowledge and love for one another. Caring doesn't come naturally to many unfortunately, but the ways of inspiring the people that don't care, are endless. We as a society can definitely think of more ways to care for one another. 
seeker: Correct, but having a kind heart does not keep me from waking up & worrying about my son and other black men in my family. 
supporter: I worry about my sons and husband and father all the time... I shift my focus on loving them and cherishing every moment we have together. Police or not, the time we have is not promised.. 
seeker: That's good advice.
seeker: Are you still there?
supporter: A hot cup of tea never hurt too! But in all seriousness, I can completely understand your sleep troubles. It is much deeper than just that. Perspective is the key to life. You are a strong and empathetic soul. 
seeker: okay
seeker: Love conquers all
supporter: That is so beautifully true 
seeker: I'm looking forward to a fulls night rest. 
supporter: That is good, lavender baths or showers will also ease and relax the troubled mind. 
seeker: Relaxing is good therapy. 
supporter: I like to relax with a book and a blanket sometimes too. 
seeker: Self care is needed.
supporter: Self care is definitely something we can overlook accidentally. Being self aware is a daily practice.
seeker: I agree.  Loving ourselves & the ones we care about too.  
supporter: It is good that we spoke today, I am going to hug my sons a little harder when I see them tonight. ","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-09-06","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hello
seeker: Hello, I am looking for help in managing some depression.
supporter: You've come to a good place to start.
supporter: Is there something in particular that is leaving you feeling depressed?
seeker: I am feeling resentful towards my husband for quitting his job, and my son for being the reason that he quit his job.
seeker: My son's behavior is causing a lot of conflict in our house and my husband not working is putting a lot of financial stress on us
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. Feeling resentment for both your husband's loss of work and your son's loss of his job is entirely understandable. 
seeker: I have a hard time not dwelling on the negative things going on.  It's hard to see anything positive or feel hopeful for the future.
supporter: I have an adult son who also lost his job recently, and I understand the added stress that can cause in your household. 
supporter: That is a really difficult position to be in. 
seeker: My son is very defiant and argues with us about everything we try and get him to do, but he expects us to give him money for fun things that he wants to do when he isn't willing to work or even help out around the house
supporter: Regardless of what your husband's actions are and your son's, could you possibly make the time to do things to support yourself, that even momentarily would provide you with some positive feelings? 
seeker: I try to go for a run every night, that does help.  
supporter: That is very hard emotionally, so I am sorry you have to deal with your son's behavior.
seeker: It is hard to keep my emotions separate from what is going on with him
supporter: That is very understandable! Setting boundaries for yourself may help. Even when it's difficult, being clear with your son that you will not be giving him money could help. 
supporter: Sometimes being clear with your own expectations can help him to see what won't be accepted from him as long as he is living in your home.
seeker: Yes, I could do better at that.  I want him to have fun and do things with friends, but I want him to be willing to work for what he wants, too.  
seeker: I do struggle with expectations.  I want him to be someone that he is not willing to be, I need to let go of that and just let him be himself and not base my emotions on his choices.
supporter: I completely understand that. Especially when it comes to people we are close to, it can be hard to separate our expectations from theirs. 
seeker: I feel guilty sometimes taking time to do things that I like and that are away from my family.  I can see that I need to do that more, though.
supporter: I've had to learn this lesson many times with my own children. It's difficult, but ultimately will give you some relief from your resentment. 
seeker: Thank you, it is helpful to know that other people have felt the same way.
supporter: Absolutely! Being a parent is difficult. Remembering to support yourself helps. Making the time to do things to support your wellbeing doesn't make you selfish at all
seeker: Thank you!
supporter: You are certainly not alone.
supporter: Has any of this been helpful? Is there more I can do for you?","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-07-14","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

supporter: Of course, Emily. I'm here for you. What's going on?
seeker: Bob and I had a big argument last night. I haven't been able to stop thinking about it.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. Arguments can be really tough. Do you want to share what happened?
seeker: Yeah, it just spiraled out of control. We started talking about our finances, and it just got heated.
supporter: Financial pressures can put so much strain on relationships. It's completely understandable to feel overwhelmed. How are you feeling now?
seeker: Exhausted, honestly. It's like we're stuck in this cycle of stress, and I don't see a way out.
supporter: It sounds really challenging, Emily. It's okay to feel this way. Have you two been able to talk it out since it happened?
seeker: Not yet. We both needed some space. Bob went for a drive, and I've just been trying to calm down.
supporter: Taking some space can be helpful to gather thoughts. Do you think you’ll be ready to talk soon?
seeker: I hope so. I don't want to keep ignoring it, but I'm also scared it'll turn into another argument.
supporter: That's understandable. Talking during a calm moment might help. Maybe planning a time to chat could prevent it from escalating?
seeker: That's a good idea. Maybe after dinner tonight. I just wish he would understand how stressed I am too.
supporter: Your feelings are very valid, Emily. It's important for both of you to feel heard. Do you feel like you can express how you’re both feeling?

supporter: That sounds like a wonderful idea. Taking a little time for self-care can help clear your mind and give you strength.
seeker: Thanks for listening. It really helps just having someone to talk to about all this.

seeker: I will. Thanks again.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-10-10","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hey Emily, how have you been doing lately?
seeker: Hi there, it's been a bit of a rollercoaster, honestly.
supporter: I can imagine. There have been quite a few changes recently, right? Would you like to share what's been on your mind?
seeker: Well, Bob just got a full-time job, which is a huge relief financially. But I’m still feeling quite overwhelmed.
supporter: That's great news about Bob's job! But it's understandable that other things have been weighing on you. What do you think is contributing to your feelings of being overwhelmed?
seeker: It's mostly George. I'm still so worried about him being bullied at school. I just don't know how to help him feel safe.
supporter: That sounds incredibly difficult. It's heart-wrenching to see our kids go through tough times like that. How is George coping?
seeker: He seems okay on the surface, but I can tell it's affecting him. He's become quieter at home, and I think he's trying to hide his feelings.
supporter: It's painful to know he's keeping it inside. Have you been able to talk to him, or his teachers, about what's been happening?
seeker: I've tried talking to him, but he just says everything is okay. I'm planning to meet with his teacher soon to see what they can do.
supporter: That sounds like a good plan. Sometimes having a discussion with the school can help in finding solutions together.
seeker: I hope so. I just can't help but feel guilty, like I'm not doing enough to protect him.
supporter: It's normal to feel that way, but remember, you’re doing what you can by being attentive and proactive about the situation.
seeker: Thanks. It's just with everything else happening, like when Jerry left, sometimes I feel like I'm losing control of everything.
supporter: It's a lot to carry on your shoulders. Losing control can bring up all kinds of emotions. Have you been able to find anything helpful to ground you during these times?
seeker: Therapy has been helpful, and Bob’s new job does lift some of the financial stress. I'm just trying to keep everything balanced.
supporter: That's a lot of positive progress, Emily. Having Bob's support and attending therapy is a big step towards managing everything that's going on.
seeker: Thank you. I guess I need to be kinder to myself and remember it's okay to lean on others sometimes.
supporter: Absolutely. You’re doing your best in tough circumstances. Needing support is completely okay, and it sounds like you've got a good plan in place.
seeker: I really appreciate you listening. It helps to talk it through with someone who understands.
supporter: Anytime, Emily. Remember, you're not alone in this. Let's check in again soon, how does that sound?
seeker: That sounds great. Thank you again for being there.
supporter: You're welcome. Take care, and talk to you soon!","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-03-05","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

supporter: Of course, Emily. I'm here for you. How have things been since you started therapy?
seeker: It's been a bit overwhelming, to be honest. I'm glad I took the step, but it's a lot to unpack.
supporter: It sounds like you're processing a lot. It's completely normal to feel overwhelmed. What's been on your mind?
seeker: Mainly my relationship with Bob and the financial strain. It's hard not to feel angry and resentful sometimes.

seeker: We're trying to talk more without arguing, but it's a struggle. I can't help but feel frustrated thinking about how he left his job.
supporter: I can hear the frustration and it's valid. It must be tough carrying the burden alone. How is the therapy helping you with these feelings?
seeker: Therapy helps, slowly. It's nice to have a space to express myself, but it doesn't change things immediately at home.
supporter: Having an outlet is important. Therapy can sometimes take time, but it's great you're making progress. Are there things you're learning that help?
seeker: I learned about setting boundaries and communicating my needs. It’s something I’m working on with Bob.
supporter: That sounds like a positive step. How is Bob responding to the changes you're trying to make?
seeker: I think he's trying, but it's hard to change old habits, especially when both of us are stressed.
supporter: Change is challenging, especially during tough times. Acknowledging the effort on both sides is a good step. What about your job? How's that affecting things?
seeker: Work is another stress. They doubled my workload after an acquisition, but no raise came with it.

seeker: I try to take walks and focus on mindfulness exercises. They help me feel a little more grounded.
supporter: That's great to hear. It's important to celebrate these small wins. {"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hey Emily, it's been a little while. How are you doing?
seeker: Hi, it's been... a tough week.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. Do you want to talk about what's been going on?
seeker: Yeah, actually. My son Jerry got in trouble at school. They caught him using his phone inappropriately.
supporter: That sounds really stressful. How did you find out about it?
seeker: We had a meeting with the school's principal. It was embarrassing, especially after telling him so many times to focus on his studies.
supporter: I can imagine how difficult that must have been for you. How did the meeting go?
seeker: It was tense. The principal was understanding but firm. I just felt so disappointed and a bit like I've failed him.
supporter: It's understandable to feel that way, but you haven't failed him. You're a caring mother who's trying her best.
seeker: Thank you. I've been trying to figure out how to handle this. The financial strain with Bob, and now Jerry acting out... it's just a lot.
supporter: That does sound overwhelming. How have you been managing everything?
seeker: Therapy helps, but outside of that, I just try to keep my head above water.
supporter: I'm glad you've found some support in therapy. What strategies have been helping you there?
seeker: The therapist has been teaching me breathing techniques and we've been working on expressing my feelings more constructively.
supporter: That sounds really valuable. Do you think any of those techniques could help with how you're feeling about Jerry?
seeker: Perhaps. I think I need to communicate better with him and find out what's really going on beneath the surface.
supporter: It sounds like you have a great approach. Being able to talk openly with him might really help both of you.
seeker: I hope so. I just want to make sure he understands that I care about him, even when I’m upset.
supporter: He’s fortunate to have you watching out for him. If you ever need to talk more about any of this, I’m here for you.
seeker: Thank you. It means a lot to have someone to lean on right now.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-10-25","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hey, are you around? I could really use someone to talk to.
supporter: Of course, Emily. I'm here for you. What's going on?
seeker: Bob and I had a big argument last night. I haven't been able to stop thinking about it.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. Arguments can be really tough. Do you want to share what happened?
seeker: Yeah, it just spiraled out of control. We started talking about our finances, and it just got heated.
supporter: Financial pressures can put so much strain on relationships. It's completely understandable to feel overwhelmed. How are you feeling now?
seeker: Exhausted, honestly. It's like we're stuck in this cycle of stress, and I don't see a way out.
supporter: It sounds really challenging, Emily. It's okay to feel this way. Have you two been able to talk it out since it happened?
seeker: Not yet. We both needed some space. Bob went for a drive, and I've just been trying to calm down.
supporter: Taking some space can be helpful to gather thoughts. Do you think you’ll be ready to talk soon?
seeker: I hope so. I don't want to keep ignoring it, but I'm also scared it'll turn into another argument.
supporter: That's understandable. Talking during a calm moment might help. Maybe planning a time to chat could prevent it from escalating?
seeker: That's a good idea. Maybe after dinner tonight. I just wish he would understand how stressed I am too.
supporter: Your feelings are very valid, Emily. It's important for both of you to feel heard. Do you feel like you can express how you’re both feeling?
seeker: I want to, but sometimes I don’t know how to start without sounding like I’m blaming him.
supporter: Starting with 'I feel' statements can help focus on your emotions rather than assigning blame. It's okay to express vulnerability.
seeker: That's true. I'll try that. Thanks for reminding me. I just want us to be okay.
supporter: You’re doing your best, and that is important. Figuring it out together might bring you closer. How are you taking care of yourself today?
seeker: I haven’t really done much for myself yet. Maybe I should go for a walk or listen to some music.
supporter: That sounds like a wonderful idea. Taking a little time for self-care can help clear your mind and give you strength.
seeker: Thanks for listening. It really helps just having someone to talk to about all this.
supporter: I'm always here for you, Emily. Take it one step at a time, and keep me updated if you need anything.
seeker: I will. Thanks again.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-10-10","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

seeker: Hello, I hope you can help me.

seeker: I work hard at my job in an office.  We acquired another company and my job is now twice the work.

supporter: Have you talked to your boss about it?
seeker: I have hinted around that my job is sooo busy and he knows it, I haven't come out and said anything yet.
supporter: I can understand how you feeling you work extremely hard and get no raise when you deserve it
seeker: Yes, I have been at the job for 15 years and make a decent salary but this amount of work is insane.  Do you think I should bring it up to him>
supporter: oh wow 15 years? I really believe you need a raise and doing more work now.
supporter: I honestly think you should bring it up to your boss
seeker: Yes, I think so too.  I like my boss but he is funny about things sometimes.  Any ideas on how I could bring it up to him.  I hate feeling this way, my attitude is really turning sour.
supporter: I can't believe he has not given you a raise by now 
seeker: I know!
supporter: Just tell him that you need to have a serious talk with him and tell him straight up what is on your mind don't hold it back
seeker: So, I guess I'll have to be honest and brave at the same time.  
seeker: Do you think I should bring in proof....paperwork, etc.  I have been working extra as well.
supporter: Yes I know you can do it but that is the only way to solve the situation is by communicating with him
supporter: Yes that would help more by bringing in proof to him 
seeker: Ok, I am just so angry over the whole thing, I'm going to have to keep my cool and let him know without getting an attitude, do you think that will work?

seeker: I will try, I hope I don't start crying!  I tend to get frustrated and cry.

seeker: O

seeker: Thank you so much for your positive support!

seeker: Thank you so much, you've been very helpful!

supporter: Merry Christmas to you to!","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-07-01","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hi I am seeking support to assist me with better sleep patterns.
supporter: Hi there, let me get a deeper understanding of your existing sleep pattern. Do you suffer from insomnia or another type of sleep disorder? 
seeker: No, it is not insomnia.  
supporter: Okay, are you drinking enough water and eating a healthy diet? 
seeker: I could improve my water intake and eat more vegatables.
supporter: I like to analyze my own habits every now and then, it helps me stay in check. You can definitely benefit from meditating and self reflecting. 
seeker: Thanks!  What other ideas do you have?
supporter: Of course! I always knock right out after a workout. But if you aren't able to, just simple things like turning all the lights off at the same time every night and laying in bed will help. It will align your circadian rhythm! 
seeker: Great, but I wake up frequently thinking about the recent events surrounding police and how they treat black people.
supporter: It definitely is a valid reason to be kept awake. The only good part about something so horrible, is that you have the power to make sure you will continue to be a good person. If everyone was as empathetic as you, the world would be a better place. Thank you for caring so deeply about such a brutal matter. 
seeker: I wish there were more caring people in the world. 
supporter: Kindness is contagious, and you definitely have a kind heart. As long as you remain soft in a hard world, people will recognize that and follow suit. The world is becoming more aware, and we have the power to raise future generations with more knowledge and love for one another. Caring doesn't come naturally to many unfortunately, but the ways of inspiring the people that don't care, are endless. We as a society can definitely think of more ways to care for one another. 
seeker: Correct, but having a kind heart does not keep me from waking up & worrying about my son and other black men in my family. 
supporter: I worry about my sons and husband and father all the time... I shift my focus on loving them and cherishing every moment we have together. Police or not, the time we have is not promised.. 
seeker: That's good advice.
seeker: Are you still there?
supporter: A hot cup of tea never hurt too! But in all seriousness, I can completely understand your sleep troubles. It is much deeper than just that. Perspective is the key to life. You are a strong and empathetic soul. 
seeker: okay
seeker: Love conquers all
supporter: That is so beautifully true 
seeker: I'm looking forward to a fulls night rest. 
supporter: That is good, lavender baths or showers will also ease and relax the troubled mind. 
seeker: Relaxing is good therapy. 
supporter: I like to relax with a book and a blanket sometimes too. 
seeker: Self care is needed.
supporter: Self care is definitely something we can overlook accidentally. Being self aware is a daily practice.
seeker: I agree.  Loving ourselves & the ones we care about too.  
supporter: It is good that we spoke today, I am going to hug my sons a little harder when I see them tonight. ","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-09-06","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

supporter: Of course, Emily. I'm here for you. How have things been since you started therapy?
seeker: It's been a bit overwhelming, to be honest. I'm glad I took the step, but it's a lot to unpack.
supporter: It sounds like you're processing a lot. It's completely normal to feel overwhelmed. What's been on your mind?
seeker: Mainly my relationship with Bob and the financial strain. It's hard not to feel angry and resentful sometimes.
supporter: That's understandable. Financial pressures can really strain relationships. How are you both handling it right now?
seeker: We're trying to talk more without arguing, but it's a struggle. I can't help but feel frustrated thinking about how he left his job.
supporter: I can hear the frustration and it's valid. It must be tough carrying the burden alone. How is the therapy helping you with these feelings?
seeker: Therapy helps, slowly. It's nice to have a space to express myself, but it doesn't change things immediately at home.
supporter: Having an outlet is important. Therapy can sometimes take time, but it's great you're making progress. Are there things you're learning that help?
seeker: I learned about setting boundaries and communicating my needs. It’s something I’m working on with Bob.
supporter: That sounds like a positive step. How is Bob responding to the changes you're trying to make?
seeker: I think he's trying, but it's hard to change old habits, especially when both of us are stressed.

seeker: Work is another stress. They doubled my workload after an acquisition, but no raise came with it.

supporter: It's okay to feel that way. It seems like you're doing your best despite everything. Are you able to find any small ways to de-stress?
seeker: I try to take walks and focus on mindfulness exercises. They help me feel a little more grounded.
supporter: That's great to hear. It's important to celebrate these small wins. seeker: Hello, I am looking for help in managing some depression.
supporter: You've come to a good place to start.
supporter: Is there something in particular that is leaving you feeling depressed?
seeker: I am feeling resentful towards my husband for quitting his job, and my son for being the reason that he quit his job.
seeker: My son's behavior is causing a lot of conflict in our house and my husband not working is putting a lot of financial stress on us
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. Feeling resentment for both your husband's loss of work and your son's loss of his job is entirely understandable. 
seeker: I have a hard time not dwelling on the negative things going on.  It's hard to see anything positive or feel hopeful for the future.
supporter: I have an adult son who also lost his job recently, and I understand the added stress that can cause in your household. 
supporter: That is a really difficult position to be in. 
seeker: My son is very defiant and argues with us about everything we try and get him to do, but he expects us to give him money for fun things that he wants to do when he isn't willing to work or even help out around the house
supporter: Regardless of what your husband's actions are and your son's, could you possibly make the time to do things to support yourself, that even momentarily would provide you with some positive feelings? 
seeker: I try to go for a run every night, that does help.

seeker: Hi, it's been... a tough week.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. Do you want to talk about what's been going on?
seeker: Yeah, actually. My son Jerry got in trouble at school. They caught him using his phone inappropriately.
supporter: That sounds really stressful. How did you find out about it?
seeker: We had a meeting with the school's principal. It was embarrassing, especially after telling him so many times to focus on his studies.
supporter: I can imagine how difficult that must have been for you. How did the meeting go?
seeker: It was tense. The principal was understanding but firm. I just felt so disappointed and a bit like I've failed him.
supporter: It's understandable to feel that way, but you haven't failed him. You're a caring mother who's trying her best.
seeker: Thank you. I've been trying to figure out how to handle this. The financial strain with Bob, and now Jerry acting out... it's just a lot.
supporter: That does sound overwhelming. How have you been managing everything?
seeker: Therapy helps, but outside of that, I just try to keep my head above water.
supporter: I'm glad you've found some support in therapy. What strategies have been helping you there?

supporter: That sounds really valuable. Do you think any of those techniques could help with how you're feeling about Jerry?
seeker: Perhaps. I think I need to communicate better with him and find out what's really going on beneath the surface.
supporter: It sounds like you have a great approach. Being able to talk openly with him might really help both of you.
seeker: I hope so. I just want to make sure he understands that I care about him, even when I’m upset.

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hey Anna, it's good to see you online. How are you doing today?
seeker: Hi... honestly, not so great. It's been a rough week.
supporter: I'm really sorry to hear that. Do you want to talk about what's been going on?
seeker: Yeah, I had an argument with my parents about my future plans, and it got really intense.
supporter: That sounds tough. What was the argument about, if you're comfortable sharing?
seeker: They want me to focus on getting into a good university, but I'm not even sure what I want to study yet.
supporter: It can be really overwhelming when you're not sure about your path, and there's pressure from others. How did that make you feel?
seeker: I just felt trapped and like I was disappointing them. It reminded me of the fight I had with my boyfriend about future plans too.
supporter: It's natural to feel that way when expectations feel piled up. How's everything with your boyfriend now?
seeker: We haven't really resolved things. It's this limbo where everything feels uncertain, and now my parents add to that stress.
supporter: That sounds like so much to carry all at once, Anna. It’s understandable to feel overwhelmed. What do you feel you need right now?
seeker: I think I need to figure out what I actually want for my future without feeling like I'm letting everyone down.
supporter: That's a really important realization. It's your future, after all. Have you had any thoughts about what interests or excites you?
seeker: I love art and writing, but I'm not sure if that's practical. It feels risky compared to more traditional paths.
supporter: Pursuing your passions is important, and finding a balance is possible. Perhaps exploring these interests, even as a hobby, could help you feel more connected to what you love?
seeker: That might actually be a good idea. Maybe starting with small steps could clarify things without committing everything right now.
supporter: Starting small sounds like a great plan. You don't have to have everything figured out at once. It's okay to take your time.
seeker: Thanks for saying that. I think I’ll try talking to my parents again once I've thought more about what I want.
supporter: That sounds like a positive step forward. I'm here for you, and remember, it's okay to ask for this space to explore your interests.
seeker: Thanks for listening. It really helps to talk about it.
supporter: Anytime, Anna. You're doing your best, and that's all anyone can ask for. Let me know how things go, okay?","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-10-20","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hey, got a minute to chat?
supporter: Of course, Anna. How have you been holding up lately?
seeker: It’s been a roller coaster. My parents apologized yesterday for being so strict with me.
supporter: Wow, that sounds like a big step for them. How did that make you feel?
seeker: Honestly, it was overwhelming. I felt a mix of relief and confusion. I never expected it.
supporter: It makes sense. The way parents communicate can really impact how we feel about ourselves. What was the discussion like?
seeker: We ended up talking about everything—my future, their expectations, how everything has been affecting me.
supporter: That’s a really open and brave conversation to have. How did they respond to your feelings?
seeker: They seemed genuinely sorry and promised to be more understanding. But a part of me is still anxious about all the pressure.
supporter: It's completely natural to feel that way, especially after what you've been through. What parts are making you most anxious?
seeker: The thought of future pressures, you know? Like, with Lily moving abroad and my midterms not going so well.
supporter: You’ve been handling a lot at once. It’s okay to feel anxious about these changes. Have you talked to Lily since she moved?
seeker: We’ve texted a bit, but it’s not the same. I miss having her around, especially now.
supporter: I can imagine. She was a big part of your support system. Do you think it might help to get more involved with your peer tutoring club?
seeker: I hope so. It’s been good for talking to more people, but it's still all new and can feel overwhelming.
supporter: That’s understandable. Starting new things takes time to get comfortable. It’s a brave step to take.
seeker: Thanks. I’m trying to balance everything, but I worry about adding more stress for my parents with the financial stuff.
supporter: You’re figuring out so much right now. It's clear you care deeply for them, but remember that your well-being is important too.
seeker: Yeah, I guess I need to keep reminding myself of that. I just don’t want to let them down.
supporter: You’re doing your best, and that’s what matters. They see how hard you're trying. It’s important to also focus on what you need.
seeker: I’ll try to keep that in mind. Thanks for listening. It really helps.

seeker: Hi. It's been a bit of a rollercoaster, to be honest. I went on a school field trip recently.

seeker: I love that idea! I think I’ll feel much better if I take that time to just relax before I really start working.
supporter: There is a famous quote " Worry is a total waste of time. It doesn't change anything. All it does is steal your joy and keep you busy doing nothing."

seeker: I feel torn because I really care about him, but our visions for the future just aren't aligning right now.

seeker: We did talk, but it didn't go well. We both ended up just getting more upset.

seeker: That's true. I know I'll probably have to make some compromises, I just need to figure out which ones I'm okay with.
supporter: It sounds like you're being very thoughtful about the situation. It's okay to take your time to figure these things out.
seeker: Thanks. I just want to find a way to make things work between us without giving up too much of myself.
supporter: Having that intention is important. You deserve to have a relationship where you feel respected and supported in pursuing your own dreams too.
seeker: I hope so. It's just hard when someone you care about seems to be on a different path.
supporter: It's completely understandable. Relationships often require understanding and patience from both sides.

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: I feel heavy pressures from my parents, they also want me to be the top of the class but I find it tough because they are other top students
seeker: Please what do I do?
supporter: Hi! how are you doing today?
seeker: Not so good, I'm feeling down
supporter: It sounds like you have low energy. What makes you feel down?
seeker: My parents keep putting pressures on me to be the best in the class and with my learning difficulties I am finding it had to cope 
supporter: I can understand parental pressure. They want to see you to be a successful person. Sometime it is overwhelming. you should talk to them that you are doing your best.
seeker: I have tried, I am even doing extra classes but they still keep on putting pressure on me. On top of that all my friends have distant from me for no reason and they ganged up on me to bully me 
supporter: It must be tough time for you. show your work report to your parents and try to tell them all the people are born with different potential.
seeker: Hmm...That doesn't seem like a bad idea. I am just worry that my parents will not be very understanding. My parents are too strict and they don't like to hear any complaints or excuses.
supporter: Most of the parents behave like this when it is regarding their kids future. When I was in school same thing happened with mw. They know us very well I realized now.  Try to talk to them everyday for a while. It might work.
seeker: Maybe you're right! Although, my parents have a very busy schedule but fingers crossed when I do find time to talk to them they will understand me. 
seeker: I sometimes feel like someone older needs to talk to them, maybe then my parents may take it more seriously
seeker: Well! Thanks I give what you said a go
supporter: Hope you are feeling bit relaxed now. 
seeker: Yes! I feel a lot better now that I know someone understands how I feel 
supporter: I am glad that I am able to make you happy. 
seeker: One more thing
seeker: How should I respond to the friends that are ganging up on me?
supporter: sure! You don't have to worry about that. that should be their problem. just ignore them or don't give attention. They will stop doing it for sure.
seeker: Hmm..interesting because now that I think about it, I believe this could have contributed to the stress and anxieties that I have been experiencing. When I don't get support from anyone I feel so alone, timid and down 
supporter: Try to take small break while studying and try to relax 
seeker: Yes, I find that has helped me a bit also because I have quite a short attention span . Also, I am currently on the path of trying to find more unique techniques to help revision more fun and exciting for me 
supporter: That's great! you will do awesome.
seeker: Thank you very much! I feel much better now and I've taken on board what you said, hopefully there will be a positive change in my parents character. :)
supporter: You are welcome!
seeker: Alright! Well I'll talk to you some other time to give an update 
supporter: Sure! take care
seeker: Thanks you too! :)","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-07-10","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: I feel heavy pressures from my parents, they also want me to be the top of the class but I find it tough because they are other top students
seeker: Please what do I do?
supporter: Hi! how are you doing today?
seeker: Not so good, I'm feeling down
supporter: It sounds like you have low energy. What makes you feel down?
seeker: My parents keep putting pressures on me to be the best in the class and with my learning difficulties I am finding it had to cope 
supporter: I can understand parental pressure. They want to see you to be a successful person. Sometime it is overwhelming. you should talk to them that you are doing your best.
seeker: I have tried, I am even doing extra classes but they still keep on putting pressure on me. On top of that all my friends have distant from me for no reason and they ganged up on me to bully me 
supporter: It must be tough time for you. show your work report to your parents and try to tell them all the people are born with different potential.
seeker: Hmm...That doesn't seem like a bad idea. I am just worry that my parents will not be very understanding. My parents are too strict and they don't like to hear any complaints or excuses.
supporter: Most of the parents behave like this when it is regarding their kids future. When I was in school same thing happened with mw. They know us very well I realized now.  Try to talk to them everyday for a while. It might work.
seeker: Maybe you're right! Although, my parents have a very busy schedule but fingers crossed when I do find time to talk to them they will understand me. 
seeker: I sometimes feel like someone older needs to talk to them, maybe then my parents may take it more seriously
seeker: Well! Thanks I give what you said a go
supporter: Hope you are feeling bit relaxed now. 
seeker: Yes! I feel a lot better now that I know someone understands how I feel 
supporter: I am glad that I am able to make you happy. 
seeker: One more thing
seeker: How should I respond to the friends that are ganging up on me?
supporter: sure! You don't have to worry about that. that should be their problem. just ignore them or don't give attention. They will stop doing it for sure.
seeker: Hmm..interesting because now that I think about it, I believe this could have contributed to the stress and anxieties that I have been experiencing. When I don't get support from anyone I feel so alone, timid and down 
supporter: Try to take small break while studying and try to relax 
seeker: Yes, I find that has helped me a bit also because I have quite a short attention span . Also, I am currently on the path of trying to find more unique techniques to help revision more fun and exciting for me 
supporter: That's great! you will do awesome.
seeker: Thank you very much! I feel much better now and I've taken on board what you said, hopefully there will be a positive change in my parents character. :)
supporter: You are welcome!
seeker: Alright! Well I'll talk to you some other time to give an update 
supporter: Sure! take care
seeker: Thanks you too! :)","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-07-10","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hi Anna, how have things been going for you lately?
seeker: Hey, it's been a bit tough to be honest.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. Would you like to talk about what's been happening?
seeker: Yeah, I had a fight with my boyfriend recently, and it's been weighing on me a lot.
supporter: That sounds really challenging. What was the fight about, if you don't mind sharing?
seeker: It was about our priorities and goals for the future. We seem to be on different pages, and I'm not sure how to handle it.
supporter: That can definitely be a hard topic to navigate. How are you feeling about the differences in your priorities?
seeker: I feel torn because I really care about him, but our visions for the future just aren't aligning right now.
supporter: It sounds like you're in a tough spot, wanting to find a balance between your feelings for him and your own future plans.
seeker: Exactly. I just don't want to lose him over this, but I also don't want to compromise too much on what I want for my future.
supporter: It's important to stay true to yourself while also considering the relationship. Have you talked to him about how you're feeling?
seeker: We did talk, but it didn't go well. We both ended up just getting more upset.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that it escalated. Sometimes it can be helpful to take a break and approach the conversation with a fresh perspective.
seeker: Yeah, we haven't spoken much since the fight. I'm hoping we can find a way to discuss things more calmly.
supporter: That's a good goal. It might also help to think about what aspects of your goals are most important to you, and where you might have some flexibility.
seeker: That's true. I know I'll probably have to make some compromises, I just need to figure out which ones I'm okay with.
supporter: It sounds like you're being very thoughtful about the situation. It's okay to take your time to figure these things out.
seeker: Thanks. I just want to find a way to make things work between us without giving up too much of myself.
supporter: Having that intention is important. You deserve to have a relationship where you feel respected and supported in pursuing your own dreams too.
seeker: I hope so. It's just hard when someone you care about seems to be on a different path.
supporter: It's completely understandable. Relationships often require understanding and patience from both sides.
seeker: I'll try to keep that in mind. Thanks for listening, it helps a lot to talk things through.
supporter: Anytime, Anna. I'm here for you whenever you need to talk. You're not alone in this.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-10-15","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hey Anna, I remember you mentioning how much Lily means to you. How are you holding up with everything that's been going on?
seeker: Hey. Honestly, it's been really tough. Finding out Lily is moving is just... too much right now.
supporter: I can only imagine how overwhelming that must feel. You've already been dealing with so much lately.

supporter: I get that. It can be scary to open up about everything. Maybe talking to a school counselor might help you manage the stress better?
seeker: I guess that's a good idea. But I'm just so tired of explaining everything over and over, you know?

seeker: Thanks. I just miss how things were before when it felt like I could handle everything.
supporter: You were really juggling a lot! It’s okay to feel thrown off by changes and challenges. You don't have to handle it all perfectly.
seeker: Yeah. I know you're right. I just wish everything would slow down for a bit.
supporter: It’s normal to want a breather. Are there things that usually help you find a little peace or distraction?
seeker: I used to read a lot, but I haven't been able to lose myself in a book for a while.
supporter: Maybe trying a new book could help, even if it’s just a distraction for a bit. Staying connected with those things that bring you comfort is important.

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hi Anna, how have things been going for you lately?
seeker: Hey, it's been a bit tough to be honest.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. Would you like to talk about what's been happening?
seeker: Yeah, I had a fight with my boyfriend recently, and it's been weighing on me a lot.
supporter: That sounds really challenging. What was the fight about, if you don't mind sharing?
seeker: It was about our priorities and goals for the future. We seem to be on different pages, and I'm not sure how to handle it.
supporter: That can definitely be a hard topic to navigate. How are you feeling about the differences in your priorities?
seeker: I feel torn because I really care about him, but our visions for the future just aren't aligning right now.
supporter: It sounds like you're in a tough spot, wanting to find a balance between your feelings for him and your own future plans.
seeker: Exactly. I just don't want to lose him over this, but I also don't want to compromise too much on what I want for my future.
supporter: It's important to stay true to yourself while also considering the relationship. Have you talked to him about how you're feeling?
seeker: We did talk, but it didn't go well. We both ended up just getting more upset.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that it escalated. Sometimes it can be helpful to take a break and approach the conversation with a fresh perspective.
seeker: Yeah, we haven't spoken much since the fight. I'm hoping we can find a way to discuss things more calmly.
supporter: That's a good goal. It might also help to think about what aspects of your goals are most important to you, and where you might have some flexibility.
seeker: That's true. I know I'll probably have to make some compromises, I just need to figure out which ones I'm okay with.
supporter: It sounds like you're being very thoughtful about the situation. It's okay to take your time to figure these things out.
seeker: Thanks. I just want to find a way to make things work between us without giving up too much of myself.
supporter: Having that intention is important. You deserve to have a relationship where you feel respected and supported in pursuing your own dreams too.
seeker: I hope so. It's just hard when someone you care about seems to be on a different path.
supporter: It's completely understandable. Relationships often require understanding and patience from both sides.
