supporter: How may I assist  you ?
seeker: Hey! I’ve been better. Just so stressed out! I don’t handle pressure well.
supporter: Something is pressuring you and you are stressed due to that. Correct me if I am wrong

supporter: It must be hard for you to prepare for it. I can understand. But there must be a way

supporter: I can easily see your seriousness and dedication for  your studies. That is awesome thing
seeker: Thanks! Education is very important in my family. My dad was a teacher so I’ve always had to live up to high expectations.

supporter: There is a famous quote " Worry is a total waste of time. It doesn't change anything. All it does is steal your joy and keep you busy doing nothing."

seeker: I don’t think I’ve ever tried banana chips! I’ll have to see if my grocery store has got them. Maybe I can get some delivered by the time I’m ready to study
supporter: you can find it in any grocery store easily known as  Plantain chips
supporter: hope you are feeling much better now
seeker: Thanks so much! I’ve added them and some of my favorite trail mix to my cart. Should be delivered in 1 hour!
seeker: I am feeling better. Thanks so much for the advice :)
supporter: That's great to know and best wishes for your exams.

seeker: Please what do I do?
supporter: Hi! how are you doing today?
seeker: Not so good, I'm feeling down
supporter: It sounds like you have low energy. What makes you feel down?
seeker: My parents keep putting pressures on me to be the best in the class and with my learning difficulties I am finding it had to cope 
supporter: I can understand parental pressure. They want to see you to be a successful person. Sometime it is overwhelming. you should talk to them that you are doing your best.
seeker: I have tried, I am even doing extra classes but they still keep on putting pressure on me. On top of that all my friends have distant from me for no reason and they ganged up on me to bully me 
supporter: It must be tough time for you. show your work report to your parents and try to tell them all the people are born with different potential.
seeker: Hmm...That doesn't seem like a bad idea. I am just worry that my parents will not be very understanding. My parents are too strict and they don't like to hear any complaints or excuses.
supporter: Most of the parents behave like this when it is regarding their kids future. When I was in school same thing happened with mw. They know us very well I realized now.  Try to talk to them everyday for a while. It might work.
seeker: Maybe you're right! Although, my parents have a very busy schedule but fingers crossed when I do find time to talk to them they will understand me. 
seeker: I sometimes feel like someone older needs to talk to them, maybe then my parents may take it more seriously
seeker: Well! Thanks I give what you said a go
supporter: Hope you are feeling bit relaxed now. 
seeker: Yes! I feel a lot better now that I know someone understands how I feel 
supporter: I am glad that I am able to make you happy. 
seeker: One more thing
seeker: How should I respond to the friends that are ganging up on me?
supporter: sure! You don't have to worry about that. that should be their problem. just ignore them or don't give attention. They will stop doing it for sure.
seeker: Hmm..interesting because now that I think about it, I believe this could have contributed to the stress and anxieties that I have been experiencing. When I don't get support from anyone I feel so alone, timid and down 
supporter: Try to take small break while studying and try to relax 
seeker: Yes, I find that has helped me a bit also because I have quite a short attention span . Also, I am currently on the path of trying to find more unique techniques to help revision more fun and exciting for me 
supporter: That's great! you will do awesome.
seeker: Thank you very much! I feel much better now and I've taken on board what you said, hopefully there will be a positive change in my parents character. :)
supporter: You are welcome!
seeker: Alright! Well I'll talk to you some other time to give an update 
supporter: Sure! take care
seeker: Thanks you too! :)","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-07-10","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

Exactly. I feel like I'm always on edge, worried about repeating past mistakes or disappointing my boss again.
It makes sense that you're feeling this way. A lot has been going on at work for you.

Missing something so important to you must be really painful. It’s okay to feel upset about it.
It is. I'm not just worried about my family, but I feel like I'm losing touch with people who matter.

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hello, what can I help you?
seeker: I really sad as my partner walked out on me. Any thoughts what could  cheer me up?
supporter: Was there anything that leads to this?
seeker: Not really. I thought everything was ok between us. That is why it kind of struck me.
supporter: That's terrible and unacceptable behavior.
supporter: How long have you been together?
seeker: I have to agree with you-it is unacceptable, considering that he didn't give me any reasons as to why he did it. We have been together for 5 years. 
supporter: That sucks. I wouldn't be able to accept either. 
supporter: Have you talked to your friends about this?
seeker: It is still rather raw,I have mentioned to it to a few of my friends and they deeply symphatise with me but I feel there is nothing much they can do to help me.They are as shocked as me to be honest.
supporter: It is understandable to have that reaction. I agree with you, only us can hep ourselves.
supporter: Have you tried doing activities that help distract you from having negative thoughts?
seeker: Kind of, most of it involves eating loads of ice cream LOL. 
supporter: Haha I feel you, I tend to eat a lot when depressed too. Look, it's treat yourself method. You deserve the best
supporter: If you can go to the mountain or big lake, I would say try spending a few hours there. Maybe have a mini picnic by yourself and enjoy the nature.
seeker: That is a brilliant idea,I do love walking and being outdoors. :) 
seeker: It surely would help me to clear my mind
supporter: Is there anything you have wanted to do but don't have the time? I always want to learn guitar and baking. This is the best time to start that
seeker: oh yeah, I suppose I have more time now to focus on things I have always wanted to do but never kind of had time for it. I bought a high end photo camera ages ago but never really had a chance to use it properly-I guess it is time to pursue my interest in photography, and spending more time outdoors would be ideal for that!
seeker: And reading! The list of books I want to read is arm long!
supporter: That's the spirit! I know being treated like that feels horrible. However, I bet you have mourned enough, at the end of the day, a person treats you like that has no respect and you shouldn't waste time on them.
supporter: It's time to invest in yourself, once you become your better version, a better partner will come to you
seeker: I really agree with you- I am worth more than that. It is time to move on, even when it is difficult. The sad side of it is that I probably will never know what I did wrong for things to end like that. Maybe I didn't do anything wrong. That is the question what will always stay with me and that actually is the hardest bit of it all. But... I am not going to delve into it.
seeker: I feel like hitting a jackpot actually hahahaha. I will be walking off those calories I get from ice cream I have been scoffing lately.So I am having the best of both worlds 
seeker: Who said you cannot have the cake and eat it all LOL
supporter: Yes!Actually don't think you did wrong. Reflecting after a relationship is good but don't put all the blame on yourself.
supporter: You have learned from this relationship too i believe, use that for your next one
seeker: I do not intend to. I am usually the kind of person who does blame oneself but I have found it is not right.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-06-10","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hello! What seems to be the problem?
seeker: am having sleep disorder problem
seeker: will you able to help?
seeker: Daily am not able to sleep on time
supporter: I will try my best. I specialise in yoga and meditation.
seeker: Great
supporter: How long has this been happening for?
seeker: past 2 weeks
seeker: will you able to help with some video links
seeker: which I can see and follow
supporter: This may be an obvious question, but can you think of something that has changed in the last two weeks?
supporter: Think about work related, personal life, changes in behaviour?
seeker: yeah. may be work related
seeker: I am spending more time on work
seeker: I need to switch some activities other than work
seeker: will you suggest to take off for few more days from work?
seeker: will that work
seeker: or any other better solution
supporter: It might solve as a temporary solution, however, if whatever happened at work to cause this continues when you return from holidays, you will just have the same problem again.
supporter: What exactly do you think is causing it? Additional work/responsibilities? New manager?
seeker: additional work being assigned to me
seeker: that causes more work stress
seeker: most of them are new to me, so am spending more time to learn 
supporter: Have you tried to speak to your manager about these additional responsibilities? Do you know if it is a short term problem or you will always have extra work being assigned?
seeker: I am trying to speak. but she is not listening much
seeker: let me try to tell my situation and get some better solution
seeker: will you able to share some yoga & mediation links?
seeker: to divert me from the extra additional work
supporter: I don't think I can share links over here, however the activities you perform directly before you go to sleep have a direct impact on your sleeping.
supporter: I would recommend trying to practice 30m-1h of yoga (you can find lodes of exercise videos on the internet to follow), followed by a mediation sound track for you to listen to in bed while you try to sleep.
supporter: Keep your body and mind clear before you go to sleep has proven to allow for a better sleep.
supporter: I used to have sleeping issues, and I started doing this 2 years ago, and I completely changed. I am an investment banker and still am, it is a very stressful environment however this has allowed me to work at the very top and remain in control of my body and mind.
supporter: Please try this for 1 week, I know you can do it and I know it will help you long term.
seeker: Sure. I can try whatever you suggested
seeker: I am sure definitely I will get some changes
seeker: I felt good after chatting with you
supporter: Thanks so good, I have really enjoyed talking to you too.
seeker: Thank you so much for your advice and have a good day.
supporter: My pleasure, you too.
seeker: Bye. closing this chat
supporter: Bye.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-07-25","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hey Charlotte, how have things been going lately?
seeker: Hi...it's been a rough couple of days. I had a pretty stressful event at work.
supporter: I'm really sorry to hear that. Do you want to talk about what happened?
seeker: Well, I found some errors in the project report I submitted, and my boss called me out in front of everyone. It was humiliating.
supporter: That sounds incredibly stressful, especially since you've been dealing with a lot of pressure at work already.
seeker: Yes, exactly. It's like everything is piling on top of me, and I can't seem to catch a break.
supporter: It makes sense that you'd feel overwhelmed. Are there any parts of the project or your workload that are more manageable for you?
seeker: I guess there are some smaller tasks I can focus on, but even those feel daunting right now.
supporter: I understand. It might help to break them down into even smaller steps, to make them feel a bit more doable.
seeker: I've thought about that, but it's hard to start when I'm just so exhausted all the time.
supporter: I remember you mentioned issues with sleep in the past and how that's been affecting your energy levels.
seeker: Yeah. It’s been a persistent problem, and the stress from work only makes it harder to manage.
supporter: That sounds really tough, especially since it’s a cycle that feeds into itself. Are there any strategies you’ve tried that have helped even a little?
seeker: I tried meditation and some breathing exercises which were somewhat helpful before. But I haven't been consistent with them.
supporter: It might be worth giving those another shot when you have a moment to yourself. Even small doses of relief can add up.
seeker: You're right. I should try to make it a routine instead of just something I turn to when things get really bad.
supporter: That sounds like a great start. Making a little time every day for yourself could help ease some of that pressure.
seeker: Thanks for listening. It means a lot to have someone to talk to who understands what I'm going through.
supporter: Anytime, Charlotte. You're doing your best under really tough circumstances, and I'm here whenever you need to talk.
seeker: Thank you. I think I'll try setting up a time every day to meditate and maybe even talk to someone at work about easing my workload.
supporter: That sounds like a solid plan. Taking those steps could make a big difference. And remember, it's okay to seek help; you're not alone.
seeker: I will. Thanks again for being there and for your support.
supporter: Of course, Charlotte. I'm always here to listen and support you.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-10-05","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hey Charlotte, how have you been holding up recently?
seeker: Hi, it's been a bit of a rollercoaster lately. I recently went to a social gathering, and my nerves were all over the place.
supporter: Social events can be overwhelming, especially if there's a lot going on. What was the gathering about?
seeker: It was supposed to be just a casual meet-up, but there were a lot of potential networking opportunities. It felt really high-stakes for me.
supporter: That does sound intense. How did you feel being in that environment?
seeker: I was really anxious at first. I've been feeling a lot of pressure at work lately, and it just sort of carried over.
supporter: Considering everything that's been happening at work, it's understandable to feel that way. How did you manage your anxiety while you were there?
seeker: I tried to focus on engaging one-on-one, which helped a bit, but it was hard to shake the feeling of being judged or not doing enough.
supporter: That's a smart strategy, reaching out in smaller settings. It's important to remember that these situations aren't always about being perfect, just about making connections.
seeker: Yeah, I guess I keep remembering the times my boss publicly criticized me for inaccuracies. It's like I'm scared of making a mistake again, but now in any setting.
supporter: That experience left a big impact on you. It's understandable to be cautious, but networking is really more about building relationships than being flawless.
seeker: I know you're right. I did meet a couple of interesting people, and a friend there was really supportive. It was nice to not feel so stuck in my head for once.
supporter: That's so great to hear! Having support, especially from friends, can make such a difference in these moments. How did the evening wrap up for you?
seeker: Actually, by the end of the night, I felt a bit more relaxed. We ended up talking and laughing about random things. It was a nice distraction from work issues.
supporter: It sounds like you found some brightness in those connections despite the initial stress. Do you feel like you could attend more events like this in the future?
seeker: I think I could. This experience taught me that not everything has to revolve around job performance. It's okay to just enjoy the moment.
supporter: Exactly, sometimes it's the small joys that help us regain balance. Have you thought about discussing these experiences with your therapist?
seeker: I might bring it up. Therapy's been a space where I can talk candidly about my work stress. Talking about the better moments could be helpful too.
supporter: That sounds like a great plan. Remember, progress isn't always linear, but acknowledging the positive steps is just as important.
seeker: Thanks, I agree. I'll try to hold onto these good moments as I move forward.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-11-15","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hey there, can we chat for a bit? I've got some things on my mind.
supporter: Of course, Charlotte. I'm here for you. What's been happening?
seeker: So, I went on this New Year's trip and made a new friend. It's been nice having someone new to talk to, but I can't shake some underlying stress.
supporter: That sounds exciting, meeting someone new can bring fresh perspectives. But it's also understandable to feel stress, especially after everything you've experienced.
seeker: Yeah, it seems like things have piled up since last fall, like the panic attack at work and the extended hours.
supporter: Those were significant challenges. And I remember your workload and social conflicts taking a toll on you. How are you managing those feeling now?
seeker: Honestly, sometimes it feels overwhelming. Making this new friend was a good distraction, but there's still tension lingering from the office issues.
supporter: It sounds like you're carrying a lot. Finding a new connection can be refreshing, but it's okay to still feel burdened by past stress. Have you been able to talk about this with your therapist, though?
seeker: Yes, I've mentioned it in our sessions. We've been working through some stress management techniques, but it's a slow process.
supporter: Taking it slowly is important. It's great to hear you're working on it in therapy. How do you feel about the progress so far?
seeker: Some days are better than others. There are moments where I feel like things are improving, but then something small can trigger that anxiety again.
supporter: Recovery has its ups and downs. It's very brave of you to acknowledge where you're at. Maybe focusing on your victories, like forming new friendships, can help you move forward.
seeker: That's true. This new friend has been understanding. We both need a fresh start this year, and it's comforting to know I'm not alone in this.
supporter: It's wonderful to have someone who comprehends what you're going through. Have you considered if they might be open to sharing support with each other?
seeker: We have talked a lot, and it seems like we're both open to supportive friendship. It's nice to feel connected like that.
supporter: That's so key—to have someone to lean on. Think of them as a partner in your journey. It's also important to continue prioritizing your mental well-being.
seeker: You're right. I need to keep working through this with therapy and allow myself to enjoy new experiences.
supporter: Absolutely. Celebrate the steps you've taken already. It’s okay to lean on friends for support, and accepting help doesn’t mean you’re not strong.
seeker: Thanks for listening. I feel a bit lighter after talking with you.
supporter: I'm glad to hear that. Remember, I'm always here whenever you need to talk. Take care of yourself, Charlotte.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-01-01","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hello, what can I help you?
seeker: I really sad as my partner walked out on me. Any thoughts what could  cheer me up?
supporter: Was there anything that leads to this?
seeker: Not really. I thought everything was ok between us. That is why it kind of struck me.
supporter: That's terrible and unacceptable behavior.
supporter: How long have you been together?
seeker: I have to agree with you-it is unacceptable, considering that he didn't give me any reasons as to why he did it. We have been together for 5 years. 
supporter: That sucks. I wouldn't be able to accept either. 
supporter: Have you talked to your friends about this?
seeker: It is still rather raw,I have mentioned to it to a few of my friends and they deeply symphatise with me but I feel there is nothing much they can do to help me.They are as shocked as me to be honest.
supporter: It is understandable to have that reaction. I agree with you, only us can hep ourselves.
supporter: Have you tried doing activities that help distract you from having negative thoughts?
seeker: Kind of, most of it involves eating loads of ice cream LOL. 
supporter: Haha I feel you, I tend to eat a lot when depressed too. Look, it's treat yourself method. You deserve the best
supporter: If you can go to the mountain or big lake, I would say try spending a few hours there. Maybe have a mini picnic by yourself and enjoy the nature.
seeker: That is a brilliant idea,I do love walking and being outdoors. :) 
seeker: It surely would help me to clear my mind
supporter: Is there anything you have wanted to do but don't have the time? I always want to learn guitar and baking. This is the best time to start that
seeker: oh yeah, I suppose I have more time now to focus on things I have always wanted to do but never kind of had time for it. I bought a high end photo camera ages ago but never really had a chance to use it properly-I guess it is time to pursue my interest in photography, and spending more time outdoors would be ideal for that!
seeker: And reading! The list of books I want to read is arm long!
supporter: That's the spirit! I know being treated like that feels horrible. However, I bet you have mourned enough, at the end of the day, a person treats you like that has no respect and you shouldn't waste time on them.
supporter: It's time to invest in yourself, once you become your better version, a better partner will come to you
seeker: I really agree with you- I am worth more than that. It is time to move on, even when it is difficult. The sad side of it is that I probably will never know what I did wrong for things to end like that. Maybe I didn't do anything wrong. That is the question what will always stay with me and that actually is the hardest bit of it all. But... I am not going to delve into it.
seeker: I feel like hitting a jackpot actually hahahaha. I will be walking off those calories I get from ice cream I have been scoffing lately.So I am having the best of both worlds 
seeker: Who said you cannot have the cake and eat it all LOL
supporter: Yes!Actually don't think you did wrong. Reflecting after a relationship is good but don't put all the blame on yourself.
supporter: You have learned from this relationship too i believe, use that for your next one
seeker: I do not intend to. I am usually the kind of person who does blame oneself but I have found it is not right.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-06-10","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

supporter: Hello, how are you today?

supporter: Do you know of some triggers that might cause this anxiety?

supporter: That sounds like something that could cause anxiety. We all strive to be recognized for our hard work. Have you conversed with your boss?

supporter: I am happy to know you will try this. I know you can do it!

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hello, what can I help you?
seeker: I really sad as my partner walked out on me. Any thoughts what could  cheer me up?
supporter: Was there anything that leads to this?
seeker: Not really. I thought everything was ok between us. That is why it kind of struck me.
supporter: That's terrible and unacceptable behavior.
supporter: How long have you been together?
seeker: I have to agree with you-it is unacceptable, considering that he didn't give me any reasons as to why he did it. We have been together for 5 years. 
supporter: That sucks. I wouldn't be able to accept either. 
supporter: Have you talked to your friends about this?
seeker: It is still rather raw,I have mentioned to it to a few of my friends and they deeply symphatise with me but I feel there is nothing much they can do to help me.They are as shocked as me to be honest.
supporter: It is understandable to have that reaction. I agree with you, only us can hep ourselves.
supporter: Have you tried doing activities that help distract you from having negative thoughts?
seeker: Kind of, most of it involves eating loads of ice cream LOL. 
supporter: Haha I feel you, I tend to eat a lot when depressed too. Look, it's treat yourself method. You deserve the best
supporter: If you can go to the mountain or big lake, I would say try spending a few hours there. Maybe have a mini picnic by yourself and enjoy the nature.
seeker: That is a brilliant idea,I do love walking and being outdoors. :) 
seeker: It surely would help me to clear my mind
supporter: Is there anything you have wanted to do but don't have the time? I always want to learn guitar and baking. This is the best time to start that
seeker: oh yeah, I suppose I have more time now to focus on things I have always wanted to do but never kind of had time for it. I bought a high end photo camera ages ago but never really had a chance to use it properly-I guess it is time to pursue my interest in photography, and spending more time outdoors would be ideal for that!
seeker: And reading! The list of books I want to read is arm long!
supporter: That's the spirit! I know being treated like that feels horrible. However, I bet you have mourned enough, at the end of the day, a person treats you like that has no respect and you shouldn't waste time on them.
supporter: It's time to invest in yourself, once you become your better version, a better partner will come to you
seeker: I really agree with you- I am worth more than that. It is time to move on, even when it is difficult. The sad side of it is that I probably will never know what I did wrong for things to end like that. Maybe I didn't do anything wrong. That is the question what will always stay with me and that actually is the hardest bit of it all. But... I am not going to delve into it.
seeker: I feel like hitting a jackpot actually hahahaha. I will be walking off those calories I get from ice cream I have been scoffing lately.So I am having the best of both worlds 
seeker: Who said you cannot have the cake and eat it all LOL
supporter: Yes!Actually don't think you did wrong. Reflecting after a relationship is good but don't put all the blame on yourself.
supporter: You have learned from this relationship too i believe, use that for your next one
seeker: I do not intend to. I am usually the kind of person who does blame oneself but I have found it is not right.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-06-10","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

seeker: am having sleep disorder problem
seeker: will you able to help?
seeker: Daily am not able to sleep on time
supporter: I will try my best. I specialise in yoga and meditation.
seeker: Great
supporter: How long has this been happening for?
seeker: past 2 weeks
seeker: will you able to help with some video links
seeker: which I can see and follow
supporter: This may be an obvious question, but can you think of something that has changed in the last two weeks?
supporter: Think about work related, personal life, changes in behaviour?
seeker: yeah. may be work related
seeker: I am spending more time on work
seeker: I need to switch some activities other than work
seeker: will you suggest to take off for few more days from work?
seeker: will that work
seeker: or any other better solution
supporter: It might solve as a temporary solution, however, if whatever happened at work to cause this continues when you return from holidays, you will just have the same problem again.
supporter: What exactly do you think is causing it? Additional work/responsibilities? New manager?
seeker: additional work being assigned to me
seeker: that causes more work stress
seeker: most of them are new to me, so am spending more time to learn 
supporter: Have you tried to speak to your manager about these additional responsibilities? Do you know if it is a short term problem or you will always have extra work being assigned?
seeker: I am trying to speak. but she is not listening much
seeker: let me try to tell my situation and get some better solution
seeker: will you able to share some yoga & mediation links?
seeker: to divert me from the extra additional work
supporter: I don't think I can share links over here, however the activities you perform directly before you go to sleep have a direct impact on your sleeping.
supporter: I would recommend trying to practice 30m-1h of yoga (you can find lodes of exercise videos on the internet to follow), followed by a mediation sound track for you to listen to in bed while you try to sleep.
supporter: Keep your body and mind clear before you go to sleep has proven to allow for a better sleep.
supporter: I used to have sleeping issues, and I started doing this 2 years ago, and I completely changed. I am an investment banker and still am, it is a very stressful environment however this has allowed me to work at the very top and remain in control of my body and mind.
supporter: Please try this for 1 week, I know you can do it and I know it will help you long term.
seeker: Sure. I can try whatever you suggested
seeker: I am sure definitely I will get some changes
seeker: I felt good after chatting with you
supporter: Thanks so good, I have really enjoyed talking to you too.
seeker: Thank you so much for your advice and have a good day.
supporter: My pleasure, you too.
seeker: Bye. closing this chat
supporter: Bye.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-07-25","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hey Charlotte! How have you been doing lately?
seeker: Hi. It's been a tough few days. I missed a big family event this past weekend because of work.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. It must be really hard to balance work and family commitments.
seeker: Yeah, it is. My family was really disappointed, and I feel so guilty. It's like I can't catch a break.
supporter: It sounds like you're carrying a heavy burden. Do you want to talk more about what happened?
seeker: Well, I got an urgent work assignment last minute. I didn't feel like I could say no, especially after everything that happened at work last year.
supporter: I remember you mentioned before about being called out for errors and having unofficial long hours. It seems like a lot has been asked of you.
seeker: Exactly. I feel like I'm always on edge, worried about repeating past mistakes or disappointing my boss again.
supporter: It makes sense that you're feeling this way. A lot has been going on at work for you.
seeker: Yeah, and missing the event just added to it. It was my cousin's wedding, and I've known her since we were kids.
supporter: Missing something so important to you must be really painful. It’s okay to feel upset about it.
seeker: It is. I'm not just worried about my family, but I feel like I'm losing touch with people who matter.
supporter: It's understandable to feel that way. Have you been able to talk to anyone about how you're feeling?
seeker: Not really. I spoke briefly to my therapist about the stress and career concerns, but we haven't gotten into the family stuff yet.
supporter: Therapy could be a good space to explore these feelings deeply. Sometimes just sharing can lighten the burden a bit.
seeker: True. I should really try to address all of this instead of just letting it pile up.
supporter: It sounds like a good step forward. Small steps can make a big difference over time.
seeker: Yeah, I just hope I don't keep repeating this pattern.
supporter: You're taking the right steps by acknowledging it. You're stronger than you think, Charlotte.
seeker: Thank you. I needed to hear that.
supporter: Anytime. Remember, you're doing your best, and that's all anyone can ask of you.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-03-10","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hey Charlotte, how have things been going lately?
seeker: Hi...it's been a rough couple of days. I had a pretty stressful event at work.
supporter: I'm really sorry to hear that. Do you want to talk about what happened?
seeker: Well, I found some errors in the project report I submitted, and my boss called me out in front of everyone. It was humiliating.
supporter: That sounds incredibly stressful, especially since you've been dealing with a lot of pressure at work already.
seeker: Yes, exactly. It's like everything is piling on top of me, and I can't seem to catch a break.

seeker: I guess there are some smaller tasks I can focus on, but even those feel daunting right now.
supporter: I understand. It might help to break them down into even smaller steps, to make them feel a bit more doable.
seeker: I've thought about that, but it's hard to start when I'm just so exhausted all the time.
supporter: I remember you mentioned issues with sleep in the past and how that's been affecting your energy levels.
seeker: Yeah. It’s been a persistent problem, and the stress from work only makes it harder to manage.
supporter: That sounds really tough, especially since it’s a cycle that feeds into itself. Are there any strategies you’ve tried that have helped even a little?

supporter: It might be worth giving those another shot when you have a moment to yourself. Even small doses of relief can add up.
seeker: You're right. I should try to make it a routine instead of just something I turn to when things get really bad.

seeker: Thanks for listening. It means a lot to have someone to talk to who understands what I'm going through.

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hey, I really need someone to talk to right now.
supporter: Of course, Charlotte. What's on your mind?
seeker: I just had a falling out with one of my closest friends. She said I've been distant lately.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. It must be so hard to hear those words from a friend.
seeker: Yeah, it really hurt. I didn't even realize I was being distant.
supporter: It sounds like you're dealing with a lot on your plate. Sometimes, things just pile up and we don't even realize how it's affecting those around us.
seeker: Exactly. Work has been a mess lately. I feel like I'm drowning, and now this with my friend... it's just too much.
supporter: With all that's happened at work, it's understandable you might feel overwhelmed. Remember how you handled the panic attack at work the last time? It can feel like there's no way out, but you managed then.
seeker: I remember. It took a lot out of me to get through that period, though. Now with the added stress of this disagreement... I don't know what to do.
supporter: It's completely normal to feel this way. You've been managing a lot between the work stress, the criticism from your boss, and now these long hours.
seeker: I just feel like I can't catch my breath. Every time I think things are getting better, something else happens.
supporter: I'm really sorry you're feeling this way, Charlotte. It's important to acknowledge how you're feeling and give yourself some grace.
seeker: Thanks. I think I need to find a way to communicate with my friend and maybe even try and talk to my boss about cutting back my hours.
supporter: That sounds like a good plan. Communication can sometimes be that bridge to understanding. Approaching your friend with openness might bring clarity.
seeker: I hope so. I'm just worried that she'll be too hurt or that I'll mess things up with my boss.
supporter: It's okay to feel worried, but acknowledging how you feel is the first step. When you reach out, it can help to be genuine and share how overwhelmed life's been for you.
seeker: Right. I guess honesty would be best. I've been avoiding it because I'm scared of saying the wrong thing.
supporter: That's totally understandable. Remember, you're human and it's okay to feel vulnerable at times. Trying to be honest with yourself and them might help.
seeker: Thanks for listening. I didn't realize how much I needed this talk.
supporter: Anytime, Charlotte. You're not alone in this, and I'm here whenever you need to chat or just vent.
seeker: I appreciate it more than you know. I'll try to take it a step at a time.
supporter: Exactly, small steps are key. Take care of yourself and remember, progress is still progress, no matter the pace.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-11-01","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hey Charlotte, how have you been holding up recently?
seeker: Hi, it's been a bit of a rollercoaster lately. I recently went to a social gathering, and my nerves were all over the place.
supporter: Social events can be overwhelming, especially if there's a lot going on. What was the gathering about?
seeker: It was supposed to be just a casual meet-up, but there were a lot of potential networking opportunities. It felt really high-stakes for me.
supporter: That does sound intense. How did you feel being in that environment?
seeker: I was really anxious at first. I've been feeling a lot of pressure at work lately, and it just sort of carried over.
supporter: Considering everything that's been happening at work, it's understandable to feel that way. How did you manage your anxiety while you were there?
seeker: I tried to focus on engaging one-on-one, which helped a bit, but it was hard to shake the feeling of being judged or not doing enough.
supporter: That's a smart strategy, reaching out in smaller settings. It's important to remember that these situations aren't always about being perfect, just about making connections.
seeker: Yeah, I guess I keep remembering the times my boss publicly criticized me for inaccuracies. It's like I'm scared of making a mistake again, but now in any setting.
supporter: That experience left a big impact on you. It's understandable to be cautious, but networking is really more about building relationships than being flawless.
seeker: I know you're right. I did meet a couple of interesting people, and a friend there was really supportive. It was nice to not feel so stuck in my head for once.
supporter: That's so great to hear! Having support, especially from friends, can make such a difference in these moments. How did the evening wrap up for you?
seeker: Actually, by the end of the night, I felt a bit more relaxed. We ended up talking and laughing about random things. It was a nice distraction from work issues.
supporter: It sounds like you found some brightness in those connections despite the initial stress. Do you feel like you could attend more events like this in the future?
seeker: I think I could. This experience taught me that not everything has to revolve around job performance. It's okay to just enjoy the moment.
supporter: Exactly, sometimes it's the small joys that help us regain balance. Have you thought about discussing these experiences with your therapist?
seeker: I might bring it up. Therapy's been a space where I can talk candidly about my work stress. Talking about the better moments could be helpful too.
supporter: That sounds like a great plan. Remember, progress isn't always linear, but acknowledging the positive steps is just as important.
seeker: Thanks, I agree. I'll try to hold onto these good moments as I move forward.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-11-15","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

supporter: Both relief and anger make sense in this context. It's okay to feel conflicted. What did you say to him?
seeker: I thanked him for reaching out but told him I'm not sure if I can handle reopening old wounds.
supporter: That sounds like a really honest and brave response. It's important to protect your own well-being. How did he react to that?
seeker: He said he understood and respected my decision. But now I'm doubting if I should have asked him more questions.
supporter: It's natural to have second thoughts about these big conversations. It sounds like you're processing this really thoughtfully. What do you think it is that you wish you had asked or said?

supporter: that's really hard, have you spoken to any of your coworkers
seeker: Yes, we are all laughing at the matter, but you can tell our boss is looking at us different. We all showed up to work Friday hungover, and he just made lots of comments and jokes to play the part, but you can tell he is looking at me and everyone different. I do not know how to redeem myself.
supporter: I would recommend speaking with him privately about the issue one on one
seeker: That sounds a lot easier said than done. I was the one who was the most drunk. But I do now know if he knows how drunk we all got since he left after one of us got hit in the face with a golf club and had to take her to the ER. So what if I say too much and apologize for what he does not know.
supporter: have you tried reaching out a company hotline or maybe an hr department in your company to speak about this issue anonymously this could help with the tension between you and your boss 
seeker: He is the doctor of the office and the 2 office managers were pretty drunk too. It was a hot mess if I have to be honest and being an office full of girls I feel like we went too far. I for one feel embarrassed, and feel like just not saying anything and it will fade away. But I know the next few weeks will be a little hard, for all of us. This one is for the books, and something I have never encountered in my 10 years of working. 
supporter: I see how you feel do you think letting it fade is the best option in the long run?
seeker: I think so. Somethings are sometimes better left unsaid. I just feel like avoiding it, but I do not know if anyone else would do the same. What would you do?

supporter: Hello, how are you today?
seeker: I'm good, I feel anxious whenever I think of my career
supporter: I understand. I often feel the same when my day starts. 
seeker: people around me seems to achieve great things and get promoted but I am still at my current position
supporter: Do you know of some triggers that might cause this anxiety?
seeker: I fell like I am late on my plan
supporter: That sounds like something that could cause anxiety. We all strive to be recognized for our hard work. Have you conversed with your boss?
seeker: No i have not, I don't feel comfortable sharing this with my boss or coworkers
supporter: It can totally be intimidating to speak to a boss about this topic. It's not always easy to be comfortable in this kinds of conversations.
supporter: Do you think your boss might have a negative reaction if you were to have this conversation?
seeker: It might, I am not sure but I don't think my boss will like the idea
supporter: Sometimes it's important to remember that part of your bosses job is having this kinds of conversations, even though he might not like the idea. 
supporter: It might be a good idea to have this conversation with your boss. Hold them accountable for this part of their job.
supporter: Do you think this could be a good idea?
seeker: You are right, I should let them know what I want too
supporter: It sounds like this might be a little intimidating for you.
seeker: I'm not a very direct person so I don't really like confronting
seeker: but I think i should have this talk with my boss
supporter: It might feel that way. But if this is something that might benefit your future, it doesn't mean it's a confrontation.
supporter: But rather, an affirmation of your skillsets.
seeker: You're right, you make me feel better about the decision
supporter: I am happy to know you will try this. I know you can do it!
seeker: Thank you for your support
supporter: It's been my pleasure. I wish you good luck!
seeker: Can you give me an idea how to start the conversation?
supporter: Of course! It's always good to make a list before the meeting. List out your skillsets and how each of those skills provide value to the company. If you can demonstrate to your boss how you provide value to the company, it can give you confidence when taking the next step; asking for a promotion
seeker: What I'm worried is if they reject my suggestion, it will come back and bite me as they will think negatively about me

seeker: thank you so much, I will start planning out what I need to talk about","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-08-15","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hello, what can I help you?
seeker: I really sad as my partner walked out on me. Any thoughts what could  cheer me up?
supporter: Was there anything that leads to this?
seeker: Not really. I thought everything was ok between us. That is why it kind of struck me.
supporter: That's terrible and unacceptable behavior.
supporter: How long have you been together?
seeker: I have to agree with you-it is unacceptable, considering that he didn't give me any reasons as to why he did it. We have been together for 5 years. 
supporter: That sucks. I wouldn't be able to accept either. 
supporter: Have you talked to your friends about this?
seeker: It is still rather raw,I have mentioned to it to a few of my friends and they deeply symphatise with me but I feel there is nothing much they can do to help me.They are as shocked as me to be honest.
supporter: It is understandable to have that reaction. I agree with you, only us can hep ourselves.
supporter: Have you tried doing activities that help distract you from having negative thoughts?
seeker: Kind of, most of it involves eating loads of ice cream LOL. 
supporter: Haha I feel you, I tend to eat a lot when depressed too. Look, it's treat yourself method. You deserve the best
supporter: If you can go to the mountain or big lake, I would say try spending a few hours there. Maybe have a mini picnic by yourself and enjoy the nature.
seeker: That is a brilliant idea,I do love walking and being outdoors. :) 
seeker: It surely would help me to clear my mind
supporter: Is there anything you have wanted to do but don't have the time? I always want to learn guitar and baking. This is the best time to start that
seeker: oh yeah, I suppose I have more time now to focus on things I have always wanted to do but never kind of had time for it. I bought a high end photo camera ages ago but never really had a chance to use it properly-I guess it is time to pursue my interest in photography, and spending more time outdoors would be ideal for that!
seeker: And reading! The list of books I want to read is arm long!
supporter: That's the spirit! I know being treated like that feels horrible. However, I bet you have mourned enough, at the end of the day, a person treats you like that has no respect and you shouldn't waste time on them.
supporter: It's time to invest in yourself, once you become your better version, a better partner will come to you
seeker: I really agree with you- I am worth more than that. It is time to move on, even when it is difficult. The sad side of it is that I probably will never know what I did wrong for things to end like that. Maybe I didn't do anything wrong. That is the question what will always stay with me and that actually is the hardest bit of it all. But... I am not going to delve into it.
seeker: I feel like hitting a jackpot actually hahahaha. I will be walking off those calories I get from ice cream I have been scoffing lately.So I am having the best of both worlds 
seeker: Who said you cannot have the cake and eat it all LOL
supporter: Yes!Actually don't think you did wrong. Reflecting after a relationship is good but don't put all the blame on yourself.
supporter: You have learned from this relationship too i believe, use that for your next one
seeker: I do not intend to. I am usually the kind of person who does blame oneself but I have found it is not right.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-06-10","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

supporter: I will try my best. I specialise in yoga and meditation.
seeker: Great
supporter: How long has this been happening for?
seeker: past 2 weeks
seeker: will you able to help with some video links
seeker: which I can see and follow
supporter: This may be an obvious question, but can you think of something that has changed in the last two weeks?
supporter: Think about work related, personal life, changes in behaviour?
seeker: yeah. may be work related
seeker: I am spending more time on work
seeker: I need to switch some activities other than work
seeker: will you suggest to take off for few more days from work?
seeker: will that work
seeker: or any other better solution
supporter: It might solve as a temporary solution, however, if whatever happened at work to cause this continues when you return from holidays, you will just have the same problem again.
supporter: What exactly do you think is causing it? Additional work/responsibilities? New manager?
seeker: additional work being assigned to me
seeker: that causes more work stress
seeker: most of them are new to me, so am spending more time to learn 
supporter: Have you tried to speak to your manager about these additional responsibilities? Do you know if it is a short term problem or you will always have extra work being assigned?

seeker: let me try to tell my situation and get some better solution
seeker: will you able to share some yoga & mediation links?
seeker: to divert me from the extra additional work
supporter: I don't think I can share links over here, however the activities you perform directly before you go to sleep have a direct impact on your sleeping.
supporter: I would recommend trying to practice 30m-1h of yoga (you can find lodes of exercise videos on the internet to follow), followed by a mediation sound track for you to listen to in bed while you try to sleep.
supporter: Keep your body and mind clear before you go to sleep has proven to allow for a better sleep.
supporter: I used to have sleeping issues, and I started doing this 2 years ago, and I completely changed. I am an investment banker and still am, it is a very stressful environment however this has allowed me to work at the very top and remain in control of my body and mind.
supporter: Please try this for 1 week, I know you can do it and I know it will help you long term.
seeker: Sure. I can try whatever you suggested
seeker: I am sure definitely I will get some changes
seeker: I felt good after chatting with you
supporter: Thanks so good, I have really enjoyed talking to you too.

supporter: My pleasure, you too.
seeker: Bye. closing this chat
supporter: Bye.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-07-25","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hey Charlotte, how have you been doing lately?
seeker: Hi there. Honestly, it's been a bit overwhelming. I had a rough week at work.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. Do you want to share what happened?
seeker: Yeah, it's been building up for a while now. My workload has been increasing, and I had a panic attack at the office this week.
supporter: That sounds really intense and scary. How are you feeling about the panic attack?
seeker: Pretty shaken, to be honest. It was like everything was closing in on me. I felt so out of control.
supporter: It must have been a frightening experience. It's important to acknowledge those feelings. Have you had panic attacks before?
seeker: Not like this. I've felt stressed, but this was different. My heart was racing, and I couldn't breathe properly.
supporter: Experiencing that for the first time can be very unsettling. How have you been managing at work since then?
seeker: I've been trying to keep up, but I'm worried it might happen again. It's hard to focus sometimes.
supporter: I understand. The worry of it happening again can add to your stress. Have you considered talking to someone at work about your workload?
seeker: I've thought about it, but I'm unsure how to approach it. I don't want to seem incapable.
supporter: It's perfectly okay to seek support or ask for help. Everyone has limits. Perhaps there's a way to address the workload without compromising your position.
seeker: Maybe I should try setting some boundaries. It's just hard to navigate sometimes.
supporter: That's a good idea. Setting boundaries can help manage stress. Have you considered any strategies for handling stress outside of work?
seeker: Not really. I think I need to find a way to relax more and maybe pick up a hobby.
supporter: Finding something you enjoy could really help. Sometimes stepping away and doing something we love can reset our mind.
seeker: You're right. I think I'll start looking for something new to do in my free time. Thanks for listening.
supporter: I'm glad to hear that. Remember, I'm here if you need to talk more or if you just need someone to listen. You're doing great, Charlotte.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-09-15","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

supporter: Of course, Charlotte. What's on your mind?
seeker: I just had a falling out with one of my closest friends. She said I've been distant lately.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. It must be so hard to hear those words from a friend.
seeker: Yeah, it really hurt. I didn't even realize I was being distant.
supporter: It sounds like you're dealing with a lot on your plate. Sometimes, things just pile up and we don't even realize how it's affecting those around us.
seeker: Exactly. Work has been a mess lately. I feel like I'm drowning, and now this with my friend... it's just too much.
supporter: With all that's happened at work, it's understandable you might feel overwhelmed. Remember how you handled the panic attack at work the last time? It can feel like there's no way out, but you managed then.
seeker: I remember. It took a lot out of me to get through that period, though. Now with the added stress of this disagreement... I don't know what to do.
supporter: It's completely normal to feel this way. You've been managing a lot between the work stress, the criticism from your boss, and now these long hours.
seeker: I just feel like I can't catch my breath. Every time I think things are getting better, something else happens.
supporter: I'm really sorry you're feeling this way, Charlotte. It's important to acknowledge how you're feeling and give yourself some grace.
seeker: Thanks. I think I need to find a way to communicate with my friend and maybe even try and talk to my boss about cutting back my hours.
supporter: That sounds like a good plan. Communication can sometimes be that bridge to understanding. Approaching your friend with openness might bring clarity.
seeker: I hope so. I'm just worried that she'll be too hurt or that I'll mess things up with my boss.

seeker: I was really anxious at first. I've been feeling a lot of pressure at work lately, and it just sort of carried over.

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hey, are you there? I could really use someone to talk to right now.
supporter: Hi Charlotte, I'm here. What's been going on?
seeker: It's Alex. He reached out to me last night.
supporter: Oh, wow. That must have brought up a lot of feelings. How are you holding up?
seeker: I'm just... I don't even know. It's been so long since we spoke. I thought I was over it, but I guess not.
supporter: It's completely understandable to feel that way, especially since it was such a significant relationship for you. What did he say?
seeker: He apologized for the way things ended. Said he wanted to offer some closure.
supporter: That sounds really intense. Apologies and closure can stir up a lot of emotions. What kind of thoughts are running through your mind right now?
seeker: I'm just confused. Part of me is relieved to hear it, but another part feels angry about how much it hurt back then.
supporter: Both relief and anger make sense in this context. It's okay to feel conflicted. What did you say to him?
seeker: I thanked him for reaching out but told him I'm not sure if I can handle reopening old wounds.
supporter: That sounds like a really honest and brave response. It's important to protect your own well-being. How did he react to that?
seeker: He said he understood and respected my decision. But now I'm doubting if I should have asked him more questions.
supporter: It's natural to have second thoughts about these big conversations. It sounds like you're processing this really thoughtfully. What do you think it is that you wish you had asked or said?
seeker: Just more about why things ended the way they did. I still don't fully understand. Maybe that would help me move on.
supporter: Seeking clarity is definitely important, but it's also okay to take time to figure out how and when you want to approach that. How do you want to move forward from here?
seeker: I think I need to talk about this in therapy. My sessions have been helping a lot with stress and career stuff. Maybe it'll help here too.
supporter: That's a great idea, Charlotte. Therapy can definitely offer a safe space to explore these emotions. It's so good to hear that it's been helpful for you.
seeker: Yeah, it really has. Thank you for listening. I feel a bit lighter being able to talk this through.
supporter: Always here for you, Charlotte. And remember, you're doing an amazing job managing everything. Take it one step at a time.
seeker: I will. Thanks again. I really appreciate it.
supporter: You're welcome. I'm just a message away if you need to talk more.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-01-12","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

supporter: Hi Charlotte! Of course, I'm here for you. What's been going on?
seeker: Well, something quite unexpected happened at work and I'm having mixed feelings about it.

seeker: I got recognition from a higher department for my work on this interdepartmental project.
supporter: Wow, that's amazing! Congratulations, Charlotte!

supporter: I can see how unexpected recognition could feel a bit overwhelming. What’s making it feel weird for you?
seeker: I guess it’s because I’ve been under so much pressure and stress these past months.
supporter: That makes a lot of sense. You've really been through a lot at work with the workload and criticism. It’s natural to feel conflicted.
seeker: Exactly, and it’s like, should I be happy or just cautious? I'm not sure.
supporter: Your feelings are completely valid. Having mixed emotions is totally normal, given all you’ve dealt with.
seeker: Thanks for understanding. I just keep thinking about that time I was called out for mistakes. It shook my confidence.
supporter: It's really tough to move past public criticism, especially when you’ve already been stretched so thin.

supporter: It’s a lot to juggle, for sure. Have you found anything that helps even a little with the stress?

supporter: It’s good to hear you’re finding some relief through socializing. Maybe leaning on supportive friends can help even more.

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hey Charlotte, how have things been going lately?

supporter: That sounds really tough, especially since it’s a cycle that feeds into itself. Are there any strategies you’ve tried that have helped even a little?

seeker: Thanks for listening. It means a lot to have someone to talk to who understands what I'm going through.
supporter: Anytime, Charlotte. You're doing your best under really tough circumstances, and I'm here whenever you need to talk.
seeker: Thank you. I think I'll try setting up a time every day to meditate and maybe even talk to someone at work about easing my workload.
supporter: That sounds like a solid plan. Taking those steps could make a big difference. And remember, it's okay to seek help; you're not alone.

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hey Charlotte, how have you been holding up recently?
seeker: Hi, it's been a bit of a rollercoaster lately. I recently went to a social gathering, and my nerves were all over the place.
supporter: Social events can be overwhelming, especially if there's a lot going on. What was the gathering about?
seeker: It was supposed to be just a casual meet-up, but there were a lot of potential networking opportunities. It felt really high-stakes for me.
supporter: That does sound intense. How did you feel being in that environment?
seeker: I was really anxious at first. I've been feeling a lot of pressure at work lately, and it just sort of carried over.
supporter: Considering everything that's been happening at work, it's understandable to feel that way. How did you manage your anxiety while you were there?
seeker: I tried to focus on engaging one-on-one, which helped a bit, but it was hard to shake the feeling of being judged or not doing enough.
supporter: That's a smart strategy, reaching out in smaller settings. It's important to remember that these situations aren't always about being perfect, just about making connections.
seeker: Yeah, I guess I keep remembering the times my boss publicly criticized me for inaccuracies. It's like I'm scared of making a mistake again, but now in any setting.
supporter: That experience left a big impact on you. It's understandable to be cautious, but networking is really more about building relationships than being flawless.
seeker: I know you're right. I did meet a couple of interesting people, and a friend there was really supportive. It was nice to not feel so stuck in my head for once.
supporter: That's so great to hear! Having support, especially from friends, can make such a difference in these moments. How did the evening wrap up for you?
seeker: Actually, by the end of the night, I felt a bit more relaxed. We ended up talking and laughing about random things. It was a nice distraction from work issues.
supporter: It sounds like you found some brightness in those connections despite the initial stress. Do you feel like you could attend more events like this in the future?
seeker: I think I could. This experience taught me that not everything has to revolve around job performance. It's okay to just enjoy the moment.
supporter: Exactly, sometimes it's the small joys that help us regain balance. Have you thought about discussing these experiences with your therapist?
seeker: I might bring it up. Therapy's been a space where I can talk candidly about my work stress. Talking about the better moments could be helpful too.
supporter: That sounds like a great plan. Remember, progress isn't always linear, but acknowledging the positive steps is just as important.
seeker: Thanks, I agree. I'll try to hold onto these good moments as I move forward.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-11-15","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

supporter: Of course, Charlotte. I'm here to listen. What's going on?
seeker: Work has been really tough lately, and my hours have increased without any official notice. It's adding so much stress.
supporter: That sounds incredibly frustrating and exhausting. It must be hard to handle those kinds of expectations without any formal agreement.
seeker: It really is. I feel like there's just no end in sight, especially after everything that happened last month.
supporter: I remember you mentioning how stressed you were after that public criticism from your boss. It seems like things haven't let up for you since then.
seeker: Exactly. I thought things might get better, but it feels like I'm just being given more and more to handle.
supporter: It's incredibly tough to manage when the workload keeps increasing. Have you had a chance to bring this up with your manager yet?
seeker: I've been thinking about it, but I'm afraid it'll make things worse or that I'll be seen as incapable.
supporter: That's a valid concern, but remember, asking for what you need doesn't make you weak. It's important to advocate for yourself.
seeker: I know you're right, but every time I think about it, my anxiety flares up. It's like I'm trapped in this cycle.
supporter: It's understandable considering your past experiences with panic and stress at work. Maybe you could start by writing down your thoughts before you approach the conversation. It might help ease some anxiety.
seeker: That could be a good idea. Organizing my thoughts might give me the confidence to bring up the conversation.
supporter: Absolutely. Plus, it might help you feel more in control and prepared. Sometimes a little structure can make a big difference.
seeker: I'll try that. I just wish I could find a way to manage all of this stress better.
supporter: It's definitely not easy, especially with your ongoing sleep issues. Have you been able to take any steps for self-care recently?
seeker: Not as much as I'd like. It's just so overwhelming right now, but I know I need to prioritize it more.
supporter: Self-care often falls to the wayside when things get tough, but it's crucial. Even small steps, like a daily walk or setting a bedtime routine, can be beneficial.
seeker: Maybe I can start with that. Create a small routine that grounds me a bit each day.
supporter: That sounds like a positive step, Charlotte. Remember, it's about finding balance and small adjustments can have a big impact.
seeker: Thank you for being there and listening. It means so much to know I'm not in this alone.
supporter: You're never alone. I'm here for you. Feel free to reach out anytime you need to talk or share.
seeker: I will. Just having this conversation has already lightened the load a bit.
supporter: I'm really glad to hear that. Keep taking it one day at a time. You've got this.
seeker: One day at a time. I'll remember that. Thanks again.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-10-10","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

seeker: Hey, I could be better. I just received a performance review at work, and it wasn't great.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. Getting negative feedback can be really tough. How are you feeling about it?
seeker: I'm feeling pretty down, actually. It's made me question my abilities and what I'm really contributing at work.
supporter: It's understandable to feel that way. You've been handling a lot, and criticism can feel overwhelming. Do you remember anything in particular from the review that hit especially hard?
seeker: There was a comment about my consistency. It feels like everything's been piling up, and I'm struggling to keep up with expectations.
supporter: It's hard when everything seems like it's accumulating. You've had a lot on your plate, especially since the conflict with a coworker and the added pressures. Do you think the feedback was fair, or does it feel more like an overwhelming time for you?

supporter: I remember you talking about how challenging that was. It sounds like some of the stress from then might still be lingering. Have you talked to anyone about how you're feeling, perhaps your therapist?

supporter: I'm glad you're staying connected with therapy. Remember, you're making progress, even if it doesn't feel like it right now. What small things can you do today to take care of yourself?

supporter: Anytime, Charlotte. You've worked hard and deserve to be gentle with yourself right now. Is there anything else on your mind that you'd like to talk about?

seeker: hi
supporter: can you talk about your feelings at this time
seeker: Currently I am worried to show up to work. We had a staff appreciation Thursday and we all got super drunk in front of our boss, and I am honestly scared he will judge me or fire me.
supporter: that's really hard, have you spoken to any of your coworkers
seeker: Yes, we are all laughing at the matter, but you can tell our boss is looking at us different. We all showed up to work Friday hungover, and he just made lots of comments and jokes to play the part, but you can tell he is looking at me and everyone different. I do not know how to redeem myself.
supporter: I would recommend speaking with him privately about the issue one on one
seeker: That sounds a lot easier said than done. I was the one who was the most drunk. But I do now know if he knows how drunk we all got since he left after one of us got hit in the face with a golf club and had to take her to the ER. So what if I say too much and apologize for what he does not know.
supporter: have you tried reaching out a company hotline or maybe an hr department in your company to speak about this issue anonymously this could help with the tension between you and your boss 
seeker: He is the doctor of the office and the 2 office managers were pretty drunk too. It was a hot mess if I have to be honest and being an office full of girls I feel like we went too far. I for one feel embarrassed, and feel like just not saying anything and it will fade away. But I know the next few weeks will be a little hard, for all of us. This one is for the books, and something I have never encountered in my 10 years of working. 
supporter: I see how you feel do you think letting it fade is the best option in the long run?
seeker: I think so. Somethings are sometimes better left unsaid. I just feel like avoiding it, but I do not know if anyone else would do the same. What would you do?
supporter: I would apologize for my behavior to the manager if it was me. Just to seem professional and get in my bosses good grace. 
seeker: You have guts. I think I will work on that and build the guts to talk to my boss if I ever have to. Thank you for that. 
supporter: You are doing your best and I think you will make the right decision that works for you
seeker: You are right. In the end I will do the right thing, even if it takes me some time to get there. 
supporter: Is anything else bother you?

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: hello
supporter: Hello, how are you today?
seeker: I'm good, I feel anxious whenever I think of my career
supporter: I understand. I often feel the same when my day starts. 
seeker: people around me seems to achieve great things and get promoted but I am still at my current position
supporter: Do you know of some triggers that might cause this anxiety?
seeker: I fell like I am late on my plan
supporter: That sounds like something that could cause anxiety. We all strive to be recognized for our hard work. Have you conversed with your boss?
seeker: No i have not, I don't feel comfortable sharing this with my boss or coworkers
supporter: It can totally be intimidating to speak to a boss about this topic. It's not always easy to be comfortable in this kinds of conversations.
supporter: Do you think your boss might have a negative reaction if you were to have this conversation?
seeker: It might, I am not sure but I don't think my boss will like the idea
supporter: Sometimes it's important to remember that part of your bosses job is having this kinds of conversations, even though he might not like the idea. 
supporter: It might be a good idea to have this conversation with your boss. Hold them accountable for this part of their job.
supporter: Do you think this could be a good idea?
seeker: You are right, I should let them know what I want too
supporter: It sounds like this might be a little intimidating for you.
seeker: I'm not a very direct person so I don't really like confronting
seeker: but I think i should have this talk with my boss
supporter: It might feel that way. But if this is something that might benefit your future, it doesn't mean it's a confrontation.
supporter: But rather, an affirmation of your skillsets.
seeker: You're right, you make me feel better about the decision
supporter: I am happy to know you will try this. I know you can do it!
seeker: Thank you for your support
supporter: It's been my pleasure. I wish you good luck!
seeker: Can you give me an idea how to start the conversation?
supporter: Of course! It's always good to make a list before the meeting. List out your skillsets and how each of those skills provide value to the company. If you can demonstrate to your boss how you provide value to the company, it can give you confidence when taking the next step; asking for a promotion
seeker: What I'm worried is if they reject my suggestion, it will come back and bite me as they will think negatively about me

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hello, what can I help you?
seeker: I really sad as my partner walked out on me. Any thoughts what could  cheer me up?
supporter: Was there anything that leads to this?
seeker: Not really. I thought everything was ok between us. That is why it kind of struck me.
supporter: That's terrible and unacceptable behavior.
supporter: How long have you been together?
seeker: I have to agree with you-it is unacceptable, considering that he didn't give me any reasons as to why he did it. We have been together for 5 years. 
supporter: That sucks. I wouldn't be able to accept either. 
supporter: Have you talked to your friends about this?
seeker: It is still rather raw,I have mentioned to it to a few of my friends and they deeply symphatise with me but I feel there is nothing much they can do to help me.They are as shocked as me to be honest.
supporter: It is understandable to have that reaction. I agree with you, only us can hep ourselves.
supporter: Have you tried doing activities that help distract you from having negative thoughts?
seeker: Kind of, most of it involves eating loads of ice cream LOL. 
supporter: Haha I feel you, I tend to eat a lot when depressed too. Look, it's treat yourself method. You deserve the best
supporter: If you can go to the mountain or big lake, I would say try spending a few hours there. Maybe have a mini picnic by yourself and enjoy the nature.
seeker: That is a brilliant idea,I do love walking and being outdoors. :) 
seeker: It surely would help me to clear my mind
supporter: Is there anything you have wanted to do but don't have the time? I always want to learn guitar and baking. This is the best time to start that
seeker: oh yeah, I suppose I have more time now to focus on things I have always wanted to do but never kind of had time for it. I bought a high end photo camera ages ago but never really had a chance to use it properly-I guess it is time to pursue my interest in photography, and spending more time outdoors would be ideal for that!
seeker: And reading! The list of books I want to read is arm long!
supporter: That's the spirit! I know being treated like that feels horrible. However, I bet you have mourned enough, at the end of the day, a person treats you like that has no respect and you shouldn't waste time on them.
supporter: It's time to invest in yourself, once you become your better version, a better partner will come to you
seeker: I really agree with you- I am worth more than that. It is time to move on, even when it is difficult. The sad side of it is that I probably will never know what I did wrong for things to end like that. Maybe I didn't do anything wrong. That is the question what will always stay with me and that actually is the hardest bit of it all. But... I am not going to delve into it.
seeker: I feel like hitting a jackpot actually hahahaha. I will be walking off those calories I get from ice cream I have been scoffing lately.So I am having the best of both worlds 
seeker: Who said you cannot have the cake and eat it all LOL
supporter: Yes!Actually don't think you did wrong. Reflecting after a relationship is good but don't put all the blame on yourself.
supporter: You have learned from this relationship too i believe, use that for your next one
seeker: I do not intend to. I am usually the kind of person who does blame oneself but I have found it is not right.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-06-10","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}
