MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hello how are you?
seeker: I'm, okay, thanks, and you?  I'm feeling a bit down because I'm alone for the holidays.
supporter: Well that's no good, does your family live far away?
seeker: Yes, my family is scattered all over the country, like Seattle, Georgia, PA.  I'm sure I'm not the only one with no plans this weekend, though.
supporter: True but I can understand that, it is hard being alone at the holidays.
supporter: Did you have plans this weekend?
seeker: No.  My nearby friends all went away for the holidays.  I could probably just occupy my time with things I need or want to do in order to distract myself.
supporter: What kind of hobbies do you have?
seeker: I'm teaching myself the piano.  I'm also teaching myself  how to work a stenography machine for possible future employment as a stenographer.  I also like to read novels.
supporter: I have never understood how those work..I find it amazing someone can type out whole words or sentences with one word
seeker: Yeah, it's pretty cool.  For example, if I hit DRAT in one stroke, then "Did there come a time" will appear in English on my machine's  LCD screen.
supporter: Wow that is crazy, I don't understand how that works, is it preprogrammed or does it go by how the word sounds? 
seeker: Each stenographer has their own "Personal Dictionary" which is a list of words in English along with how you in particular write out those words or phrases in steno.  This dictionary is present within the actual steno machine after you transfer it from your laptop to the machine via cable or wifi.  Thus your machine then knows how you write out words in particular and how to translate those words from steno to English - each stenographer writes a little differently.
supporter: OK that makes sense, so you basically program it as the user. I take it your stenography machine becomes pretty close to you lol
supporter: Is this your first holiday alone?
seeker: Yes, exactly!  And it's very important to back up your personal dictionary to the cloud or a seperate drive so that you don't lose it in a hard-drive crash.  A lot of work goes into creating that dictionary!  No, it's happened before, being along for the holidays; but you've helped to cheer me up, so thanks!
supporter: No problem, I hope I have made your day a little better!
seeker: You have, thanks!  Did you do anything special?
supporter: Have a good rest of this year and don't forget to make your New Year's resolution!
seeker: I will do that - you too.  Thanks, again...
supporter: Not really, stayed home lol... Have a good one!
seeker: You too... bye now...
supporter: Good day!
supporter: What else can I help you with today?","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-12-25","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hello, how are you ?
supporter: Hello
supporter: I am good, how are you?
seeker: I'm doing well, but it could have been better
supporter: What seems to be bothering you tonight?
seeker: Yes, my boy friend of 3 years has refused to take our relationship to the next level and I'm kind of getting tired, I don't want to play games anymore
supporter: So just to make sure I understand completely, you are ready to move on to the next step of your relationship and you don't feel as though your boyfriend is and this is making you anxious and upset, 
seeker: exactly, I hate to feel that I'm wasting my time
supporter: I completely understand that, as I was in a long term relationship and I felt as though my girlfriend at the time did not want to take things to the next step and I was not happy about it. 
seeker: Yes, I love him so dearly to want to settle down with him, but if he doesn't want that for me I would rather call it quits now than continue and be disappointed at the long run. 
supporter: Have you had that conversation with him? I know it might be a difficult conversation to have, but it is often good to get expectations out in the open so you are on the same page with your partner. 
seeker: Yes, sort of and he gave me the impression that he is not there yet and that was a like almost a year ago, I don't want it to look like I'm pushing him if I try to talk to him again about it. His nonchalant attitude in not seeing the seriousness of it is killing me, I'm just not happy. 
supporter: That is tough, but sometimes people just portray things differently, for instance I am also very laid back and nonchalant about most things which can lead to miscommunications. 
supporter: I don't think it would be pushing if you haven't had that conversation in almost a year.
seeker: I hope you are right, just don't want to come across as a desperate person and that's why I'm setting myself up to call it quits if he tries to sound like he sounded the last time. 
supporter: You need to know where he is so you can make a good decision for yourself!
supporter: I know it is difficult, but I know you can get through it!
seeker: You are right, that's exactly what I'm going to do because the wait is killing me. 
supporter: Good, I am happy for you!
seeker: Thank you very much, you've been a great help
supporter: I am glad I was able to help!
seeker: Thanks, it was nice chatting with you.
supporter: You're welcome! If you need any more help just chat back with us again.
seeker: no problem, take care.
supporter: You as well!","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-09-10","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: hi there
supporter: Hello! How are you doing? 
seeker: I'm not doing so good at the moment. I'm feeling very stressed and burned out from work
supporter: That sounds very frustrating. Is this a recent development at your job? 
seeker: It's been building up for a while now, but it's really starting to get a but overwhelming
supporter: I can understand how that can have an effect on your mental well-being. Have you spoken to your supervisor about your frustrations at work? 
seeker: I have, but sometimes I feel like she doesn't really listen and she sort of talks over me a lot
supporter: It sounds like you don't feel listened to. 
seeker: That's right... I guess that is quite a lot of the problem. 
seeker: I don't mind so much the work, I know it is busy for everyone right now, it's a combination of the workload plus not being listened to
supporter: I had a similar issue at my last job. My supervisor constantly spoke over me in meetings, and it would drive me crazy. I never could get a word in edge-wise. 
seeker: Yeah, that sounds a lot like what I am experiencing
supporter: Are you considering switching jobs? 
seeker: It's been in the back of my mind, but it's a hard time just now with everything else going on
supporter: Absolutely. It's a rough time job searching under the best of circumstances. 
seeker: It is. 
supporter: Have you tried reaching out to anyone in your network to look for a new position? It helped me when I was previously job searching. 
seeker: I haven't, but it might be worth getting in touch with some people
supporter: Absolutely. I also spoke with a therapist before and it helped me a lot. 
supporter: Have you considered reaching out to a professional to talk to? 
seeker: I did consider that, but aren't they expensive?
supporter: They can be, but many local governments and municipalities have therapists that work on a sliding scale if the financial aspect of therapy is a concern. 
supporter: Therapy can definitely be a large expense though. 
seeker: It might be worth it in the long run though I guess, if it helps how I am feeling
supporter: If it helps to reframe the expense, you can try to think of it as an investment in your mental health. 
seeker: Yes, that sounds like a more positive way of thinking of it
supporter: The therapist could likely give you some tools to help manage the frustrations at your workplace more constructively. 
seeker: Yes, I imagine they will have come across this before so will be able to help
supporter: Absolutely. I hope that you're able to find some peace at your workplace with your boss. 
seeker: Thank you, you have helped a lot
seeker: Helped give me some ideas to try to help
supporter: It's my pleasure. I'm happy to have helped you. 
supporter: Is there anything else I can help you with? ","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-06-10","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hello, how are you doing today?
seeker: I am feeling angry today about work. 
supporter: Oh no, what happened to make you feel this way?
seeker: My coworker expects me to do things the way she does and is constantly critical. I just want her to understand that I am able to do things my way and it is still okay. I told her this and she ignored me. 
supporter: I'm sure that's terribly frustrating having someone treat you like that. Is this something that your boss is aware of?
seeker: I have not told her yet. I do not want to get her into trouble and I want to have a good relationship with her. 
supporter: Can you discuss it with her in a respectful way to get her to understand that you're not trying to undermine her but that this is how you work most efficiently? And maybe mention that you don't want to involve the boss?
seeker: That's something I could try. I really care about my coworker and it makes me so angry that she treats me this way. 
supporter: I think sometimes it's easy to jump to anger when you feel hurt. It might be worth telling her how you feel and also maybe ask why she thinks you should be doing things her way. Maybe there's a give and take in this situation. Some of her methods could be beneficial.
seeker: Do you have any advice on how to start my conversation with her? I have found some of her ideas to be beneficial. I just would like my ideas expressed as well. I feel we can learn from each other. 
supporter: Tell her the things that you like about her method and maybe suggest some of your methods to her as well. Maybe she'll find them to be more efficient. Make it a partnership rather than a fight for whose method is better.
supporter: She could feel threatened by you so it's worth digging into those feelings with her and proving to her that you're working toward the same goal.
seeker: That's a great idea. It is possible. I am the new kid on the block. I will try by being non confrontational. Any specific ideas to how  I can do that? She gets offended easily. I want her to know I am helping. 
supporter: I'd suggest how much she's helped you since you are in fact the new kid on the block.  And tell her that you want to work with her to have the most efficient partnership possible and use each of your talents to the best of your ability. Then you can lay out how you work best and see where it goes from there.
seeker: Thanks! I will try that. You made me feel so much better! 
supporter: I'm so glad, these can be frustrating situations but sometimes it's worth looking at the other person's perspective.
seeker: I agree. Sometimes you just have to take a step back and have a conversation with someone not in the thick of it. 
supporter: Absolutely, I have no emotional stake in this. The two of you do and that can cloud things sometimes.
seeker: I think people get territorial when they have worked somewhere and a new person comes in. I see that now. I am optimistic we will work it out and be a great team!
supporter: That's great to hear, I'm glad we were able to chat!
seeker: Me too! You really helped me. Have a wonderful day! I know I will since you helped me out. 
supporter: That's great, good luck!","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-09-01","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: I feel sad, and feel like need help
supporter: Can you identify why you feel sad?
seeker: yes, my aunt pass away a couple weeks ago
seeker: and since then im feeling really sad
supporter: It is natural to feel sad when someone you care about dies.
seeker: IS there something I can do to feel better?
supporter: Are you with family?   Sometimes it helps to be with others who are grieving?
seeker: No, I live alone, my family lives in another state
supporter: Being by yourself is rough after a death.    Can you talk with your family by phone?   Do you have a friend who has gone through a similar loss?
seeker: I feel like everybody is in their own bussines and have no time to hear my complains
seeker: I talk to my family, but the whole family is not doing really fine
supporter: It sounds like you feel people think you are complaining when you talk about your Aunt's death making you sad.    Is that correct?
seeker: yes
supporter: Do you feel you are complaining?
seeker: yes, I feel like noone wants to listen
seeker: I need to do something by mnyself
seeker: Can you recommend someting for me to do to feel better?

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hi Amanda, it's good to see you online. How have you been doing lately?
seeker: Hey! I've been feeling a bit off after attending my aunt's memorial service last week.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. It must have been an emotional experience for you.
seeker: Yeah, it really was. Not only because we were saying goodbye, but also because I got to see so many relatives I hadn't seen in years.
supporter: That sounds like it brought up a lot of feelings. How did that affect you?
seeker: It was bittersweet. On one hand, it was wonderful to reconnect, but on the other hand, it made me realize how distant I've become from them.
supporter: It sounds like you're processing a mix of emotions—grief and perhaps some regret?
seeker: Exactly. I feel guilty for not staying in touch more. It was strange talking about memories with people I used to be so close to.
supporter: That's understandable. Guilt can be hard to shake off, but reconnecting at the memorial could be a new beginning.
seeker: I hope so. I exchanged numbers with a few of them and promised to keep in touch.
supporter: That's a great step forward. How does it feel to have taken that initiative?
seeker: A little reassuring, honestly. But there's still this nagging feeling of having missed out on so much with them.
supporter: It's natural to feel that way, but it's important to give yourself grace. Every relationship has its own timeline.
seeker: You're right. I guess I should focus on making the most of the present.
supporter: That's a positive perspective. How do you plan to keep your connections going from here?
seeker: I'm thinking of arranging a small family gathering, something more joy-filled, to keep everyone in touch.
supporter: That sounds like a wonderful idea! It could be a new tradition that brings everyone closer.
seeker: I hope so. It feels good just talking about it. Thanks for listening and helping me work through this.
supporter: Anytime, Amanda. Remember, you're taking meaningful steps. Keep nurturing those connections.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-07-25","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hey, I really need to talk to someone right now.
supporter: Of course, Amanda. What's on your mind?
seeker: It's Valentine's Day, and I'm feeling really unsettled. I didn't expect it to hit me so hard.
supporter: Valentine's can be tough, especially with so much going on in your life. Do you want to share more about what you're feeling?
seeker: Well, I thought I was over Bill, but with today being Valentine's, old feelings are creeping back up.
supporter: It's understandable to have those feelings resurface, especially on a day like today. How long has it been since you two split?
seeker: We broke up last October. It's been a few months, and I thought I was doing okay. But seeing everyone celebrating today brought back memories.
supporter: That makes sense. Our minds often replay moments from the past during similar times of the year. How are you dealing with seeing those memories again?
seeker: Honestly, it's confusing. I'm bombarded with regret about the breakup, but also relief because deep down I know our goals didn't align.
supporter: Feeling both regret and relief can be quite overwhelming. Have you had any thoughts about reaching out to Bill or are you just processing these feelings alone for now?
seeker: I haven’t reached out. Actually, discovering that he was dating someone else really shook me. I think it's best I keep my distance.
supporter: That's a wise choice if you feel it's best for your emotional well-being. It's important to focus on what helps you move forward while honoring your feelings.
seeker: I agree. I’ve been trying to focus on myself and work to distract from these emotions, but it's tough when work isn't exactly fulfilling either.
supporter: It sounds like you're facing challenges on multiple fronts. How has work been since our last chat?
seeker: Still stressful. My supervisor undermines my efforts and doesn't recognize my contributions. It's discouraging.
supporter: That does sound frustrating, especially when you're already dealing with personal emotions. Have you thought about seeking any support or changes at work?
seeker: I had a talk with my supervisor back in January, but not much has changed. I might explore other opportunities soon because it’s becoming too much.
supporter: Exploring new opportunities sounds like a proactive step. You deserve to be in a place where you're appreciated and valued.
seeker: Thank you. Hearing that helps. I'm trying to stay hopeful but it's challenging when feeling this mix of nostalgia and frustration today.
supporter: You're doing great by acknowledging all these emotions. Valentine’s can magnify past feelings, but it’s also a chance to practice self-compassion.
seeker: Self-compassion... I like that. Maybe I'll do something kind for myself tonight. Maybe a small self-care evening.
supporter: That sounds wonderful. It's essential to nurture yourself. What are some things that bring you joy and peace?
seeker: I love a good movie marathon with snacks and some aromatherapy. I think that’s exactly what I need tonight.
supporter: That sounds perfect. Treat yourself to a cozy night. You deserve it.
seeker: Thanks for listening and for the support. I already feel a bit lighter sharing this.
supporter: I'm really glad to hear that. You’re never alone in this; feel free to reach out anytime.
seeker: I will. Thank you again. I hope you have a good night too.
supporter: Thank you, Amanda. Take care, and remember to be kind to yourself.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-02-14","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hey, I just need someone to talk to.
supporter: Hi Amanda, I'm here for you. What's on your mind?
seeker: I've been feeling really overwhelmed lately. I decided to start painting as a hobby, but it's starting to stress me out.
supporter: That sounds tough. Picking up something new should be relaxing. What's stressing you about it?
seeker: I guess I put a lot of pressure on myself to be good at it right away. It's supposed to be fun, but I just feel like I'm failing.
supporter: It's understandable to want to excel, Amanda. Remember, it's okay not to be perfect. It's about the process, right?
seeker: Yeah, I know. It's just hard not to get competitive with myself. And with everything else going on, it feels like I need to be good at something.
supporter: I get that. You've been dealing with a lot, especially with work and your relationships. How has painting been helping you otherwise?
seeker: Well, for a while, it did help shift my mind away from work and personal stress. I kind of get lost in the colors and strokes. But then I start criticizing myself.
supporter: Criticism can be so draining. Sometimes our own expectations create more stress. Have you tried just painting without any goals in mind?
seeker: I haven't really. I always set a goal, maybe from habit because of work. But I think I'll try just playing around with it.
supporter: That sounds like a great idea. Letting go of expectations could bring back some joy and relaxation to it.
seeker: Yeah, I'll give it a shot. I could use some light-heartedness right now.
supporter: That's the spirit! Remember, it's okay to just enjoy the moment without judgment.
seeker: Thanks. It's just been a rough patch with everything, work, and Bill... And then my ex...
supporter: It sounds like you have a full plate. Dealing with all those emotions about Bill and your ex can be really challenging.
seeker: It is. Sometimes I just miss Bill, and seeing my ex with someone else hit me harder than I expected. I'm trying not to let it affect me, but sometimes it just hurts.
supporter: Heart matters can be so complex. It's important to give yourself time and space to feel those emotions. Healing isn't linear.
seeker: You're right. I think painting was supposed to be a distraction, but maybe I need to let myself feel without distraction sometimes.
supporter: Yes, allowing yourself to feel is part of the healing process. Balance between distraction and reflection can be helpful.
seeker: I'm going to try to be kinder to myself and let go of the pressure. Maybe then painting will just be painting.
supporter: That sounds like a positive step forward, Amanda. You're doing your best, and that matters.
seeker: Thanks for listening. I didn't realize how much I needed to talk about all this. I feel a bit lighter now.
supporter: I'm really glad to hear that. Anytime you need to talk, I'm here for you. Take care, Amanda.
seeker: Thank you, I appreciate it. I will. Take care!","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-03-10","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hey, just wanted to talk to someone about a lot that's been on my mind lately.
supporter: Of course, Amanda! I'm here to listen. What's been going on?
seeker: Well, I received a really sweet note from a coworker yesterday. It made me smile, which was nice for a change.
supporter: That sounds lovely! It's amazing how a small gesture can uplift your spirits. What did the note say?
seeker: It was just a little thank you for helping them with a project. It reminded me that my efforts at work don’t go unnoticed by everyone.
supporter: It's great that your contributions are appreciated by your coworkers. How did that make you feel, especially given your situation with your supervisor?
seeker: Honestly, it felt really nice, especially after the stress I've been dealing with from my supervisor's negative review.
supporter: I remember you mentioning feeling undervalued at work before. It's got to be challenging to balance the negative feedback with the positive support from coworkers.
seeker: Exactly, it’s a mixed bag. The note was a small reminder that not everyone sees me the same way my supervisor does.
supporter: It's good to hold onto that perspective. You do valuable work. Sometimes it’s just hard to remember that amid criticism.
seeker: True. I've been trying to focus on my painting to destress but even that has become a bit overwhelming.
supporter: Taking up painting sounds like a great creative outlet. What’s making it overwhelming?
seeker: I think I put too much pressure on myself to excel at it, instead of just enjoying the process.
supporter: It's understandable to want to do well in something new. Maybe allowing yourself to just enjoy the activity would make it more relaxing.
seeker: I guess I just need to remind myself to let go of perfectionism. It's tough sometimes.
supporter: It really is. It might help to remember that hobbies are meant to bring joy and relaxation, not stress.
seeker: That’s true. I’ll try to keep that in mind the next time I pick up the brush.
supporter: That sounds like a good plan. It’s important to be kind to yourself during this journey.
seeker: Thanks for reminding me of that. I needed to hear it.
supporter: Anytime, Amanda. You're doing your best, and that's enough.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-03-25","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

supporter: I'm here, Amanda. What's on your mind?

seeker: Valentine's Day opened that can of worms again. Everything seemed to come at once and continues to be a mess.
supporter: That sounds tough, Amanda. Managing your feelings about your ex on top of work stress and family concerns can be draining.
seeker: Exactly, and when I argue with my best friend, it feels like I have nowhere to turn.
supporter: It must be lonely and frustrating feeling like your support system is compromised.
seeker: It is. I'm trying to keep it together, stay strong for everyone, but I feel like I'm the one falling apart.
supporter: Remember, it's okay to take moments for yourself. You're carrying a lot, and it's okay to not be okay.
seeker: Thanks for saying that. I don't know, I just wish things were simpler.
supporter: It's normal to wish for simpler times. Small steps, like focusing on one task at a time, might help lessen the load.
seeker: Yeah, maybe I need to start with that. Taking things one day at a time.
supporter: That's a good starting point. And remember, leaning on others, like you're doing now, is a strength, not a weakness.
seeker: Thank you. I really appreciate you being here and listening.

seeker: I will. Thanks for being such a great friend.

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hey Amanda, how have you been holding up lately?
seeker: Hi, honestly, it's been a tough couple of days. I finally had the big talk with Bill, and we decided to break up.
supporter: I'm really sorry to hear that. It sounds like a really difficult decision to come to. Do you want to talk about what happened?
seeker: Yeah, it's just... we've been together for three years, but we've been stuck on what our future looks like. Our life goals just don't align anymore.
supporter: That must be so hard, especially after investing so much time and emotion into the relationship. How are you feeling about it all?
seeker: A mix of emotions, really. I feel sad and a little lost. But there's also relief, you know? Like, at least now I can move forward instead of being in limbo.
supporter: It's understandable to feel conflicted. Breakups can bring about such a wide range of emotions. It's good you're finding some silver lining in it.
seeker: Yeah, it's just that I thought we were going to build a life together, and now it's like I have to start over in a way.
supporter: It definitely feels overwhelming having to rethink your future plans. Do you feel like talking to your relatives again has given you any support?
seeker: Actually, yes. Since I reconnected with my family at my aunt's memorial, they've been really supportive. It's nice to know they're there for me.
supporter: That's so important, having a support system to lean on. Have you spoken to any of your friends or coworkers about it?
seeker: I told a few friends, and they've been great. Work's been a distraction, and ever since my coworker and I made up, it's been a more positive environment.
supporter: It sounds like you're doing a great job surrounding yourself with positive energy and support. What about self-care? Are you finding time for yourself?
seeker: I'm trying to. I watched a favorite movie and went for a long walk yesterday to clear my head. It's the little things, I guess.
supporter: Definitely, those small acts of self-care can make such a big difference. What do you feel like you need most right now?
seeker: I think I just need time to process everything, to let myself feel and heal without rushing into anything new.
supporter: Taking the time you need is so important. Give yourself grace, and don't hesitate to reach out if you need someone to talk to.
seeker: Thank you, that means a lot. I'll definitely keep that in mind.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-10-15","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hey Amanda, it looks like you've been experiencing a lot lately. How are you holding up?
seeker: Hi, yeah, it's been a bit rough. Work is really getting to me right now.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. Is it your supervisor again?
seeker: Yes, exactly. I just feel like no matter how hard I try, my efforts aren't valued.
supporter: That sounds incredibly frustrating. It's understandable to feel that way when you're working so hard. What happened recently that's making it worse?
seeker: Yesterday, I suggested a new project plan, but he just dismissed it without even giving it a second thought. I felt humiliated in front of my team.
supporter: That must have been so discouraging. Knowing that this has been an ongoing issue, how are you coping with the stress?
seeker: I'm trying to stay focused on the projects and find satisfaction in my work itself, but it's tough.
supporter: It's admirable that you're trying to find inner satisfaction. Have you been able to talk about this with anyone else at work, maybe someone who could support your ideas?
seeker: I talked with a coworker who apologized for past issues a while ago. They seem supportive, but there's only so much they can do.
supporter: It's good to have even a little bit of support. Have you considered any strategies to improve the situation with your supervisor?
seeker: I've thought about it, but honestly, I feel stuck. I want to have an open dialogue, but every time I try, it backfires.
supporter: That sounds incredibly challenging. It seems like you're stuck between a rock and a hard place. How can I support you through this?
seeker: I think just talking about it helps. Sometimes I feel so alone in this, and it's reassuring to have someone listen.
supporter: I'm here anytime you need to talk. You're definitely not alone, and what you're feeling is completely valid.
seeker: Thanks, that really means a lot. I think I've also been emotionally drained since my breakup last month.
supporter: Breakups are incredibly tough, especially on top of everything else. Have you been able to find some personal time to process everything?
seeker: I've been trying to, but between work stress and personal life, it's been challenging to find time for myself.
supporter: It's important to carve out some 'you' time whenever you can. Perhaps it might help to set small boundaries, even if just for a moment of calm.
seeker: That's a good idea, actually. Maybe a short walk during lunch or some time reading a book could work.
supporter: That sounds perfect. Even small steps like that can make a huge difference in how you feel.
seeker: I'll try to make it a habit. I need something positive to focus on.
supporter: That's the spirit. Remember, I'm here whenever you need someone to talk to. You're doing the best you can, and that's more than enough.
seeker: Thank you so much. Having someone to talk to really helps keep me grounded.
supporter: You're very welcome. Anytime you need me, just reach out. You've got this, Amanda.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-11-05","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

supporter: Oh Amanda, I'm sorry. It must be really tough to hear that news. How are you feeling about it?
seeker: I feel a mix of emotions. On one hand, I know we broke up for good reasons, but on the other, it still hurts seeing him move on so quickly.
supporter: It's completely understandable to feel that way. Breakups have a way of stirring up unexpected feelings. Would talking about it more with me help?
seeker: Maybe. I'm starting to question if I'm the one who's taking too long to move on. It's like I'm stuck in this limbo.
supporter: You're not stuck, you're just processing everything at your own pace. Everyone's journey is different, and it's okay to take the time you need.
seeker: I guess. But seeing him happy with someone else makes me doubt myself, like, was I not enough, or did I make the right choice?
supporter: Those are hard questions to grapple with. Remember, breaking up was about differences in life goals, not your worth or abilities. You did it for your future.
seeker: True, we did have differing goals. I just wish I could turn off the emotional part and focus on that rationality.
supporter: Emotions can be really stubborn like that. It's okay to feel and express them, though. They're part of being human and make us whole.
seeker: Yeah, I suppose. It's just exhausting at times, especially with everything else going on... like work stress.

turns.content: Hey, can we talk? I'm just feeling a bit overwhelmed.
Of course, Amanda. What's been going on?
I had a meeting with my supervisor today and it didn't go as I'd hoped.
I'm sorry to hear that. What happened in the meeting?
Well, I tried to bring up how I've been feeling undervalued and how it's affecting my motivation at work.
That sounds really tough. Were they at least receptive to what you said?
Not really... They seemed to dismiss my concerns again, just like last time.
I'm really sorry to hear that, Amanda. It must be so frustrating to feel unheard.
It is. I've been trying so hard to improve things since the negative review, but it feels like nothing I do is ever enough.
You're putting in so much effort, and it's unfortunate that it's not being recognized. How are you holding up emotionally?
Honestly, it feels draining. Sometimes I wonder if I'm just not good enough for this job.
That's such a difficult place to be in. But remember, your worth isn't determined by someone else's recognition or lack thereof.
Thank you for saying that. It helps a little to hear. I just wish things were different at work.
It's completely okay to want things to change. Would it help to focus on small steps towards feeling valued elsewhere, maybe with your coworkers?
Actually, I made amends with a coworker a few months back and our collaboration has improved a lot.
That's great to hear! Having supportive colleagues can make a huge difference. Maybe that's a positive thing to build on?
Yes, it feels nice to have at least one person be supportive. But it's still hard with my supervisor actively undermining my efforts.
I can imagine how exhausting that is. Have you thought about what steps you might want to take next regarding your job situation?
I have thought about looking for a new job, but I'm not sure if I have the energy to go through that process right now.
Looking for a new job is a big step and it can be intimidating. Maybe focus on building your confidence first and taking it one day at a time?
You're right. I think building my confidence is something I can work on. I'll start looking at my options more lightheartedly.

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hi, I really need to talk about something that's been weighing on me recently.
supporter: Of course, Amanda. I'm here for you. What's going on?
seeker: I received another negative performance review from my supervisor, and it's really getting to me.
supporter: I'm so sorry to hear that. How are you feeling about the review?
seeker: It's just so frustrating. I feel like no matter how hard I work, it's never enough.
supporter: That's really tough. It sounds like you're putting in so much effort and not getting the recognition you deserve.
seeker: Exactly. It's not just this review; it's been a pattern with my supervisor for a while now.
supporter: That's understandable. It must be incredibly discouraging to face that repeatedly.
seeker: Yes, and it's starting to affect my motivation. I feel so undervalued.
supporter: Feeling undervalued at work can be so draining. Do you have any support or allies in the workplace that you can talk to about this?
seeker: I've mended things with a coworker recently, which has helped a bit. But it's still so lonely dealing with this.
supporter: I'm glad to hear that you have someone you can at least partially lean on. Have you thought about addressing this with anyone higher up or in HR?
seeker: I have, but I'm worried it might make things worse with my supervisor if they find out.
supporter: That's a valid concern. It's important to weigh the potential outcomes. How are you handling the stress outside of work?
seeker: Honestly, not well. The stress is impacting my personal life too, especially after my recent breakup.
supporter: It sounds like you're dealing with a lot on your plate all at once. It must be hard to find peace right now.
seeker: It is. I'm trying to stay connected with family, but I still feel quite lost.
supporter: Reconnecting with family after the memorial service was a positive step. It’s okay to lean on them for support in times like these.
seeker: You're right. I need to reach out more, even though it's hard.
supporter: Taking that step can be tough, but you have the strength to do it. Remember, you don’t have to go through any of this alone.
seeker: Thanks for saying that. I really appreciate your support.
supporter: Anytime, Amanda. I'm here whenever you need someone to talk to. You're not alone in this.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-11-20","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

seeker: Hi, yeah, it's been a bit rough. Work is really getting to me right now.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. Is it your supervisor again?
seeker: Yes, exactly. I just feel like no matter how hard I try, my efforts aren't valued.
supporter: That sounds incredibly frustrating. It's understandable to feel that way when you're working so hard. What happened recently that's making it worse?
seeker: Yesterday, I suggested a new project plan, but he just dismissed it without even giving it a second thought. I felt humiliated in front of my team.
supporter: That must have been so discouraging. Knowing that this has been an ongoing issue, how are you coping with the stress?
seeker: I'm trying to stay focused on the projects and find satisfaction in my work itself, but it's tough.
supporter: It's admirable that you're trying to find inner satisfaction. Have you been able to talk about this with anyone else at work, maybe someone who could support your ideas?
seeker: I talked with a coworker who apologized for past issues a while ago. They seem supportive, but there's only so much they can do.
supporter: It's good to have even a little bit of support. Have you considered any strategies to improve the situation with your supervisor?
seeker: I've thought about it, but honestly, I feel stuck. I want to have an open dialogue, but every time I try, it backfires.
supporter: That sounds incredibly challenging. It seems like you're stuck between a rock and a hard place. How can I support you through this?
seeker: I think just talking about it helps. Sometimes I feel so alone in this, and it's reassuring to have someone listen.
supporter: I'm here anytime you need to talk. You're definitely not alone, and what you're feeling is completely valid.
seeker: Thanks, that really means a lot. I think I've also been emotionally drained since my breakup last month.
supporter: Breakups are incredibly tough, especially on top of everything else. Have you been able to find some personal time to process everything?
seeker: I've been trying to, but between work stress and personal life, it's been challenging to find time for myself.
supporter: It's important to carve out some 'you' time whenever you can. Perhaps it might help to set small boundaries, even if just for a moment of calm.
seeker: That's a good idea, actually. Maybe a short walk during lunch or some time reading a book could work.
supporter: That sounds perfect. Even small steps like that can make a huge difference in how you feel.
seeker: I'll try to make it a habit. I need something positive to focus on.
supporter: That's the spirit. Remember, I'm here whenever you need someone to talk to. You're doing the best you can, and that's more than enough.
seeker: Thank you so much. Having someone to talk to really helps keep me grounded.
supporter: You're very welcome. Anytime you need me, just reach out. You've got this, Amanda.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-11-05","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hello, how are you doing today?
seeker: I am feeling angry today about work. 
supporter: Oh no, what happened to make you feel this way?
seeker: My coworker expects me to do things the way she does and is constantly critical. I just want her to understand that I am able to do things my way and it is still okay. I told her this and she ignored me. 
supporter: I'm sure that's terribly frustrating having someone treat you like that. Is this something that your boss is aware of?
seeker: I have not told her yet. I do not want to get her into trouble and I want to have a good relationship with her. 
supporter: Can you discuss it with her in a respectful way to get her to understand that you're not trying to undermine her but that this is how you work most efficiently? And maybe mention that you don't want to involve the boss?
seeker: That's something I could try. I really care about my coworker and it makes me so angry that she treats me this way. 
supporter: I think sometimes it's easy to jump to anger when you feel hurt. It might be worth telling her how you feel and also maybe ask why she thinks you should be doing things her way. Maybe there's a give and take in this situation. Some of her methods could be beneficial.
seeker: Do you have any advice on how to start my conversation with her? I have found some of her ideas to be beneficial. I just would like my ideas expressed as well. I feel we can learn from each other. 
supporter: Tell her the things that you like about her method and maybe suggest some of your methods to her as well. Maybe she'll find them to be more efficient. Make it a partnership rather than a fight for whose method is better.
supporter: She could feel threatened by you so it's worth digging into those feelings with her and proving to her that you're working toward the same goal.
seeker: That's a great idea. It is possible. I am the new kid on the block. I will try by being non confrontational. Any specific ideas to how  I can do that? She gets offended easily. I want her to know I am helping. 
supporter: I'd suggest how much she's helped you since you are in fact the new kid on the block.  And tell her that you want to work with her to have the most efficient partnership possible and use each of your talents to the best of your ability. Then you can lay out how you work best and see where it goes from there.
seeker: Thanks! I will try that. You made me feel so much better! 
supporter: I'm so glad, these can be frustrating situations but sometimes it's worth looking at the other person's perspective.
seeker: I agree. Sometimes you just have to take a step back and have a conversation with someone not in the thick of it. 
supporter: Absolutely, I have no emotional stake in this. The two of you do and that can cloud things sometimes.
seeker: I think people get territorial when they have worked somewhere and a new person comes in. I see that now. I am optimistic we will work it out and be a great team!
supporter: That's great to hear, I'm glad we were able to chat!
seeker: Me too! You really helped me. Have a wonderful day! I know I will since you helped me out. 
supporter: That's great, good luck!","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-09-01","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

supporter: Can you identify why you feel sad?
seeker: yes, my aunt pass away a couple weeks ago
seeker: and since then im feeling really sad

seeker: IS there something I can do to feel better?
supporter: Are you with family?   Sometimes it helps to be with others who are grieving?
seeker: No, I live alone, my family lives in another state
supporter: Being by yourself is rough after a death.    Can you talk with your family by phone?   Do you have a friend who has gone through a similar loss?
seeker: I feel like everybody is in their own bussines and have no time to hear my complains
seeker: I talk to my family, but the whole family is not doing really fine
supporter: It sounds like you feel people think you are complaining when you talk about your Aunt's death making you sad.    Is that correct?
seeker: yes
supporter: Do you feel you are complaining?
seeker: yes, I feel like noone wants to listen
seeker: I need to do something by mnyself
seeker: Can you recommend someting for me to do to feel better?
supporter: My own experiences with family deaths is they are sad.    I just wanted to "feel better".    My experience was it did not help to complain about "being sad" but it did help to talk about why I missed my family member.     If no one was available,   sometimes I would journal. seeker: and try to chat a bit more at leaat with my family

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hi Amanda, it's good to see you online. How have you been doing lately?
seeker: Hey! I've been feeling a bit off after attending my aunt's memorial service last week.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. It must have been an emotional experience for you.
seeker: Yeah, it really was. Not only because we were saying goodbye, but also because I got to see so many relatives I hadn't seen in years.
supporter: That sounds like it brought up a lot of feelings. How did that affect you?
seeker: It was bittersweet. On one hand, it was wonderful to reconnect, but on the other hand, it made me realize how distant I've become from them.
supporter: It sounds like you're processing a mix of emotions—grief and perhaps some regret?
seeker: Exactly. I feel guilty for not staying in touch more. It was strange talking about memories with people I used to be so close to.
supporter: That's understandable. Guilt can be hard to shake off, but reconnecting at the memorial could be a new beginning.
seeker: I hope so. I exchanged numbers with a few of them and promised to keep in touch.
supporter: That's a great step forward. How does it feel to have taken that initiative?
seeker: A little reassuring, honestly. But there's still this nagging feeling of having missed out on so much with them.
supporter: It's natural to feel that way, but it's important to give yourself grace. Every relationship has its own timeline.
seeker: You're right. I guess I should focus on making the most of the present.
supporter: That's a positive perspective. How do you plan to keep your connections going from here?
seeker: I'm thinking of arranging a small family gathering, something more joy-filled, to keep everyone in touch.
supporter: That sounds like a wonderful idea! It could be a new tradition that brings everyone closer.
seeker: I hope so. It feels good just talking about it. Thanks for listening and helping me work through this.
supporter: Anytime, Amanda. Remember, you're taking meaningful steps. Keep nurturing those connections.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-07-25","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hey Amanda, how have you been holding up lately?
seeker: Hi, honestly, it's been a tough couple of days. I finally had the big talk with Bill, and we decided to break up.
supporter: I'm really sorry to hear that. It sounds like a really difficult decision to come to. Do you want to talk about what happened?
seeker: Yeah, it's just... we've been together for three years, but we've been stuck on what our future looks like. Our life goals just don't align anymore.
supporter: That must be so hard, especially after investing so much time and emotion into the relationship. How are you feeling about it all?
seeker: A mix of emotions, really. I feel sad and a little lost. But there's also relief, you know? Like, at least now I can move forward instead of being in limbo.
supporter: It's understandable to feel conflicted. Breakups can bring about such a wide range of emotions. It's good you're finding some silver lining in it.
seeker: Yeah, it's just that I thought we were going to build a life together, and now it's like I have to start over in a way.
supporter: It definitely feels overwhelming having to rethink your future plans. Do you feel like talking to your relatives again has given you any support?
seeker: Actually, yes. Since I reconnected with my family at my aunt's memorial, they've been really supportive. It's nice to know they're there for me.
supporter: That's so important, having a support system to lean on. Have you spoken to any of your friends or coworkers about it?
seeker: I told a few friends, and they've been great. Work's been a distraction, and ever since my coworker and I made up, it's been a more positive environment.
supporter: It sounds like you're doing a great job surrounding yourself with positive energy and support. What about self-care? Are you finding time for yourself?
seeker: I'm trying to. I watched a favorite movie and went for a long walk yesterday to clear my head. It's the little things, I guess.
supporter: Definitely, those small acts of self-care can make such a big difference. What do you feel like you need most right now?
seeker: I think I just need time to process everything, to let myself feel and heal without rushing into anything new.
supporter: Taking the time you need is so important. Give yourself grace, and don't hesitate to reach out if you need someone to talk to.
seeker: Thank you, that means a lot. I'll definitely keep that in mind.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-10-15","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hi Amanda, it's good to see you online. How have you been doing lately?
seeker: Hey! I've been feeling a bit off after attending my aunt's memorial service last week.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. It must have been an emotional experience for you.
seeker: Yeah, it really was. Not only because we were saying goodbye, but also because I got to see so many relatives I hadn't seen in years.
supporter: That sounds like it brought up a lot of feelings. How did that affect you?
seeker: It was bittersweet. On one hand, it was wonderful to reconnect, but on the other hand, it made me realize how distant I've become from them.
supporter: It sounds like you're processing a mix of emotions—grief and perhaps some regret?
seeker: Exactly. I feel guilty for not staying in touch more. It was strange talking about memories with people I used to be so close to.
supporter: That's understandable. Guilt can be hard to shake off, but reconnecting at the memorial could be a new beginning.
seeker: I hope so. I exchanged numbers with a few of them and promised to keep in touch.
supporter: That's a great step forward. How does it feel to have taken that initiative?
seeker: A little reassuring, honestly. But there's still this nagging feeling of having missed out on so much with them.
supporter: It's natural to feel that way, but it's important to give yourself grace. Every relationship has its own timeline.
seeker: You're right. I guess I should focus on making the most of the present.
supporter: That's a positive perspective. How do you plan to keep your connections going from here?

supporter: That sounds like a wonderful idea! It could be a new tradition that brings everyone closer.

supporter: Anytime, Amanda. Remember, you're taking meaningful steps. Keep nurturing those connections.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-07-25","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

turns.content: Hey, I just need someone to talk to.
Hi Amanda, I'm here for you. What's on your mind?
I've been feeling really overwhelmed lately. I decided to start painting as a hobby, but it's starting to stress me out.
That sounds tough. Picking up something new should be relaxing. What's stressing you about it?
I guess I put a lot of pressure on myself to be good at it right away. It's supposed to be fun, but I just feel like I'm failing.
It's understandable to want to excel, Amanda. Remember, it's okay not to be perfect. It's about the process, right?
Yeah, I know. It's just hard not to get competitive with myself. And with everything else going on, it feels like I need to be good at something.
I get that. You've been dealing with a lot, especially with work and your relationships. How has painting been helping you otherwise?
Well, for a while, it did help shift my mind away from work and personal stress. I kind of get lost in the colors and strokes. But then I start criticizing myself.
Criticism can be so draining. Sometimes our own expectations create more stress. Have you tried just painting without any goals in mind?
I haven't really. I always set a goal, maybe from habit because of work. But I think I'll try just playing around with it.
That sounds like a great idea. Letting go of expectations could bring back some joy and relaxation to it.
Yeah, I'll give it a shot. I could use some light-heartedness right now.
That's the spirit! Remember, it's okay to just enjoy the moment without judgment.
Thanks. It's just been a rough patch with everything, work, and Bill... And then my ex...
It sounds like you have a full plate. Dealing with all those emotions about Bill and your ex can be really challenging.
It is. Sometimes I just miss Bill, and seeing my ex with someone else hit me harder than I expected. I'm trying not to let it affect me, but sometimes it just hurts.
Heart matters can be so complex. It's important to give yourself time and space to feel those emotions. Healing isn't linear.
You're right. I think painting was supposed to be a distraction, but maybe I need to let myself feel without distraction sometimes.
Yes, allowing yourself to feel is part of the healing process. Balance between distraction and reflection can be helpful.
I'm going to try to be kinder to myself and let go of the pressure. Maybe then painting will just be painting.
That sounds like a positive step forward, Amanda. You're doing your best, and that matters.
Thanks for listening. I didn't realize how much I needed to talk about all this. I feel a bit lighter now.

supporter: Hi Amanda! I'm here. What's on your mind?
seeker: It's been a rough few days. I had a pretty intense argument with Emily.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. Arguments with friends can be really draining. Do you want to talk about what happened?
seeker: Yeah, I suppose it started with this unresolved tension between us. I've been so stressed with work and everything... I guess I just unloaded on her.
supporter: It sounds like you're carrying a lot right now. Work stress has been tough for you lately, hasn't it?
seeker: It really has. My supervisor's been making things difficult again. I thought things would get better after our last meeting, but I'm still feeling so undervalued.
supporter: That must be so frustrating, especially since you took the step to speak up. It’s no wonder you’re feeling overwhelmed.
seeker: Exactly. And then there’s this issue with Emily. We've been friends forever, but lately it feels like we're on different paths.
supporter: I can imagine how hard it must be to navigate that. Friendships can change over time, but sometimes it helps to address those changes openly.
seeker: I know. I just don’t want to lose her too. We've been friends since college.
supporter: I understand. It sounds like she's really important to you. It might be worth having an honest conversation about what each of you needs right now.
seeker: You're right. I guess I’m just scared she won't understand.
supporter: That fear makes sense, considering everything else you’re handling. But you might be surprised at how supportive she could be. You both care about each other.
seeker: I hope so. It's just all been hitting at once—Emily, work, and even seeing my ex moved on has been rough.
supporter: You’re facing so many different changes and emotions. It's okay to feel overwhelmed. Have you had any time to focus on yourself in all this?
seeker: Not really. I guess I haven’t been great at taking care of myself lately.
supporter: That’s understandable given everything going on. Maybe carving out a little time just for you could help. What do you think might be comforting?
seeker: Maybe a walk in the park or reading a book. I used to love doing that.
supporter: Those sound like wonderful ideas. Allowing yourself some moments of peace could really help clear your mind and recharge.
seeker: I’ll try to do that. Thanks for listening and helping me sort through this.
supporter: Anytime, Amanda. You’re not alone in this. Reach out whenever you need to talk.
seeker: I will. Thanks again for being there.
supporter: You’re welcome. Take care and let me know how you’re doing, okay?
seeker: I will. Have a great day!","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-01-15","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

seeker: Hi, yeah, it's been a bit rough. Work is really getting to me right now.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. Is it your supervisor again?
seeker: Yes, exactly. I just feel like no matter how hard I try, my efforts aren't valued.
supporter: That sounds incredibly frustrating. It's understandable to feel that way when you're working so hard. What happened recently that's making it worse?
seeker: Yesterday, I suggested a new project plan, but he just dismissed it without even giving it a second thought. I felt humiliated in front of my team.
supporter: That must have been so discouraging. Knowing that this has been an ongoing issue, how are you coping with the stress?
seeker: I'm trying to stay focused on the projects and find satisfaction in my work itself, but it's tough.
supporter: It's admirable that you're trying to find inner satisfaction. Have you been able to talk about this with anyone else at work, maybe someone who could support your ideas?
seeker: I talked with a coworker who apologized for past issues a while ago. They seem supportive, but there's only so much they can do.
supporter: It's good to have even a little bit of support. Have you considered any strategies to improve the situation with your supervisor?
seeker: I've thought about it, but honestly, I feel stuck. I want to have an open dialogue, but every time I try, it backfires.
supporter: That sounds incredibly challenging. It seems like you're stuck between a rock and a hard place. How can I support you through this?
seeker: I think just talking about it helps. Sometimes I feel so alone in this, and it's reassuring to have someone listen.
supporter: I'm here anytime you need to talk. You're definitely not alone, and what you're feeling is completely valid.
seeker: Thanks, that really means a lot. I think I've also been emotionally drained since my breakup last month.
supporter: Breakups are incredibly tough, especially on top of everything else. Have you been able to find some personal time to process everything?
seeker: I've been trying to, but between work stress and personal life, it's been challenging to find time for myself.
supporter: It's important to carve out some 'you' time whenever you can. Perhaps it might help to set small boundaries, even if just for a moment of calm.
seeker: That's a good idea, actually. Maybe a short walk during lunch or some time reading a book could work.
supporter: That sounds perfect. Even small steps like that can make a huge difference in how you feel.
seeker: I'll try to make it a habit. I need something positive to focus on.
supporter: That's the spirit. Remember, I'm here whenever you need someone to talk to. You're doing the best you can, and that's more than enough.
seeker: Thank you so much. Having someone to talk to really helps keep me grounded.
supporter: You're very welcome. Anytime you need me, just reach out. You've got this, Amanda.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-11-05","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

seeker: Hey, I just found out that Bill, my ex, is dating someone new. I didn't think it would affect me so much.
supporter: Oh Amanda, I'm sorry. It must be really tough to hear that news. How are you feeling about it?
seeker: I feel a mix of emotions. On one hand, I know we broke up for good reasons, but on the other, it still hurts seeing him move on so quickly.
supporter: It's completely understandable to feel that way. Breakups have a way of stirring up unexpected feelings. Would talking about it more with me help?
seeker: Maybe. I'm starting to question if I'm the one who's taking too long to move on. It's like I'm stuck in this limbo.
supporter: You're not stuck, you're just processing everything at your own pace. Everyone's journey is different, and it's okay to take the time you need.
seeker: I guess. But seeing him happy with someone else makes me doubt myself, like, was I not enough, or did I make the right choice?
supporter: Those are hard questions to grapple with. Remember, breaking up was about differences in life goals, not your worth or abilities. You did it for your future.
seeker: True, we did have differing goals. I just wish I could turn off the emotional part and focus on that rationality.
supporter: Emotions can be really stubborn like that. It's okay to feel and express them, though. They're part of being human and make us whole.
seeker: Yeah, I suppose. It's just exhausting at times, especially with everything else going on... like work stress.
supporter: I remember you mentioned how undervalued you feel at work. That must amplify everything. How is that going?
seeker: Not great. My supervisor is still making things difficult, and I recently got a negative performance review. It's been crushing my confidence.
supporter: That sounds incredibly challenging. Dealing with work stress on top of personal issues seems overwhelming. Have you considered seeking any outside support?
seeker: I thought about it. Maybe seeing a therapist could help, but it's intimidating to take that step.
supporter: It's a big step, but it can also be really empowering. Having a space to speak openly and get professional guidance might ease that burden.
seeker: You're right. I need to prioritize myself more. It's been hard juggling everything alone.
supporter: I'm glad you're considering it. Remember, you're not alone in this. Feel free to reach out whenever you need to talk.
seeker: Thanks. It helps knowing there's someone I can lean on. I'll think more seriously about getting support.
supporter: That's a great step forward, Amanda. I'm really proud of you for facing all of this and seeking the path that's best for you.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-12-10","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

supporter: I have never understood how those work..I find it amazing someone can type out whole words or sentences with one word
seeker: Yeah, it's pretty cool.  For example, if I hit DRAT in one stroke, then "Did there come a time" will appear in English on my machine's  LCD screen.

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: hi there
supporter: Hello! How are you doing? 
seeker: I'm not doing so good at the moment. I'm feeling very stressed and burned out from work
supporter: That sounds very frustrating. Is this a recent development at your job? 
seeker: It's been building up for a while now, but it's really starting to get a but overwhelming
supporter: I can understand how that can have an effect on your mental well-being. Have you spoken to your supervisor about your frustrations at work? 
seeker: I have, but sometimes I feel like she doesn't really listen and she sort of talks over me a lot
supporter: It sounds like you don't feel listened to. 
seeker: That's right... I guess that is quite a lot of the problem. 
seeker: I don't mind so much the work, I know it is busy for everyone right now, it's a combination of the workload plus not being listened to
supporter: I had a similar issue at my last job. My supervisor constantly spoke over me in meetings, and it would drive me crazy. I never could get a word in edge-wise. 
seeker: Yeah, that sounds a lot like what I am experiencing
supporter: Are you considering switching jobs? 
seeker: It's been in the back of my mind, but it's a hard time just now with everything else going on
supporter: Absolutely. It's a rough time job searching under the best of circumstances. 
seeker: It is. 
supporter: Have you tried reaching out to anyone in your network to look for a new position? It helped me when I was previously job searching. 
seeker: I haven't, but it might be worth getting in touch with some people
supporter: Absolutely. I also spoke with a therapist before and it helped me a lot. 
supporter: Have you considered reaching out to a professional to talk to? 
seeker: I did consider that, but aren't they expensive?
supporter: They can be, but many local governments and municipalities have therapists that work on a sliding scale if the financial aspect of therapy is a concern. 
supporter: Therapy can definitely be a large expense though. 
seeker: It might be worth it in the long run though I guess, if it helps how I am feeling
supporter: If it helps to reframe the expense, you can try to think of it as an investment in your mental health. 
seeker: Yes, that sounds like a more positive way of thinking of it
supporter: The therapist could likely give you some tools to help manage the frustrations at your workplace more constructively. 
seeker: Yes, I imagine they will have come across this before so will be able to help
supporter: Absolutely. I hope that you're able to find some peace at your workplace with your boss. 
seeker: Thank you, you have helped a lot
seeker: Helped give me some ideas to try to help
supporter: It's my pleasure. I'm happy to have helped you. 
supporter: Is there anything else I can help you with? ","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-06-10","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hello, how are you doing today?
seeker: I am feeling angry today about work. 
supporter: Oh no, what happened to make you feel this way?
seeker: My coworker expects me to do things the way she does and is constantly critical. I just want her to understand that I am able to do things my way and it is still okay. I told her this and she ignored me. 
supporter: I'm sure that's terribly frustrating having someone treat you like that. Is this something that your boss is aware of?
seeker: I have not told her yet. I do not want to get her into trouble and I want to have a good relationship with her. 
supporter: Can you discuss it with her in a respectful way to get her to understand that you're not trying to undermine her but that this is how you work most efficiently? And maybe mention that you don't want to involve the boss?
seeker: That's something I could try. I really care about my coworker and it makes me so angry that she treats me this way. 
supporter: I think sometimes it's easy to jump to anger when you feel hurt. It might be worth telling her how you feel and also maybe ask why she thinks you should be doing things her way. Maybe there's a give and take in this situation. Some of her methods could be beneficial.
seeker: Do you have any advice on how to start my conversation with her? I have found some of her ideas to be beneficial. I just would like my ideas expressed as well. I feel we can learn from each other. 
supporter: Tell her the things that you like about her method and maybe suggest some of your methods to her as well. Maybe she'll find them to be more efficient. Make it a partnership rather than a fight for whose method is better.
supporter: She could feel threatened by you so it's worth digging into those feelings with her and proving to her that you're working toward the same goal.
seeker: That's a great idea. It is possible. I am the new kid on the block. I will try by being non confrontational. Any specific ideas to how  I can do that? She gets offended easily. I want her to know I am helping. 
supporter: I'd suggest how much she's helped you since you are in fact the new kid on the block.  And tell her that you want to work with her to have the most efficient partnership possible and use each of your talents to the best of your ability. Then you can lay out how you work best and see where it goes from there.
seeker: Thanks! I will try that. You made me feel so much better! 
supporter: I'm so glad, these can be frustrating situations but sometimes it's worth looking at the other person's perspective.
seeker: I agree. Sometimes you just have to take a step back and have a conversation with someone not in the thick of it. 
supporter: Absolutely, I have no emotional stake in this. The two of you do and that can cloud things sometimes.
seeker: I think people get territorial when they have worked somewhere and a new person comes in. I see that now. I am optimistic we will work it out and be a great team!
supporter: That's great to hear, I'm glad we were able to chat!
seeker: Me too! You really helped me. Have a wonderful day! I know I will since you helped me out. 
supporter: That's great, good luck!","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-09-01","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

supporter: Can you identify why you feel sad?
seeker: yes, my aunt pass away a couple weeks ago
seeker: and since then im feeling really sad

seeker: IS there something I can do to feel better?
supporter: Are you with family?   Sometimes it helps to be with others who are grieving?
seeker: No, I live alone, my family lives in another state
supporter: Being by yourself is rough after a death.    Can you talk with your family by phone?   Do you have a friend who has gone through a similar loss?
seeker: I feel like everybody is in their own bussines and have no time to hear my complains

supporter: It sounds like you feel people think you are complaining when you talk about your Aunt's death making you sad.    Is that correct?

supporter: Do you feel you are complaining?
seeker: yes, I feel like noone wants to listen
seeker: I need to do something by mnyself
seeker: Can you recommend someting for me to do to feel better?

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hi Amanda, it's good to see you online. How have you been doing lately?
seeker: Hey! I've been feeling a bit off after attending my aunt's memorial service last week.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. It must have been an emotional experience for you.
seeker: Yeah, it really was. Not only because we were saying goodbye, but also because I got to see so many relatives I hadn't seen in years.
supporter: That sounds like it brought up a lot of feelings. How did that affect you?
seeker: It was bittersweet. On one hand, it was wonderful to reconnect, but on the other hand, it made me realize how distant I've become from them.
supporter: It sounds like you're processing a mix of emotions—grief and perhaps some regret?
seeker: Exactly. I feel guilty for not staying in touch more. It was strange talking about memories with people I used to be so close to.
supporter: That's understandable. Guilt can be hard to shake off, but reconnecting at the memorial could be a new beginning.
seeker: I hope so. I exchanged numbers with a few of them and promised to keep in touch.
supporter: That's a great step forward. How does it feel to have taken that initiative?
seeker: A little reassuring, honestly. But there's still this nagging feeling of having missed out on so much with them.
supporter: It's natural to feel that way, but it's important to give yourself grace. Every relationship has its own timeline.
seeker: You're right. I guess I should focus on making the most of the present.
supporter: That's a positive perspective. How do you plan to keep your connections going from here?
seeker: I'm thinking of arranging a small family gathering, something more joy-filled, to keep everyone in touch.
supporter: That sounds like a wonderful idea! It could be a new tradition that brings everyone closer.
seeker: I hope so. It feels good just talking about it. Thanks for listening and helping me work through this.
supporter: Anytime, Amanda. Remember, you're taking meaningful steps. Keep nurturing those connections.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-07-25","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

seeker: Hi, honestly, it's been a tough couple of days. I finally had the big talk with Bill, and we decided to break up.

turns.content: Hi Amanda, it's good to see you online. How have you been doing lately?
Hey! I've been feeling a bit off after attending my aunt's memorial service last week.
I'm sorry to hear that. It must have been an emotional experience for you.
Yeah, it really was. Not only because we were saying goodbye, but also because I got to see so many relatives I hadn't seen in years.
That sounds like it brought up a lot of feelings. How did that affect you?
It was bittersweet. On one hand, it was wonderful to reconnect, but on the other hand, it made me realize how distant I've become from them.
It sounds like you're processing a mix of emotions—grief and perhaps some regret?
Exactly. I feel guilty for not staying in touch more. It was strange talking about memories with people I used to be so close to.
That's understandable. Guilt can be hard to shake off, but reconnecting at the memorial could be a new beginning.
I hope so. I exchanged numbers with a few of them and promised to keep in touch.
That's a great step forward. How does it feel to have taken that initiative?
A little reassuring, honestly. But there's still this nagging feeling of having missed out on so much with them.
It's natural to feel that way, but it's important to give yourself grace. Every relationship has its own timeline.
You're right. I guess I should focus on making the most of the present.

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hello
supporter: How are you doing today?
seeker: hello
supporter: How can I help you?
seeker: I need ways alleviate stress while studying 
supporter: It sounds like you are having some difficulty at school, I have definitely been there.
seeker: yeah, it can be tough sometimes and feel like you're in a dead end situation
supporter: Yes I worked a dead end job for ages when I was younger and sometimes you just feel stuck
seeker: How did you push past that job?
supporter: I am going to be honest a little luck was involved I managed to impress a customer that came in and ended up applying at their work.
seeker: Are you still with that job now, enough to consider it a career?
supporter: I would say so I am an insurance broker, it has only been a year or so but there seems to be room to move up. You can find something too
seeker: Is there any advice for getting out of my situation?
seeker: aside from luck that is
supporter: Can you give me some more details?
seeker: I just find the work mundane and way too remedial 
supporter: That is completely understandable
seeker: did you look at any websites or other job searching tools before you found your new job?
supporter: I have you a few, there are also many ways to gain skills online that buff up your resume a bit
seeker: what types of skill can I gain online?
supporter: Indeed is one of the better ones to look for jobs, honestly I would suggest looking at jobs that you normally wouldn't and see what kind of qualifications they need and see if you can get that done online.
seeker: so filter based on my absolute needs and go for online skills that I can complete?
supporter: yes I think that is a great idea, look for jobs that meet your needs and figure out what you can do to look attractive to employers
seeker: I have tried glassdoor before, have you had any luck there?
supporter: I used it a bit, I mainly used indeed.
seeker: and have you showcased your skills using LinkedIn before? I have had that one recommended to me before, they said its a great way to neatly organize accomplishments and personal background
supporter: Yes especially if you are applying for anything in a professional setting that is very important.
seeker: do you have any examples of online skills you completed?
supporter: coursera has a lot of great courses, it really depends on what you are looking for.
seeker: if I was looking to enter the engineering field, any recommendations?
supporter: Is that what you are going to school for?
seeker: yes but I may change my mind
supporter: What year are you in? most engineering programs have a practicum and that is a great opportunity to make contacts and potentially get offered a job
seeker: yes I have been networking as I go
supporter: Honestly you seem like you are pretty on top of this I don't think you will have any issues finding a job.
seeker: yeah I mean the topic was about final exam stress but we got on a tangent
supporter: Yes that is fair enough, how much time do you have until your exam?
seeker: 15 minutes
supporter: While that is plenty of time to get some studying done:)
seeker: yes I probably should, thank you for your insight!
supporter: Honestly I find that if you are going for the test right away I always like to just breath and relax a bit.
seeker: yeah no use in cramming for more info when I could just chill out
supporter: You seem like you know what you are doing, I think you will do just fine
seeker: yup thanks","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-06-25","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}
