{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: How can I help you today?
seeker: I'm disgusted with my professors that they don't see me as a human with real emotions and feelings.
supporter: I understand that you are feeling like your professors don't see you as a person with feelings. What happened to make you feel this way?
seeker: I have testing all the time and study non-stop, but the professors don't seem to encourage or support me.  They just see me as a number I feel.
supporter: That's hard to feel like they are treating you like a number when you are working so hard.  Have you talked to them about it?
seeker: It's hard to trust them when I'm seen as 1 of 100 people.  If I am struggling they don't flinch or ask me how they can assist.  I just am expected to 
seeker: tough it out.
supporter: I had a similar experience in my college days. It was very difficult to have so much pressure to succeed and feel so alone.  You can do though because you are working hard and want to succeed.
seeker: Thanks for the encouragement.  Where do I start to help myself feel better?
supporter: I see you are anxious about this when talking to you, but have you thought about getting some support from other students in your position?
seeker: That sounds like a good idea.  Maybe they are feeling this way too.
supporter: Also sometimes just stepping back and taking some deep breaths can help to alleviate some anxieties. Have you tried that ever?
seeker: I will have to give that a try.  I've done that in the past and had forgotten just how much that helped me before.  
supporter: That is reassuring that it worked before for you and  can work again.
seeker: I'm so worried about failing because I just don't feel the support from my professors to care either way for my successes.  It's so different from high school and home when my parents encouraged me and supported me full-heartedly.  
supporter: College can be quite a change from the protective atmosphere of home.  Have you tried any support groups or religious groups for encouragement?
seeker: I am religious so perhaps I could seek a group out and they could help with encouraging me.  
supporter: I was a  part of a religious group in college and they were very supportive even praying for me on exam days.  I felt they helped me with my success by planting seeds of positive feedback to me.
seeker: I used to be part of one during high school years, and that sounds like it would help.
supporter: Are you starting to feel better about the situation?
seeker: Yes, I do thinking about other people filling in the gaps and supporting me when others won't or can't. Thanks for chatting.  This was helpful.
supporter: You are welcome.  I wish you well.
seeker: I think I have a few tools now to make things better.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-07-15","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hello there! How can I encourage you today?
seeker: Hi, I have been going through a lot of stress with school and am also sad and lonely as of late and not sure how to make myself feel better
supporter: So you have had a lot of stress with school lately and are struggling to keep yourself cheerful?
supporter: Is there something in particular at school that is stressing you out? Exams? Relationships?
seeker: Yes! Its very hard to keep positive with all the work I have and I feel I am not doing well.
seeker: Yes, I have a lot of exams right now and that on top of not hanging out with friends a lot lately has made life tough.
supporter: I can understand being stressed if you think you are not doing well in school and have a lot of work. How are your grades now?
seeker: I still have decent grades but I feel like I am not prepared for big exams currently and they are worth a lot
supporter: Yes, that can be tough. When I had a lot of tests coming up and a lot to study for, I wrote down goals to study -- like I broke down the classes and made certain goals to study a bit in each class. And then if I did that, I could go out with friends or some reward like that. 
supporter: For example, if you have 7 classes, you can make a chart for when you will study for each of those classes and then check them off as you accomplish it, maybe not all in one day, maybe break it up in reasonable bits. Then study according to your goal, if that makes sense.
supporter: I remember after each class, I would take 15 minutes to review all my notes from class, that seems short, but really, it adds up and helped so much.
seeker: Yes, I think you have excellent advice about organization. I feel like I lose track of what I have and when to do it. I also bounce between classes, feeling stressed because there is so much. Do you think doing one class at a time is best?
seeker: I also tend to save stuff sometimes so I have a lot of work build up with tests on the same days. I am not sure how to stop procrastinating.
supporter: Yes, stick to one subject at a time. For example, if you think 1/2 hour is good enough to study, then stick to that. When done, your done until the next time it is on your schedule.
seeker: Ok. Thank you so much for the ideas. It seems like you have had similar experiences with stress from school.
supporter: Procrastination never makes us feel good. If I keep putting something off, I then feel guilty. If I make a goal, and I reach it, I can put a reward. For example, if you study 3 subjects 1/2 hour each, you can go out for yogurt with a friend. So you reward yourself for sticking to that goal.
supporter: Yes, I did. lol I'm really old now. This technique I use in all my life. Even house chores, I break it down into a schedule, put it in writing, then check off what I do. Then I feel good about my accomplishments.
seeker: Yes, that was my other question to you. It sounds great to just do a little time for each class but I often get overwhelmed and need a break
seeker: I have never used check lists or planners. I think it is part of how I get overwhelmed maybe.
supporter: Definitely you need a break, so schedule them as rewards. You can even do 15 minutes in say 4 subjects, then take a walk, take a cup of tea, or call a friend, then back to the books. 
supporter: Keep it as SIMPLE as possible, don't get bogged down. I used to think planning was TERRIBLE< but actually, it sets one FREE. You feel so much better and accomplished when you see how much you have done. It really is amazing. 
supporter: HOw man classes do you have?
supporter: many *
seeker: I have 6 classes
supporter: That's a lot but it is totally doable. Here is a good example, If you plant seeds in a garden today, you have to weed it a bit tomorrow, the next day, the next day, you have to wait for rain, then weed some more, the harvest comes and YAY! You are happy. But if you lie on your bed, never planting, never weeding, you procrastinate, you get nothing.
supporter: If you write your classes down and then write a reasonable time to study each one. Maybe 3 today, 3 tomorrow, then add rewards if you do that, maybe make a list of rewards, so you can pick and choose, then you check off when you do the subject.  Like a chore chart. 
seeker: Yes haha. That is a good comparison. You have been super helpful. I will for sure try to use your advice. Thank you!
seeker: Have a great day and thanks again
supporter: You are quite welcome! God bless have a great day!","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-06-10","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hello
supporter: How are you doing today?
seeker: hello
supporter: How can I help you?
seeker: I need ways alleviate stress while studying 
supporter: It sounds like you are having some difficulty at school, I have definitely been there.
seeker: yeah, it can be tough sometimes and feel like you're in a dead end situation
supporter: Yes I worked a dead end job for ages when I was younger and sometimes you just feel stuck
seeker: How did you push past that job?
supporter: I am going to be honest a little luck was involved I managed to impress a customer that came in and ended up applying at their work.
seeker: Are you still with that job now, enough to consider it a career?
supporter: I would say so I am an insurance broker, it has only been a year or so but there seems to be room to move up. You can find something too
seeker: Is there any advice for getting out of my situation?
seeker: aside from luck that is
supporter: Can you give me some more details?
seeker: I just find the work mundane and way too remedial 
supporter: That is completely understandable
seeker: did you look at any websites or other job searching tools before you found your new job?
supporter: I have you a few, there are also many ways to gain skills online that buff up your resume a bit
seeker: what types of skill can I gain online?
supporter: Indeed is one of the better ones to look for jobs, honestly I would suggest looking at jobs that you normally wouldn't and see what kind of qualifications they need and see if you can get that done online.
seeker: so filter based on my absolute needs and go for online skills that I can complete?
supporter: yes I think that is a great idea, look for jobs that meet your needs and figure out what you can do to look attractive to employers
seeker: I have tried glassdoor before, have you had any luck there?
supporter: I used it a bit, I mainly used indeed.
seeker: and have you showcased your skills using LinkedIn before? I have had that one recommended to me before, they said its a great way to neatly organize accomplishments and personal background
supporter: Yes especially if you are applying for anything in a professional setting that is very important.
seeker: do you have any examples of online skills you completed?
supporter: coursera has a lot of great courses, it really depends on what you are looking for.
seeker: if I was looking to enter the engineering field, any recommendations?
supporter: Is that what you are going to school for?
seeker: yes but I may change my mind
supporter: What year are you in? most engineering programs have a practicum and that is a great opportunity to make contacts and potentially get offered a job
seeker: yes I have been networking as I go
supporter: Honestly you seem like you are pretty on top of this I don't think you will have any issues finding a job.
seeker: yeah I mean the topic was about final exam stress but we got on a tangent
supporter: Yes that is fair enough, how much time do you have until your exam?
seeker: 15 minutes
supporter: While that is plenty of time to get some studying done:)
seeker: yes I probably should, thank you for your insight!
supporter: Honestly I find that if you are going for the test right away I always like to just breath and relax a bit.
seeker: yeah no use in cramming for more info when I could just chill out
supporter: You seem like you know what you are doing, I think you will do just fine
seeker: yup thanks","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-06-25","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: How can I help you today?
seeker: I'm disgusted with my professors that they don't see me as a human with real emotions and feelings.
supporter: I understand that you are feeling like your professors don't see you as a person with feelings. What happened to make you feel this way?
seeker: I have testing all the time and study non-stop, but the professors don't seem to encourage or support me.  They just see me as a number I feel.
supporter: That's hard to feel like they are treating you like a number when you are working so hard.  Have you talked to them about it?
seeker: It's hard to trust them when I'm seen as 1 of 100 people.  If I am struggling they don't flinch or ask me how they can assist.  I just am expected to 
seeker: tough it out.
supporter: I had a similar experience in my college days. It was very difficult to have so much pressure to succeed and feel so alone.  You can do though because you are working hard and want to succeed.
seeker: Thanks for the encouragement.  Where do I start to help myself feel better?
supporter: I see you are anxious about this when talking to you, but have you thought about getting some support from other students in your position?
seeker: That sounds like a good idea.  Maybe they are feeling this way too.
supporter: Also sometimes just stepping back and taking some deep breaths can help to alleviate some anxieties. Have you tried that ever?
seeker: I will have to give that a try.  I've done that in the past and had forgotten just how much that helped me before.  
supporter: That is reassuring that it worked before for you and  can work again.
seeker: I'm so worried about failing because I just don't feel the support from my professors to care either way for my successes.  It's so different from high school and home when my parents encouraged me and supported me full-heartedly.  
supporter: College can be quite a change from the protective atmosphere of home.  Have you tried any support groups or religious groups for encouragement?
seeker: I am religious so perhaps I could seek a group out and they could help with encouraging me.  
supporter: I was a  part of a religious group in college and they were very supportive even praying for me on exam days.  I felt they helped me with my success by planting seeds of positive feedback to me.
seeker: I used to be part of one during high school years, and that sounds like it would help.
supporter: Are you starting to feel better about the situation?
seeker: Yes, I do thinking about other people filling in the gaps and supporting me when others won't or can't. Thanks for chatting.  This was helpful.
supporter: You are welcome.  I wish you well.
seeker: I think I have a few tools now to make things better.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-07-15","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hello there! How can I encourage you today?
seeker: Hi, I have been going through a lot of stress with school and am also sad and lonely as of late and not sure how to make myself feel better
supporter: So you have had a lot of stress with school lately and are struggling to keep yourself cheerful?
supporter: Is there something in particular at school that is stressing you out? Exams? Relationships?
seeker: Yes! Its very hard to keep positive with all the work I have and I feel I am not doing well.
seeker: Yes, I have a lot of exams right now and that on top of not hanging out with friends a lot lately has made life tough.
supporter: I can understand being stressed if you think you are not doing well in school and have a lot of work. How are your grades now?
seeker: I still have decent grades but I feel like I am not prepared for big exams currently and they are worth a lot
supporter: Yes, that can be tough. When I had a lot of tests coming up and a lot to study for, I wrote down goals to study -- like I broke down the classes and made certain goals to study a bit in each class. And then if I did that, I could go out with friends or some reward like that. 
supporter: For example, if you have 7 classes, you can make a chart for when you will study for each of those classes and then check them off as you accomplish it, maybe not all in one day, maybe break it up in reasonable bits. Then study according to your goal, if that makes sense.
supporter: I remember after each class, I would take 15 minutes to review all my notes from class, that seems short, but really, it adds up and helped so much.
seeker: Yes, I think you have excellent advice about organization. I feel like I lose track of what I have and when to do it. I also bounce between classes, feeling stressed because there is so much. Do you think doing one class at a time is best?
seeker: I also tend to save stuff sometimes so I have a lot of work build up with tests on the same days. I am not sure how to stop procrastinating.
supporter: Yes, stick to one subject at a time. For example, if you think 1/2 hour is good enough to study, then stick to that. When done, your done until the next time it is on your schedule.
seeker: Ok. Thank you so much for the ideas. It seems like you have had similar experiences with stress from school.
supporter: Procrastination never makes us feel good. If I keep putting something off, I then feel guilty. If I make a goal, and I reach it, I can put a reward. For example, if you study 3 subjects 1/2 hour each, you can go out for yogurt with a friend. So you reward yourself for sticking to that goal.
supporter: Yes, I did. lol I'm really old now. This technique I use in all my life. Even house chores, I break it down into a schedule, put it in writing, then check off what I do. Then I feel good about my accomplishments.
seeker: Yes, that was my other question to you. It sounds great to just do a little time for each class but I often get overwhelmed and need a break
seeker: I have never used check lists or planners. I think it is part of how I get overwhelmed maybe.
supporter: Definitely you need a break, so schedule them as rewards. You can even do 15 minutes in say 4 subjects, then take a walk, take a cup of tea, or call a friend, then back to the books. 
supporter: Keep it as SIMPLE as possible, don't get bogged down. I used to think planning was TERRIBLE< but actually, it sets one FREE. You feel so much better and accomplished when you see how much you have done. It really is amazing. 
supporter: HOw man classes do you have?
supporter: many *
seeker: I have 6 classes
supporter: That's a lot but it is totally doable. Here is a good example, If you plant seeds in a garden today, you have to weed it a bit tomorrow, the next day, the next day, you have to wait for rain, then weed some more, the harvest comes and YAY! You are happy. But if you lie on your bed, never planting, never weeding, you procrastinate, you get nothing.
supporter: If you write your classes down and then write a reasonable time to study each one. Maybe 3 today, 3 tomorrow, then add rewards if you do that, maybe make a list of rewards, so you can pick and choose, then you check off when you do the subject.  Like a chore chart. 
seeker: Yes haha. That is a good comparison. You have been super helpful. I will for sure try to use your advice. Thank you!
seeker: Have a great day and thanks again
supporter: You are quite welcome! God bless have a great day!","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-06-10","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hello there! How can I encourage you today?
seeker: Hi, I have been going through a lot of stress with school and am also sad and lonely as of late and not sure how to make myself feel better
supporter: So you have had a lot of stress with school lately and are struggling to keep yourself cheerful?
supporter: Is there something in particular at school that is stressing you out? Exams? Relationships?
seeker: Yes! Its very hard to keep positive with all the work I have and I feel I am not doing well.
seeker: Yes, I have a lot of exams right now and that on top of not hanging out with friends a lot lately has made life tough.
supporter: I can understand being stressed if you think you are not doing well in school and have a lot of work. How are your grades now?
seeker: I still have decent grades but I feel like I am not prepared for big exams currently and they are worth a lot
supporter: Yes, that can be tough. When I had a lot of tests coming up and a lot to study for, I wrote down goals to study -- like I broke down the classes and made certain goals to study a bit in each class. And then if I did that, I could go out with friends or some reward like that. 
supporter: For example, if you have 7 classes, you can make a chart for when you will study for each of those classes and then check them off as you accomplish it, maybe not all in one day, maybe break it up in reasonable bits. Then study according to your goal, if that makes sense.
supporter: I remember after each class, I would take 15 minutes to review all my notes from class, that seems short, but really, it adds up and helped so much.
seeker: Yes, I think you have excellent advice about organization. I feel like I lose track of what I have and when to do it. I also bounce between classes, feeling stressed because there is so much. Do you think doing one class at a time is best?
seeker: I also tend to save stuff sometimes so I have a lot of work build up with tests on the same days. I am not sure how to stop procrastinating.
supporter: Yes, stick to one subject at a time. For example, if you think 1/2 hour is good enough to study, then stick to that. When done, your done until the next time it is on your schedule.
seeker: Ok. Thank you so much for the ideas. It seems like you have had similar experiences with stress from school.
supporter: Procrastination never makes us feel good. If I keep putting something off, I then feel guilty. If I make a goal, and I reach it, I can put a reward. For example, if you study 3 subjects 1/2 hour each, you can go out for yogurt with a friend. So you reward yourself for sticking to that goal.
supporter: Yes, I did. lol I'm really old now. This technique I use in all my life. Even house chores, I break it down into a schedule, put it in writing, then check off what I do. Then I feel good about my accomplishments.
seeker: Yes, that was my other question to you. It sounds great to just do a little time for each class but I often get overwhelmed and need a break
seeker: I have never used check lists or planners. I think it is part of how I get overwhelmed maybe.
supporter: Definitely you need a break, so schedule them as rewards. You can even do 15 minutes in say 4 subjects, then take a walk, take a cup of tea, or call a friend, then back to the books. 
supporter: Keep it as SIMPLE as possible, don't get bogged down. I used to think planning was TERRIBLE< but actually, it sets one FREE. You feel so much better and accomplished when you see how much you have done. It really is amazing. 
supporter: HOw man classes do you have?
supporter: many *
seeker: I have 6 classes
supporter: That's a lot but it is totally doable. Here is a good example, If you plant seeds in a garden today, you have to weed it a bit tomorrow, the next day, the next day, you have to wait for rain, then weed some more, the harvest comes and YAY! You are happy. But if you lie on your bed, never planting, never weeding, you procrastinate, you get nothing.
supporter: If you write your classes down and then write a reasonable time to study each one. Maybe 3 today, 3 tomorrow, then add rewards if you do that, maybe make a list of rewards, so you can pick and choose, then you check off when you do the subject.  Like a chore chart. 
seeker: Yes haha. That is a good comparison. You have been super helpful. I will for sure try to use your advice. Thank you!
seeker: Have a great day and thanks again

supporter: I remember after each class, I would take 15 minutes to review all my notes from class, that seems short, but really, it adds up and helped so much.

supporter: Yes, stick to one subject at a time. For example, if you think 1/2 hour is good enough to study, then stick to that. When done, your done until the next time it is on your schedule.
seeker: Ok. Thank you so much for the ideas. It seems like you have had similar experiences with stress from school.

For example, if you study 3 subjects 1/2 hour each, you can go out for yogurt with a friend. So you reward yourself for sticking to that goal.
supporter: Yes, I did. lol I'm really old now. This technique I use in all my life. Even house chores, I break it down into a schedule, put it in writing, then check off what I do. Then I feel good about my accomplishments.

supporter: Keep it as SIMPLE as possible, don't get bogged down. I used to think planning was TERRIBLE< but actually, it sets one FREE. You feel so much better and accomplished when you see how much you have done. It really is amazing. 
supporter: HOw man classes do you have?

Here is a good example, If you plant seeds in a garden today, you have to weed it a bit tomorrow, the next day, the next day, you have to wait for rain, then weed some more, the harvest comes and YAY! You are happy. But if you lie on your bed, never planting, never weeding, you procrastinate, you get nothing.

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hey, just need someone to talk to. Things have been rough lately.
supporter: I'm here for you, Andrew. What's been going on?
seeker: Jenny and I had this huge fight about our careers. It feels like everything is falling apart.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. Conflicts like that can be really tough. Do you want to share more about what happened?
seeker: We both have different goals right now. She's focused on her career and I am trying to balance my studies and future plans, but we're not aligned.
supporter: That must be really stressful, trying to juggle everything. It's understandable that you'd want to have shared goals. How does that make you feel?
seeker: Frustrated and a bit scared, honestly. I love Jenny a lot, but I don't know how to bridge this gap between us.
supporter: It sounds like you're feeling really torn. Having a partner is about being on the same page, and when that doesn't happen, it's really hard. Have you two had a chance to sit down and talk more calmly about your priorities?
seeker: We tried, but every conversation seems to circle back to the same issues. It's like we're speaking different languages.
supporter: Communication can be so tricky, especially when emotions run high. Have you considered maybe seeking some outside help, like a counselor or someone who might help you both communicate more effectively?
seeker: I've thought about it. Just not sure how she'll react to the suggestion. I'm scared it might make things worse between us.
supporter: I can understand your hesitation. Sometimes it might feel risky, but often it can open new avenues you haven't considered. You know, the fact that you care this much shows how much you're willing to make things work.
seeker: Yeah, I guess you're right. I do really want this to work out. I can't imagine not being with her.
supporter: It’s clear you deeply value your relationship. Maybe in time, you both can find a compromise. Meanwhile, it's important to not lose sight of taking care of yourself too.
seeker: True, I haven't really been paying much attention to myself. I’ve been swamped with studies and stress over all this.
supporter: It's really easy to forget self-care when you're dealing with so much. Maybe taking some time to regroup could help you clear your mind and see things more clearly.
seeker: You're right. I should probably take a step back, even just a little bit. Maybe it will help me see things from a different perspective.
supporter: I think that's a great start, Andrew. It doesn’t mean you're giving up; it means you're taking the time to recharge so you can come back stronger.
seeker: Thanks, I think I'll try to find some space for myself. And maybe talk to Jenny about counseling, test the waters at least.
supporter: Sounds like a solid plan. Remember, I'm just a message away if you need more support.
seeker: Thanks for listening and for the advice. It’s really helped just to talk things out.
supporter: Anytime, Andrew. You're going through a lot, but I'm confident you'll figure things out. Take care of yourself, okay?
seeker: I will. Thanks again.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-10-15","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: How can I help you today?
seeker: I'm disgusted with my professors that they don't see me as a human with real emotions and feelings.
supporter: I understand that you are feeling like your professors don't see you as a person with feelings. What happened to make you feel this way?
seeker: I have testing all the time and study non-stop, but the professors don't seem to encourage or support me.  They just see me as a number I feel.
supporter: That's hard to feel like they are treating you like a number when you are working so hard.  Have you talked to them about it?
seeker: It's hard to trust them when I'm seen as 1 of 100 people.  If I am struggling they don't flinch or ask me how they can assist.  I just am expected to 
seeker: tough it out.
supporter: I had a similar experience in my college days. It was very difficult to have so much pressure to succeed and feel so alone.  You can do though because you are working hard and want to succeed.
seeker: Thanks for the encouragement.  Where do I start to help myself feel better?
supporter: I see you are anxious about this when talking to you, but have you thought about getting some support from other students in your position?
seeker: That sounds like a good idea.  Maybe they are feeling this way too.
supporter: Also sometimes just stepping back and taking some deep breaths can help to alleviate some anxieties. Have you tried that ever?
seeker: I will have to give that a try.  I've done that in the past and had forgotten just how much that helped me before.  
supporter: That is reassuring that it worked before for you and  can work again.
seeker: I'm so worried about failing because I just don't feel the support from my professors to care either way for my successes.  It's so different from high school and home when my parents encouraged me and supported me full-heartedly.  
supporter: College can be quite a change from the protective atmosphere of home.  Have you tried any support groups or religious groups for encouragement?
seeker: I am religious so perhaps I could seek a group out and they could help with encouraging me.  
supporter: I was a  part of a religious group in college and they were very supportive even praying for me on exam days.  I felt they helped me with my success by planting seeds of positive feedback to me.
seeker: I used to be part of one during high school years, and that sounds like it would help.
supporter: Are you starting to feel better about the situation?
seeker: Yes, I do thinking about other people filling in the gaps and supporting me when others won't or can't. Thanks for chatting.  This was helpful.
supporter: You are welcome.  I wish you well.
seeker: I think I have a few tools now to make things better.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-07-15","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hello there! How can I encourage you today?
seeker: Hi, I have been going through a lot of stress with school and am also sad and lonely as of late and not sure how to make myself feel better
supporter: So you have had a lot of stress with school lately and are struggling to keep yourself cheerful?
supporter: Is there something in particular at school that is stressing you out? Exams? Relationships?
seeker: Yes! Its very hard to keep positive with all the work I have and I feel I am not doing well.
seeker: Yes, I have a lot of exams right now and that on top of not hanging out with friends a lot lately has made life tough.
supporter: I can understand being stressed if you think you are not doing well in school and have a lot of work. How are your grades now?
seeker: I still have decent grades but I feel like I am not prepared for big exams currently and they are worth a lot
supporter: Yes, that can be tough. When I had a lot of tests coming up and a lot to study for, I wrote down goals to study -- like I broke down the classes and made certain goals to study a bit in each class. And then if I did that, I could go out with friends or some reward like that. 
supporter: For example, if you have 7 classes, you can make a chart for when you will study for each of those classes and then check them off as you accomplish it, maybe not all in one day, maybe break it up in reasonable bits. Then study according to your goal, if that makes sense.
supporter: I remember after each class, I would take 15 minutes to review all my notes from class, that seems short, but really, it adds up and helped so much.
seeker: Yes, I think you have excellent advice about organization. I feel like I lose track of what I have and when to do it. I also bounce between classes, feeling stressed because there is so much. Do you think doing one class at a time is best?
seeker: I also tend to save stuff sometimes so I have a lot of work build up with tests on the same days. I am not sure how to stop procrastinating.
supporter: Yes, stick to one subject at a time. For example, if you think 1/2 hour is good enough to study, then stick to that. When done, your done until the next time it is on your schedule.
seeker: Ok. Thank you so much for the ideas. It seems like you have had similar experiences with stress from school.
supporter: Procrastination never makes us feel good. If I keep putting something off, I then feel guilty. If I make a goal, and I reach it, I can put a reward. For example, if you study 3 subjects 1/2 hour each, you can go out for yogurt with a friend. So you reward yourself for sticking to that goal.
supporter: Yes, I did. lol I'm really old now. This technique I use in all my life. Even house chores, I break it down into a schedule, put it in writing, then check off what I do. Then I feel good about my accomplishments.
seeker: Yes, that was my other question to you. It sounds great to just do a little time for each class but I often get overwhelmed and need a break
seeker: I have never used check lists or planners. I think it is part of how I get overwhelmed maybe.
supporter: Definitely you need a break, so schedule them as rewards. You can even do 15 minutes in say 4 subjects, then take a walk, take a cup of tea, or call a friend, then back to the books. 
supporter: Keep it as SIMPLE as possible, don't get bogged down. I used to think planning was TERRIBLE< but actually, it sets one FREE. You feel so much better and accomplished when you see how much you have done. It really is amazing. 
supporter: HOw man classes do you have?
supporter: many *
seeker: I have 6 classes
supporter: That's a lot but it is totally doable. Here is a good example, If you plant seeds in a garden today, you have to weed it a bit tomorrow, the next day, the next day, you have to wait for rain, then weed some more, the harvest comes and YAY! You are happy. But if you lie on your bed, never planting, never weeding, you procrastinate, you get nothing.
supporter: If you write your classes down and then write a reasonable time to study each one. Maybe 3 today, 3 tomorrow, then add rewards if you do that, maybe make a list of rewards, so you can pick and choose, then you check off when you do the subject.  Like a chore chart. 
seeker: Yes haha. That is a good comparison. You have been super helpful. I will for sure try to use your advice. Thank you!
seeker: Have a great day and thanks again
supporter: You are quite welcome! God bless have a great day!","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-06-10","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

seeker: Hey, honestly, I've been a bit overwhelmed. I'm considering changing my research focus, and it's been weighing on me.
supporter: I can imagine that must be a tough decision. What’s making you think about changing your focus?
seeker: I haven't made much progress lately, and I'm just not interested in my current topic anymore. Plus, the feedback from my advisor was disheartening.

seeker: I'm disgusted with my professors that they don't see me as a human with real emotions and feelings.

seeker: It's hard to trust them when I'm seen as 1 of 100 people.  If I am struggling they don't flinch or ask me how they can assist.  I just am expected to

seeker: I used to be part of one during high school years, and that sounds like it would help.
supporter: Are you starting to feel better about the situation?

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hello there! How can I encourage you today?
seeker: Hi, I have been going through a lot of stress with school and am also sad and lonely as of late and not sure how to make myself feel better
supporter: So you have had a lot of stress with school lately and are struggling to keep yourself cheerful?
supporter: Is there something in particular at school that is stressing you out? Exams? Relationships?
seeker: Yes! Its very hard to keep positive with all the work I have and I feel I am not doing well.
seeker: Yes, I have a lot of exams right now and that on top of not hanging out with friends a lot lately has made life tough.
supporter: I can understand being stressed if you think you are not doing well in school and have a lot of work. How are your grades now?
seeker: I still have decent grades but I feel like I am not prepared for big exams currently and they are worth a lot
supporter: Yes, that can be tough. When I had a lot of tests coming up and a lot to study for, I wrote down goals to study -- like I broke down the classes and made certain goals to study a bit in each class. And then if I did that, I could go out with friends or some reward like that. 
supporter: For example, if you have 7 classes, you can make a chart for when you will study for each of those classes and then check them off as you accomplish it, maybe not all in one day, maybe break it up in reasonable bits. Then study according to your goal, if that makes sense.
supporter: I remember after each class, I would take 15 minutes to review all my notes from class, that seems short, but really, it adds up and helped so much.
seeker: Yes, I think you have excellent advice about organization. I feel like I lose track of what I have and when to do it. I also bounce between classes, feeling stressed because there is so much. Do you think doing one class at a time is best?
seeker: I also tend to save stuff sometimes so I have a lot of work build up with tests on the same days. I am not sure how to stop procrastinating.
supporter: Yes, stick to one subject at a time. For example, if you think 1/2 hour is good enough to study, then stick to that. When done, your done until the next time it is on your schedule.
seeker: Ok. Thank you so much for the ideas. It seems like you have had similar experiences with stress from school.
supporter: Procrastination never makes us feel good. If I keep putting something off, I then feel guilty. If I make a goal, and I reach it, I can put a reward. For example, if you study 3 subjects 1/2 hour each, you can go out for yogurt with a friend. So you reward yourself for sticking to that goal.
supporter: Yes, I did. lol I'm really old now. This technique I use in all my life. Even house chores, I break it down into a schedule, put it in writing, then check off what I do. Then I feel good about my accomplishments.
seeker: Yes, that was my other question to you. It sounds great to just do a little time for each class but I often get overwhelmed and need a break
seeker: I have never used check lists or planners. I think it is part of how I get overwhelmed maybe.
supporter: Definitely you need a break, so schedule them as rewards. You can even do 15 minutes in say 4 subjects, then take a walk, take a cup of tea, or call a friend, then back to the books. 
supporter: Keep it as SIMPLE as possible, don't get bogged down. I used to think planning was TERRIBLE< but actually, it sets one FREE. You feel so much better and accomplished when you see how much you have done. It really is amazing. 
supporter: HOw man classes do you have?
supporter: many *
seeker: I have 6 classes
supporter: That's a lot but it is totally doable. Here is a good example, If you plant seeds in a garden today, you have to weed it a bit tomorrow, the next day, the next day, you have to wait for rain, then weed some more, the harvest comes and YAY! You are happy. But if you lie on your bed, never planting, never weeding, you procrastinate, you get nothing.
supporter: If you write your classes down and then write a reasonable time to study each one. Maybe 3 today, 3 tomorrow, then add rewards if you do that, maybe make a list of rewards, so you can pick and choose, then you check off when you do the subject.  Like a chore chart. 
seeker: Yes haha. That is a good comparison. You have been super helpful. I will for sure try to use your advice. Thank you!
seeker: Have a great day and thanks again
supporter: You are quite welcome! God bless have a great day!","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-06-10","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

seeker: I'm disgusted with my professors that they don't see me as a human with real emotions and feelings.
supporter: I understand that you are feeling like your professors don't see you as a person with feelings. What happened to make you feel this way?
seeker: I have testing all the time and study non-stop, but the professors don't seem to encourage or support me.  They just see me as a number I feel.
supporter: That's hard to feel like they are treating you like a number when you are working so hard.  Have you talked to them about it?
seeker: It's hard to trust them when I'm seen as 1 of 100 people.  If I am struggling they don't flinch or ask me how they can assist.  I just am expected to 
seeker: tough it out.
supporter: I had a similar experience in my college days. It was very difficult to have so much pressure to succeed and feel so alone.  You can do though because you are working hard and want to succeed.
seeker: Thanks for the encouragement.  Where do I start to help myself feel better?
supporter: I see you are anxious about this when talking to you, but have you thought about getting some support from other students in your position?
seeker: That sounds like a good idea.  Maybe they are feeling this way too.
supporter: Also sometimes just stepping back and taking some deep breaths can help to alleviate some anxieties. Have you tried that ever?
seeker: I will have to give that a try.  I've done that in the past and had forgotten just how much that helped me before.  
supporter: That is reassuring that it worked before for you and  can work again.
seeker: I'm so worried about failing because I just don't feel the support from my professors to care either way for my successes.  It's so different from high school and home when my parents encouraged me and supported me full-heartedly.  
supporter: College can be quite a change from the protective atmosphere of home.  Have you tried any support groups or religious groups for encouragement?
seeker: I am religious so perhaps I could seek a group out and they could help with encouraging me.  
supporter: I was a  part of a religious group in college and they were very supportive even praying for me on exam days.  I felt they helped me with my success by planting seeds of positive feedback to me.
seeker: I used to be part of one during high school years, and that sounds like it would help.
supporter: Are you starting to feel better about the situation?
seeker: Yes, I do thinking about other people filling in the gaps and supporting me when others won't or can't. Thanks for chatting.  This was helpful.
supporter: You are welcome.  I wish you well.
seeker: I think I have a few tools now to make things better.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-07-15","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hello
supporter: How are you doing today?
seeker: hello
supporter: How can I help you?
seeker: I need ways alleviate stress while studying 
supporter: It sounds like you are having some difficulty at school, I have definitely been there.
seeker: yeah, it can be tough sometimes and feel like you're in a dead end situation
supporter: Yes I worked a dead end job for ages when I was younger and sometimes you just feel stuck
seeker: How did you push past that job?
supporter: I am going to be honest a little luck was involved I managed to impress a customer that came in and ended up applying at their work.
seeker: Are you still with that job now, enough to consider it a career?
supporter: I would say so I am an insurance broker, it has only been a year or so but there seems to be room to move up. You can find something too
seeker: Is there any advice for getting out of my situation?
seeker: aside from luck that is
supporter: Can you give me some more details?
seeker: I just find the work mundane and way too remedial 
supporter: That is completely understandable
seeker: did you look at any websites or other job searching tools before you found your new job?
supporter: I have you a few, there are also many ways to gain skills online that buff up your resume a bit
seeker: what types of skill can I gain online?
supporter: Indeed is one of the better ones to look for jobs, honestly I would suggest looking at jobs that you normally wouldn't and see what kind of qualifications they need and see if you can get that done online.
seeker: so filter based on my absolute needs and go for online skills that I can complete?
supporter: yes I think that is a great idea, look for jobs that meet your needs and figure out what you can do to look attractive to employers
seeker: I have tried glassdoor before, have you had any luck there?
supporter: I used it a bit, I mainly used indeed.
seeker: and have you showcased your skills using LinkedIn before? I have had that one recommended to me before, they said its a great way to neatly organize accomplishments and personal background
supporter: Yes especially if you are applying for anything in a professional setting that is very important.
seeker: do you have any examples of online skills you completed?
supporter: coursera has a lot of great courses, it really depends on what you are looking for.
seeker: if I was looking to enter the engineering field, any recommendations?
supporter: Is that what you are going to school for?
seeker: yes but I may change my mind
supporter: What year are you in? most engineering programs have a practicum and that is a great opportunity to make contacts and potentially get offered a job
seeker: yes I have been networking as I go
supporter: Honestly you seem like you are pretty on top of this I don't think you will have any issues finding a job.
seeker: yeah I mean the topic was about final exam stress but we got on a tangent
supporter: Yes that is fair enough, how much time do you have until your exam?
seeker: 15 minutes
supporter: While that is plenty of time to get some studying done:)
seeker: yes I probably should, thank you for your insight!
supporter: Honestly I find that if you are going for the test right away I always like to just breath and relax a bit.
seeker: yeah no use in cramming for more info when I could just chill out
supporter: You seem like you know what you are doing, I think you will do just fine
seeker: yup thanks","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-06-25","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hello there! How can I encourage you today?
seeker: Hi, I have been going through a lot of stress with school and am also sad and lonely as of late and not sure how to make myself feel better
supporter: So you have had a lot of stress with school lately and are struggling to keep yourself cheerful?
supporter: Is there something in particular at school that is stressing you out? Exams? Relationships?
seeker: Yes! Its very hard to keep positive with all the work I have and I feel I am not doing well.
seeker: Yes, I have a lot of exams right now and that on top of not hanging out with friends a lot lately has made life tough.
supporter: I can understand being stressed if you think you are not doing well in school and have a lot of work. How are your grades now?
seeker: I still have decent grades but I feel like I am not prepared for big exams currently and they are worth a lot
supporter: Yes, that can be tough. When I had a lot of tests coming up and a lot to study for, I wrote down goals to study -- like I broke down the classes and made certain goals to study a bit in each class. And then if I did that, I could go out with friends or some reward like that. 
supporter: For example, if you have 7 classes, you can make a chart for when you will study for each of those classes and then check them off as you accomplish it, maybe not all in one day, maybe break it up in reasonable bits. Then study according to your goal, if that makes sense.
supporter: I remember after each class, I would take 15 minutes to review all my notes from class, that seems short, but really, it adds up and helped so much.
seeker: Yes, I think you have excellent advice about organization. I feel like I lose track of what I have and when to do it. I also bounce between classes, feeling stressed because there is so much. Do you think doing one class at a time is best?
seeker: I also tend to save stuff sometimes so I have a lot of work build up with tests on the same days. I am not sure how to stop procrastinating.
supporter: Yes, stick to one subject at a time. For example, if you think 1/2 hour is good enough to study, then stick to that. When done, your done until the next time it is on your schedule.
seeker: Ok. Thank you so much for the ideas. It seems like you have had similar experiences with stress from school.
supporter: Procrastination never makes us feel good. If I keep putting something off, I then feel guilty. If I make a goal, and I reach it, I can put a reward. For example, if you study 3 subjects 1/2 hour each, you can go out for yogurt with a friend. So you reward yourself for sticking to that goal.
supporter: Yes, I did. lol I'm really old now. This technique I use in all my life. Even house chores, I break it down into a schedule, put it in writing, then check off what I do. Then I feel good about my accomplishments.
seeker: Yes, that was my other question to you. It sounds great to just do a little time for each class but I often get overwhelmed and need a break
seeker: I have never used check lists or planners. I think it is part of how I get overwhelmed maybe.
supporter: Definitely you need a break, so schedule them as rewards. You can even do 15 minutes in say 4 subjects, then take a walk, take a cup of tea, or call a friend, then back to the books. 
supporter: Keep it as SIMPLE as possible, don't get bogged down. I used to think planning was TERRIBLE< but actually, it sets one FREE. You feel so much better and accomplished when you see how much you have done. It really is amazing. 
supporter: HOw man classes do you have?
supporter: many *
seeker: I have 6 classes
supporter: That's a lot but it is totally doable. Here is a good example, If you plant seeds in a garden today, you have to weed it a bit tomorrow, the next day, the next day, you have to wait for rain, then weed some more, the harvest comes and YAY! You are happy. But if you lie on your bed, never planting, never weeding, you procrastinate, you get nothing.
supporter: If you write your classes down and then write a reasonable time to study each one. Maybe 3 today, 3 tomorrow, then add rewards if you do that, maybe make a list of rewards, so you can pick and choose, then you check off when you do the subject.  Like a chore chart. 
seeker: Yes haha. That is a good comparison. You have been super helpful. I will for sure try to use your advice. Thank you!
seeker: Have a great day and thanks again
supporter: You are quite welcome! God bless have a great day!","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-06-10","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

turns.content: Hey Andrew, how have you been feeling lately?
Hey, honestly, I've been a bit overwhelmed. I'm considering changing my research focus, and it's been weighing on me.
I can imagine that must be a tough decision. What’s making you think about changing your focus?
I haven't made much progress lately, and I'm just not interested in my current topic anymore. Plus, the feedback from my advisor was disheartening.
That sounds really frustrating. Feedback like that can really bring you down, especially when you're already feeling uncertain. How did you feel after hearing it?
I felt a bit lost, to be honest. Like I’m just not cut out for this. It's hard because it makes me question my decisions.
It's completely normal to question yourself when you're going through such challenges. Remember, you’ve made it this far for a reason. What do you think would rekindle your interest in research?
I've been considering exploring alternative energy sources, like renewables. It's something that aligns with my values and seems rewarding.

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hey Andrew, how are you feeling today?
seeker: Hey. Not great, to be honest. Just got some feedback on my thesis that's really got me down.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. Do you want to talk about what they said?
seeker: Yeah, sure. My advisor thought it lacked depth and wasn't very clear in parts. It feels like so much work just went down the drain.
supporter: That sounds really frustrating. You've put so much effort into this. It makes sense that you'd feel discouraged.
seeker: Yeah, and it's just on top of everything else. Things with Jenny aren't great either. We argued about my career priorities last week.
supporter: It seems like there's a lot going on for you right now. The argument with Jenny must be weighing heavily on your mind too.
seeker: It is. I'm just feeling like I'm not making anyone happy, including myself.
supporter: It makes sense you'd feel that way. Sometimes when things stack up, it feels overwhelming. What do you think might help right now?
seeker: Honestly, I don't even know. Maybe just talking it through with someone helps a bit, like this conversation.
supporter: That's good to hear. I'm here to listen. You're not alone in this, even if it feels like it sometimes.
seeker: Thanks. I guess with everything happening, I just forgot how to take care of myself for a bit.
supporter: It's understandable. Self-care is often the first thing we overlook when life's pressures pile up. Is there anything small you can do for yourself today?
seeker: Maybe I'll take a walk. It usually clears my head, even if just a bit.
supporter: That sounds like a great idea. Fresh air and a change of scenery can work wonders.
seeker: Yeah, I should do that more. I generally get lost in my work these days.
supporter: It can be easy to get caught up, especially when there's pressure to perform. Do you feel like you're getting enough support from those around you?
seeker: Not really. My friends didn't react well when I confronted them about feeling left out, and things with Jenny are tense.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. Friendships can be complicated, especially when you feel left out. Do you think any of them might be open to another conversation?
seeker: Maybe. I'll have to see. I just wish things would settle down.
supporter: It's understandable to feel that way. It's clear you're dealing with a lot right now. Having someone to talk to each step of the way can make it just a bit easier.
seeker: Yeah. I'm glad I reached out today. It helps to get some perspective.
supporter: Anytime, Andrew. You're doing your best, and that's all anyone can ask right now.
seeker: Thanks for listening. I needed it.
supporter: You're welcome. Take care of yourself and remember to reach out whenever you need to.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-10-20","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

seeker: Not too great, to be honest. Things have been a little rough with my friends.

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hello
supporter: How are you doing today?
seeker: hello
supporter: How can I help you?
seeker: I need ways alleviate stress while studying 
supporter: It sounds like you are having some difficulty at school, I have definitely been there.
seeker: yeah, it can be tough sometimes and feel like you're in a dead end situation
supporter: Yes I worked a dead end job for ages when I was younger and sometimes you just feel stuck
seeker: How did you push past that job?
supporter: I am going to be honest a little luck was involved I managed to impress a customer that came in and ended up applying at their work.
seeker: Are you still with that job now, enough to consider it a career?
supporter: I would say so I am an insurance broker, it has only been a year or so but there seems to be room to move up. You can find something too
seeker: Is there any advice for getting out of my situation?
seeker: aside from luck that is
supporter: Can you give me some more details?
seeker: I just find the work mundane and way too remedial 
supporter: That is completely understandable
seeker: did you look at any websites or other job searching tools before you found your new job?
supporter: I have you a few, there are also many ways to gain skills online that buff up your resume a bit
seeker: what types of skill can I gain online?
supporter: Indeed is one of the better ones to look for jobs, honestly I would suggest looking at jobs that you normally wouldn't and see what kind of qualifications they need and see if you can get that done online.
seeker: so filter based on my absolute needs and go for online skills that I can complete?
supporter: yes I think that is a great idea, look for jobs that meet your needs and figure out what you can do to look attractive to employers
seeker: I have tried glassdoor before, have you had any luck there?
supporter: I used it a bit, I mainly used indeed.
seeker: and have you showcased your skills using LinkedIn before? I have had that one recommended to me before, they said its a great way to neatly organize accomplishments and personal background
supporter: Yes especially if you are applying for anything in a professional setting that is very important.
seeker: do you have any examples of online skills you completed?
supporter: coursera has a lot of great courses, it really depends on what you are looking for.
seeker: if I was looking to enter the engineering field, any recommendations?
supporter: Is that what you are going to school for?
seeker: yes but I may change my mind
supporter: What year are you in? most engineering programs have a practicum and that is a great opportunity to make contacts and potentially get offered a job
seeker: yes I have been networking as I go
supporter: Honestly you seem like you are pretty on top of this I don't think you will have any issues finding a job.
seeker: yeah I mean the topic was about final exam stress but we got on a tangent
supporter: Yes that is fair enough, how much time do you have until your exam?
seeker: 15 minutes
supporter: While that is plenty of time to get some studying done:)
seeker: yes I probably should, thank you for your insight!
supporter: Honestly I find that if you are going for the test right away I always like to just breath and relax a bit.
seeker: yeah no use in cramming for more info when I could just chill out
supporter: You seem like you know what you are doing, I think you will do just fine
seeker: yup thanks","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-06-25","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: How can I help you today?
seeker: I'm disgusted with my professors that they don't see me as a human with real emotions and feelings.
supporter: I understand that you are feeling like your professors don't see you as a person with feelings. What happened to make you feel this way?
seeker: I have testing all the time and study non-stop, but the professors don't seem to encourage or support me.  They just see me as a number I feel.
supporter: That's hard to feel like they are treating you like a number when you are working so hard.  Have you talked to them about it?
seeker: It's hard to trust them when I'm seen as 1 of 100 people.  If I am struggling they don't flinch or ask me how they can assist.  I just am expected to 
seeker: tough it out.
supporter: I had a similar experience in my college days. It was very difficult to have so much pressure to succeed and feel so alone.  You can do though because you are working hard and want to succeed.
seeker: Thanks for the encouragement.  Where do I start to help myself feel better?
supporter: I see you are anxious about this when talking to you, but have you thought about getting some support from other students in your position?
seeker: That sounds like a good idea.  Maybe they are feeling this way too.
supporter: Also sometimes just stepping back and taking some deep breaths can help to alleviate some anxieties. Have you tried that ever?
seeker: I will have to give that a try.  I've done that in the past and had forgotten just how much that helped me before.  
supporter: That is reassuring that it worked before for you and  can work again.
seeker: I'm so worried about failing because I just don't feel the support from my professors to care either way for my successes.  It's so different from high school and home when my parents encouraged me and supported me full-heartedly.  
supporter: College can be quite a change from the protective atmosphere of home.  Have you tried any support groups or religious groups for encouragement?
seeker: I am religious so perhaps I could seek a group out and they could help with encouraging me.  
supporter: I was a  part of a religious group in college and they were very supportive even praying for me on exam days.  I felt they helped me with my success by planting seeds of positive feedback to me.
seeker: I used to be part of one during high school years, and that sounds like it would help.
supporter: Are you starting to feel better about the situation?
seeker: Yes, I do thinking about other people filling in the gaps and supporting me when others won't or can't. Thanks for chatting.  This was helpful.
supporter: You are welcome.  I wish you well.
seeker: I think I have a few tools now to make things better.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-07-15","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hello there! How can I encourage you today?
seeker: Hi, I have been going through a lot of stress with school and am also sad and lonely as of late and not sure how to make myself feel better
supporter: So you have had a lot of stress with school lately and are struggling to keep yourself cheerful?
supporter: Is there something in particular at school that is stressing you out? Exams? Relationships?
seeker: Yes! Its very hard to keep positive with all the work I have and I feel I am not doing well.
seeker: Yes, I have a lot of exams right now and that on top of not hanging out with friends a lot lately has made life tough.
supporter: I can understand being stressed if you think you are not doing well in school and have a lot of work. How are your grades now?
seeker: I still have decent grades but I feel like I am not prepared for big exams currently and they are worth a lot
supporter: Yes, that can be tough. When I had a lot of tests coming up and a lot to study for, I wrote down goals to study -- like I broke down the classes and made certain goals to study a bit in each class. And then if I did that, I could go out with friends or some reward like that. 
supporter: For example, if you have 7 classes, you can make a chart for when you will study for each of those classes and then check them off as you accomplish it, maybe not all in one day, maybe break it up in reasonable bits. Then study according to your goal, if that makes sense.
supporter: I remember after each class, I would take 15 minutes to review all my notes from class, that seems short, but really, it adds up and helped so much.
seeker: Yes, I think you have excellent advice about organization. I feel like I lose track of what I have and when to do it. I also bounce between classes, feeling stressed because there is so much. Do you think doing one class at a time is best?
seeker: I also tend to save stuff sometimes so I have a lot of work build up with tests on the same days. I am not sure how to stop procrastinating.
supporter: Yes, stick to one subject at a time. For example, if you think 1/2 hour is good enough to study, then stick to that. When done, your done until the next time it is on your schedule.
seeker: Ok. Thank you so much for the ideas. It seems like you have had similar experiences with stress from school.
supporter: Procrastination never makes us feel good. If I keep putting something off, I then feel guilty. If I make a goal, and I reach it, I can put a reward. For example, if you study 3 subjects 1/2 hour each, you can go out for yogurt with a friend. So you reward yourself for sticking to that goal.
supporter: Yes, I did. lol I'm really old now. This technique I use in all my life. Even house chores, I break it down into a schedule, put it in writing, then check off what I do. Then I feel good about my accomplishments.
seeker: Yes, that was my other question to you. It sounds great to just do a little time for each class but I often get overwhelmed and need a break
seeker: I have never used check lists or planners. I think it is part of how I get overwhelmed maybe.
supporter: Definitely you need a break, so schedule them as rewards. You can even do 15 minutes in say 4 subjects, then take a walk, take a cup of tea, or call a friend, then back to the books. 
supporter: Keep it as SIMPLE as possible, don't get bogged down. I used to think planning was TERRIBLE< but actually, it sets one FREE. You feel so much better and accomplished when you see how much you have done. It really is amazing. 
supporter: HOw man classes do you have?
supporter: many *
seeker: I have 6 classes
supporter: That's a lot but it is totally doable. Here is a good example, If you plant seeds in a garden today, you have to weed it a bit tomorrow, the next day, the next day, you have to wait for rain, then weed some more, the harvest comes and YAY! You are happy. But if you lie on your bed, never planting, never weeding, you procrastinate, you get nothing.
supporter: If you write your classes down and then write a reasonable time to study each one. Maybe 3 today, 3 tomorrow, then add rewards if you do that, maybe make a list of rewards, so you can pick and choose, then you check off when you do the subject.  Like a chore chart. 
seeker: Yes haha. That is a good comparison. You have been super helpful. I will for sure try to use your advice. Thank you!
seeker: Have a great day and thanks again
supporter: You are quite welcome! God bless have a great day!","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-06-10","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

supporter: Keep it as SIMPLE as possible, don't get bogged down. I used to think planning was TERRIBLE< but actually, it sets one FREE. You feel so much better and accomplished when you see how much you have done. It really is amazing.

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: How can I help you
seeker: hi. my friend told my ex boyfriend he was an idiot for dumping me. it made me feel uncomfortable since i was in the same room. now he is talking to me again. i think he might want me back
supporter: What are your thoughts on the relationship?
seeker: my feelings fluctuate. i resent him that he ended it. it confuses me he still wants to be in my life. he said he wanted to be friends but then asked me out again. i think he is trying to work his way back in. i know i can't keep it up unless he makes it clear he wants to be with me. i don't have time for games
supporter: That does sound hard that he is giving mixed signals.
seeker: yeah i don't like that. neither does my friend. why she told him he is an idiot for letting me go
supporter: Do you think he took your friend's comments seriously?
seeker: yes cuz that's when he wanted me to be around him more
supporter: It sounds like your friend got him thinking.
seeker: it seemed like it did
supporter: Do you feel his change is genuine?
seeker: to a degree. i think he has ulterior motives too. 
supporter: What would he have to do to prove himself?
seeker: say he wants me back or something to that effect. i'd like him to be more direct in what he wants from me
supporter: It sounds like it would help if he were direct with you and not sending mixed signals.  Is that correct?
seeker: yes that would be nice. he tends to beat around the bush then lets me know
supporter: Have you talked to anyone else besides your friend about your concerns?  Do you think your family or other friends could give some additional support to you?
seeker: yes i've talked to them about it. they've given me some insight into it. i know they want me to be careful. they don't want me to be hurt
supporter: That's understandable that they want you to be careful.  My parents and friends watched out for me too.
seeker: we are lucky they look out for us. they can't all be wrong if they're guiding us a certain way
supporter: I think you hit the nail on the head that it's helpful to have that support.
seeker: absolutely. i appreciate your help! nity nite
supporter: Thanks.  Can I assist you with anything else?
seeker: nope. im good
supporter: Have a good night.  ","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-09-12","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hi, How are you?
seeker: I am the youngest of 5 siblings and I feel all most days now because of my parents
supporter: It sounds like you're having a hard time feeling like you have your parents' attention, is that right?
seeker: Not their attention, but more on their expectations on me
supporter: That sounds frustrating, I'm sorry
supporter: Do they do or say anything specific that makes you feel those expectations?
seeker: Yes, its more on comparing me to the children of their friends. They always say why don't I have a better job or even plans on marrying rich. Stuff like that is very frustrating
seeker: They also expect me to take care of them financially soon, I'm just starting my adult life I want to enjoy it
supporter: That sounds very frustrating. I think if I felt those kind of expectations I would be anxious.
supporter: Do you feel comfortable talking to them about your feelings?
seeker: I do feel anxious every time. 
seeker: I tried a couple of times, but my mom always sees it as being too sensitive
supporter: Sometimes it can feel impossible to talk to parents
seeker: I know, is it better if I stay away for awhile? since taking to them won't make sense?
supporter: I think that it can be very healthy to get some distance, but I think it can also feel difficult -- do you have good friends in your life that you could lean on if you needed some distance from your parents?
seeker: Yes, I do. They actually helped me coped up. I always think that I wasn't blessed with my family, but I'm blessed with good friends
supporter: Good friends can be a huge comfort and it sounds like you're a good friends yourself if you have those kinds of friendships
seeker: Thinking about it, they really did help a lot. So I should really distance myself for a while right?
supporter: I think if making distance helps you feel better, you deserve and have a right to that space
seeker: Yes, thank you. I really need to that. 
supporter: You're welcome
supporter: It sounds like you are making healthy and careful emotional decisions 
supporter: Is there anything else you want to discuss about your parents?","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-09-01","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hey Taylor, it's good to see you here. How are you holding up these days?
seeker: Hey. I'm managing, I guess. Just trying to keep up with everything.
supporter: I hear you. With school and everything else on your plate, it must be a lot. Anything in particular that's been weighing on you?
seeker: Yeah, it's mostly about Nate, my ex. We had a big argument and things have been weird since then.
supporter: I'm really sorry to hear that. It sounds tough to go through a fallout with someone who used to mean a lot to you.
seeker: Yeah, it really sucks. I thought we were on the same page about things, but that argument just brought up a lot of unresolved issues.
supporter: Conflicts like that can be really revealing, but also painful. Do you feel comfortable sharing what the argument was about?
seeker: Sure. It started off as a small disagreement about our future plans, but it escalated quickly.
supporter: It's amazing how sometimes the smallest things become a big deal. Do you think it was more about the future or something else underlying it?
seeker: I think it was a bit of both. We've had different ideas about our futures for a while, and maybe we were ignoring it until now.
supporter: That makes sense. It's hard to navigate differences when you're emotionally invested. How does that make you feel now?
seeker: Honestly, it's exhausting. I keep playing the argument over and over in my head, trying to make sense of it.
supporter: I can imagine how tiring that must be. Sometimes our minds just want to find an answer, even when one isn't clear-cut.
seeker: Exactly. It's like I'm looking for signs of who was right or wrong, but I end up just feeling more tangled.
supporter: Maybe it's not about right or wrong but about understanding where each of you is coming from. What do you hope to achieve by unraveling these feelings?
seeker: I'd just like to find some peace with it, I guess. Maybe closure or even a chance to talk about it calmly.
supporter: Closure sounds like a healthy goal. Giving yourself time to process everything is important, though. Do you feel like there's space to have that calm conversation with Nate?
seeker: Part of me hopes so, but I'm not sure if either of us is ready yet. There's still a lot of raw emotions.
supporter: Emotions can take time to settle. It's okay to wait until it feels right. Meanwhile, how are you taking care of yourself?
seeker: I've been writing a lot, which helps. It's been a good outlet, even if it's just jotting down how I feel.
supporter: Writing can be really therapeutic, I agree. You have a wonderful gift for expressing your emotions through words.
seeker: Thank you for saying that. It makes me feel less alone in all of this.
supporter: You're definitely not alone, Taylor. I'm always here to listen whenever you need.
seeker: I appreciate it. It means a lot to have someone to talk to who gets it.
supporter: Anytime. Take your time with everything and remember to be kind to yourself.
seeker: I'll try to keep that in mind. Thank you for being here for me.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-10-05","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hi Taylor! How have you been lately?
seeker: Hey, I've been feeling a lot of things lately. It's been a bit overwhelming.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. Do you want to talk about what's been going on?
seeker: Yeah, I had a session with my therapist recently. We talked a lot about my self-worth.
supporter: That sounds like an important conversation. What came up for you during the session?
seeker: We talked about how I've been weighing my worth based on my academic and creative successes. It was eye-opening.
supporter: It's tough when our value feels tied to achievements. How did you feel after the session?
seeker: Honestly, I felt both relieved and a bit anxious. Relieved to recognize it but anxious about how to change it.
supporter: Change can be challenging, but recognizing the issue is a great first step. How have things been at university?
seeker: University's been okay. The workload is a lot, and I still struggle with feeling like I'm not doing enough.
supporter: That makes sense, especially with everything you have on your plate. How's your creative writing going?
seeker: It's been up and down. I joined a writing workshop that helped, but the imposter syndrome creeps in.
supporter: I'm glad the workshop helped. The feeling of not being enough can be so persistent. You're not alone in that.
seeker: Thanks. It helps to know I'm not alone. The online community has been supportive too.
supporter: That's great to hear! Sometimes finding a supportive community can make a big difference.
seeker: Definitely! They remind me that it's okay to struggle and that growth takes time.
supporter: Absolutely! You're on a journey, and it's perfectly okay to have ups and downs along the way.
seeker: I truly appreciate you listening and being here for me. It means a lot.
supporter: Anytime, Taylor. You're doing amazing things, and I'm here whenever you need to talk.
seeker: Thank you. I'll try to take things one step at a time. Catch up soon?
supporter: Definitely! Take care and reach out whenever you feel like it.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-12-10","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}
