MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hey there, is it okay to talk? I'm just feeling a bit overwhelmed with emotions right now.
supporter: Of course, Taylor. I'm here for you. What's been going on lately?
seeker: It's Nate, my ex. He reached out to apologize recently, and it's stirred up a lot of old memories and feelings.
supporter: I can imagine that must be really tough. How did it feel when he reached out to you?
seeker: Confusing, honestly. Part of me was glad he apologized, but another part isn't sure if I can trust his intentions.
supporter: That's completely valid. Trust can be hard to rebuild, especially after everything you've been through.
seeker: Exactly. I keep thinking about our past arguments and how they made me feel. It's all just resurfacing now.
supporter: It sounds like those memories are really triggering some deep emotions. How are you handling them right now?
seeker: Not too well, if I'm honest. I'm finding it hard to focus on my studies and my writing, and this time of year is already stressful.
supporter: It's completely understandable. Between the pressure from studies and your relationship history, it sounds like you're dealing with a lot.
seeker: It feels like too much sometimes, especially after failing a mid-term recently. My self-worth is really taking a hit.
supporter: I'm really sorry you're feeling this way, Taylor. Remember, one exam doesn't define your abilities or worth. You've achieved so much already.
seeker: Thanks for saying that. My therapist did mention the importance of focusing on self-worth, but it’s hard to internalize it sometimes.
supporter: It’s a process, and it’s okay to have days where it feels more challenging. Have you tried any of the strategies your therapist suggested?
seeker: I've been trying to focus on my writing and stay active in the online community I found. It helps to some extent.
supporter: That’s a great outlet for your emotions. Writing can be such a powerful way to process your thoughts and experiences.
seeker: Yeah, it's one of the few things that helps me clear my mind. But the writer's block is still a bit persistent.
supporter: Writer's block can be really frustrating, especially when you're already feeling overwhelmed. Is there anything specific about writing that's been challenging?
seeker: It's like I'm second-guessing everything I put down on paper, feeling like it’s not good enough compared to my peers.
supporter: Imposter syndrome is really tough to deal with. Just remember, your voice is unique and valuable in its own right.
seeker: Thanks for reminding me. I often forget that when I'm deep in self-doubt. It means a lot to have your support.
supporter: I'm always here for you, Taylor. Make sure to be kind to yourself and take things one day at a time. You're doing your best.
seeker: Thanks. I really needed to hear that. I’ll try to focus on what's within my control and take small steps forward.
supporter: That's a great approach. You're stronger than you realize, and I'm proud of you for reaching out and talking this through.
seeker: I appreciate it. It feels good to get everything off my chest and know I'm not facing this alone.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-12-18","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

supporter: I hear you. With school and everything else on your plate, it must be a lot. Anything in particular that's been weighing on you?
seeker: Yeah, it's mostly about Nate, my ex. We had a big argument and things have been weird since then.
supporter: I'm really sorry to hear that. It sounds tough to go through a fallout with someone who used to mean a lot to you.
seeker: Yeah, it really sucks. I thought we were on the same page about things, but that argument just brought up a lot of unresolved issues.
supporter: Conflicts like that can be really revealing, but also painful. Do you feel comfortable sharing what the argument was about?
seeker: Sure. It started off as a small disagreement about our future plans, but it escalated quickly.
supporter: It's amazing how sometimes the smallest things become a big deal. Do you think it was more about the future or something else underlying it?
seeker: I think it was a bit of both. We've had different ideas about our futures for a while, and maybe we were ignoring it until now.
supporter: That makes sense. It's hard to navigate differences when you're emotionally invested. How does that make you feel now?
seeker: Honestly, it's exhausting. I keep playing the argument over and over in my head, trying to make sense of it.
supporter: I can imagine how tiring that must be. Sometimes our minds just want to find an answer, even when one isn't clear-cut.
seeker: Exactly. It's like I'm looking for signs of who was right or wrong, but I end up just feeling more tangled.
supporter: Maybe it's not about right or wrong but about understanding where each of you is coming from. What do you hope to achieve by unraveling these feelings?

supporter: Emotions can take time to settle. It's okay to wait until it feels right. Meanwhile, how are you taking care of yourself?

seeker: Thank you for saying that. It makes me feel less alone in all of this.

seeker: I appreciate it. It means a lot to have someone to talk to who gets it.

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hello. I wanted to talk about my academic pressures.
supporter: Hi there. What academic pressures are troubling you today?

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: hi there! how are you feeling today?
seeker: i feel depressed
supporter: i'm sorry to hear that. is there a specific reason you are having these feelings?
seeker: i feel alone. i feel like i do not have anyone to talk to when it comes to my emotions.
supporter: I understand. I have been feeling quite lonely too, I find myself feeling lonely at work and struggling to find someone I trust to talk to about these emotions. Do you have a friend or family member that you trust who might understand some of these feelings?
seeker: i do have a few friends that i think i can talk to about how i am feeling however the thought of them being too busy with their work is what prevents me from reaching out to them. 
supporter: I understand. Correct me if i'm wrong, it sounds like you're nervous to open up to these trusted people because you think they might be distracted by their work to provide the empathy you need and fully understand how you are feeling. Does that sound right?
seeker: you know i think that you are right about this. it has always been difficult for me to open to others even with those that have been there for me when i needed someone. i feel like a mix of emotions nervous but at the same time wanting to reaching out for help
supporter: I understand these feelings very well. Sometimes, my fear overshadows my want for help. I find it easier to open up to others through writing rather than face to face. Have you considered putting your feelings in writing and opening up to trusted friends and family in this way?
seeker: i have been writing for a while but due to my emotions i have stopped writing like i used to. when i did write i did notice a change in my feelings it became more positive and less depressed. now that i stopped writing its like i went back into depression 
supporter: It sounds like writing your feelings down helped you greatly in the past. May I suggest going back to writing and even letting someone you trust read what you have written down to understand how you are feeling?
seeker: yes, writing has been a huge help for me. I would take your suggestion and begin writing again to feel better. and i have let others read what i wrote and they have said it has helped them get over their depression and helped them understand me more
supporter: That's great! I am glad to hear that you will begin writing again. Thank you for opening up to me about your feelings. How do you feel about the solution we have come to today?
seeker: now that i was able to talk about how i feel with you and you giving me a useful suggestion i feel less depressed and feel motivated to write again. your help has been really helpful for me 
supporter: That's wonderful! I appreciate your honesty about how you are feeling. I am proud of you for seeking help. Is there anything else you would like to discuss?
seeker: thank you so much for helping me. and that is all that i would like to discuss. you have been a big help for me 
supporter: I am glad I could be here for you! I am hoping you continue to feel better and your writing helps to work out these feelings.  Thank you so much for being open with me. I hope you have a fantastic rest of your day! :)
seeker: thank you. hope you enjoy your day","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-07-25","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: How can I help you
seeker: hi. my friend told my ex boyfriend he was an idiot for dumping me. it made me feel uncomfortable since i was in the same room. now he is talking to me again. i think he might want me back
supporter: What are your thoughts on the relationship?
seeker: my feelings fluctuate. i resent him that he ended it. it confuses me he still wants to be in my life. he said he wanted to be friends but then asked me out again. i think he is trying to work his way back in. i know i can't keep it up unless he makes it clear he wants to be with me. i don't have time for games
supporter: That does sound hard that he is giving mixed signals.
seeker: yeah i don't like that. neither does my friend. why she told him he is an idiot for letting me go
supporter: Do you think he took your friend's comments seriously?
seeker: yes cuz that's when he wanted me to be around him more
supporter: It sounds like your friend got him thinking.
seeker: it seemed like it did
supporter: Do you feel his change is genuine?
seeker: to a degree. i think he has ulterior motives too. 
supporter: What would he have to do to prove himself?
seeker: say he wants me back or something to that effect. i'd like him to be more direct in what he wants from me
supporter: It sounds like it would help if he were direct with you and not sending mixed signals.  Is that correct?
seeker: yes that would be nice. he tends to beat around the bush then lets me know
supporter: Have you talked to anyone else besides your friend about your concerns?  Do you think your family or other friends could give some additional support to you?
seeker: yes i've talked to them about it. they've given me some insight into it. i know they want me to be careful. they don't want me to be hurt
supporter: That's understandable that they want you to be careful.  My parents and friends watched out for me too.
seeker: we are lucky they look out for us. they can't all be wrong if they're guiding us a certain way
supporter: I think you hit the nail on the head that it's helpful to have that support.
seeker: absolutely. i appreciate your help! nity nite
supporter: Thanks.  Can I assist you with anything else?
seeker: nope. im good
supporter: Have a good night.  ","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-09-12","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hi, How are you?
seeker: I am the youngest of 5 siblings and I feel all most days now because of my parents
supporter: It sounds like you're having a hard time feeling like you have your parents' attention, is that right?
seeker: Not their attention, but more on their expectations on me
supporter: That sounds frustrating, I'm sorry
supporter: Do they do or say anything specific that makes you feel those expectations?
seeker: Yes, its more on comparing me to the children of their friends. They always say why don't I have a better job or even plans on marrying rich. Stuff like that is very frustrating
seeker: They also expect me to take care of them financially soon, I'm just starting my adult life I want to enjoy it
supporter: That sounds very frustrating. I think if I felt those kind of expectations I would be anxious.
supporter: Do you feel comfortable talking to them about your feelings?
seeker: I do feel anxious every time. 
seeker: I tried a couple of times, but my mom always sees it as being too sensitive
supporter: Sometimes it can feel impossible to talk to parents
seeker: I know, is it better if I stay away for awhile? since taking to them won't make sense?

supporter: Good friends can be a huge comfort and it sounds like you're a good friends yourself if you have those kinds of friendships
seeker: Thinking about it, they really did help a lot. So I should really distance myself for a while right?
supporter: I think if making distance helps you feel better, you deserve and have a right to that space
seeker: Yes, thank you. I really need to that. 
supporter: You're welcome
supporter: It sounds like you are making healthy and careful emotional decisions 
supporter: Is there anything else you want to discuss about your parents?","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-09-01","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hi, How are you?
seeker: I am the youngest of 5 siblings and I feel all most days now because of my parents
supporter: It sounds like you're having a hard time feeling like you have your parents' attention, is that right?
seeker: Not their attention, but more on their expectations on me
supporter: That sounds frustrating, I'm sorry
supporter: Do they do or say anything specific that makes you feel those expectations?
seeker: Yes, its more on comparing me to the children of their friends. They always say why don't I have a better job or even plans on marrying rich. Stuff like that is very frustrating
seeker: They also expect me to take care of them financially soon, I'm just starting my adult life I want to enjoy it
supporter: That sounds very frustrating. I think if I felt those kind of expectations I would be anxious.
supporter: Do you feel comfortable talking to them about your feelings?
seeker: I do feel anxious every time. 
seeker: I tried a couple of times, but my mom always sees it as being too sensitive
supporter: Sometimes it can feel impossible to talk to parents
seeker: I know, is it better if I stay away for awhile? since taking to them won't make sense?
supporter: I think that it can be very healthy to get some distance, but I think it can also feel difficult -- do you have good friends in your life that you could lean on if you needed some distance from your parents?
seeker: Yes, I do. They actually helped me coped up. I always think that I wasn't blessed with my family, but I'm blessed with good friends
supporter: Good friends can be a huge comfort and it sounds like you're a good friends yourself if you have those kinds of friendships
seeker: Thinking about it, they really did help a lot. So I should really distance myself for a while right?
supporter: I think if making distance helps you feel better, you deserve and have a right to that space
seeker: Yes, thank you. I really need to that. 
supporter: You're welcome
supporter: It sounds like you are making healthy and careful emotional decisions 
supporter: Is there anything else you want to discuss about your parents?","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-09-01","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hey Taylor, how are you holding up this week?
seeker: Hi. It's been a rough one honestly. I feel kind of isolated and anxious.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. Exam weeks can be really tough, especially with everything else going on.
seeker: Yeah, that's putting it lightly. I can't shake this feeling of being overwhelmed. It's like everything's happening at once.
supporter: That sounds incredibly stressful. Do you want to talk about what's been weighing you down the most?
seeker: I guess it's a mix of things. I've been feeling distracted ever since the thing with my ex and then failing the mid-term.
supporter: Those are both really big things. It makes sense that they'd still be affecting you.
seeker: I know, but I feel like I should be able to handle it better. I mean, other people seem to.
supporter: Everyone deals with pressure differently, and it's okay to feel like you're struggling. You're handling a lot.

supporter: Your feelings are valid. You're really talented, but sometimes anxiety can make you doubt what you're capable of.
seeker: It's just hard to remember that when I feel so stuck. And isolation during exam week hasn't helped.
supporter: Being isolated can definitely amplify those feelings. Do you have anyone you could reach out to for support?
seeker: I guess I could talk to some classmates. We've been good study buddies in the past.
supporter: That sounds like a great idea. Having a support system can make a huge difference.
seeker: I'll try reaching out. I just hope I can keep it together for the rest of the exams.
supporter: Taking one day at a time might help. I'm here whenever you need to talk though, okay?
seeker: I appreciate that, a lot. I didn't realize how much I needed to vent until now.
supporter: I'm glad you reached out. You're doing your best, and that's something to be proud of.

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: hi there! how are you feeling today?
seeker: i feel depressed
supporter: i'm sorry to hear that. is there a specific reason you are having these feelings?
seeker: i feel alone. i feel like i do not have anyone to talk to when it comes to my emotions.
supporter: I understand. I have been feeling quite lonely too, I find myself feeling lonely at work and struggling to find someone I trust to talk to about these emotions. Do you have a friend or family member that you trust who might understand some of these feelings?
seeker: i do have a few friends that i think i can talk to about how i am feeling however the thought of them being too busy with their work is what prevents me from reaching out to them. 
supporter: I understand. Correct me if i'm wrong, it sounds like you're nervous to open up to these trusted people because you think they might be distracted by their work to provide the empathy you need and fully understand how you are feeling. Does that sound right?
seeker: you know i think that you are right about this. it has always been difficult for me to open to others even with those that have been there for me when i needed someone. i feel like a mix of emotions nervous but at the same time wanting to reaching out for help
supporter: I understand these feelings very well. Sometimes, my fear overshadows my want for help. I find it easier to open up to others through writing rather than face to face. Have you considered putting your feelings in writing and opening up to trusted friends and family in this way?
seeker: i have been writing for a while but due to my emotions i have stopped writing like i used to. when i did write i did notice a change in my feelings it became more positive and less depressed. now that i stopped writing its like i went back into depression 
supporter: It sounds like writing your feelings down helped you greatly in the past. May I suggest going back to writing and even letting someone you trust read what you have written down to understand how you are feeling?
seeker: yes, writing has been a huge help for me. I would take your suggestion and begin writing again to feel better. and i have let others read what i wrote and they have said it has helped them get over their depression and helped them understand me more
supporter: That's great! I am glad to hear that you will begin writing again. Thank you for opening up to me about your feelings. How do you feel about the solution we have come to today?
seeker: now that i was able to talk about how i feel with you and you giving me a useful suggestion i feel less depressed and feel motivated to write again. your help has been really helpful for me 
supporter: That's wonderful! I appreciate your honesty about how you are feeling. I am proud of you for seeking help. Is there anything else you would like to discuss?
seeker: thank you so much for helping me. and that is all that i would like to discuss. you have been a big help for me 
supporter: I am glad I could be here for you! I am hoping you continue to feel better and your writing helps to work out these feelings.  Thank you so much for being open with me. I hope you have a fantastic rest of your day! :)
seeker: thank you. hope you enjoy your day","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-07-25","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: How can I help you
seeker: hi. my friend told my ex boyfriend he was an idiot for dumping me. it made me feel uncomfortable since i was in the same room. now he is talking to me again. i think he might want me back
supporter: What are your thoughts on the relationship?
seeker: my feelings fluctuate. i resent him that he ended it. it confuses me he still wants to be in my life. he said he wanted to be friends but then asked me out again. i think he is trying to work his way back in. i know i can't keep it up unless he makes it clear he wants to be with me. i don't have time for games
supporter: That does sound hard that he is giving mixed signals.
seeker: yeah i don't like that. neither does my friend. why she told him he is an idiot for letting me go
supporter: Do you think he took your friend's comments seriously?
seeker: yes cuz that's when he wanted me to be around him more
supporter: It sounds like your friend got him thinking.
seeker: it seemed like it did
supporter: Do you feel his change is genuine?
seeker: to a degree. i think he has ulterior motives too. 
supporter: What would he have to do to prove himself?
seeker: say he wants me back or something to that effect. i'd like him to be more direct in what he wants from me
supporter: It sounds like it would help if he were direct with you and not sending mixed signals.  Is that correct?
seeker: yes that would be nice. he tends to beat around the bush then lets me know
supporter: Have you talked to anyone else besides your friend about your concerns?  Do you think your family or other friends could give some additional support to you?
seeker: yes i've talked to them about it. they've given me some insight into it. i know they want me to be careful. they don't want me to be hurt
supporter: That's understandable that they want you to be careful.  My parents and friends watched out for me too.
seeker: we are lucky they look out for us. they can't all be wrong if they're guiding us a certain way
supporter: I think you hit the nail on the head that it's helpful to have that support.
seeker: absolutely. i appreciate your help! nity nite
supporter: Thanks.  Can I assist you with anything else?
seeker: nope. im good
supporter: Have a good night.  ","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-09-12","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

supporter: I hear you. With school and everything else on your plate, it must be a lot. Anything in particular that's been weighing on you?
seeker: Yeah, it's mostly about Nate, my ex. We had a big argument and things have been weird since then.
supporter: I'm really sorry to hear that. It sounds tough to go through a fallout with someone who used to mean a lot to you.
seeker: Yeah, it really sucks. I thought we were on the same page about things, but that argument just brought up a lot of unresolved issues.
supporter: Conflicts like that can be really revealing, but also painful. Do you feel comfortable sharing what the argument was about?
seeker: Sure. It started off as a small disagreement about our future plans, but it escalated quickly.
supporter: It's amazing how sometimes the smallest things become a big deal. Do you think it was more about the future or something else underlying it?
seeker: I think it was a bit of both. We've had different ideas about our futures for a while, and maybe we were ignoring it until now.
supporter: That makes sense. It's hard to navigate differences when you're emotionally invested. How does that make you feel now?
seeker: Honestly, it's exhausting. I keep playing the argument over and over in my head, trying to make sense of it.
supporter: I can imagine how tiring that must be. Sometimes our minds just want to find an answer, even when one isn't clear-cut.
seeker: Exactly. It's like I'm looking for signs of who was right or wrong, but I end up just feeling more tangled.
supporter: Maybe it's not about right or wrong but about understanding where each of you is coming from. What do you hope to achieve by unraveling these feelings?

supporter: Closure sounds like a healthy goal. Giving yourself time to process everything is important, though. Do you feel like there's space to have that calm conversation with Nate?
seeker: Part of me hopes so, but I'm not sure if either of us is ready yet. There's still a lot of raw emotions.
supporter: Emotions can take time to settle. It's okay to wait until it feels right. Meanwhile, how are you taking care of yourself?
seeker: I've been writing a lot, which helps. It's been a good outlet, even if it's just jotting down how I feel.
supporter: Writing can be really therapeutic, I agree. You have a wonderful gift for expressing your emotions through words.
seeker: Thank you for saying that. It makes me feel less alone in all of this.

seeker: I appreciate it. It means a lot to have someone to talk to who gets it.

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hi Taylor! How have you been lately?
seeker: Hey, I've been feeling a lot of things lately. It's been a bit overwhelming.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. Do you want to talk about what's been going on?
seeker: Yeah, I had a session with my therapist recently. We talked a lot about my self-worth.
supporter: That sounds like an important conversation. What came up for you during the session?
seeker: We talked about how I've been weighing my worth based on my academic and creative successes. It was eye-opening.
supporter: It's tough when our value feels tied to achievements. How did you feel after the session?
seeker: Honestly, I felt both relieved and a bit anxious. Relieved to recognize it but anxious about how to change it.
supporter: Change can be challenging, but recognizing the issue is a great first step. How have things been at university?
seeker: University's been okay. The workload is a lot, and I still struggle with feeling like I'm not doing enough.
supporter: That makes sense, especially with everything you have on your plate. How's your creative writing going?
seeker: It's been up and down. I joined a writing workshop that helped, but the imposter syndrome creeps in.
supporter: I'm glad the workshop helped. The feeling of not being enough can be so persistent. You're not alone in that.
seeker: Thanks. It helps to know I'm not alone. The online community has been supportive too.
supporter: That's great to hear! Sometimes finding a supportive community can make a big difference.
seeker: Definitely! They remind me that it's okay to struggle and that growth takes time.
supporter: Absolutely! You're on a journey, and it's perfectly okay to have ups and downs along the way.
seeker: I truly appreciate you listening and being here for me. It means a lot.
supporter: Anytime, Taylor. You're doing amazing things, and I'm here whenever you need to talk.
seeker: Thank you. I'll try to take things one step at a time. Catch up soon?
supporter: Definitely! Take care and reach out whenever you feel like it.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-12-10","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hey there, is it okay to talk? I'm just feeling a bit overwhelmed with emotions right now.
supporter: Of course, Taylor. I'm here for you. What's been going on lately?
seeker: It's Nate, my ex. He reached out to apologize recently, and it's stirred up a lot of old memories and feelings.
supporter: I can imagine that must be really tough. How did it feel when he reached out to you?
seeker: Confusing, honestly. Part of me was glad he apologized, but another part isn't sure if I can trust his intentions.
supporter: That's completely valid. Trust can be hard to rebuild, especially after everything you've been through.
seeker: Exactly. I keep thinking about our past arguments and how they made me feel. It's all just resurfacing now.
supporter: It sounds like those memories are really triggering some deep emotions. How are you handling them right now?
seeker: Not too well, if I'm honest. I'm finding it hard to focus on my studies and my writing, and this time of year is already stressful.
supporter: It's completely understandable. Between the pressure from studies and your relationship history, it sounds like you're dealing with a lot.
seeker: It feels like too much sometimes, especially after failing a mid-term recently. My self-worth is really taking a hit.
supporter: I'm really sorry you're feeling this way, Taylor. Remember, one exam doesn't define your abilities or worth. You've achieved so much already.
seeker: Thanks for saying that. My therapist did mention the importance of focusing on self-worth, but it’s hard to internalize it sometimes.
supporter: It’s a process, and it’s okay to have days where it feels more challenging. Have you tried any of the strategies your therapist suggested?
seeker: I've been trying to focus on my writing and stay active in the online community I found. It helps to some extent.
supporter: That’s a great outlet for your emotions. Writing can be such a powerful way to process your thoughts and experiences.
seeker: Yeah, it's one of the few things that helps me clear my mind. But the writer's block is still a bit persistent.
supporter: Writer's block can be really frustrating, especially when you're already feeling overwhelmed. Is there anything specific about writing that's been challenging?
seeker: It's like I'm second-guessing everything I put down on paper, feeling like it’s not good enough compared to my peers.
supporter: Imposter syndrome is really tough to deal with. Just remember, your voice is unique and valuable in its own right.
seeker: Thanks for reminding me. I often forget that when I'm deep in self-doubt. It means a lot to have your support.
supporter: I'm always here for you, Taylor. Make sure to be kind to yourself and take things one day at a time. You're doing your best.
seeker: Thanks. I really needed to hear that. I’ll try to focus on what's within my control and take small steps forward.
supporter: That's a great approach. You're stronger than you realize, and I'm proud of you for reaching out and talking this through.
seeker: I appreciate it. It feels good to get everything off my chest and know I'm not facing this alone.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-12-18","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hey, are you online? I really need someone to talk to right now.
supporter: Hey Taylor, I'm here. What's going on?
seeker: I had a panic attack today, just before a social event. It was terrifying.
supporter: I'm so sorry to hear that. Panic attacks can be really overwhelming. Do you want to share more about what happened?
seeker: I was supposed to go to this gathering with some classmates, and out of nowhere, I just felt completely frozen.
supporter: That sounds incredibly tough. It makes sense you might feel that way given everything you've been dealing with lately. How are you feeling now?
seeker: A bit better, but still shaky. I keep thinking about all the stress from before—school, my ex, even stuff at home. It all feels like too much at times.
supporter: You’ve been through a lot recently, so it’s understandable you're feeling overwhelmed. It’s good that you’re reaching out and acknowledging what you’re experiencing.
seeker: Thanks. I thought I was doing better with the writing workshop and finding that online community, but days like this hit hard.
supporter: Those were really positive steps forward, and they still are. It’s okay to have setbacks. They don’t define you or erase your progress.
seeker: I guess I just feel like I'm falling behind everyone else. The imposter syndrome keeps creeping in, especially when I see peers succeeding.
supporter: Those feelings are difficult, but remember that you're not alone in experiencing them. You've achieved so much already, and you deserve to be proud of your journey.
seeker: I know, it's just hard to see sometimes. My therapist said something about self-worth the other day, but I'm struggling to internalize it.
supporter: That’s a common struggle. Maybe try to focus on one small thing you like or are proud of about yourself each day. It can slowly shift your perspective over time.
seeker: That's a good idea. I’ll try to start doing that. I think just talking about it now is helping a bit.
supporter: I'm really glad to hear that. Remember, it’s okay to have hard days. Just keep reaching out and taking things one step at a time.
seeker: Thanks for being here. I was feeling really alone after today.
supporter: You’re never alone in this. I’m here anytime you need to talk. We can get through this together.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-01-05","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

seeker: Honestly, not great. I found out that my grade slipped again even after I reattempted the exam.

seeker: Yeah, it's pretty crushing. I thought that notifying my professor and putting in the extra work would help, but apparently not.
supporter: It sounds like you’ve been trying really hard to make things right. It must feel discouraging to not see the progress you were expecting.
seeker: Exactly. It's like nothing I do is ever enough. And it doesn't help that I still feel this disconnect with my professor after everything.
supporter: That can be incredibly tough, especially when the relationship with your professor is strained. Do you think it might be worth discussing your feelings with them?
seeker: I've thought about it, but it's intimidating. What if they don’t take me seriously or think I’m just making excuses?
supporter: It's understandable to feel that way. However, sharing your concerns could potentially help rebuild that trust and understanding between you both.
seeker: I guess you're right. I did have a good talk with my therapist about self-worth, and maybe I should try to use those insights to approach this situation.
supporter: That sounds like a strong plan. You've already taken steps to understand yourself better, and using that knowledge could really help in this case.
seeker: I hope so. It’s just hard not to feel like an imposter when I see my peers succeeding so easily.
supporter: Imposter syndrome can be really tough to battle. Remember, everyone's journey is different, and your progress is valuable too.
seeker: Thank you for saying that. It's just been difficult to see my own value lately, especially with everything else piling up.
supporter: It definitely sounds like a lot is on your plate right now. Just know that it's okay to feel overwhelmed, and that you're doing your best.
seeker: I appreciate you reminding me of that. Things have felt really heavy since the argument with my ex and all these academic pressures.
supporter: You’ve been through so much. It’s important to give yourself credit for handling these challenges. How have you been managing?

supporter: Writing can be a powerful outlet. It’s great that you’re turning to creativity as a way of processing your emotions.
seeker: Yeah, it's been a lifeline, honestly. That, and the supportive online community I found for writers.

seeker: It's just hard. I used to be so confident about my writing and studies, and now I doubt everything.

seeker: I hope so. I miss feeling assured about my choices.

seeker: I might do that. Maybe write something just for myself, not for a grade.

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hey Taylor! How have you been?
seeker: Hey. I've been feeling a bit overwhelmed lately.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. Do you want to talk about it?
seeker: Yeah... I've been struggling with imposter syndrome. It's been on my mind a lot.
supporter: That sounds tough. What triggered these feelings for you?

supporter: Seeing others succeed can definitely stir up those feelings. It's natural, but it doesn't mean you're any less capable.

supporter: Progress can be small and still meaningful. You've taken steps before, like joining that creative writing workshop. That shows dedication.

supporter: Exactly, and you can overcome this too. Have you considered reaching out to someone in the workshop for support?
seeker: Not really, but maybe I should. It might be good to connect with someone who's going through similar things.
supporter: That sounds like a great idea! Having someone to share experiences with can really help with those feelings of imposter syndrome.

supporter: Anytime, Taylor. I'm always here to listen and support you. Remember, you're not alone in this.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-11-25","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

turns.content: Hey Taylor, I've been thinking about you. How are you holding up today?
Hey... It's been a rough day. I found out my close friend was hospitalized, and it just feels like too much right now.
I'm so sorry to hear about your friend. That must be really hard to process. Do you want to talk more about it?
Yeah, it's just...she've always been there for me, especially through the whole thing with my ex and when I was struggling at school. It feels surreal not being able to support her now.
It sounds like they mean a lot to you, and not being able to be there for her must be really tough. It’s understandable to feel overwhelmed.
Exactly. And it's like all these emotions from the past are surfacing again - the argument with my parents, the panic attacks, the trust issues with my professor. Everything seems to be piling up.
It’s okay to have all these emotions. You've been through a lot recently. How are you managing to cope with everything?
Well, I'm trying to stick to some of the things my therapist suggested, like journaling and mindfulness exercises, but sometimes it feels like I’m just going through the motions.
Journaling and mindfulness can be great tools, but it’s also okay to not have it all figured out right now. Are there moments where you feel a bit more at ease?
Maybe when I'm writing, or when I'm engaging with the online writing community. I get what it feels like to be overwhelmed creatively and emotionally.
That's wonderful to hear. It’s important to have spaces where you feel understood and supported. What’s been inspiring your writing lately?
I haven’t been writing as much because of the writer's block, but the supportive messages from the community have been motivating me to start again, even if it's just jotting down ideas.
It sounds like you're slowly finding your way back to your passion, which is amazing. Give yourself time and space; creativity can be a healing process too.
True. I guess I just need to be kinder to myself. It’s just hard when everything feels so uncertain and unstable.

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hello. I wanted to talk about my academic pressures.
supporter: Hi there. What academic pressures are troubling you today?
seeker: Just lots of classes and expectations. Especially with group projects.

seeker: Yep. 
seeker: What should I do to relax my mind?

seeker: With friends, most are busy with their own struggles and I don't want to be bothering them as much
supporter: I see, it sounds like you are dealing with your academic pressures all on your own right now then?

supporter: Is there possibly a school councilor you could seek advice from?

supporter: I hear you, it's definitely not for everyone.

seeker: It really helps to get this off my chest

seeker: Thanks for the conversation!

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: hi there! how are you feeling today?
seeker: i feel depressed
supporter: i'm sorry to hear that. is there a specific reason you are having these feelings?
seeker: i feel alone. i feel like i do not have anyone to talk to when it comes to my emotions.
supporter: I understand. I have been feeling quite lonely too, I find myself feeling lonely at work and struggling to find someone I trust to talk to about these emotions. Do you have a friend or family member that you trust who might understand some of these feelings?
seeker: i do have a few friends that i think i can talk to about how i am feeling however the thought of them being too busy with their work is what prevents me from reaching out to them. 
supporter: I understand. Correct me if i'm wrong, it sounds like you're nervous to open up to these trusted people because you think they might be distracted by their work to provide the empathy you need and fully understand how you are feeling. Does that sound right?
seeker: you know i think that you are right about this. it has always been difficult for me to open to others even with those that have been there for me when i needed someone. i feel like a mix of emotions nervous but at the same time wanting to reaching out for help
supporter: I understand these feelings very well. Sometimes, my fear overshadows my want for help. I find it easier to open up to others through writing rather than face to face. Have you considered putting your feelings in writing and opening up to trusted friends and family in this way?
seeker: i have been writing for a while but due to my emotions i have stopped writing like i used to. when i did write i did notice a change in my feelings it became more positive and less depressed. now that i stopped writing its like i went back into depression 
supporter: It sounds like writing your feelings down helped you greatly in the past. May I suggest going back to writing and even letting someone you trust read what you have written down to understand how you are feeling?
seeker: yes, writing has been a huge help for me. I would take your suggestion and begin writing again to feel better. and i have let others read what i wrote and they have said it has helped them get over their depression and helped them understand me more
supporter: That's great! I am glad to hear that you will begin writing again. Thank you for opening up to me about your feelings. How do you feel about the solution we have come to today?
seeker: now that i was able to talk about how i feel with you and you giving me a useful suggestion i feel less depressed and feel motivated to write again. your help has been really helpful for me 
supporter: That's wonderful! I appreciate your honesty about how you are feeling. I am proud of you for seeking help. Is there anything else you would like to discuss?
seeker: thank you so much for helping me. and that is all that i would like to discuss. you have been a big help for me 
supporter: I am glad I could be here for you! I am hoping you continue to feel better and your writing helps to work out these feelings.  Thank you so much for being open with me. I hope you have a fantastic rest of your day! :)
seeker: thank you. hope you enjoy your day","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-07-25","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

seeker: hi. my friend told my ex boyfriend he was an idiot for dumping me. it made me feel uncomfortable since i was in the same room. now he is talking to me again. i think he might want me back
supporter: What are your thoughts on the relationship?
seeker: my feelings fluctuate. i resent him that he ended it. it confuses me he still wants to be in my life. he said he wanted to be friends but then asked me out again. i think he is trying to work his way back in. i know i can't keep it up unless he makes it clear he wants to be with me. i don't have time for games

supporter: Do you think he took your friend's comments seriously?

supporter: It sounds like your friend got him thinking.
seeker: it seemed like it did
supporter: Do you feel his change is genuine?
seeker: to a degree. i think he has ulterior motives too. 
supporter: What would he have to do to prove himself?
seeker: say he wants me back or something to that effect. i'd like him to be more direct in what he wants from me

supporter: Have you talked to anyone else besides your friend about your concerns?  Do you think your family or other friends could give some additional support to you?

supporter: Thanks.  Can I assist you with anything else?
seeker: nope. im good
supporter: Have a good night.  ","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-09-12","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hey there, is it okay to talk? I'm just feeling a bit overwhelmed with emotions right now.
supporter: Of course, Taylor. I'm here for you. What's been going on lately?
seeker: It's Nate, my ex. He reached out to apologize recently, and it's stirred up a lot of old memories and feelings.
supporter: I can imagine that must be really tough. How did it feel when he reached out to you?
seeker: Confusing, honestly. Part of me was glad he apologized, but another part isn't sure if I can trust his intentions.
supporter: That's completely valid. Trust can be hard to rebuild, especially after everything you've been through.
seeker: Exactly. I keep thinking about our past arguments and how they made me feel. It's all just resurfacing now.
supporter: It sounds like those memories are really triggering some deep emotions. How are you handling them right now?
seeker: Not too well, if I'm honest. I'm finding it hard to focus on my studies and my writing, and this time of year is already stressful.
supporter: It's completely understandable. Between the pressure from studies and your relationship history, it sounds like you're dealing with a lot.
seeker: It feels like too much sometimes, especially after failing a mid-term recently. My self-worth is really taking a hit.
supporter: I'm really sorry you're feeling this way, Taylor. Remember, one exam doesn't define your abilities or worth. You've achieved so much already.
seeker: Thanks for saying that. My therapist did mention the importance of focusing on self-worth, but it’s hard to internalize it sometimes.
supporter: It’s a process, and it’s okay to have days where it feels more challenging. Have you tried any of the strategies your therapist suggested?
seeker: I've been trying to focus on my writing and stay active in the online community I found. It helps to some extent.
supporter: That’s a great outlet for your emotions. Writing can be such a powerful way to process your thoughts and experiences.
seeker: Yeah, it's one of the few things that helps me clear my mind. But the writer's block is still a bit persistent.
supporter: Writer's block can be really frustrating, especially when you're already feeling overwhelmed. Is there anything specific about writing that's been challenging?
seeker: It's like I'm second-guessing everything I put down on paper, feeling like it’s not good enough compared to my peers.
supporter: Imposter syndrome is really tough to deal with. Just remember, your voice is unique and valuable in its own right.
seeker: Thanks for reminding me. I often forget that when I'm deep in self-doubt. It means a lot to have your support.
supporter: I'm always here for you, Taylor. Make sure to be kind to yourself and take things one day at a time. You're doing your best.
seeker: Thanks. I really needed to hear that. I’ll try to focus on what's within my control and take small steps forward.
supporter: That's a great approach. You're stronger than you realize, and I'm proud of you for reaching out and talking this through.
seeker: I appreciate it. It feels good to get everything off my chest and know I'm not facing this alone.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-12-18","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hey, are you online? I really need someone to talk to right now.
supporter: Hey Taylor, I'm here. What's going on?
seeker: I had a panic attack today, just before a social event. It was terrifying.
supporter: I'm so sorry to hear that. Panic attacks can be really overwhelming. Do you want to share more about what happened?
seeker: I was supposed to go to this gathering with some classmates, and out of nowhere, I just felt completely frozen.
supporter: That sounds incredibly tough. It makes sense you might feel that way given everything you've been dealing with lately. How are you feeling now?

supporter: I'm really glad to hear that. Remember, it’s okay to have hard days. Just keep reaching out and taking things one step at a time.
seeker: Thanks for being here. I was feeling really alone after today.

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hey Taylor, how have you been feeling lately?
seeker: Honestly, not great. I found out that my grade slipped again even after I reattempted the exam.
supporter: I’m really sorry to hear that. I can imagine how frustrating that must be after putting in all that effort.
seeker: Yeah, it's pretty crushing. I thought that notifying my professor and putting in the extra work would help, but apparently not.
supporter: It sounds like you’ve been trying really hard to make things right. It must feel discouraging to not see the progress you were expecting.
seeker: Exactly. It's like nothing I do is ever enough. And it doesn't help that I still feel this disconnect with my professor after everything.
supporter: That can be incredibly tough, especially when the relationship with your professor is strained. Do you think it might be worth discussing your feelings with them?
seeker: I've thought about it, but it's intimidating. What if they don’t take me seriously or think I’m just making excuses?
supporter: It's understandable to feel that way. However, sharing your concerns could potentially help rebuild that trust and understanding between you both.
seeker: I guess you're right. I did have a good talk with my therapist about self-worth, and maybe I should try to use those insights to approach this situation.
supporter: That sounds like a strong plan. You've already taken steps to understand yourself better, and using that knowledge could really help in this case.
seeker: I hope so. It’s just hard not to feel like an imposter when I see my peers succeeding so easily.
supporter: Imposter syndrome can be really tough to battle. Remember, everyone's journey is different, and your progress is valuable too.
seeker: Thank you for saying that. It's just been difficult to see my own value lately, especially with everything else piling up.
supporter: It definitely sounds like a lot is on your plate right now. Just know that it's okay to feel overwhelmed, and that you're doing your best.
seeker: I appreciate you reminding me of that. Things have felt really heavy since the argument with my ex and all these academic pressures.
supporter: You’ve been through so much. It’s important to give yourself credit for handling these challenges. How have you been managing?
seeker: I've been journaling a lot and trying to keep up with my creative writing. It helps sometimes, but I still feel stuck occasionally.
supporter: Writing can be a powerful outlet. It’s great that you’re turning to creativity as a way of processing your emotions.
seeker: Yeah, it's been a lifeline, honestly. That, and the supportive online community I found for writers.
supporter: I’m glad you have that. Connecting with others who understand what you're going through can be really comforting.
seeker: It truly is. Sometimes hearing from others who have faced similar struggles makes everything feel a bit more manageable.
supporter: Absolutely. Remember, it's completely okay to lean on those communities and your support system. You’re not alone in this.
seeker: I’ll try to keep that in mind. Thank you for listening and offering your support. It means a lot.
supporter: Anytime, Taylor. I’m here whenever you need to talk. Take each day as it comes, and be gentle with yourself.

supporter: Hi Taylor! Yes, I'm here. What's on your mind?

seeker: i feel depressed
supporter: i'm sorry to hear that. is there a specific reason you are having these feelings?
seeker: i feel alone. i feel like i do not have anyone to talk to when it comes to my emotions.
supporter: I understand. I have been feeling quite lonely too, I find myself feeling lonely at work and struggling to find someone I trust to talk to about these emotions. Do you have a friend or family member that you trust who might understand some of these feelings?
seeker: i do have a few friends that i think i can talk to about how i am feeling however the thought of them being too busy with their work is what prevents me from reaching out to them. 
supporter: I understand. Correct me if i'm wrong, it sounds like you're nervous to open up to these trusted people because you think they might be distracted by their work to provide the empathy you need and fully understand how you are feeling. Does that sound right?
seeker: you know i think that you are right about this. it has always been difficult for me to open to others even with those that have been there for me when i needed someone. i feel like a mix of emotions nervous but at the same time wanting to reaching out for help
supporter: I understand these feelings very well. Sometimes, my fear overshadows my want for help. I find it easier to open up to others through writing rather than face to face. Have you considered putting your feelings in writing and opening up to trusted friends and family in this way?
seeker: i have been writing for a while but due to my emotions i have stopped writing like i used to. when i did write i did notice a change in my feelings it became more positive and less depressed. now that i stopped writing its like i went back into depression 
supporter: It sounds like writing your feelings down helped you greatly in the past. May I suggest going back to writing and even letting someone you trust read what you have written down to understand how you are feeling?
seeker: yes, writing has been a huge help for me. I would take your suggestion and begin writing again to feel better. and i have let others read what i wrote and they have said it has helped them get over their depression and helped them understand me more
supporter: That's great! I am glad to hear that you will begin writing again. Thank you for opening up to me about your feelings. How do you feel about the solution we have come to today?
seeker: now that i was able to talk about how i feel with you and you giving me a useful suggestion i feel less depressed and feel motivated to write again. your help has been really helpful for me 
supporter: That's wonderful! I appreciate your honesty about how you are feeling. I am proud of you for seeking help. Is there anything else you would like to discuss?
seeker: thank you so much for helping me. and that is all that i would like to discuss. you have been a big help for me 
supporter: I am glad I could be here for you! I am hoping you continue to feel better and your writing helps to work out these feelings.  Thank you so much for being open with me. I hope you have a fantastic rest of your day! :)
seeker: thank you. hope you enjoy your day","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-07-25","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: How can I help you
seeker: hi. my friend told my ex boyfriend he was an idiot for dumping me. it made me feel uncomfortable since i was in the same room. now he is talking to me again. i think he might want me back
supporter: What are your thoughts on the relationship?
seeker: my feelings fluctuate. i resent him that he ended it. it confuses me he still wants to be in my life. he said he wanted to be friends but then asked me out again. i think he is trying to work his way back in. i know i can't keep it up unless he makes it clear he wants to be with me. i don't have time for games
supporter: That does sound hard that he is giving mixed signals.
seeker: yeah i don't like that. neither does my friend. why she told him he is an idiot for letting me go
supporter: Do you think he took your friend's comments seriously?
seeker: yes cuz that's when he wanted me to be around him more
supporter: It sounds like your friend got him thinking.
seeker: it seemed like it did
supporter: Do you feel his change is genuine?
seeker: to a degree. i think he has ulterior motives too. 
supporter: What would he have to do to prove himself?
seeker: say he wants me back or something to that effect. i'd like him to be more direct in what he wants from me
supporter: It sounds like it would help if he were direct with you and not sending mixed signals.  Is that correct?
seeker: yes that would be nice. he tends to beat around the bush then lets me know
supporter: Have you talked to anyone else besides your friend about your concerns?  Do you think your family or other friends could give some additional support to you?
seeker: yes i've talked to them about it. they've given me some insight into it. i know they want me to be careful. they don't want me to be hurt
supporter: That's understandable that they want you to be careful.  My parents and friends watched out for me too.
seeker: we are lucky they look out for us. they can't all be wrong if they're guiding us a certain way
supporter: I think you hit the nail on the head that it's helpful to have that support.
seeker: absolutely. i appreciate your help! nity nite
supporter: Thanks.  Can I assist you with anything else?
seeker: nope. im good
supporter: Have a good night.  ","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-09-12","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hi, How are you?
seeker: I am the youngest of 5 siblings and I feel all most days now because of my parents
supporter: It sounds like you're having a hard time feeling like you have your parents' attention, is that right?
seeker: Not their attention, but more on their expectations on me
supporter: That sounds frustrating, I'm sorry
supporter: Do they do or say anything specific that makes you feel those expectations?
seeker: Yes, its more on comparing me to the children of their friends. They always say why don't I have a better job or even plans on marrying rich. Stuff like that is very frustrating
seeker: They also expect me to take care of them financially soon, I'm just starting my adult life I want to enjoy it
supporter: That sounds very frustrating. I think if I felt those kind of expectations I would be anxious.
supporter: Do you feel comfortable talking to them about your feelings?
seeker: I do feel anxious every time. 
seeker: I tried a couple of times, but my mom always sees it as being too sensitive
supporter: Sometimes it can feel impossible to talk to parents
seeker: I know, is it better if I stay away for awhile? since taking to them won't make sense?
supporter: I think that it can be very healthy to get some distance, but I think it can also feel difficult -- do you have good friends in your life that you could lean on if you needed some distance from your parents?
seeker: Yes, I do. They actually helped me coped up. I always think that I wasn't blessed with my family, but I'm blessed with good friends
supporter: Good friends can be a huge comfort and it sounds like you're a good friends yourself if you have those kinds of friendships
seeker: Thinking about it, they really did help a lot. So I should really distance myself for a while right?
supporter: I think if making distance helps you feel better, you deserve and have a right to that space
seeker: Yes, thank you. I really need to that. 
supporter: You're welcome
supporter: It sounds like you are making healthy and careful emotional decisions 
supporter: Is there anything else you want to discuss about your parents?","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-09-01","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hey Taylor, it's good to see you here. How are you holding up these days?
seeker: Hey. I'm managing, I guess. Just trying to keep up with everything.
supporter: I hear you. With school and everything else on your plate, it must be a lot. Anything in particular that's been weighing on you?
seeker: Yeah, it's mostly about Nate, my ex. We had a big argument and things have been weird since then.
supporter: I'm really sorry to hear that. It sounds tough to go through a fallout with someone who used to mean a lot to you.
seeker: Yeah, it really sucks. I thought we were on the same page about things, but that argument just brought up a lot of unresolved issues.
supporter: Conflicts like that can be really revealing, but also painful. Do you feel comfortable sharing what the argument was about?
seeker: Sure. It started off as a small disagreement about our future plans, but it escalated quickly.
supporter: It's amazing how sometimes the smallest things become a big deal. Do you think it was more about the future or something else underlying it?
seeker: I think it was a bit of both. We've had different ideas about our futures for a while, and maybe we were ignoring it until now.
supporter: That makes sense. It's hard to navigate differences when you're emotionally invested. How does that make you feel now?
seeker: Honestly, it's exhausting. I keep playing the argument over and over in my head, trying to make sense of it.
supporter: I can imagine how tiring that must be. Sometimes our minds just want to find an answer, even when one isn't clear-cut.
seeker: Exactly. It's like I'm looking for signs of who was right or wrong, but I end up just feeling more tangled.
supporter: Maybe it's not about right or wrong but about understanding where each of you is coming from. What do you hope to achieve by unraveling these feelings?
seeker: I'd just like to find some peace with it, I guess. Maybe closure or even a chance to talk about it calmly.
supporter: Closure sounds like a healthy goal. Giving yourself time to process everything is important, though. Do you feel like there's space to have that calm conversation with Nate?
seeker: Part of me hopes so, but I'm not sure if either of us is ready yet. There's still a lot of raw emotions.
supporter: Emotions can take time to settle. It's okay to wait until it feels right. Meanwhile, how are you taking care of yourself?
seeker: I've been writing a lot, which helps. It's been a good outlet, even if it's just jotting down how I feel.
supporter: Writing can be really therapeutic, I agree. You have a wonderful gift for expressing your emotions through words.
seeker: Thank you for saying that. It makes me feel less alone in all of this.
supporter: You're definitely not alone, Taylor. I'm always here to listen whenever you need.
seeker: I appreciate it. It means a lot to have someone to talk to who gets it.
supporter: Anytime. Take your time with everything and remember to be kind to yourself.
seeker: I'll try to keep that in mind. Thank you for being here for me.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-10-05","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hi Taylor! How have you been lately?
seeker: Hey, I've been feeling a lot of things lately. It's been a bit overwhelming.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. Do you want to talk about what's been going on?
seeker: Yeah, I had a session with my therapist recently. We talked a lot about my self-worth.
supporter: That sounds like an important conversation. What came up for you during the session?
seeker: We talked about how I've been weighing my worth based on my academic and creative successes. It was eye-opening.
supporter: It's tough when our value feels tied to achievements. How did you feel after the session?
seeker: Honestly, I felt both relieved and a bit anxious. Relieved to recognize it but anxious about how to change it.
supporter: Change can be challenging, but recognizing the issue is a great first step. How have things been at university?
seeker: University's been okay. The workload is a lot, and I still struggle with feeling like I'm not doing enough.
supporter: That makes sense, especially with everything you have on your plate. How's your creative writing going?
seeker: It's been up and down. I joined a writing workshop that helped, but the imposter syndrome creeps in.
supporter: I'm glad the workshop helped. The feeling of not being enough can be so persistent. You're not alone in that.
seeker: Thanks. It helps to know I'm not alone. The online community has been supportive too.
supporter: That's great to hear! Sometimes finding a supportive community can make a big difference.
seeker: Definitely! They remind me that it's okay to struggle and that growth takes time.
supporter: Absolutely! You're on a journey, and it's perfectly okay to have ups and downs along the way.
seeker: I truly appreciate you listening and being here for me. It means a lot.
supporter: Anytime, Taylor. You're doing amazing things, and I'm here whenever you need to talk.
seeker: Thank you. I'll try to take things one step at a time. Catch up soon?
supporter: Definitely! Take care and reach out whenever you feel like it.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-12-10","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

supporter: Of course, Taylor. I'm here for you. What's on your mind?
seeker: I've been trying to get back into writing, but it just feels impossible right now.
supporter: Writer's block can be really tough. It sounds like you're feeling stuck. Do you want to tell me more about it?

seeker: Well, there's been a lot going on lately. I had a big argument with my ex, and my grades haven't been great either.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. It sounds like you're carrying a lot of emotional weight. It’s natural for that to affect your creative process.
seeker: Yeah, and during exam week, I felt so isolated and anxious. It's been hard to shake off that feeling.
supporter: That sounds really overwhelming. Being in a challenging environment and feeling isolated can certainly impact your mental space.
seeker: I just feel like I'm losing touch with the one thing that used to make me happy.
supporter: It's understandable to feel that way when you're passionate about something. Have you thought about any small steps that might help you reconnect with your writing?
seeker: I tried to just sit and let myself write without pressure, but the words still didn't come.
supporter: Giving yourself some grace during this time is important. Maybe journaling or even reading could help spark some inspiration?
seeker: That's a good idea. I've been meaning to read a book that inspired me a lot last year.
supporter: That sounds like a wonderful way to reignite that creative spark. It's okay to take it one day at a time and find joy in small victories.
seeker: Thanks, I appreciate it. Just talking about it makes it feel a bit more manageable.
supporter: I'm glad to hear that. Remember, it's okay to reach out whenever you need to, and you’re not alone in this.
seeker: I will, and thanks again for being there. I'll keep trying.

supporter: Hi Taylor! Yes, I'm here. What's on your mind?
seeker: I'm really struggling. I just can't seem to get anything right lately.

seeker: i feel depressed
supporter: i'm sorry to hear that. is there a specific reason you are having these feelings?
seeker: i feel alone. i feel like i do not have anyone to talk to when it comes to my emotions.
supporter: I understand. I have been feeling quite lonely too, I find myself feeling lonely at work and struggling to find someone I trust to talk to about these emotions. Do you have a friend or family member that you trust who might understand some of these feelings?
seeker: i do have a few friends that i think i can talk to about how i am feeling however the thought of them being too busy with their work is what prevents me from reaching out to them. 
supporter: I understand. Correct me if i'm wrong, it sounds like you're nervous to open up to these trusted people because you think they might be distracted by their work to provide the empathy you need and fully understand how you are feeling. Does that sound right?
seeker: you know i think that you are right about this. it has always been difficult for me to open to others even with those that have been there for me when i needed someone. i feel like a mix of emotions nervous but at the same time wanting to reaching out for help
supporter: I understand these feelings very well. Sometimes, my fear overshadows my want for help. I find it easier to open up to others through writing rather than face to face. Have you considered putting your feelings in writing and opening up to trusted friends and family in this way?
seeker: i have been writing for a while but due to my emotions i have stopped writing like i used to. when i did write i did notice a change in my feelings it became more positive and less depressed. now that i stopped writing its like i went back into depression 
supporter: It sounds like writing your feelings down helped you greatly in the past. May I suggest going back to writing and even letting someone you trust read what you have written down to understand how you are feeling?

seeker: now that i was able to talk about how i feel with you and you giving me a useful suggestion i feel less depressed and feel motivated to write again. your help has been really helpful for me 
supporter: That's wonderful! I appreciate your honesty about how you are feeling. I am proud of you for seeking help. Is there anything else you would like to discuss?
seeker: thank you so much for helping me. and that is all that i would like to discuss. you have been a big help for me 
supporter: I am glad I could be here for you! I am hoping you continue to feel better and your writing helps to work out these feelings.  Thank you so much for being open with me. I hope you have a fantastic rest of your day! :)
seeker: thank you. hope you enjoy your day","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-07-25","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hey Taylor, it's good to see you here. How are you holding up these days?
seeker: Hey. I'm managing, I guess. Just trying to keep up with everything.
supporter: I hear you. With school and everything else on your plate, it must be a lot. Anything in particular that's been weighing on you?
seeker: Yeah, it's mostly about Nate, my ex. We had a big argument and things have been weird since then.
supporter: I'm really sorry to hear that. It sounds tough to go through a fallout with someone who used to mean a lot to you.
seeker: Yeah, it really sucks. I thought we were on the same page about things, but that argument just brought up a lot of unresolved issues.
supporter: Conflicts like that can be really revealing, but also painful. Do you feel comfortable sharing what the argument was about?
seeker: Sure. It started off as a small disagreement about our future plans, but it escalated quickly.
supporter: It's amazing how sometimes the smallest things become a big deal. Do you think it was more about the future or something else underlying it?
seeker: I think it was a bit of both. We've had different ideas about our futures for a while, and maybe we were ignoring it until now.
supporter: That makes sense. It's hard to navigate differences when you're emotionally invested. How does that make you feel now?
seeker: Honestly, it's exhausting. I keep playing the argument over and over in my head, trying to make sense of it.
supporter: I can imagine how tiring that must be. Sometimes our minds just want to find an answer, even when one isn't clear-cut.
seeker: Exactly. It's like I'm looking for signs of who was right or wrong, but I end up just feeling more tangled.
supporter: Maybe it's not about right or wrong but about understanding where each of you is coming from. What do you hope to achieve by unraveling these feelings?
seeker: I'd just like to find some peace with it, I guess. Maybe closure or even a chance to talk about it calmly.
supporter: Closure sounds like a healthy goal. Giving yourself time to process everything is important, though. Do you feel like there's space to have that calm conversation with Nate?
seeker: Part of me hopes so, but I'm not sure if either of us is ready yet. There's still a lot of raw emotions.
supporter: Emotions can take time to settle. It's okay to wait until it feels right. Meanwhile, how are you taking care of yourself?
seeker: I've been writing a lot, which helps. It's been a good outlet, even if it's just jotting down how I feel.
supporter: Writing can be really therapeutic, I agree. You have a wonderful gift for expressing your emotions through words.
seeker: Thank you for saying that. It makes me feel less alone in all of this.
supporter: You're definitely not alone, Taylor. I'm always here to listen whenever you need.
seeker: I appreciate it. It means a lot to have someone to talk to who gets it.
supporter: Anytime. Take your time with everything and remember to be kind to yourself.
seeker: I'll try to keep that in mind. Thank you for being here for me.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-10-05","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

seeker: i feel depressed
supporter: i'm sorry to hear that. is there a specific reason you are having these feelings?
seeker: i feel alone. i feel like i do not have anyone to talk to when it comes to my emotions.
supporter: I understand. I have been feeling quite lonely too, I find myself feeling lonely at work and struggling to find someone I trust to talk to about these emotions. Do you have a friend or family member that you trust who might understand some of these feelings?
seeker: i do have a few friends that i think i can talk to about how i am feeling however the thought of them being too busy with their work is what prevents me from reaching out to them. 
supporter: I understand. Correct me if i'm wrong, it sounds like you're nervous to open up to these trusted people because you think they might be distracted by their work to provide the empathy you need and fully understand how you are feeling. Does that sound right?
seeker: you know i think that you are right about this. it has always been difficult for me to open to others even with those that have been there for me when i needed someone. i feel like a mix of emotions nervous but at the same time wanting to reaching out for help
supporter: I understand these feelings very well. Sometimes, my fear overshadows my want for help. I find it easier to open up to others through writing rather than face to face. Have you considered putting your feelings in writing and opening up to trusted friends and family in this way?
seeker: i have been writing for a while but due to my emotions i have stopped writing like i used to. when i did write i did notice a change in my feelings it became more positive and less depressed. now that i stopped writing its like i went back into depression 
supporter: It sounds like writing your feelings down helped you greatly in the past. May I suggest going back to writing and even letting someone you trust read what you have written down to understand how you are feeling?
seeker: yes, writing has been a huge help for me. I would take your suggestion and begin writing again to feel better. and i have let others read what i wrote and they have said it has helped them get over their depression and helped them understand me more
supporter: That's great! I am glad to hear that you will begin writing again. Thank you for opening up to me about your feelings. How do you feel about the solution we have come to today?
seeker: now that i was able to talk about how i feel with you and you giving me a useful suggestion i feel less depressed and feel motivated to write again. your help has been really helpful for me 
supporter: That's wonderful! I appreciate your honesty about how you are feeling. I am proud of you for seeking help. Is there anything else you would like to discuss?
seeker: thank you so much for helping me. and that is all that i would like to discuss. you have been a big help for me 
supporter: I am glad I could be here for you! I am hoping you continue to feel better and your writing helps to work out these feelings.  Thank you so much for being open with me. I hope you have a fantastic rest of your day! :)
seeker: thank you. hope you enjoy your day","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-07-25","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}
