MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: How can I help you
seeker: hi. my friend told my ex boyfriend he was an idiot for dumping me. it made me feel uncomfortable since i was in the same room. now he is talking to me again. i think he might want me back
supporter: What are your thoughts on the relationship?
seeker: my feelings fluctuate. i resent him that he ended it. it confuses me he still wants to be in my life. he said he wanted to be friends but then asked me out again. i think he is trying to work his way back in. i know i can't keep it up unless he makes it clear he wants to be with me. i don't have time for games
supporter: That does sound hard that he is giving mixed signals.
seeker: yeah i don't like that. neither does my friend. why she told him he is an idiot for letting me go
supporter: Do you think he took your friend's comments seriously?
seeker: yes cuz that's when he wanted me to be around him more
supporter: It sounds like your friend got him thinking.
seeker: it seemed like it did
supporter: Do you feel his change is genuine?
seeker: to a degree. i think he has ulterior motives too. 
supporter: What would he have to do to prove himself?
seeker: say he wants me back or something to that effect. i'd like him to be more direct in what he wants from me
supporter: It sounds like it would help if he were direct with you and not sending mixed signals.  Is that correct?
seeker: yes that would be nice. he tends to beat around the bush then lets me know
supporter: Have you talked to anyone else besides your friend about your concerns?  Do you think your family or other friends could give some additional support to you?
seeker: yes i've talked to them about it. they've given me some insight into it. i know they want me to be careful. they don't want me to be hurt
supporter: That's understandable that they want you to be careful.  My parents and friends watched out for me too.
seeker: we are lucky they look out for us. they can't all be wrong if they're guiding us a certain way
supporter: I think you hit the nail on the head that it's helpful to have that support.
seeker: absolutely. i appreciate your help! nity nite
supporter: Thanks.  Can I assist you with anything else?
seeker: nope. im good
supporter: Have a good night.  ","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-09-12","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hi, How are you?
seeker: I am the youngest of 5 siblings and I feel all most days now because of my parents
supporter: It sounds like you're having a hard time feeling like you have your parents' attention, is that right?
seeker: Not their attention, but more on their expectations on me
supporter: That sounds frustrating, I'm sorry
supporter: Do they do or say anything specific that makes you feel those expectations?
seeker: Yes, its more on comparing me to the children of their friends. They always say why don't I have a better job or even plans on marrying rich. Stuff like that is very frustrating
seeker: They also expect me to take care of them financially soon, I'm just starting my adult life I want to enjoy it
supporter: That sounds very frustrating. I think if I felt those kind of expectations I would be anxious.
supporter: Do you feel comfortable talking to them about your feelings?
seeker: I do feel anxious every time. 
seeker: I tried a couple of times, but my mom always sees it as being too sensitive
supporter: Sometimes it can feel impossible to talk to parents
seeker: I know, is it better if I stay away for awhile? since taking to them won't make sense?
supporter: I think that it can be very healthy to get some distance, but I think it can also feel difficult -- do you have good friends in your life that you could lean on if you needed some distance from your parents?
seeker: Yes, I do. They actually helped me coped up. I always think that I wasn't blessed with my family, but I'm blessed with good friends
supporter: Good friends can be a huge comfort and it sounds like you're a good friends yourself if you have those kinds of friendships
seeker: Thinking about it, they really did help a lot. So I should really distance myself for a while right?
supporter: I think if making distance helps you feel better, you deserve and have a right to that space
seeker: Yes, thank you. I really need to that. 
supporter: You're welcome
supporter: It sounds like you are making healthy and careful emotional decisions 
supporter: Is there anything else you want to discuss about your parents?","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-09-01","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hey Taylor, it's good to see you here. How are you holding up these days?
seeker: Hey. I'm managing, I guess. Just trying to keep up with everything.
supporter: I hear you. With school and everything else on your plate, it must be a lot. Anything in particular that's been weighing on you?
seeker: Yeah, it's mostly about Nate, my ex. We had a big argument and things have been weird since then.
supporter: I'm really sorry to hear that. It sounds tough to go through a fallout with someone who used to mean a lot to you.
seeker: Yeah, it really sucks. I thought we were on the same page about things, but that argument just brought up a lot of unresolved issues.
supporter: Conflicts like that can be really revealing, but also painful. Do you feel comfortable sharing what the argument was about?
seeker: Sure. It started off as a small disagreement about our future plans, but it escalated quickly.
supporter: It's amazing how sometimes the smallest things become a big deal. Do you think it was more about the future or something else underlying it?
seeker: I think it was a bit of both. We've had different ideas about our futures for a while, and maybe we were ignoring it until now.
supporter: That makes sense. It's hard to navigate differences when you're emotionally invested. How does that make you feel now?
seeker: Honestly, it's exhausting. I keep playing the argument over and over in my head, trying to make sense of it.
supporter: I can imagine how tiring that must be. Sometimes our minds just want to find an answer, even when one isn't clear-cut.
seeker: Exactly. It's like I'm looking for signs of who was right or wrong, but I end up just feeling more tangled.
supporter: Maybe it's not about right or wrong but about understanding where each of you is coming from. What do you hope to achieve by unraveling these feelings?
seeker: I'd just like to find some peace with it, I guess. Maybe closure or even a chance to talk about it calmly.
supporter: Closure sounds like a healthy goal. Giving yourself time to process everything is important, though. Do you feel like there's space to have that calm conversation with Nate?
seeker: Part of me hopes so, but I'm not sure if either of us is ready yet. There's still a lot of raw emotions.
supporter: Emotions can take time to settle. It's okay to wait until it feels right. Meanwhile, how are you taking care of yourself?
seeker: I've been writing a lot, which helps. It's been a good outlet, even if it's just jotting down how I feel.
supporter: Writing can be really therapeutic, I agree. You have a wonderful gift for expressing your emotions through words.
seeker: Thank you for saying that. It makes me feel less alone in all of this.
supporter: You're definitely not alone, Taylor. I'm always here to listen whenever you need.
seeker: I appreciate it. It means a lot to have someone to talk to who gets it.
supporter: Anytime. Take your time with everything and remember to be kind to yourself.
seeker: I'll try to keep that in mind. Thank you for being here for me.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-10-05","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hi Taylor! How have you been lately?
seeker: Hey, I've been feeling a lot of things lately. It's been a bit overwhelming.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. Do you want to talk about what's been going on?
seeker: Yeah, I had a session with my therapist recently. We talked a lot about my self-worth.
supporter: That sounds like an important conversation. What came up for you during the session?
seeker: We talked about how I've been weighing my worth based on my academic and creative successes. It was eye-opening.
supporter: It's tough when our value feels tied to achievements. How did you feel after the session?
seeker: Honestly, I felt both relieved and a bit anxious. Relieved to recognize it but anxious about how to change it.
supporter: Change can be challenging, but recognizing the issue is a great first step. How have things been at university?
seeker: University's been okay. The workload is a lot, and I still struggle with feeling like I'm not doing enough.
supporter: That makes sense, especially with everything you have on your plate. How's your creative writing going?
seeker: It's been up and down. I joined a writing workshop that helped, but the imposter syndrome creeps in.
supporter: I'm glad the workshop helped. The feeling of not being enough can be so persistent. You're not alone in that.
seeker: Thanks. It helps to know I'm not alone. The online community has been supportive too.
supporter: That's great to hear! Sometimes finding a supportive community can make a big difference.
seeker: Definitely! They remind me that it's okay to struggle and that growth takes time.
supporter: Absolutely! You're on a journey, and it's perfectly okay to have ups and downs along the way.
seeker: I truly appreciate you listening and being here for me. It means a lot.
supporter: Anytime, Taylor. You're doing amazing things, and I'm here whenever you need to talk.
seeker: Thank you. I'll try to take things one step at a time. Catch up soon?
supporter: Definitely! Take care and reach out whenever you feel like it.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-12-10","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

seeker: Honestly, not great. I found out that my grade slipped again even after I reattempted the exam.

supporter: It sounds like you’ve been trying really hard to make things right. It must feel discouraging to not see the progress you were expecting.

seeker: I hope so. It’s just hard not to feel like an imposter when I see my peers succeeding so easily.
supporter: Imposter syndrome can be really tough to battle. Remember, everyone's journey is different, and your progress is valuable too.
seeker: Thank you for saying that. It's just been difficult to see my own value lately, especially with everything else piling up.

seeker: I appreciate you reminding me of that. Things have felt really heavy since the argument with my ex and all these academic pressures.
supporter: You’ve been through so much. It’s important to give yourself credit for handling these challenges. How have you been managing?

turns.content: Hey, got a moment to chat?
Of course, Nick! What's on your mind?
I've been feeling a bit all over the place lately.
I'm here for you. Can you tell me more about what's been going on?
Well, since switching my major to psychology, things have been mostly positive, but I'm just juggling a lot.
It makes sense that you'd feel that way, especially during a big transition like that. How are you managing the workload now?
It's more manageable than physics, for sure. But I still get anxious about falling behind.
That anxiety is understandable. It's a lot to handle. Have you found any new strategies that help with the anxiety?
I've been trying to stay organized with a planner, but sometimes it feels overwhelming.
Organization can be really helpful, but it's important to avoid burnout. Are you taking time for yourself, too?
Not as much as I should be. I know it matters, but it's hard to prioritize.
It's definitely hard to balance, especially with everything else you're managing. Maybe starting with small breaks could help?
Yeah, I think I could start with just a few minutes to breathe. It's worth trying.
Absolutely! Sometimes the smallest changes make a big difference. How's your relationship with your professors, now that you've switched majors?
Better actually, they've been a lot more approachable in the new department.
That's great to hear! Having supportive professors can really make a difference. Are you comfortable reaching out to them if you need help?
I think so. It's still new to me, but knowing they're there is reassuring.
It's good to have that support system. Remember that asking for help is a strength, not a weakness.
Thanks, I need to remind myself of that sometimes. It's easy to forget.
Totally normal to forget. Just know you're doing the best you can, and that's enough.
Thanks, I really appreciate you listening. It's helped clear my head a bit.

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hey, I guess I just need someone to talk to right now.
supporter: Of course, Nick. I'm here for you. What's on your mind?
seeker: It's about my physics course again. My professor contacted me today to offer help.
supporter: That sounds like a positive step. How do you feel about it?
seeker: I feel a bit conflicted. On one hand, it's great to know someone cares, but on the other, I'm just so stressed and unsure it can make a difference.
supporter: It's understandable to feel that way, especially after the struggles you've had. Did the professor offer any specific advice?
seeker: Yeah, they suggested a few resources and offered to arrange a tutoring session. But honestly, I'm not sure if it'll help with how behind I am now.
supporter: It's good that they provided some options, but I get that feeling of being in over your head. Have you tried reaching out to other students for support?
seeker: I haven't. I guess I'm just embarrassed by how far I've fallen behind.
supporter: It's tough to ask for help, but remember you're not alone in this. Many students face similar challenges. It might be worth trying to find a study group or even just one buddy to tackle things with.
seeker: That makes sense. I think I could try talking to that one classmate who seemed in a similar spot last semester.
supporter: That's a great idea! You might find you're stronger when working together. And don't forget, you've been through difficult times before, like with your friend incident. You managed to turn things around then.
seeker: Yeah, you're right. I did sort things out with him. It was tough, but I'm glad I pushed through.
supporter: Exactly. You've shown resilience. It's okay to feel stressed, but you've got the strength to push through this as well.
seeker: I hope so. It's just hard to keep motivated when it feels like everything's piling up.
supporter: That's completely valid. Taking small steps can help make those piles seem less overwhelming. Maybe set one small goal to start with.
seeker: That's a good idea. Perhaps I could start by organizing my notes and seeing what's most urgent.
supporter: That sounds like a solid plan, and it'll help clear your head. Remember, you're doing your best and that counts for a lot.
seeker: Thanks for listening. I really appreciate having someone to talk to.
supporter: Anytime, Nick. I'm glad you're opening up, and I'm here whenever you need to talk.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-06-15","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hey, I've been reflecting a lot on my studies lately, and I've decided to make a big change.
supporter: Hey Nick, that sounds like a significant step. What change are you thinking about?
seeker: Well, I've decided to switch my major. I realized physics just wasn't the right fit for me.
supporter: That's a huge decision, Nick. How are you feeling about it?
seeker: I'm a mix of relieved and anxious. Relieved because I've been struggling with it for a while, but anxious because it's a big shift.
supporter: It's understandable to feel both relief and anxiety, especially after making such an important decision. What led you to finally decide?
seeker: I kept remembering how overwhelmed I felt with the assignments and the stress it brought. Talking to my professor helped too, but it made me see I needed a change.
supporter: Your professor seemed like a great support. It's good that they were there for guidance. What new direction are you considering?
seeker: I'm thinking of switching to a major in psychology. I've always been fascinated by how the mind works, and it feels more aligned with my interests.
supporter: Psychology sounds like a fascinating field. It's wonderful that you've found something that resonates more with you. How have your family and friends reacted to your decision?
seeker: I told my family first. They were really understanding, which helped a lot, especially since they know I've been struggling.
supporter: Family support can make a big difference. It's great that they’re understanding about your choice. Have you talked to your classmates or your best friend?
seeker: Not yet. I'm a bit nervous about their reactions, especially since some of them are sticking with physics.
supporter: It’s normal to feel nervous, Nick. Remember, it's about what's right for you. Those who care will likely understand and support your decision.
seeker: Yeah, I guess that's true. Just want to feel like I'm doing the right thing, you know?
supporter: Finding the right path for you is important, and it sounds like you're taking thoughtful steps. Trust yourself in this process.
seeker: Thanks, that means a lot. I'm hoping this new path will be a better fit and lead to less stress.
supporter: I believe you're on the right track, Nick. And remember, it's okay to reach out if you ever need to talk through any worries or changes.
seeker: I will. Thanks for listening and being supportive. It really helps to talk it through.
supporter: Anytime, Nick. I'm here for you. Good luck with everything, and I'm sure you'll do great in psychology.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-07-05","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hey, do you have a moment to chat? I'm feeling a bit overwhelmed.
supporter: Of course, Nick. What's going on?
seeker: I've been swamped with assignments, and it's starting to really wear me down.
supporter: That sounds really tough. Are these assignments from your physics course?
seeker: Yeah, mostly. It's just been so relentless, and I really don't feel any support from the university.
supporter: I remember you mentioning before how the teaching quality has been lacking. Has it gotten worse?

supporter: That's such a hard decision. Dropping a course can feel like a big step, but you're the one who knows what's best for you.
seeker: Exactly. I just feel like I'm drowning in work with no payoff, you know? It's exhausting.
supporter: Definitely. It's important to weigh the pros and cons though. How do you feel about physics overall?
seeker: I used to love it, but now it's just become a source of stress. I miss being excited about it.
supporter: It's really tough when something you used to love becomes stressful. Is there anything you've considered doing differently to reignite that passion?
seeker: I've thought about seeking outside resources or maybe talking to a different professor, but it feels daunting.
supporter: That's understandable. Sometimes reaching out for help can feel challenging, but it could make a difference. You shouldn't have to tackle this all alone.
seeker: I guess I could try, but I'm worried about failing either way. I hate feeling this uncertain.
supporter: It's okay to feel uncertain, Nick. Remember when you and Henry had that fallout and reconciled? You took a brave step then and it worked out.
seeker: True, I appreciate you bringing that up. It's nice to remember that things can turn around.
supporter: Exactly. You've got the resilience to turn this around too. Maybe start with small steps and see how it feels?
seeker: Yeah, maybe reaching out to a professor wouldn't be so bad to start with. Thank you for talking this through with me.
supporter: Anytime, Nick. I'm always here to support you in any way I can. Let me know how it goes when you take that first step.
seeker: Will do. I'm actually feeling a bit lighter talking about it now.
supporter: I'm glad to hear that. Keep taking care of yourself, okay?","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-05-30","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

seeker: Hey, it's been a bit tough honestly. I decided to talk to my family about everything that's been happening.

seeker: That sounds like a good way to ease into it. I think I'll give it a try.

supporter: Hello. How are you today?

supporter: What can I help you with?
seeker: Lately, my friends started to make jokes about my face being ugly. They even called my face as flat as a pan! What should I do? I see them everyday on the bus
supporter: Have you tried confronting them and asking why they are being bullies?

seeker: Still though, it makes me want to avoid them when I go to school on the bus

supporter: I understand, school was tough for me too.
supporter: I suggest you tell them to knock it off or you can sit somewhere away from the bus.
seeker: Should I just beat them up with my backpack
supporter: No, beating them up will only get you in trouble and that won't help.
seeker: There's another bus route. Should I just take that instead
supporter: I think that could be a good idea if it's not too far out of your way.
seeker: I think I will. Their comments make me very insecure
supporter: You could also tell a teacher what is happening. They will help you out.
supporter: I bet you are handsome! Don't let it get to you.

supporter: Try to tell yourself you are good looking and deserve good things to happen every morning! Look in that mirror and tell yourself good things.

supporter: That sounds like a fantastic idea.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-02-22","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

seeker: Hey... I've been feeling pretty down recently.

seeker: Hi
seeker: I had problems in the past and somehow right now
supporter: What sort of problems were in your past and now?
seeker: I loved physics and I decided to attend university, but soon after I slowly lost my interest and became unmotivated

supporter: More reason to speak to a school counselor or school administrator. We need to provide help to students, not have bad teachers deter them.

seeker: Thanks, I wish  you luck in your future endeavours
seeker: Bye then ; )
supporter: Goodbye","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-01-25","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

seeker: Hey, I'm feeling a mix of things actually. There's a lot on my mind.

supporter: Hello. How are you today?
seeker: I'm doing good. I need some advice
supporter: What can I help you with?
seeker: Lately, my friends started to make jokes about my face being ugly. They even called my face as flat as a pan! What should I do? I see them everyday on the bus
supporter: Have you tried confronting them and asking why they are being bullies?
seeker: I did and they respond by saying that they are just joking and that I'm handsome. But it's starting to get on my nerves because it's all they make fun about every time they see me!
supporter: I'm sure you are very handsome! They could just be jealous.
seeker: Haha I would hope so
seeker: Still though, it makes me want to avoid them when I go to school on the bus
seeker: What do you think I should do then?
supporter: I understand, school was tough for me too.
supporter: I suggest you tell them to knock it off or you can sit somewhere away from the bus.
seeker: Should I just beat them up with my backpack
supporter: No, beating them up will only get you in trouble and that won't help.
seeker: There's another bus route. Should I just take that instead
supporter: I think that could be a good idea if it's not too far out of your way.
seeker: I think I will. Their comments make me very insecure
supporter: You could also tell a teacher what is happening. They will help you out.
supporter: I bet you are handsome! Don't let it get to you.
seeker: The teacher would probably make fun of me!
seeker: Thanks it's hard to look in the mirror now
supporter: Try to tell yourself you are good looking and deserve good things to happen every morning! Look in that mirror and tell yourself good things.
seeker: I'll try to be positive for once.
seeker: Do you believe working out will help
supporter: Working out will help a lot! When I was feeling down on myself I decided to go to the gym three times a week. It was a great confidence boost.
seeker: Awesome. I will start to take care of myself and not worry about others then.
supporter: That sounds like a fantastic idea.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-02-22","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hey Nick, how have you been feeling lately?
seeker: Hey... I've been feeling pretty down recently.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. Do you want to talk about what's been going on?
seeker: Yeah, it's about Henry. We argued again, and this time it got ugly.
supporter: That sounds tough. What happened between you two?
seeker: It started with some jokes they made. I found them really insensitive and hurtful.
supporter: I can understand why that would be upsetting. Did you talk to them about how you felt?
seeker: I tried, but it just turned into a shouting match. I didn't expect it would escalate.
supporter: That sounds really frustrating. It can be hard when someone you care about doesn't understand your perspective.
seeker: Exactly. I mean, we've been friends for so long. I thought we'd be on the same page about these things.
supporter: It's natural to feel disappointed in situations like this. It's okay to feel hurt.
seeker: Thanks. I just can't help but think if maybe I'm overreacting.
supporter: Your feelings are valid, Nick. It's important to acknowledge when something bothers you.
seeker: True, but what if I drive him away by holding onto this?
supporter: It might help to express why those jokes affected you deeply. If he's a true friend, he should understand and respect your feelings.
seeker: Yeah, I think I should try talking to him when things cool down. I don't want to lose our friendship over this.
supporter: That sounds like a good plan. Give it some time, and approach it when you're both calmer.
seeker: I will. Thanks for listening. It really helps to talk it through.
supporter: Anytime, Nick. I'm here whenever you need to chat or get things off your chest.
seeker: I appreciate that. Hopefully, next time we'll be talking about something more positive!
supporter: I'm sure we will. Hang in there, Nick. You've got this.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-03-01","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

supporter: Of course, Nick! What's on your mind?

seeker: Hey, I'm feeling a mix of things actually. There's a lot on my mind.
supporter: I’m here to listen. What's been going on?

supporter: That sounds like a solid plan. Communication is so key. How are you feeling about that agreement?
seeker: Hopeful, mostly. I guess I'm just trying to stay positive about it.

seeker: Definitely. It’s nice to know I'm not alone in this.

seeker: Thanks again. I really appreciate our chats.

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hey, do you have a moment to chat? I'm feeling a bit overwhelmed.
supporter: Of course, Nick. What's going on?
seeker: I've been swamped with assignments, and it's starting to really wear me down.
supporter: That sounds really tough. Are these assignments from your physics course?
seeker: Yeah, mostly. It's just been so relentless, and I really don't feel any support from the university.
supporter: I remember you mentioning before how the teaching quality has been lacking. Has it gotten worse?
seeker: Pretty much. It feels like I'm teaching myself. I'm even thinking of dropping the course.
supporter: That's such a hard decision. Dropping a course can feel like a big step, but you're the one who knows what's best for you.
seeker: Exactly. I just feel like I'm drowning in work with no payoff, you know? It's exhausting.
supporter: Definitely. It's important to weigh the pros and cons though. How do you feel about physics overall?
seeker: I used to love it, but now it's just become a source of stress. I miss being excited about it.
supporter: It's really tough when something you used to love becomes stressful. Is there anything you've considered doing differently to reignite that passion?
seeker: I've thought about seeking outside resources or maybe talking to a different professor, but it feels daunting.
supporter: That's understandable. Sometimes reaching out for help can feel challenging, but it could make a difference. You shouldn't have to tackle this all alone.
seeker: I guess I could try, but I'm worried about failing either way. I hate feeling this uncertain.
supporter: It's okay to feel uncertain, Nick. Remember when you and Henry had that fallout and reconciled? You took a brave step then and it worked out.
seeker: True, I appreciate you bringing that up. It's nice to remember that things can turn around.
supporter: Exactly. You've got the resilience to turn this around too. Maybe start with small steps and see how it feels?
seeker: Yeah, maybe reaching out to a professor wouldn't be so bad to start with. Thank you for talking this through with me.
supporter: Anytime, Nick. I'm always here to support you in any way I can. Let me know how it goes when you take that first step.
seeker: Will do. I'm actually feeling a bit lighter talking about it now.
supporter: I'm glad to hear that. Keep taking care of yourself, okay?","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-05-30","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

seeker: Hey, it's been a bit tough honestly. I decided to talk to my family about everything that's been happening.

supporter: I'm proud of you for taking this step, Nick. Remember, I'm here for you and you're not alone in this.

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hey, Nick! How are you holding up these days?
seeker: Hey! Overall, I'm doing okay, but there's something on my mind recently.
supporter: I'm here to listen, Nick. What's been on your mind?

seeker: We used to just shut down or lash out. But this time, we addressed a few small things calmly.
supporter: It seems like both of you are putting in effort to handle things differently. Have you felt things improve in other areas as well?
seeker: Yes, we're more supportive of each other's goals now. She's genuinely interested in my new major, which means a lot.

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hello. Is anyone there
supporter: Hello. How are you today?
seeker: I'm doing good. I need some advice
supporter: What can I help you with?
seeker: Lately, my friends started to make jokes about my face being ugly. They even called my face as flat as a pan! What should I do? I see them everyday on the bus
supporter: Have you tried confronting them and asking why they are being bullies?
seeker: I did and they respond by saying that they are just joking and that I'm handsome. But it's starting to get on my nerves because it's all they make fun about every time they see me!
supporter: I'm sure you are very handsome! They could just be jealous.
seeker: Haha I would hope so
seeker: Still though, it makes me want to avoid them when I go to school on the bus
seeker: What do you think I should do then?
supporter: I understand, school was tough for me too.
supporter: I suggest you tell them to knock it off or you can sit somewhere away from the bus.
seeker: Should I just beat them up with my backpack
supporter: No, beating them up will only get you in trouble and that won't help.
seeker: There's another bus route. Should I just take that instead
supporter: I think that could be a good idea if it's not too far out of your way.
seeker: I think I will. Their comments make me very insecure
supporter: You could also tell a teacher what is happening. They will help you out.
supporter: I bet you are handsome! Don't let it get to you.
seeker: The teacher would probably make fun of me!
seeker: Thanks it's hard to look in the mirror now
supporter: Try to tell yourself you are good looking and deserve good things to happen every morning! Look in that mirror and tell yourself good things.
seeker: I'll try to be positive for once.
seeker: Do you believe working out will help
supporter: Working out will help a lot! When I was feeling down on myself I decided to go to the gym three times a week. It was a great confidence boost.
seeker: Awesome. I will start to take care of myself and not worry about others then.
supporter: That sounds like a fantastic idea.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-02-22","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hello, how is your life at the moment? Do you want to talk about anything? 
seeker: I am doing ok. I just broke up with my girlfriend and sad about it
supporter: so I hear you are not feeling at all your best at the moment? 
seeker: That is correct.
supporter: Do you feel as though you have no-one to talk to about this situation? I am happy to listen. 
seeker: I am so sad and just wonder why did it happen!!!
supporter: Do you have no idea? Do you think you might have done something wrong or perhaps she was being unfaithful to you? 
seeker: We had simple disagreement and both of us were keep fighting.. now I can not get over it.
supporter: Do you consider that there might be any hope for the  two of you at all? 
seeker: I don't know. What should I do?
supporter: Well, I think you should give her some space but people do sometimes get back together after they've separated 
seeker: I see your point.
supporter: You really do need to give her some space though - don't crowd her 
seeker: Should I call her directly? What should I say?
supporter: I would give her a little time. Maybe two or three days? She might need some time to clear her head 
seeker: That's a good idea. What should I say? Should I apologize? 
supporter: Perhaps you could send flowers and a note asking her if she'd like to talk? 
seeker: That's a good idea. I will try that. Thank you.
supporter: She might be feeling receptive to that but if she's not you might have to accept that it's over. 
seeker: Thanks.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-09-06","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hi, what I can help you with today?
seeker: Hi
seeker: I had problems in the past and somehow right now
supporter: What sort of problems were in your past and now?
seeker: I loved physics and I decided to attend university, but soon after I slowly lost my interest and became unmotivated
supporter: What was happening in your life that made you lose interest?
seeker: Actually the professors and the class atmosphere was the reason, and of course the quality of teaching
seeker: so I started to skipping the classes and failing
supporter: It sounds like that is a lot of reasons to be stressed. Have you spoken to a school counselor?
seeker: Yes lots of stress and pressure. I did not, because we didn't have such things or at least I wasn't aware
seeker: But nobody even pointed that why I'm failing, they just didn't care
supporter: I agree it is a lot of pressure, but do not let bad teachers deter you. I would reach out to a school counselor and let them know your situation. Every school must have one. 
supporter: Also, physics is a difficult course to study, but if you chose it, that means you have a very strong mind. 
seeker: I loved physics a lot more than now, but what's the point of studying when the teachers are pulsing you not to study! (because of the quality of teaching)
seeker: I hope there was someone, but I don't think we have a counselor
supporter: More reason to speak to a school counselor or school administrator. We need to provide help to students, not have bad teachers deter them. 
seeker: Yeah, same with me! I wish I could attend a better univeristy
supporter: What made you choose this particular university you are at?
seeker: I didn't have another choice but this
supporter: Have you looked into other Universities for the possibility of transferring
seeker: Hmmm, actually I didn't think about this option
supporter: Just think about what you want in a good university and research from there
seeker: Yeah, I should do it
seeker: Thanks for the talk
seeker: you've been more helpful than my teachers!
supporter: You're welcome I hope you find the perfect university for you
seeker: Thanks, I wish  you luck in your future endeavours
seeker: Bye then ; )
supporter: Goodbye","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-01-25","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

supporter: Of course, Nick. What's on your mind?
seeker: It's my family. We had a pretty big falling out recently over some differences in lifestyle choices.

seeker: I guess I could try, but I'm worried about failing either way. I hate feeling this uncertain.

seeker: Yeah, maybe reaching out to a professor wouldn't be so bad to start with. Thank you for talking this through with me.

seeker: Will do. I'm actually feeling a bit lighter talking about it now.

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hey Nick, how have you been doing lately?
seeker: Hey, it's been a bit tough honestly. I decided to talk to my family about everything that's been happening.
supporter: I'm glad you opened up to them. How did that conversation go?
seeker: It was a relief in some ways. They listened to me, which was good.
supporter: That's great to hear! Did they offer any advice or support?
seeker: They did offer support, but it still feels like they don't fully understand the pressure I'm under with my physics course.
supporter: I can imagine that's frustrating. Do you feel like you got to express everything you wanted to?
seeker: Mostly, yes. But it's hard for them to really grasp the academic stress when they haven't experienced it themselves.
supporter: It's definitely tough when others can't fully relate. How are you handling the pressure now?
seeker: I'm trying to stay on top of my assignments, but the quality of teaching hasn't improved. It feels like a constant uphill battle.
supporter: That sounds really challenging, especially when support isn't available. Have you thought again about possibly dropping the course?
seeker: I have, but it's also hard to think about leaving something unfinished. I don't want to feel like I've failed.
supporter: It's understandable. Remember, taking a step back doesn't mean you're failing—it can be a strategic move for your well-being.
seeker: That's a good point. I just wish there was more support from the university, like better teaching or someone I could talk to.
supporter: Have you considered reaching out to a student advisor or counseling services at your university?
seeker: I've thought about it, but it's a bit intimidating to take that step. I guess I'm worried about not being taken seriously.
supporter: It's totally normal to feel that way. Maybe starting with a small step, like emailing an advisor, could make it feel more manageable.
seeker: That sounds like a good way to ease into it. I think I'll give it a try.
supporter: I'm proud of you for taking this step, Nick. Remember, I'm here for you and you're not alone in this.
seeker: Thanks, I really appreciate it. It helps to know there's someone who understands what I'm going through.
supporter: Anytime, Nick. Keep me posted on how things go with the advisor, okay?
seeker: Will do. Thanks again for being there for me.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-06-05","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hey, I guess I just need someone to talk to right now.
supporter: Of course, Nick. I'm here for you. What's on your mind?
seeker: It's about my physics course again. My professor contacted me today to offer help.
supporter: That sounds like a positive step. How do you feel about it?
seeker: I feel a bit conflicted. On one hand, it's great to know someone cares, but on the other, I'm just so stressed and unsure it can make a difference.
supporter: It's understandable to feel that way, especially after the struggles you've had. Did the professor offer any specific advice?
seeker: Yeah, they suggested a few resources and offered to arrange a tutoring session. But honestly, I'm not sure if it'll help with how behind I am now.
supporter: It's good that they provided some options, but I get that feeling of being in over your head. Have you tried reaching out to other students for support?
seeker: I haven't. I guess I'm just embarrassed by how far I've fallen behind.
supporter: It's tough to ask for help, but remember you're not alone in this. Many students face similar challenges. It might be worth trying to find a study group or even just one buddy to tackle things with.
seeker: That makes sense. I think I could try talking to that one classmate who seemed in a similar spot last semester.
supporter: That's a great idea! You might find you're stronger when working together. And don't forget, you've been through difficult times before, like with your friend incident. You managed to turn things around then.
seeker: Yeah, you're right. I did sort things out with him. It was tough, but I'm glad I pushed through.
supporter: Exactly. You've shown resilience. It's okay to feel stressed, but you've got the strength to push through this as well.
seeker: I hope so. It's just hard to keep motivated when it feels like everything's piling up.
supporter: That's completely valid. Taking small steps can help make those piles seem less overwhelming. Maybe set one small goal to start with.
seeker: That's a good idea. Perhaps I could start by organizing my notes and seeing what's most urgent.
supporter: That sounds like a solid plan, and it'll help clear your head. Remember, you're doing your best and that counts for a lot.
seeker: Thanks for listening. I really appreciate having someone to talk to.
supporter: Anytime, Nick. I'm glad you're opening up, and I'm here whenever you need to talk.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-06-15","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hey, I've been reflecting a lot on my studies lately, and I've decided to make a big change.
supporter: Hey Nick, that sounds like a significant step. What change are you thinking about?
seeker: Well, I've decided to switch my major. I realized physics just wasn't the right fit for me.
supporter: That's a huge decision, Nick. How are you feeling about it?
seeker: I'm a mix of relieved and anxious. Relieved because I've been struggling with it for a while, but anxious because it's a big shift.
supporter: It's understandable to feel both relief and anxiety, especially after making such an important decision. What led you to finally decide?
seeker: I kept remembering how overwhelmed I felt with the assignments and the stress it brought. Talking to my professor helped too, but it made me see I needed a change.
supporter: Your professor seemed like a great support. It's good that they were there for guidance. What new direction are you considering?
seeker: I'm thinking of switching to a major in psychology. I've always been fascinated by how the mind works, and it feels more aligned with my interests.
supporter: Psychology sounds like a fascinating field. It's wonderful that you've found something that resonates more with you. How have your family and friends reacted to your decision?
seeker: I told my family first. They were really understanding, which helped a lot, especially since they know I've been struggling.
supporter: Family support can make a big difference. It's great that they’re understanding about your choice. Have you talked to your classmates or your best friend?
seeker: Not yet. I'm a bit nervous about their reactions, especially since some of them are sticking with physics.
supporter: It’s normal to feel nervous, Nick. Remember, it's about what's right for you. Those who care will likely understand and support your decision.
seeker: Yeah, I guess that's true. Just want to feel like I'm doing the right thing, you know?
supporter: Finding the right path for you is important, and it sounds like you're taking thoughtful steps. Trust yourself in this process.
seeker: Thanks, that means a lot. I'm hoping this new path will be a better fit and lead to less stress.
supporter: I believe you're on the right track, Nick. And remember, it's okay to reach out if you ever need to talk through any worries or changes.
seeker: I will. Thanks for listening and being supportive. It really helps to talk it through.
supporter: Anytime, Nick. I'm here for you. Good luck with everything, and I'm sure you'll do great in psychology.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-07-05","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

seeker: Hey... I've been feeling pretty down recently.

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hey, do you have a moment to chat? I'm feeling a bit overwhelmed.
supporter: Of course, Nick. What's going on?
seeker: I've been swamped with assignments, and it's starting to really wear me down.
supporter: That sounds really tough. Are these assignments from your physics course?
seeker: Yeah, mostly. It's just been so relentless, and I really don't feel any support from the university.

seeker: I've thought about seeking outside resources or maybe talking to a different professor, but it feels daunting.

supporter: Hello. How are you today?
seeker: I'm doing good. I need some advice

seeker: Still though, it makes me want to avoid them when I go to school on the bus

supporter: I understand, school was tough for me too.

seeker: Should I just beat them up with my backpack

supporter: I think that could be a good idea if it's not too far out of your way.

supporter: You could also tell a teacher what is happening. They will help you out.

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hey, I guess I just need someone to talk to right now.
supporter: Of course, Nick. I'm here for you. What's on your mind?
seeker: It's about my physics course again. My professor contacted me today to offer help.
supporter: That sounds like a positive step. How do you feel about it?
seeker: I feel a bit conflicted. On one hand, it's great to know someone cares, but on the other, I'm just so stressed and unsure it can make a difference.
supporter: It's understandable to feel that way, especially after the struggles you've had. Did the professor offer any specific advice?
seeker: Yeah, they suggested a few resources and offered to arrange a tutoring session. But honestly, I'm not sure if it'll help with how behind I am now.
supporter: It's good that they provided some options, but I get that feeling of being in over your head. Have you tried reaching out to other students for support?
seeker: I haven't. I guess I'm just embarrassed by how far I've fallen behind.
supporter: It's tough to ask for help, but remember you're not alone in this. Many students face similar challenges. It might be worth trying to find a study group or even just one buddy to tackle things with.
seeker: That makes sense. I think I could try talking to that one classmate who seemed in a similar spot last semester.
supporter: That's a great idea! You might find you're stronger when working together. And don't forget, you've been through difficult times before, like with your friend incident. You managed to turn things around then.
seeker: Yeah, you're right. I did sort things out with him. It was tough, but I'm glad I pushed through.
supporter: Exactly. You've shown resilience. It's okay to feel stressed, but you've got the strength to push through this as well.
seeker: I hope so. It's just hard to keep motivated when it feels like everything's piling up.
supporter: That's completely valid. Taking small steps can help make those piles seem less overwhelming. Maybe set one small goal to start with.
seeker: That's a good idea. Perhaps I could start by organizing my notes and seeing what's most urgent.
supporter: That sounds like a solid plan, and it'll help clear your head. Remember, you're doing your best and that counts for a lot.
seeker: Thanks for listening. I really appreciate having someone to talk to.
supporter: Anytime, Nick. I'm glad you're opening up, and I'm here whenever you need to talk.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-06-15","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hey, I've been reflecting a lot on my studies lately, and I've decided to make a big change.
supporter: Hey Nick, that sounds like a significant step. What change are you thinking about?
seeker: Well, I've decided to switch my major. I realized physics just wasn't the right fit for me.
supporter: That's a huge decision, Nick. How are you feeling about it?
seeker: I'm a mix of relieved and anxious. Relieved because I've been struggling with it for a while, but anxious because it's a big shift.
supporter: It's understandable to feel both relief and anxiety, especially after making such an important decision. What led you to finally decide?
seeker: I kept remembering how overwhelmed I felt with the assignments and the stress it brought. Talking to my professor helped too, but it made me see I needed a change.
supporter: Your professor seemed like a great support. It's good that they were there for guidance. What new direction are you considering?
seeker: I'm thinking of switching to a major in psychology. I've always been fascinated by how the mind works, and it feels more aligned with my interests.
supporter: Psychology sounds like a fascinating field. It's wonderful that you've found something that resonates more with you. How have your family and friends reacted to your decision?
seeker: I told my family first. They were really understanding, which helped a lot, especially since they know I've been struggling.
supporter: Family support can make a big difference. It's great that they’re understanding about your choice. Have you talked to your classmates or your best friend?
seeker: Not yet. I'm a bit nervous about their reactions, especially since some of them are sticking with physics.
supporter: It’s normal to feel nervous, Nick. Remember, it's about what's right for you. Those who care will likely understand and support your decision.
seeker: Yeah, I guess that's true. Just want to feel like I'm doing the right thing, you know?
supporter: Finding the right path for you is important, and it sounds like you're taking thoughtful steps. Trust yourself in this process.
seeker: Thanks, that means a lot. I'm hoping this new path will be a better fit and lead to less stress.
supporter: I believe you're on the right track, Nick. And remember, it's okay to reach out if you ever need to talk through any worries or changes.
seeker: I will. Thanks for listening and being supportive. It really helps to talk it through.
supporter: Anytime, Nick. I'm here for you. Good luck with everything, and I'm sure you'll do great in psychology.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-07-05","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

seeker: I am doing ok. I just broke up with my girlfriend and sad about it
supporter: so I hear you are not feeling at all your best at the moment? 
seeker: That is correct.
supporter: Do you feel as though you have no-one to talk to about this situation? I am happy to listen. 
seeker: I am so sad and just wonder why did it happen!!!
supporter: Do you have no idea? Do you think you might have done something wrong or perhaps she was being unfaithful to you?

supporter: Do you consider that there might be any hope for the  two of you at all?

supporter: I would give her a little time. Maybe two or three days? She might need some time to clear her head 
seeker: That's a good idea. What should I say? Should I apologize? 
supporter: Perhaps you could send flowers and a note asking her if she'd like to talk? 
seeker: That's a good idea. I will try that. Thank you.

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hello. Is anyone there
supporter: Hello. How are you today?
seeker: I'm doing good. I need some advice
supporter: What can I help you with?
seeker: Lately, my friends started to make jokes about my face being ugly. They even called my face as flat as a pan! What should I do? I see them everyday on the bus
supporter: Have you tried confronting them and asking why they are being bullies?
seeker: I did and they respond by saying that they are just joking and that I'm handsome. But it's starting to get on my nerves because it's all they make fun about every time they see me!
supporter: I'm sure you are very handsome! They could just be jealous.
seeker: Haha I would hope so
seeker: Still though, it makes me want to avoid them when I go to school on the bus
seeker: What do you think I should do then?
supporter: I understand, school was tough for me too.
supporter: I suggest you tell them to knock it off or you can sit somewhere away from the bus.
seeker: Should I just beat them up with my backpack
supporter: No, beating them up will only get you in trouble and that won't help.
seeker: There's another bus route. Should I just take that instead
supporter: I think that could be a good idea if it's not too far out of your way.
seeker: I think I will. Their comments make me very insecure
supporter: You could also tell a teacher what is happening. They will help you out.
supporter: I bet you are handsome! Don't let it get to you.
seeker: The teacher would probably make fun of me!
seeker: Thanks it's hard to look in the mirror now
supporter: Try to tell yourself you are good looking and deserve good things to happen every morning! Look in that mirror and tell yourself good things.
seeker: I'll try to be positive for once.
seeker: Do you believe working out will help
supporter: Working out will help a lot! When I was feeling down on myself I decided to go to the gym three times a week. It was a great confidence boost.
seeker: Awesome. I will start to take care of myself and not worry about others then.
supporter: That sounds like a fantastic idea.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-02-22","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hi, what I can help you with today?
seeker: Hi
seeker: I had problems in the past and somehow right now
supporter: What sort of problems were in your past and now?
seeker: I loved physics and I decided to attend university, but soon after I slowly lost my interest and became unmotivated
supporter: What was happening in your life that made you lose interest?
seeker: Actually the professors and the class atmosphere was the reason, and of course the quality of teaching
seeker: so I started to skipping the classes and failing
supporter: It sounds like that is a lot of reasons to be stressed. Have you spoken to a school counselor?
seeker: Yes lots of stress and pressure. I did not, because we didn't have such things or at least I wasn't aware
seeker: But nobody even pointed that why I'm failing, they just didn't care
supporter: I agree it is a lot of pressure, but do not let bad teachers deter you. I would reach out to a school counselor and let them know your situation. Every school must have one. 
supporter: Also, physics is a difficult course to study, but if you chose it, that means you have a very strong mind. 
seeker: I loved physics a lot more than now, but what's the point of studying when the teachers are pulsing you not to study! (because of the quality of teaching)
seeker: I hope there was someone, but I don't think we have a counselor
supporter: More reason to speak to a school counselor or school administrator. We need to provide help to students, not have bad teachers deter them. 
seeker: Yeah, same with me! I wish I could attend a better univeristy
supporter: What made you choose this particular university you are at?
seeker: I didn't have another choice but this
supporter: Have you looked into other Universities for the possibility of transferring
seeker: Hmmm, actually I didn't think about this option
supporter: Just think about what you want in a good university and research from there
seeker: Yeah, I should do it
seeker: Thanks for the talk
seeker: you've been more helpful than my teachers!
supporter: You're welcome I hope you find the perfect university for you
seeker: Thanks, I wish  you luck in your future endeavours
seeker: Bye then ; )
supporter: Goodbye","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-01-25","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hey, do you have a moment to chat? I'm feeling a bit overwhelmed.
supporter: Of course, Nick. What's going on?
seeker: I've been swamped with assignments, and it's starting to really wear me down.
supporter: That sounds really tough. Are these assignments from your physics course?
seeker: Yeah, mostly. It's just been so relentless, and I really don't feel any support from the university.
supporter: I remember you mentioning before how the teaching quality has been lacking. Has it gotten worse?
seeker: Pretty much. It feels like I'm teaching myself. I'm even thinking of dropping the course.
supporter: That's such a hard decision. Dropping a course can feel like a big step, but you're the one who knows what's best for you.
seeker: Exactly. I just feel like I'm drowning in work with no payoff, you know? It's exhausting.
supporter: Definitely. It's important to weigh the pros and cons though. How do you feel about physics overall?
seeker: I used to love it, but now it's just become a source of stress. I miss being excited about it.
supporter: It's really tough when something you used to love becomes stressful. Is there anything you've considered doing differently to reignite that passion?
seeker: I've thought about seeking outside resources or maybe talking to a different professor, but it feels daunting.
supporter: That's understandable. Sometimes reaching out for help can feel challenging, but it could make a difference. You shouldn't have to tackle this all alone.
seeker: I guess I could try, but I'm worried about failing either way. I hate feeling this uncertain.
supporter: It's okay to feel uncertain, Nick. Remember when you and Henry had that fallout and reconciled? You took a brave step then and it worked out.
seeker: True, I appreciate you bringing that up. It's nice to remember that things can turn around.
supporter: Exactly. You've got the resilience to turn this around too. Maybe start with small steps and see how it feels?
seeker: Yeah, maybe reaching out to a professor wouldn't be so bad to start with. Thank you for talking this through with me.
supporter: Anytime, Nick. I'm always here to support you in any way I can. Let me know how it goes when you take that first step.
seeker: Will do. I'm actually feeling a bit lighter talking about it now.
supporter: I'm glad to hear that. Keep taking care of yourself, okay?","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-05-30","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hey Nick, how have you been doing lately?
seeker: Hey, it's been a bit tough honestly. I decided to talk to my family about everything that's been happening.
supporter: I'm glad you opened up to them. How did that conversation go?
seeker: It was a relief in some ways. They listened to me, which was good.
supporter: That's great to hear! Did they offer any advice or support?
seeker: They did offer support, but it still feels like they don't fully understand the pressure I'm under with my physics course.
supporter: I can imagine that's frustrating. Do you feel like you got to express everything you wanted to?
seeker: Mostly, yes. But it's hard for them to really grasp the academic stress when they haven't experienced it themselves.
supporter: It's definitely tough when others can't fully relate. How are you handling the pressure now?
seeker: I'm trying to stay on top of my assignments, but the quality of teaching hasn't improved. It feels like a constant uphill battle.
supporter: That sounds really challenging, especially when support isn't available. Have you thought again about possibly dropping the course?
seeker: I have, but it's also hard to think about leaving something unfinished. I don't want to feel like I've failed.
supporter: It's understandable. Remember, taking a step back doesn't mean you're failing—it can be a strategic move for your well-being.
seeker: That's a good point. I just wish there was more support from the university, like better teaching or someone I could talk to.
supporter: Have you considered reaching out to a student advisor or counseling services at your university?
seeker: I've thought about it, but it's a bit intimidating to take that step. I guess I'm worried about not being taken seriously.
supporter: It's totally normal to feel that way. Maybe starting with a small step, like emailing an advisor, could make it feel more manageable.
seeker: That sounds like a good way to ease into it. I think I'll give it a try.
supporter: I'm proud of you for taking this step, Nick. Remember, I'm here for you and you're not alone in this.
seeker: Thanks, I really appreciate it. It helps to know there's someone who understands what I'm going through.
supporter: Anytime, Nick. Keep me posted on how things go with the advisor, okay?
seeker: Will do. Thanks again for being there for me.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-06-05","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hey, I guess I just need someone to talk to right now.
supporter: Of course, Nick. I'm here for you. What's on your mind?
seeker: It's about my physics course again. My professor contacted me today to offer help.
supporter: That sounds like a positive step. How do you feel about it?
seeker: I feel a bit conflicted. On one hand, it's great to know someone cares, but on the other, I'm just so stressed and unsure it can make a difference.
supporter: It's understandable to feel that way, especially after the struggles you've had. Did the professor offer any specific advice?
seeker: Yeah, they suggested a few resources and offered to arrange a tutoring session. But honestly, I'm not sure if it'll help with how behind I am now.
supporter: It's good that they provided some options, but I get that feeling of being in over your head. Have you tried reaching out to other students for support?
seeker: I haven't. I guess I'm just embarrassed by how far I've fallen behind.
supporter: It's tough to ask for help, but remember you're not alone in this. Many students face similar challenges. It might be worth trying to find a study group or even just one buddy to tackle things with.
seeker: That makes sense. I think I could try talking to that one classmate who seemed in a similar spot last semester.
supporter: That's a great idea! You might find you're stronger when working together. And don't forget, you've been through difficult times before, like with your friend incident. You managed to turn things around then.
seeker: Yeah, you're right. I did sort things out with him. It was tough, but I'm glad I pushed through.
supporter: Exactly. You've shown resilience. It's okay to feel stressed, but you've got the strength to push through this as well.
seeker: I hope so. It's just hard to keep motivated when it feels like everything's piling up.
supporter: That's completely valid. Taking small steps can help make those piles seem less overwhelming. Maybe set one small goal to start with.
seeker: That's a good idea. Perhaps I could start by organizing my notes and seeing what's most urgent.
supporter: That sounds like a solid plan, and it'll help clear your head. Remember, you're doing your best and that counts for a lot.
seeker: Thanks for listening. I really appreciate having someone to talk to.
supporter: Anytime, Nick. I'm glad you're opening up, and I'm here whenever you need to talk.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-06-15","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hey, I've been reflecting a lot on my studies lately, and I've decided to make a big change.
supporter: Hey Nick, that sounds like a significant step. What change are you thinking about?
seeker: Well, I've decided to switch my major. I realized physics just wasn't the right fit for me.
supporter: That's a huge decision, Nick. How are you feeling about it?
seeker: I'm a mix of relieved and anxious. Relieved because I've been struggling with it for a while, but anxious because it's a big shift.
supporter: It's understandable to feel both relief and anxiety, especially after making such an important decision. What led you to finally decide?
seeker: I kept remembering how overwhelmed I felt with the assignments and the stress it brought. Talking to my professor helped too, but it made me see I needed a change.
supporter: Your professor seemed like a great support. It's good that they were there for guidance. What new direction are you considering?
seeker: I'm thinking of switching to a major in psychology. I've always been fascinated by how the mind works, and it feels more aligned with my interests.
supporter: Psychology sounds like a fascinating field. It's wonderful that you've found something that resonates more with you. How have your family and friends reacted to your decision?
seeker: I told my family first. They were really understanding, which helped a lot, especially since they know I've been struggling.
supporter: Family support can make a big difference. It's great that they’re understanding about your choice. Have you talked to your classmates or your best friend?
seeker: Not yet. I'm a bit nervous about their reactions, especially since some of them are sticking with physics.
supporter: It’s normal to feel nervous, Nick. Remember, it's about what's right for you. Those who care will likely understand and support your decision.
seeker: Yeah, I guess that's true. Just want to feel like I'm doing the right thing, you know?
supporter: Finding the right path for you is important, and it sounds like you're taking thoughtful steps. Trust yourself in this process.
seeker: Thanks, that means a lot. I'm hoping this new path will be a better fit and lead to less stress.
supporter: I believe you're on the right track, Nick. And remember, it's okay to reach out if you ever need to talk through any worries or changes.
seeker: I will. Thanks for listening and being supportive. It really helps to talk it through.
supporter: Anytime, Nick. I'm here for you. Good luck with everything, and I'm sure you'll do great in psychology.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-07-05","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

supporter: Hello. How are you today?

supporter: What can I help you with?
seeker: Lately, my friends started to make jokes about my face being ugly. They even called my face as flat as a pan! What should I do? I see them everyday on the bus
supporter: Have you tried confronting them and asking why they are being bullies?
seeker: I did and they respond by saying that they are just joking and that I'm handsome. But it's starting to get on my nerves because it's all they make fun about every time they see me!
supporter: I'm sure you are very handsome! They could just be jealous.

supporter: I understand, school was tough for me too.

supporter: That sounds like a fantastic idea.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-02-22","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hello, how is your life at the moment? Do you want to talk about anything? 
seeker: I am doing ok. I just broke up with my girlfriend and sad about it
supporter: so I hear you are not feeling at all your best at the moment? 
seeker: That is correct.
supporter: Do you feel as though you have no-one to talk to about this situation? I am happy to listen. 
seeker: I am so sad and just wonder why did it happen!!!
supporter: Do you have no idea? Do you think you might have done something wrong or perhaps she was being unfaithful to you? 
seeker: We had simple disagreement and both of us were keep fighting.. now I can not get over it.
supporter: Do you consider that there might be any hope for the  two of you at all? 
seeker: I don't know. What should I do?
supporter: Well, I think you should give her some space but people do sometimes get back together after they've separated 
seeker: I see your point.

supporter: I would give her a little time. Maybe two or three days? She might need some time to clear her head

seeker: That's a good idea. I will try that. Thank you.
supporter: She might be feeling receptive to that but if she's not you might have to accept that it's over. 
seeker: Thanks.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-09-06","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hi, what I can help you with today?
seeker: Hi
seeker: I had problems in the past and somehow right now
supporter: What sort of problems were in your past and now?
seeker: I loved physics and I decided to attend university, but soon after I slowly lost my interest and became unmotivated
supporter: What was happening in your life that made you lose interest?
seeker: Actually the professors and the class atmosphere was the reason, and of course the quality of teaching
seeker: so I started to skipping the classes and failing
supporter: It sounds like that is a lot of reasons to be stressed. Have you spoken to a school counselor?
seeker: Yes lots of stress and pressure. I did not, because we didn't have such things or at least I wasn't aware
seeker: But nobody even pointed that why I'm failing, they just didn't care
supporter: I agree it is a lot of pressure, but do not let bad teachers deter you. I would reach out to a school counselor and let them know your situation. Every school must have one. 
supporter: Also, physics is a difficult course to study, but if you chose it, that means you have a very strong mind. 
seeker: I loved physics a lot more than now, but what's the point of studying when the teachers are pulsing you not to study! (because of the quality of teaching)
seeker: I hope there was someone, but I don't think we have a counselor
supporter: More reason to speak to a school counselor or school administrator. We need to provide help to students, not have bad teachers deter them. 
seeker: Yeah, same with me! I wish I could attend a better univeristy
supporter: What made you choose this particular university you are at?
seeker: I didn't have another choice but this
supporter: Have you looked into other Universities for the possibility of transferring
seeker: Hmmm, actually I didn't think about this option
supporter: Just think about what you want in a good university and research from there
seeker: Yeah, I should do it
seeker: Thanks for the talk
seeker: you've been more helpful than my teachers!
supporter: You're welcome I hope you find the perfect university for you
seeker: Thanks, I wish  you luck in your future endeavours
seeker: Bye then ; )
supporter: Goodbye","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-01-25","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hey Nick, how have you been feeling lately?
seeker: Hey... I've been feeling pretty down recently.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. Do you want to talk about what's been going on?
seeker: Yeah, it's about Henry. We argued again, and this time it got ugly.
supporter: That sounds tough. What happened between you two?
seeker: It started with some jokes they made. I found them really insensitive and hurtful.
supporter: I can understand why that would be upsetting. Did you talk to them about how you felt?
seeker: I tried, but it just turned into a shouting match. I didn't expect it would escalate.
supporter: That sounds really frustrating. It can be hard when someone you care about doesn't understand your perspective.
seeker: Exactly. I mean, we've been friends for so long. I thought we'd be on the same page about these things.
supporter: It's natural to feel disappointed in situations like this. It's okay to feel hurt.
seeker: Thanks. I just can't help but think if maybe I'm overreacting.
supporter: Your feelings are valid, Nick. It's important to acknowledge when something bothers you.
seeker: True, but what if I drive him away by holding onto this?
supporter: It might help to express why those jokes affected you deeply. If he's a true friend, he should understand and respect your feelings.
seeker: Yeah, I think I should try talking to him when things cool down. I don't want to lose our friendship over this.
supporter: That sounds like a good plan. Give it some time, and approach it when you're both calmer.
seeker: I will. Thanks for listening. It really helps to talk it through.
supporter: Anytime, Nick. I'm here whenever you need to chat or get things off your chest.
seeker: I appreciate that. Hopefully, next time we'll be talking about something more positive!
supporter: I'm sure we will. Hang in there, Nick. You've got this.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-03-01","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hey, do you have a moment to talk?
supporter: Of course, Nick. What's on your mind?
seeker: It's my family. We had a pretty big falling out recently over some differences in lifestyle choices.
supporter: I'm really sorry to hear that. Family conflicts can be really tough to deal with. Do you want to share more about what happened?
seeker: Well, it's just... they don't really agree with how I'm choosing to live my life now that I'm at university, especially with my decision to switch majors and my relationship with Sally.
supporter: It sounds like they're having a hard time accepting your choices. That's really frustrating, especially when you're trying to follow your own path.
seeker: Exactly. I just feel like they don't understand my perspective or even try to.
supporter: Have you been able to communicate how you're feeling to them, or what these choices mean to you?
seeker: I tried, but it just ended up becoming another argument. I honestly feel worn out trying to explain myself sometimes.
supporter: It's important to take care of yourself first. Maybe giving everyone some space could help calm things down before the next conversation.
seeker: Yeah, I think that's a good idea. It's just hard because I really value their opinion, but I also know I have to live my own life.
supporter: Balancing your own needs with family expectations can be challenging, but it's crucial to stay true to yourself.
seeker: I know. And I can't help but feel like I'm disappointing them sometimes.
supporter: It's understandable to feel that way, but remember, you're making decisions that are best for you and your future.
seeker: Thanks for reminding me of that. It's just not easy, you know?
supporter: Absolutely, I get it. It won't always feel easy, but you're building a life you believe in. That's something to be proud of.
seeker: You're right. And I have people like you and Sally who understand and support me.
supporter: That's so important, Nick. Surrounding yourself with supportive people can make a huge difference. You're not alone in this.
seeker: Thanks. I appreciate having someone to talk to who understands.
supporter: Anytime, Nick. I'm here whenever you need to talk. You're doing great, really.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-10-25","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

supporter: Of course, Nick! What's on your mind?
seeker: I've been feeling a bit disconnected lately, even though I joined a new club at university.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. Joining a club was a great step, though. What's been making you feel disconnected?
seeker: I guess it's just hard to break the ice. Everyone seems to know each other already.
supporter: I get that. It can be tough when it feels like you're the odd one out. Have you managed to talk to anyone there yet?

supporter: That can definitely make it feel isolating. Were there any members who seemed particularly approachable?
seeker: There was this one guy, Alex, who seemed friendly. We talked a bit about our coursework.
supporter: That's a great start! Maybe you could suggest grabbing coffee or doing something casual outside the club to get to know each other better?
seeker: Yeah, I was thinking about that. I just get nervous about reaching out.
supporter: It's understandable to feel nervous. Remember how you rekindled things with Sally—taking small steps can lead to meaningful connections.
seeker: You're right. That took some courage, and it really paid off in the end.
supporter: Absolutely. You've shown before that you can handle stepping outside your comfort zone.
seeker: Thanks for reminding me. I think I just need to trust myself more.
supporter: Exactly. And remember, it's okay if things don't go perfectly at first. It's all about making genuine efforts.
seeker: True, I'll keep that in mind. I'll try to reach out to Alex next week.
supporter: That's a solid plan. I'm proud of you for taking this step, Nick.
