{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: My friend Lisa borrowed money from me but she won't return it now
supporter: I am sorry about that. It is always hard when we trust someone and they let us down. is that waht you are feeling? Disappointment in your friend?
seeker: Yes,i am very dissapointed because i trusted her completely.
supporter: I understand. I have been through a similar situation.
supporter: Was it a large amount of money?
seeker: What did you do to come out of the tricky situation?
seeker: Yes,it was for me,a total of $10000
supporter: Oh, That is a very large amount of money. I can understand your being upset with them
supporter: Have you talked to them about the money and returning it?
seeker: Yes,i am very very upset.What would you do in my position?
seeker: Yes,she just sounded non-comittal,saying that she will return it when she can
supporter: I see. It is a financially difficult time for us all. I am wondering if your friend might be upset and embarrassed that they can not pay you back immediately? Have you asked her if she could even afford some sort of small payments?
seeker: Yes,i asked her how we could restructure the payment in her favor because i understand how difficult it is for everyone right now but she did not answer
supporter: Were you speaking on the phone or in person? Is this a financial burden for you?
supporter: Would you consider this person a good friend? Would you be sad if they were not in your life anymore?
seeker: We were speaking on phone because i wanted to set up a physical meeting where we could discuss the logistics
seeker: Yes,it is a financial burden because this is money i was saving for a venture
supporter: That is very difficult. It is hard to judge things on the phone. 
seeker: Yes,this is a really close friend from way back and i would be devastated to lose the friendship
seeker: It is difficult to judge on the phone yes,which is why i wanted a physical meeting but she snapped at me and said that she will just pay me when she can
supporter: I see. I am very sorry about that! it is very difficult when a friend betrays your trust like that. 
seeker: Yes,very difficult
supporter: It sounds like you are doing what you can. It is very nice of you to have been this patient.
seeker: How do you suggest i shoulp proceed?
supporter: Is the friendship more important than the money? That is what it came down to for me.
seeker: And you chose what?
supporter: If you can not get her to meet with you, perhaps it might be time to seek advice from a lawyer? That is providing that you are willing to possibly lose a friend. 
seeker: Thank you very much for the advice
supporter: you are welcome. Good luck! I hope you find resolution and find a way to save your friendship!","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-10-05","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hey Jane, how have you been holding up lately?
seeker: Hi. Not too great, to be honest. It's been a rough couple of weeks.
supporter: I'm really sorry to hear that. Would you like to talk about what's been going on?
seeker: Well, do you remember Lisa? My friend I mentioned before?
supporter: Yes, I remember you talking about them. What's up with Lisa?
seeker: So, we've hit this weird and stressful snag. I lent her some money months ago and she hasn’t paid me back yet.
supporter: That definitely sounds stressful. How is it affecting your relationship with Lisa?
seeker: She's completely cut off communication with me. No calls, texts, nothing.
supporter: That must be really hard on you, especially since she was such a close friend.
seeker: It feels like losing a part of my life. We used to hang out all the time and now it's just silence.
supporter: It sounds like you're mourning the loss of that friendship. Have you had a chance to reach out or communicate with her recently?
seeker: I’ve tried. Sent a couple of messages, but they’ve gone unanswered.
supporter: It must feel really disappointing not to hear back. What do you miss most about your friendship with Lisa?
seeker: We used to bounce ideas off each other, and she was the first person I'd call when something great happened at work.
supporter: It's understandable to miss those shared moments and support. How are you managing everything else alongside this?
seeker: It's made focusing on work tough. I feel a bit isolated, honestly.
supporter: I'm so sorry you're feeling this way. Feeling isolated can really weigh on you. Is there anyone else you feel comfortable confiding in?
seeker: I haven't really opened up to anyone else about this. It's been hard admitting to myself how deep this issue has affected me.
supporter: It takes a lot of courage to open up. It's important to take time for yourself and process everything. Is there anything you can do to help ease your mind a bit right now?
seeker: Maybe get back into some hobbies. I used to enjoy painting but haven't done it in a while.
supporter: That sounds like a wonderful idea. Engaging in something creative can be really therapeutic. Would you like support picking it back up?
seeker: I think that would help. Just getting started again might lift this weight a little.
supporter: I'm here to support you with this. Whenever you're ready, you can share your progress, and I’d love to hear how it goes.
seeker: Thank you. It feels a bit better knowing someone’s there to listen. I appreciate it.
supporter: Anytime, Jane. You’re not alone in this. We'll take it one step at a time.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-10-15","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hey, feeling a bit all over the place today. Mind if I share?
supporter: Of course, Jane. I'm here to listen. What's been going on?
seeker: Well, you know how Eliza and I had that big fight about her wedding?
supporter: Yes, you’ve mentioned feeling misunderstood during that time. How are things between you two now?
seeker: We actually had a really deep conversation a few days ago. Lots of tears but good ones, I think.
supporter: That sounds intense but potentially healing. How did that feel for you?
seeker: It was a mix of relief and lingering sadness. I’m happy we cleared the air, but all those pent-up emotions were exhausting.
supporter: It makes sense to feel drained after such a heart-to-heart. It's brave of you both to confront those emotions together.
seeker: Thanks. I just wish it didn't have to get so messy before getting better.
supporter: Relationships can be messy, but the reconciling part is important. How’s your perspective on everything now?
seeker: I feel closer to her actually. We both admitted how much the wedding planning has stressed us out.
supporter: That’s insightful. Acknowledging shared stress can bring people together. How’s the wedding planning going now?
seeker: Better. We’ve agreed to communicate openly about decisions. It feels more like a partnership now, rather than me just helping her.
supporter: That’s great to hear, Jane. Open communication is key in any relationship.
seeker: Yeah, I've also started journaling again. It helps sort through these complicated feelings.
supporter: Journaling is a great tool. How does writing about your thoughts and emotions help you?
seeker: It gives me clarity. Putting pen to paper makes everything feel less overwhelming and more manageable.
supporter: I’m glad it’s helping you. Have you noticed any other changes since you reconciled with Eliza?
seeker: I feel a bit lighter emotionally. Mending the rift with her feels like a burden lifted.
supporter: That’s a beautiful way to put it. Rebuilding that connection must feel rewarding.
seeker: It does. I’m also trying to be more proactive about addressing my financial stress instead of letting it control me.
supporter: That’s a positive step forward. You've been through a lot, and it’s important to take care of yourself too.
seeker: Trying my best. It’s a work in progress, you know? Balancing everything is tough.
supporter: Absolutely. You’re making great progress, even if it doesn’t always feel that way. I’m here whenever you need to talk.
seeker: Thank you, that means a lot. I’ll keep leaning on you if that's okay.
supporter: Always, Jane. Your journey is important, and I’m here to support you along the way.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-03-20","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hi, I really need to talk.
supporter: Of course, Jane. I'm here for you. What's on your mind?
seeker: It's about Jack. He tried reaching out to me again, and it really threw me off.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that, Jane. How did you feel when he contacted you?
seeker: Honestly, I felt a wave of anxiety and a bit of anger. I thought I was moving on, you know?
supporter: That sounds really tough. It's understandable to have those feelings, especially when someone from your past re-emerges unexpectedly.
seeker: Yeah, it's like all those feelings I had during our breakup came rushing back.
supporter: Breakups can leave a lasting impact, especially if things ended with unresolved issues. What worries you the most about Jack reaching out?
seeker: I guess I'm afraid of falling back into habits that were bad for me, like constantly questioning myself. We had a pretty toxic dynamic at times.
supporter: It's important that you're aware of the impact he had on you. It sounds like you're protecting yourself, which is a good step.
seeker: I'm trying. But it's hard when I think of all the other stressors in my life, like work and money. Everything feels so overwhelming.
supporter: It must be really challenging juggling all these pressures at once. Have you found anything that helps you manage when things get overwhelming?
seeker: Writing in my journal sometimes helps, but lately, I find it hard to focus or even sleep well.
supporter: Journaling is a great tool, and it's understandable that sleep and focus might be affected by anxiety. Do you have any relaxation techniques that help at night?
seeker: I try breathing exercises, but my mind races a lot. Maybe I need to establish a better nighttime routine.
supporter: That sounds like a good idea. A consistent routine can sometimes make a difference. Have you considered reaching out for professional help to guide you through this?
seeker: I have thought about therapy, but I'm worried about the cost, especially with my financial situation.
supporter: That's a valid concern. Some therapists offer sliding scales or there may be community resources available. It might be worth exploring if it can help you find balance.
seeker: I'll look into it. Just talking to you has helped a bit already.
supporter: I'm really glad to hear that. I'm always here whenever you need to talk. Take it one step at a time, Jane.
seeker: Thank you. It feels good to know I'm not alone in this.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-05-01","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hey, do you have a moment to chat?
supporter: Of course, Jane. What's on your mind?
seeker: I got a message out of the blue from someone I used to be really close with. It's brought up so many mixed feelings.
supporter: That sounds complicated. Who was it, if you don't mind sharing?
seeker: It was from my old friend, who I haven't spoken to since the whole money situation last year.
supporter: Ah, I remember you mentioned them before. It's understandable that you'd feel a bit caught off guard.
seeker: Yeah, exactly. Part of me is nostalgic, but another part of me is wary. I don't want to go through that emotional turmoil again.
supporter: It's natural to have those feelings when someone from the past reaches out, especially given what transpired.
seeker: I just can't shake off the memory of how it ended. Losing a friend like that was tough.
supporter: It must've been really hard. Do you feel like you're ready to respond, or do you need more time to process?
seeker: I'm really unsure. A part of me misses the friendship, but I'm scared of being hurt again.
supporter: Both of those feelings make a lot of sense. It's important to protect your heart while also honoring what used to be.
seeker: Right. I also think back to how stressful things were—like with my job performance review and financial stress. It was too much.
supporter: Those were tough times for you. It shows how much strength it took for you to get through them.
seeker: Thanks. I guess I'm just worried that engaging in any more complicated relationships could bring back old stressors.
supporter: I completely understand your apprehension. Do you think setting boundaries might help if you decide to reconnect?
seeker: That might be a good idea. It could prevent past issues from repeating.
supporter: And if you ever feel overwhelmed, remember you can always pause and take the time you need.
seeker: You're right. I'll think about what I want and maybe draft a response if that time comes.
supporter: That sounds like a solid plan. It's all about doing what's best for you.
seeker: Thanks for listening. I just needed to get that off my chest.
supporter: Anytime, Jane. I'm here if you need to talk more.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-08-05","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hey, I'm feeling a bit overwhelmed today.
supporter: Hi Jane, I'm here for you. What's on your mind?
seeker: My sister Eliza just announced her engagement.

seeker: Hey, not the best to be honest. Things aren't getting any better.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. Do you want to talk about what's been going on?

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hey! How are you?
seeker: Hi, I am having a really hard time. I just found out that my boyfriend cheated on me a year ago.
supporter: Have you confronted him about it yet?
seeker: Yes, I told him that my best friend confessed it to me. It was my best friend and him. I was so shocked.
supporter: Have you broken up yet?
seeker: No, I am so mad but I don't want to break up with him. I told my best friends that I never want to see her again though. My boyfriend and I have plans to get engaged this month. I am furious at him though.
supporter: I think you should postpone the engagement as infidelity during marriage is far more painful
supporter: You are strong if you are able to forgive him though because I know I wouldn't 
seeker: I have never been so blind sided. Maybe I should reconsider! I have had a guy after me for at least the last year but I never cheated! I really wanted to though.
supporter: No you should never cheat, because you would be on the same wavelength as your boyfriend. Instead, if you like the other man then you should go where your feelings take you :)
seeker: I am thinking that you are right. I feel like my whole world is upside down and I have wasted all this time with the wrong guy and the wrong best friend. I also wonder who else he might have cheated on my with. 
supporter: Yeah, that might be true, a relationship isn't healthy if you are cheated on
seeker: I am so grossed out because I am a germaphobe to begin with. I have not slept with any other person in my whole life so I feel like I am ruined. I want to throw up when I think of him cheating on me. I want to get married and I have a timeline so I am also really confused on what to do if I dump him.
supporter: To dump him is the best thing to do in my opinion. But always go where your heart is, because you won't be happy if you don't. If you do though, there are plenty men out there, and one of them is chasing you
seeker: Yeah, the guy who liked me was super rich too! My boyfriend is telling me that he wants my best friend to still be in the wedding party too. She was suppose to be my maid of honor, no less.
supporter: Yeah, but don't go with him because of he money though, genuinely get to know him first
seeker: I have compartmentalized my life and never thought of looking around at my other options. You are making really good points. I need to just stop and really look at my options. I never realized that I have options, it's not like i am even engaged yet.
supporter: Yeah, you have a lot of options at this stage, so always do what your heart is telling you at the end of the day
seeker: It feels good sharing how I feel with you because you don't have a dog in the fight so to speak.
supporter: yeah, lool something like that ;). Glad your better
seeker: I never listen to my heart and think that is a great place to start. I always have a plan and go with that but you are making a lot of sense. Thank you for your time today.
supporter: Your welcome ;)
seeker: Have a great day and I might be back soon to give an update.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-09-01","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: I am worried about being perfect on my job.  I don't want to lose my job.
supporter: I hear you are trying to be perfect on your job because you are worried about losing your job.  How long have you been at your job?
seeker: I have been working for about 4 months, but I just am not as fast at it as everyone else.  I'm trying so hard working late and everything but it's never enough.
supporter: That can be hard when you are working so hard to try to do your best.  Can you consult with a supervisor or co-workers to get some help?
seeker: Maybe I could ask my friend and co-worker for some tips.  I'm a little embarrassed to do so, but don't know where to turn. I don't want to get fired.
supporter: Asking for help isn't always a bad thing.  I asked for help at my last job and they gave me someone to help out.  I was so relieved.
seeker: That's true maybe it could turn out for the better.  But what if they see me as incompetant?
supporter: I can see that you have worry of being seen incompetent but as long as you are doing your best, they have to see the efforts you are making as positive.
seeker: That's a good way to put it.
supporter: Sometimes deep breaths can help keep you calm when approaching others in an anxiety provoking situation.
seeker: I will have to try that.  That might help.
supporter: Have you thought of doing additional work related trainings?  Sometimes they can give suggestions to improve work abilities.
seeker: That sounds great.  Do you think my work would be supportive?
supporter: Work can often pay for trainings or offer suggestions what may improve work strategies.
seeker: Wow, I hope I can take advantage of that.  I will have to check into that.  Who should I approach at work?
supporter: You could ask your immediate supervisor or sometimes Human resources for support.
seeker: I can do that.  I think I'll reach out tomorrow to Human Resources for some help.
supporter: That sounds like a good plan to reach out for support.  Is there anything else I can help with?
seeker: No that should be all.  I am feeling more confident in strategies to use to help me.  Thanks
supporter: You are very welcome.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-11-01","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

supporter: That definitely sounds stressful. How is it affecting your relationship with Lisa?
seeker: She's completely cut off communication with me. No calls, texts, nothing.
supporter: That must be really hard on you, especially since she was such a close friend.

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hi, I really need to talk.
supporter: Of course, Jane. I'm here for you. What's on your mind?
seeker: It's about Jack. He tried reaching out to me again, and it really threw me off.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that, Jane. How did you feel when he contacted you?
seeker: Honestly, I felt a wave of anxiety and a bit of anger. I thought I was moving on, you know?
supporter: That sounds really tough. It's understandable to have those feelings, especially when someone from your past re-emerges unexpectedly.
seeker: Yeah, it's like all those feelings I had during our breakup came rushing back.
supporter: Breakups can leave a lasting impact, especially if things ended with unresolved issues. What worries you the most about Jack reaching out?
seeker: I guess I'm afraid of falling back into habits that were bad for me, like constantly questioning myself. We had a pretty toxic dynamic at times.
supporter: It's important that you're aware of the impact he had on you. It sounds like you're protecting yourself, which is a good step.
seeker: I'm trying. But it's hard when I think of all the other stressors in my life, like work and money. Everything feels so overwhelming.
supporter: It must be really challenging juggling all these pressures at once. Have you found anything that helps you manage when things get overwhelming?
seeker: Writing in my journal sometimes helps, but lately, I find it hard to focus or even sleep well.
supporter: Journaling is a great tool, and it's understandable that sleep and focus might be affected by anxiety. Do you have any relaxation techniques that help at night?
seeker: I try breathing exercises, but my mind races a lot. Maybe I need to establish a better nighttime routine.
supporter: That sounds like a good idea. A consistent routine can sometimes make a difference. Have you considered reaching out for professional help to guide you through this?
seeker: I have thought about therapy, but I'm worried about the cost, especially with my financial situation.
supporter: That's a valid concern. Some therapists offer sliding scales or there may be community resources available. It might be worth exploring if it can help you find balance.
seeker: I'll look into it. Just talking to you has helped a bit already.
supporter: I'm really glad to hear that. I'm always here whenever you need to talk. Take it one step at a time, Jane.
seeker: Thank you. It feels good to know I'm not alone in this.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-05-01","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

supporter: Of course, Jane. What's going on?
seeker: I just got hit with an unexpected bill, and it's really stressing me out.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. Financial stress can be so overwhelming. Do you want to talk more about the bill?
seeker: Yeah, it's for my car insurance. I thought I had paid it, but apparently, there was some sort of oversight, and now I owe more than I expected.
supporter: That sounds frustrating, especially when you're already stretched thin. How are you handling it so far?
seeker: Honestly, not well. I'm feeling pretty anxious about it because money has been tight lately, especially since the whole situation with my friend.
supporter: I remember you mentioned that. It must be tough still dealing with those effects. How does that add to your current stress?
seeker: It just feels like a never-ending cycle. Losing that friendship was hard, and now this bill feels like another setback.
supporter: That's completely understandable. It's like everything piles up at once. How are you coping with these feelings?
seeker: I've been trying to budget more strictly and cut unnecessary expenses, but unexpected things keep popping up.
supporter: That can make it feel like you're running in place, right? Are there any specific concerns you're dwelling on?
seeker: I'm worried I'll fall behind on other payments. I hate feeling this insecure financially. I just want to feel stable again.

supporter: It's okay to ask for help, Jane. You've been doing so much on your own. Sometimes, a fresh perspective makes all the difference.

supporter: I'm glad to hear that. You're handling this situation with a lot of grace, even if it doesn't feel like it right now.
seeker: Thanks. It helps to talk about it. I'm feeling a little more at ease just expressing what's been on my mind.
supporter: Anytime, Jane. I'm here for you whenever you need to talk.

seeker: Hi, I'm okay, I guess. I got a new journal today to help me figure things out.

supporter: It must be difficult to juggle work with all these thoughts in your mind. Do you feel like journaling might help untangle some of them?

supporter: Starting is often the hardest part, but it sounds like you're on the right track. Taking time for yourself can be really healing. What do you hope to gain from journaling?

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hi, just needed someone to talk to.
supporter: Hi Jane! Of course, I'm here for you. What's on your mind?
seeker: I had my performance review at work today... and it wasn't great.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. It sounds like it must be really tough to hear. How are you feeling about it?
seeker: I'm feeling anxious and a bit of self-doubt creeping in. I thought I was handling everything okay.
supporter: It's completely understandable to feel that way. It seems like there's been a lot on your plate recently. Would you like to talk more about it?
seeker: I guess everything's just been snowballing since the thing with Lisa. I still can't believe how it all fell apart.
supporter: Losing a friend, especially over something like money, can feel really isolating. How has it been affecting you lately?
seeker: It's made focusing on work harder. And getting hit with that unexpected bill last month didn't help. Everything feels out of control.
supporter: It sounds like you're dealing with a lot of financial and emotional stress right now. It's a lot for anyone to handle. How have you been coping with it all?
seeker: I started writing in a journal. It helps sometimes, but the stress keeps piling up. I thought it would get better by now.
supporter: Journaling can be a great outlet. It's important to give yourself grace with everything happening. You're doing your best in a really challenging time.
seeker: Thank you. I keep telling myself that, but it's hard to believe it sometimes. I just wish things would turn around.
supporter: It makes sense to want things to improve quickly. Progress can be slow, but you're taking steps in the right direction by reaching out and processing everything going on.
seeker: Yeah, it helps to talk about it. I suppose I need to take it one day at a time.
supporter: Absolutely. It's like building a path through all these challenges— day by day, step by step. You have the strength to navigate this, even if it doesn't feel like it sometimes.
seeker: I really appreciate your support. It makes things feel a bit less overwhelming.
supporter: I'm glad to be here for you. Remember, you're not alone in this. We can keep talking anytime you need.
seeker: Thanks a lot. I might take you up on that.
supporter: Anytime, Jane. Take care of yourself, and reach out whenever you need to.
seeker: Will do. Take care, too.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-11-05","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hey! How are you?
seeker: Hi, I am having a really hard time. I just found out that my boyfriend cheated on me a year ago.
supporter: Have you confronted him about it yet?
seeker: Yes, I told him that my best friend confessed it to me. It was my best friend and him. I was so shocked.
supporter: Have you broken up yet?
seeker: No, I am so mad but I don't want to break up with him. I told my best friends that I never want to see her again though. My boyfriend and I have plans to get engaged this month. I am furious at him though.
supporter: I think you should postpone the engagement as infidelity during marriage is far more painful
supporter: You are strong if you are able to forgive him though because I know I wouldn't 
seeker: I have never been so blind sided. Maybe I should reconsider! I have had a guy after me for at least the last year but I never cheated! I really wanted to though.
supporter: No you should never cheat, because you would be on the same wavelength as your boyfriend. Instead, if you like the other man then you should go where your feelings take you :)
seeker: I am thinking that you are right. I feel like my whole world is upside down and I have wasted all this time with the wrong guy and the wrong best friend. I also wonder who else he might have cheated on my with. 
supporter: Yeah, that might be true, a relationship isn't healthy if you are cheated on
seeker: I am so grossed out because I am a germaphobe to begin with. I have not slept with any other person in my whole life so I feel like I am ruined. I want to throw up when I think of him cheating on me. I want to get married and I have a timeline so I am also really confused on what to do if I dump him.
supporter: To dump him is the best thing to do in my opinion. But always go where your heart is, because you won't be happy if you don't. If you do though, there are plenty men out there, and one of them is chasing you
seeker: Yeah, the guy who liked me was super rich too! My boyfriend is telling me that he wants my best friend to still be in the wedding party too. She was suppose to be my maid of honor, no less.
supporter: Yeah, but don't go with him because of he money though, genuinely get to know him first
seeker: I have compartmentalized my life and never thought of looking around at my other options. You are making really good points. I need to just stop and really look at my options. I never realized that I have options, it's not like i am even engaged yet.
supporter: Yeah, you have a lot of options at this stage, so always do what your heart is telling you at the end of the day
seeker: It feels good sharing how I feel with you because you don't have a dog in the fight so to speak.
supporter: yeah, lool something like that ;). Glad your better
seeker: I never listen to my heart and think that is a great place to start. I always have a plan and go with that but you are making a lot of sense. Thank you for your time today.
supporter: Your welcome ;)
seeker: Have a great day and I might be back soon to give an update.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-09-01","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: I am worried about being perfect on my job.  I don't want to lose my job.
supporter: I hear you are trying to be perfect on your job because you are worried about losing your job.  How long have you been at your job?
seeker: I have been working for about 4 months, but I just am not as fast at it as everyone else.  I'm trying so hard working late and everything but it's never enough.
supporter: That can be hard when you are working so hard to try to do your best.  Can you consult with a supervisor or co-workers to get some help?
seeker: Maybe I could ask my friend and co-worker for some tips.  I'm a little embarrassed to do so, but don't know where to turn. I don't want to get fired.
supporter: Asking for help isn't always a bad thing.  I asked for help at my last job and they gave me someone to help out.  I was so relieved.
seeker: That's true maybe it could turn out for the better.  But what if they see me as incompetant?
supporter: I can see that you have worry of being seen incompetent but as long as you are doing your best, they have to see the efforts you are making as positive.
seeker: That's a good way to put it.
supporter: Sometimes deep breaths can help keep you calm when approaching others in an anxiety provoking situation.
seeker: I will have to try that.  That might help.
supporter: Have you thought of doing additional work related trainings?  Sometimes they can give suggestions to improve work abilities.
seeker: That sounds great.  Do you think my work would be supportive?
supporter: Work can often pay for trainings or offer suggestions what may improve work strategies.
seeker: Wow, I hope I can take advantage of that.  I will have to check into that.  Who should I approach at work?
supporter: You could ask your immediate supervisor or sometimes Human resources for support.
seeker: I can do that.  I think I'll reach out tomorrow to Human Resources for some help.
supporter: That sounds like a good plan to reach out for support.  Is there anything else I can help with?
seeker: No that should be all.  I am feeling more confident in strategies to use to help me.  Thanks
supporter: You are very welcome.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-11-01","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: My friend Lisa borrowed money from me but she won't return it now
supporter: I am sorry about that. It is always hard when we trust someone and they let us down. is that waht you are feeling? Disappointment in your friend?
seeker: Yes,i am very dissapointed because i trusted her completely.
supporter: I understand. I have been through a similar situation.
supporter: Was it a large amount of money?
seeker: What did you do to come out of the tricky situation?
seeker: Yes,it was for me,a total of $10000
supporter: Oh, That is a very large amount of money. I can understand your being upset with them
supporter: Have you talked to them about the money and returning it?
seeker: Yes,i am very very upset.What would you do in my position?
seeker: Yes,she just sounded non-comittal,saying that she will return it when she can
supporter: I see. It is a financially difficult time for us all. I am wondering if your friend might be upset and embarrassed that they can not pay you back immediately? Have you asked her if she could even afford some sort of small payments?
seeker: Yes,i asked her how we could restructure the payment in her favor because i understand how difficult it is for everyone right now but she did not answer
supporter: Were you speaking on the phone or in person? Is this a financial burden for you?
supporter: Would you consider this person a good friend? Would you be sad if they were not in your life anymore?
seeker: We were speaking on phone because i wanted to set up a physical meeting where we could discuss the logistics
seeker: Yes,it is a financial burden because this is money i was saving for a venture
supporter: That is very difficult. It is hard to judge things on the phone. 
seeker: Yes,this is a really close friend from way back and i would be devastated to lose the friendship
seeker: It is difficult to judge on the phone yes,which is why i wanted a physical meeting but she snapped at me and said that she will just pay me when she can
supporter: I see. I am very sorry about that! it is very difficult when a friend betrays your trust like that. 
seeker: Yes,very difficult
supporter: It sounds like you are doing what you can. It is very nice of you to have been this patient.
seeker: How do you suggest i shoulp proceed?
supporter: Is the friendship more important than the money? That is what it came down to for me.
seeker: And you chose what?
supporter: If you can not get her to meet with you, perhaps it might be time to seek advice from a lawyer? That is providing that you are willing to possibly lose a friend. 
seeker: Thank you very much for the advice
supporter: you are welcome. Good luck! I hope you find resolution and find a way to save your friendship!","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-10-05","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

turns.content: Hi Jane, it's good to see you here. How have you been feeling lately?

Thank you for saying that. It feels like my career growth isn't going as planned, and that's adding to my stress.

I guess I'm just trying to take things one day at a time. I started a journal a while back to track my thoughts and emotions, and that's been somewhat helpful.
Journaling is a fantastic way to process emotions. Have you found it easier to express your feelings on paper?
Yes, in some ways it helps, but I still feel stuck. It's like writing doesn't change the actual situation I'm in.

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hey, can I vent about something?
supporter: Of course, Jane. What's on your mind?
seeker: I just found out I missed out on the overseas promotion I was offered a while back.
supporter: Oh no, that's really disappointing, especially after having been offered it. How are you feeling about it?
seeker: Honestly, I feel a bit betrayed. No one even told me; I just found out through the grapevine.
supporter: That sounds really tough, Jane. It's hard to be left out of the loop like that. How are you coping with all these emotions?
seeker: I'm trying to process it, but it's hard not to feel like it's a reflection of my value at work.
supporter: It's understandable to feel that way. Your work and contributions are valuable, even if it doesn't feel like it right now. Do you want to talk more about what led to this?
seeker: I think it's a combination of things. There was so much going on—my anxiety, all the financial stress, and then this on top of it.
supporter: It's a lot to deal with, for sure. It reminds me of when you were considering the promotion and feeling overwhelmed. Do you think those feelings had an impact?
seeker: Maybe. I was really torn about the decision, fearing how it would affect my relationship with Eliza and just leaving everything behind.
supporter: It's such a big decision with lots of factors to weigh. It makes sense that it took a toll on you. How are you feeling about your relationship with Eliza now, after everything?
seeker: We’ve been better. We managed to patch things up after the wedding planning fallout, but I wonder how she’d have reacted if I moved.
supporter: It sounds like your bond with her is important to you. Maybe those fears were valid, but it's good to hear you've reconciled. How do you see your career moving forward after this setback?
seeker: It's hard to say. I feel stuck, but in some ways, relieved I don't have to move overseas. Yet, there's this nagging fear I'll remain stagnant in my career.
supporter: It’s definitely a complex situation. Being relieved but also worried about stagnation can be conflicting. Have you thought about discussing your career goals and concerns with your manager?
seeker: I have, but I'm hesitant. After the performance review last year, I just don't feel confident my concerns will be taken seriously.
supporter: It's tough to bring up concerns at work, especially after what happened. Is there someone you trust at work who might offer advice or support on how to approach your manager?
seeker: Maybe. There's a colleague I'm on good terms with. I might talk to them first and see how they handled similar situations.
supporter: That sounds like a good plan—having someone to bounce ideas off can make a big difference. Whatever you decide, I’m here to support you as you navigate this.
seeker: Thanks, I really appreciate it. It's just been a lot to process, but talking about it helps.
supporter: I'm glad talking it through helped a bit. Remember, you're not alone in this. Anytime you need to talk, I'm here.
seeker: Thanks, that means a lot. I’ll keep you posted on how things go. Talk soon?
supporter: Definitely. Take care of yourself, Jane.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-08-20","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hi, just needed someone to talk to.
supporter: Hi Jane! Of course, I'm here for you. What's on your mind?
seeker: I had my performance review at work today... and it wasn't great.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. It sounds like it must be really tough to hear. How are you feeling about it?
seeker: I'm feeling anxious and a bit of self-doubt creeping in. I thought I was handling everything okay.
supporter: It's completely understandable to feel that way. It seems like there's been a lot on your plate recently. Would you like to talk more about it?
seeker: I guess everything's just been snowballing since the thing with Lisa. I still can't believe how it all fell apart.
supporter: Losing a friend, especially over something like money, can feel really isolating. How has it been affecting you lately?
seeker: It's made focusing on work harder. And getting hit with that unexpected bill last month didn't help. Everything feels out of control.
supporter: It sounds like you're dealing with a lot of financial and emotional stress right now. It's a lot for anyone to handle. How have you been coping with it all?
seeker: I started writing in a journal. It helps sometimes, but the stress keeps piling up. I thought it would get better by now.
supporter: Journaling can be a great outlet. It's important to give yourself grace with everything happening. You're doing your best in a really challenging time.
seeker: Thank you. I keep telling myself that, but it's hard to believe it sometimes. I just wish things would turn around.
supporter: It makes sense to want things to improve quickly. Progress can be slow, but you're taking steps in the right direction by reaching out and processing everything going on.
seeker: Yeah, it helps to talk about it. I suppose I need to take it one day at a time.
supporter: Absolutely. It's like building a path through all these challenges— day by day, step by step. You have the strength to navigate this, even if it doesn't feel like it sometimes.
seeker: I really appreciate your support. It makes things feel a bit less overwhelming.
supporter: I'm glad to be here for you. Remember, you're not alone in this. We can keep talking anytime you need.
seeker: Thanks a lot. I might take you up on that.
supporter: Anytime, Jane. Take care of yourself, and reach out whenever you need to.
seeker: Will do. Take care, too.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-11-05","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hey! How are you?
seeker: Hi, I am having a really hard time. I just found out that my boyfriend cheated on me a year ago.
supporter: Have you confronted him about it yet?
seeker: Yes, I told him that my best friend confessed it to me. It was my best friend and him. I was so shocked.
supporter: Have you broken up yet?
seeker: No, I am so mad but I don't want to break up with him. I told my best friends that I never want to see her again though. My boyfriend and I have plans to get engaged this month. I am furious at him though.
supporter: I think you should postpone the engagement as infidelity during marriage is far more painful
supporter: You are strong if you are able to forgive him though because I know I wouldn't 
seeker: I have never been so blind sided. Maybe I should reconsider! I have had a guy after me for at least the last year but I never cheated! I really wanted to though.
supporter: No you should never cheat, because you would be on the same wavelength as your boyfriend. Instead, if you like the other man then you should go where your feelings take you :)
seeker: I am thinking that you are right. I feel like my whole world is upside down and I have wasted all this time with the wrong guy and the wrong best friend. I also wonder who else he might have cheated on my with. 
supporter: Yeah, that might be true, a relationship isn't healthy if you are cheated on
seeker: I am so grossed out because I am a germaphobe to begin with. I have not slept with any other person in my whole life so I feel like I am ruined. I want to throw up when I think of him cheating on me. I want to get married and I have a timeline so I am also really confused on what to do if I dump him.
supporter: To dump him is the best thing to do in my opinion. But always go where your heart is, because you won't be happy if you don't. If you do though, there are plenty men out there, and one of them is chasing you
seeker: Yeah, the guy who liked me was super rich too! My boyfriend is telling me that he wants my best friend to still be in the wedding party too. She was suppose to be my maid of honor, no less.
supporter: Yeah, but don't go with him because of he money though, genuinely get to know him first
seeker: I have compartmentalized my life and never thought of looking around at my other options. You are making really good points. I need to just stop and really look at my options. I never realized that I have options, it's not like i am even engaged yet.
supporter: Yeah, you have a lot of options at this stage, so always do what your heart is telling you at the end of the day
seeker: It feels good sharing how I feel with you because you don't have a dog in the fight so to speak.
supporter: yeah, lool something like that ;). Glad your better
seeker: I never listen to my heart and think that is a great place to start. I always have a plan and go with that but you are making a lot of sense. Thank you for your time today.
supporter: Your welcome ;)
seeker: Have a great day and I might be back soon to give an update.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-09-01","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: I am worried about being perfect on my job.  I don't want to lose my job.
supporter: I hear you are trying to be perfect on your job because you are worried about losing your job.  How long have you been at your job?
seeker: I have been working for about 4 months, but I just am not as fast at it as everyone else.  I'm trying so hard working late and everything but it's never enough.
supporter: That can be hard when you are working so hard to try to do your best.  Can you consult with a supervisor or co-workers to get some help?
seeker: Maybe I could ask my friend and co-worker for some tips.  I'm a little embarrassed to do so, but don't know where to turn. I don't want to get fired.
supporter: Asking for help isn't always a bad thing.  I asked for help at my last job and they gave me someone to help out.  I was so relieved.
seeker: That's true maybe it could turn out for the better.  But what if they see me as incompetant?
supporter: I can see that you have worry of being seen incompetent but as long as you are doing your best, they have to see the efforts you are making as positive.
seeker: That's a good way to put it.
supporter: Sometimes deep breaths can help keep you calm when approaching others in an anxiety provoking situation.
seeker: I will have to try that.  That might help.
supporter: Have you thought of doing additional work related trainings?  Sometimes they can give suggestions to improve work abilities.
seeker: That sounds great.  Do you think my work would be supportive?
supporter: Work can often pay for trainings or offer suggestions what may improve work strategies.
seeker: Wow, I hope I can take advantage of that.  I will have to check into that.  Who should I approach at work?
supporter: You could ask your immediate supervisor or sometimes Human resources for support.
seeker: I can do that.  I think I'll reach out tomorrow to Human Resources for some help.
supporter: That sounds like a good plan to reach out for support.  Is there anything else I can help with?
seeker: No that should be all.  I am feeling more confident in strategies to use to help me.  Thanks
supporter: You are very welcome.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-11-01","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: My friend Lisa borrowed money from me but she won't return it now
supporter: I am sorry about that. It is always hard when we trust someone and they let us down. is that waht you are feeling? Disappointment in your friend?
seeker: Yes,i am very dissapointed because i trusted her completely.
supporter: I understand. I have been through a similar situation.
supporter: Was it a large amount of money?
seeker: What did you do to come out of the tricky situation?
seeker: Yes,it was for me,a total of $10000
supporter: Oh, That is a very large amount of money. I can understand your being upset with them
supporter: Have you talked to them about the money and returning it?
seeker: Yes,i am very very upset.What would you do in my position?
seeker: Yes,she just sounded non-comittal,saying that she will return it when she can
supporter: I see. It is a financially difficult time for us all. I am wondering if your friend might be upset and embarrassed that they can not pay you back immediately? Have you asked her if she could even afford some sort of small payments?
seeker: Yes,i asked her how we could restructure the payment in her favor because i understand how difficult it is for everyone right now but she did not answer
supporter: Were you speaking on the phone or in person? Is this a financial burden for you?
supporter: Would you consider this person a good friend? Would you be sad if they were not in your life anymore?
seeker: We were speaking on phone because i wanted to set up a physical meeting where we could discuss the logistics
seeker: Yes,it is a financial burden because this is money i was saving for a venture
supporter: That is very difficult. It is hard to judge things on the phone. 
seeker: Yes,this is a really close friend from way back and i would be devastated to lose the friendship
seeker: It is difficult to judge on the phone yes,which is why i wanted a physical meeting but she snapped at me and said that she will just pay me when she can
supporter: I see. I am very sorry about that! it is very difficult when a friend betrays your trust like that. 
seeker: Yes,very difficult
supporter: It sounds like you are doing what you can. It is very nice of you to have been this patient.
seeker: How do you suggest i shoulp proceed?
supporter: Is the friendship more important than the money? That is what it came down to for me.
seeker: And you chose what?
supporter: If you can not get her to meet with you, perhaps it might be time to seek advice from a lawyer? That is providing that you are willing to possibly lose a friend. 
seeker: Thank you very much for the advice
supporter: you are welcome. Good luck! I hope you find resolution and find a way to save your friendship!","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-10-05","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hey Jane, how have you been holding up lately?
seeker: Hi. Not too great, to be honest. It's been a rough couple of weeks.
supporter: I'm really sorry to hear that. Would you like to talk about what's been going on?
seeker: Well, do you remember Lisa? My friend I mentioned before?
supporter: Yes, I remember you talking about them. What's up with Lisa?
seeker: So, we've hit this weird and stressful snag. I lent her some money months ago and she hasn’t paid me back yet.
supporter: That definitely sounds stressful. How is it affecting your relationship with Lisa?
seeker: She's completely cut off communication with me. No calls, texts, nothing.
supporter: That must be really hard on you, especially since she was such a close friend.
seeker: It feels like losing a part of my life. We used to hang out all the time and now it's just silence.
supporter: It sounds like you're mourning the loss of that friendship. Have you had a chance to reach out or communicate with her recently?
seeker: I’ve tried. Sent a couple of messages, but they’ve gone unanswered.
supporter: It must feel really disappointing not to hear back. What do you miss most about your friendship with Lisa?
seeker: We used to bounce ideas off each other, and she was the first person I'd call when something great happened at work.
supporter: It's understandable to miss those shared moments and support. How are you managing everything else alongside this?
seeker: It's made focusing on work tough. I feel a bit isolated, honestly.
supporter: I'm so sorry you're feeling this way. Feeling isolated can really weigh on you. Is there anyone else you feel comfortable confiding in?
seeker: I haven't really opened up to anyone else about this. It's been hard admitting to myself how deep this issue has affected me.
supporter: It takes a lot of courage to open up. It's important to take time for yourself and process everything. Is there anything you can do to help ease your mind a bit right now?
seeker: Maybe get back into some hobbies. I used to enjoy painting but haven't done it in a while.
supporter: That sounds like a wonderful idea. Engaging in something creative can be really therapeutic. Would you like support picking it back up?

supporter: I'm here to support you with this. Whenever you're ready, you can share your progress, and I’d love to hear how it goes.

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hey, feeling a bit all over the place today. Mind if I share?
supporter: Of course, Jane. I'm here to listen. What's been going on?
seeker: Well, you know how Eliza and I had that big fight about her wedding?
supporter: Yes, you’ve mentioned feeling misunderstood during that time. How are things between you two now?
seeker: We actually had a really deep conversation a few days ago. Lots of tears but good ones, I think.
supporter: That sounds intense but potentially healing. How did that feel for you?
seeker: It was a mix of relief and lingering sadness. I’m happy we cleared the air, but all those pent-up emotions were exhausting.
supporter: It makes sense to feel drained after such a heart-to-heart. It's brave of you both to confront those emotions together.
seeker: Thanks. I just wish it didn't have to get so messy before getting better.
supporter: Relationships can be messy, but the reconciling part is important. How’s your perspective on everything now?
seeker: I feel closer to her actually. We both admitted how much the wedding planning has stressed us out.
supporter: That’s insightful. Acknowledging shared stress can bring people together. How’s the wedding planning going now?
seeker: Better. We’ve agreed to communicate openly about decisions. It feels more like a partnership now, rather than me just helping her.
supporter: That’s great to hear, Jane. Open communication is key in any relationship.
seeker: Yeah, I've also started journaling again. It helps sort through these complicated feelings.
supporter: Journaling is a great tool. How does writing about your thoughts and emotions help you?
seeker: It gives me clarity. Putting pen to paper makes everything feel less overwhelming and more manageable.
supporter: I’m glad it’s helping you. Have you noticed any other changes since you reconciled with Eliza?
seeker: I feel a bit lighter emotionally. Mending the rift with her feels like a burden lifted.
supporter: That’s a beautiful way to put it. Rebuilding that connection must feel rewarding.
seeker: It does. I’m also trying to be more proactive about addressing my financial stress instead of letting it control me.
supporter: That’s a positive step forward. You've been through a lot, and it’s important to take care of yourself too.
seeker: Trying my best. It’s a work in progress, you know? Balancing everything is tough.
supporter: Absolutely. You’re making great progress, even if it doesn’t always feel that way. I’m here whenever you need to talk.
seeker: Thank you, that means a lot. I’ll keep leaning on you if that's okay.
supporter: Always, Jane. Your journey is important, and I’m here to support you along the way.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-03-20","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

supporter: Hi Jane! I'm here. What's going on?
seeker: I don't know, it's just been a lot lately. I got a promotion offer, but there's a catch.
supporter: Congratulations on the promotion offer! But what’s the catch?
seeker: Thanks. It means relocating overseas. I’m feeling pretty overwhelmed.
supporter: That's a big decision. It sounds like there's a lot to consider. How are you feeling about moving overseas?
seeker: Honestly, I have mixed feelings. It's a great opportunity, but I’m scared of leaving everything behind. What if I fail?
supporter: It’s completely natural to feel that way. You've been through a lot of stressful situations before, remember when you had the falling out with your friend over the money issue, and you managed to handle it?
seeker: True, I did handle that. But this feels different, like if I accept, everything changes.
supporter: Change can be daunting, but it also can be exciting. Deep down, what does your gut tell you?
seeker: A part of me wants to embrace this challenge. But I worry about my family, especially Eliza after we just started getting along again.
supporter: It's understandable to worry about your relationship with Eliza. Have you talked to her about this yet?
seeker: Not yet. I'm afraid she’ll feel like I'm abandoning her right when things are starting to get better between us.
supporter: Maybe having an open conversation with Eliza would help. She might surprise you with her support, especially after you both mended fences.
seeker: You’re right. I should probably talk to her. I just don't want to ruin anything.
supporter: It sounds like your relationship is stronger than you think. Keeping communication open could help strengthen it further.
seeker: I hope so. Moving would also mean leaving behind memories, and part of me is afraid of the unknown.
supporter: The unknown can be intimidating, but it also holds a lot of potential. It sounds like you’re searching for a balance between embracing new opportunities and holding onto what you value.
seeker: That's exactly it. I want to grow and advance my career, but I don't want to lose myself in the process.
supporter: You’re approaching this thoughtfully. Trust yourself to find that balance. Sometimes writing down your thoughts, like in your journal, might help clarify things.
seeker: That’s a good idea. Journaling helped last time. Maybe it will help me weigh the pros and cons more clearly this time too.
supporter: Absolutely. You’ve navigated tough situations before, and you've come out stronger each time. No matter what you decide, you’re capable of handling it.
seeker: Thank you. That means a lot. I guess I just needed to talk it out.
supporter: Anytime, Jane. Just remember, you’re not alone in this. I’m here for you, and so is your support network.
seeker: Thanks, I’ll reach out if I need more advice. Take care.

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hey, do you have a moment to chat?
supporter: Of course, Jane. What's on your mind?
seeker: I got a message out of the blue from someone I used to be really close with. It's brought up so many mixed feelings.
supporter: That sounds complicated. Who was it, if you don't mind sharing?
seeker: It was from my old friend, who I haven't spoken to since the whole money situation last year.
supporter: Ah, I remember you mentioned them before. It's understandable that you'd feel a bit caught off guard.
seeker: Yeah, exactly. Part of me is nostalgic, but another part of me is wary. I don't want to go through that emotional turmoil again.
supporter: It's natural to have those feelings when someone from the past reaches out, especially given what transpired.
seeker: I just can't shake off the memory of how it ended. Losing a friend like that was tough.
supporter: It must've been really hard. Do you feel like you're ready to respond, or do you need more time to process?
seeker: I'm really unsure. A part of me misses the friendship, but I'm scared of being hurt again.
supporter: Both of those feelings make a lot of sense. It's important to protect your heart while also honoring what used to be.
seeker: Right. I also think back to how stressful things were—like with my job performance review and financial stress. It was too much.
supporter: Those were tough times for you. It shows how much strength it took for you to get through them.
seeker: Thanks. I guess I'm just worried that engaging in any more complicated relationships could bring back old stressors.
supporter: I completely understand your apprehension. Do you think setting boundaries might help if you decide to reconnect?
seeker: That might be a good idea. It could prevent past issues from repeating.
supporter: And if you ever feel overwhelmed, remember you can always pause and take the time you need.
seeker: You're right. I'll think about what I want and maybe draft a response if that time comes.
supporter: That sounds like a solid plan. It's all about doing what's best for you.
seeker: Thanks for listening. I just needed to get that off my chest.
supporter: Anytime, Jane. I'm here if you need to talk more.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-08-05","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hey, I'm feeling a bit overwhelmed today.
supporter: Hi Jane, I'm here for you. What's on your mind?
seeker: My sister Eliza just announced her engagement.
supporter: Oh wow, that must be a big piece of news for the family. How are you processing it?
seeker: I'm happy for her, truly, but it also makes me reflect on where I am in my life.
supporter: It's completely natural to have mixed feelings. Have you been able to talk to Eliza about how you're feeling?
seeker: Not yet. I don’t want to dampen her excitement with my own worries.
supporter: That's considerate of you. How has this news been affecting you emotionally?
seeker: I feel lonely, to be honest. Recently, things haven't been great for me...work stress, financial issues...it's cumulative.

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hi Jane, how are you holding up lately?
seeker: Hey, not the best to be honest. Things aren't getting any better.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. Do you want to talk about what's been going on?
seeker: It's mostly about my sister, Eliza. We had a huge argument while planning her wedding.
supporter: I'm really sorry to hear that. It can be tough when someone close to you is involved. What happened?
seeker: She just doesn't appreciate my suggestions. I was only trying to help, but she took it the wrong way.
supporter: That sounds frustrating, especially when you're just trying to be helpful. How did she react?
seeker: She accused me of trying to control everything and said I wasn't being supportive.
supporter: It must be really hurtful to feel misunderstood like that. How are you feeling about it now?
seeker: I feel terrible. I love her and want to be there for her, but now it seems I've done the opposite.
supporter: Remember, it's not always easy to navigate these situations. Has this tension changed how you feel about attending the wedding?
seeker: A bit, yeah. I was looking forward to being part of it, but now it feels awkward.
supporter: It's understandable to feel conflicted. Being part of her big day is important, but so is your peace of mind.
seeker: Exactly. I just worry that our relationship might not be the same after this.
supporter: Are there moments from the past where you've overcome conflicts together?
seeker: Yes, there were times we've disagreed but always managed to mend things eventually.
supporter: That's promising. Perhaps this can be mended over time too. Do you think talking to her calmly might help?
seeker: Maybe. I guess I need to find the right time and words to explain my intentions.
supporter: That sounds like a thoughtful approach. Taking time to sort out your feelings first could also be beneficial.
seeker: Yes, I think writing about it in my journal could help me process everything.
supporter: That's a great idea, Jane. The journal seems like a good outlet for you.
seeker: Thanks. It always helps me get things off my chest and see things more clearly.
supporter: You have a lot on your plate right now, but I'm confident you'll find a way to navigate through it.
seeker: I hope so. Thanks for listening. It makes a difference knowing someone understands.
supporter: I'm always here for you, Jane. Whenever you need someone to talk to, just reach out.
seeker: I really appreciate that. Talk to you soon.
supporter: Take care. Remember to be gentle with yourself.
seeker: I will. Thank you!","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-03-15","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hey, feeling a bit all over the place today. Mind if I share?
supporter: Of course, Jane. I'm here to listen. What's been going on?
seeker: Well, you know how Eliza and I had that big fight about her wedding?
supporter: Yes, you’ve mentioned feeling misunderstood during that time. How are things between you two now?
seeker: We actually had a really deep conversation a few days ago. Lots of tears but good ones, I think.
supporter: That sounds intense but potentially healing. How did that feel for you?
seeker: It was a mix of relief and lingering sadness. I’m happy we cleared the air, but all those pent-up emotions were exhausting.
supporter: It makes sense to feel drained after such a heart-to-heart. It's brave of you both to confront those emotions together.
seeker: Thanks. I just wish it didn't have to get so messy before getting better.
supporter: Relationships can be messy, but the reconciling part is important. How’s your perspective on everything now?
seeker: I feel closer to her actually. We both admitted how much the wedding planning has stressed us out.
supporter: That’s insightful. Acknowledging shared stress can bring people together. How’s the wedding planning going now?
seeker: Better. We’ve agreed to communicate openly about decisions. It feels more like a partnership now, rather than me just helping her.
supporter: That’s great to hear, Jane. Open communication is key in any relationship.
seeker: Yeah, I've also started journaling again. It helps sort through these complicated feelings.

supporter: That’s a beautiful way to put it. Rebuilding that connection must feel rewarding.
seeker: It does. I’m also trying to be more proactive about addressing my financial stress instead of letting it control me.

supporter: Absolutely. You’re making great progress, even if it doesn’t always feel that way. I’m here whenever you need to talk.
seeker: Thank you, that means a lot. I’ll keep leaning on you if that's okay.

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hey! How are you?
seeker: Hi, I am having a really hard time. I just found out that my boyfriend cheated on me a year ago.
supporter: Have you confronted him about it yet?
seeker: Yes, I told him that my best friend confessed it to me. It was my best friend and him. I was so shocked.
supporter: Have you broken up yet?
seeker: No, I am so mad but I don't want to break up with him. I told my best friends that I never want to see her again though. My boyfriend and I have plans to get engaged this month. I am furious at him though.
supporter: I think you should postpone the engagement as infidelity during marriage is far more painful
supporter: You are strong if you are able to forgive him though because I know I wouldn't 
seeker: I have never been so blind sided. Maybe I should reconsider! I have had a guy after me for at least the last year but I never cheated! I really wanted to though.
supporter: No you should never cheat, because you would be on the same wavelength as your boyfriend. Instead, if you like the other man then you should go where your feelings take you :)
seeker: I am thinking that you are right. I feel like my whole world is upside down and I have wasted all this time with the wrong guy and the wrong best friend. I also wonder who else he might have cheated on my with. 
supporter: Yeah, that might be true, a relationship isn't healthy if you are cheated on
seeker: I am so grossed out because I am a germaphobe to begin with. I have not slept with any other person in my whole life so I feel like I am ruined. I want to throw up when I think of him cheating on me. I want to get married and I have a timeline so I am also really confused on what to do if I dump him.
supporter: To dump him is the best thing to do in my opinion. But always go where your heart is, because you won't be happy if you don't. If you do though, there are plenty men out there, and one of them is chasing you
seeker: Yeah, the guy who liked me was super rich too! My boyfriend is telling me that he wants my best friend to still be in the wedding party too. She was suppose to be my maid of honor, no less.
supporter: Yeah, but don't go with him because of he money though, genuinely get to know him first
seeker: I have compartmentalized my life and never thought of looking around at my other options. You are making really good points. I need to just stop and really look at my options. I never realized that I have options, it's not like i am even engaged yet.
supporter: Yeah, you have a lot of options at this stage, so always do what your heart is telling you at the end of the day
seeker: It feels good sharing how I feel with you because you don't have a dog in the fight so to speak.
supporter: yeah, lool something like that ;). Glad your better
seeker: I never listen to my heart and think that is a great place to start. I always have a plan and go with that but you are making a lot of sense. Thank you for your time today.
supporter: Your welcome ;)
seeker: Have a great day and I might be back soon to give an update.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-09-01","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: I am worried about being perfect on my job.  I don't want to lose my job.
supporter: I hear you are trying to be perfect on your job because you are worried about losing your job.  How long have you been at your job?
seeker: I have been working for about 4 months, but I just am not as fast at it as everyone else.  I'm trying so hard working late and everything but it's never enough.
supporter: That can be hard when you are working so hard to try to do your best.  Can you consult with a supervisor or co-workers to get some help?
seeker: Maybe I could ask my friend and co-worker for some tips.  I'm a little embarrassed to do so, but don't know where to turn. I don't want to get fired.
supporter: Asking for help isn't always a bad thing.  I asked for help at my last job and they gave me someone to help out.  I was so relieved.
seeker: That's true maybe it could turn out for the better.  But what if they see me as incompetant?
supporter: I can see that you have worry of being seen incompetent but as long as you are doing your best, they have to see the efforts you are making as positive.
seeker: That's a good way to put it.
supporter: Sometimes deep breaths can help keep you calm when approaching others in an anxiety provoking situation.
seeker: I will have to try that.  That might help.
supporter: Have you thought of doing additional work related trainings?  Sometimes they can give suggestions to improve work abilities.
seeker: That sounds great.  Do you think my work would be supportive?
supporter: Work can often pay for trainings or offer suggestions what may improve work strategies.
seeker: Wow, I hope I can take advantage of that.  I will have to check into that.  Who should I approach at work?
supporter: You could ask your immediate supervisor or sometimes Human resources for support.
seeker: I can do that.  I think I'll reach out tomorrow to Human Resources for some help.
supporter: That sounds like a good plan to reach out for support.  Is there anything else I can help with?
seeker: No that should be all.  I am feeling more confident in strategies to use to help me.  Thanks
supporter: You are very welcome.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-11-01","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: My friend Lisa borrowed money from me but she won't return it now
supporter: I am sorry about that. It is always hard when we trust someone and they let us down. is that waht you are feeling? Disappointment in your friend?
seeker: Yes,i am very dissapointed because i trusted her completely.
supporter: I understand. I have been through a similar situation.
supporter: Was it a large amount of money?
seeker: What did you do to come out of the tricky situation?
seeker: Yes,it was for me,a total of $10000
supporter: Oh, That is a very large amount of money. I can understand your being upset with them
supporter: Have you talked to them about the money and returning it?
seeker: Yes,i am very very upset.What would you do in my position?
seeker: Yes,she just sounded non-comittal,saying that she will return it when she can
supporter: I see. It is a financially difficult time for us all. I am wondering if your friend might be upset and embarrassed that they can not pay you back immediately? Have you asked her if she could even afford some sort of small payments?
seeker: Yes,i asked her how we could restructure the payment in her favor because i understand how difficult it is for everyone right now but she did not answer
supporter: Were you speaking on the phone or in person? Is this a financial burden for you?
supporter: Would you consider this person a good friend? Would you be sad if they were not in your life anymore?
seeker: We were speaking on phone because i wanted to set up a physical meeting where we could discuss the logistics
seeker: Yes,it is a financial burden because this is money i was saving for a venture
supporter: That is very difficult. It is hard to judge things on the phone. 
seeker: Yes,this is a really close friend from way back and i would be devastated to lose the friendship
seeker: It is difficult to judge on the phone yes,which is why i wanted a physical meeting but she snapped at me and said that she will just pay me when she can
supporter: I see. I am very sorry about that! it is very difficult when a friend betrays your trust like that. 
seeker: Yes,very difficult
supporter: It sounds like you are doing what you can. It is very nice of you to have been this patient.
seeker: How do you suggest i shoulp proceed?
supporter: Is the friendship more important than the money? That is what it came down to for me.
seeker: And you chose what?
supporter: If you can not get her to meet with you, perhaps it might be time to seek advice from a lawyer? That is providing that you are willing to possibly lose a friend. 
seeker: Thank you very much for the advice
supporter: you are welcome. Good luck! I hope you find resolution and find a way to save your friendship!","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-10-05","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

seeker: Thanks. It helps to talk about it. I'm feeling a little more at ease just expressing what's been on my mind.
supporter: Anytime, Jane. I'm here for you whenever you need to talk.

seeker: Hi, I'm okay, I guess. I got a new journal today to help me figure things out.
supporter: That sounds like a positive step. What inspired you to start journaling?
seeker: Well, things have been pretty overwhelming lately with everything going on. I thought it might help me process my thoughts and emotions better.
supporter: It's great that you're taking proactive steps to manage your stress. Would you like to share more about what's been on your mind?

supporter: That sounds really tough. Financial stress combined with losing a friend can be a lot to handle. How are you managing everything?
seeker: It's hard. I feel anxious most of the time. I'm constantly worried about my finances and how to make ends meet, especially with that insurance bill.

seeker: Hey, it's been tough, honestly. I've been dealing with a lot of stress and barely sleeping.
supporter: I'm so sorry to hear that. Stress and insomnia can really take a toll. What's been weighing on you the most?
seeker: It's a mix of things... Financial issues, work, and I guess, the whole fallout with Lisa.
supporter: Losing a friend over money is really difficult. Do you want to talk more about what's been going on with work as well?
seeker: Yeah, I had a poor performance review last week, and it shook my confidence. It's hard to focus when my mind is elsewhere.
supporter: That sounds really challenging, especially when you're already feeling anxious. Have you noticed any patterns or triggers for the stress?
seeker: I think it's the feeling of everything piling up at once. Every little thing just feels like too much now.
supporter: When it all becomes overwhelming, it's so important to prioritize taking care of yourself. Have you been able to use your journal to help manage the stress?
seeker: Yes, I try to write in it every night. It does help to put my thoughts on paper, but sometimes the anxiety is just too strong.
supporter: It's good that you're using your journal as a tool. It's natural to still feel overwhelmed, especially given everything you're handling right now.
seeker: Thanks. I know you’re right, but sometimes I just feel so alone in this.
supporter: You’re definitely not alone, Jane. I'm here for you, and it’s okay to reach out whenever you need someone to listen.
seeker: I really appreciate that. It’s comforting to have someone to talk to.
supporter: Do you have any plans to tackle the financial stress, or is there someone who could help you navigate that?
seeker: I’ve been looking into budgeting more strictly, but it’s tough. I think I just feel angry and sad about how things ended with Lisa.
supporter: It's understandable to feel that guilt, but you're doing your best under challenging circumstances. It's important to be gentle with yourself.
seeker: Yeah, I know logically I did what I could, but emotionally it’s hard to let go.
supporter: Emotions can be tough to navigate, but it’s a process. Small steps are still progress. Have you been able to find moments of peace or relaxation?
seeker: I try to meditate a bit or take a walk when I can. It helps, even if just a little.

seeker: Thank you. It means a lot to hear that, especially when I feel like I'm drowning.
supporter: Always happy to remind you. You’re stronger than you realize, and it takes courage to face these challenges.

supporter: Holding onto hope is incredibly powerful.
