turns.content: Hi Jane, how are you holding up lately?
Hey, not the best to be honest. Things aren't getting any better.
I'm sorry to hear that. Do you want to talk about what's been going on?
It's mostly about my sister, Eliza. We had a huge argument while planning her wedding.
I'm really sorry to hear that. It can be tough when someone close to you is involved. What happened?
She just doesn't appreciate my suggestions. I was only trying to help, but she took it the wrong way.
That sounds frustrating, especially when you're just trying to be helpful. How did she react?
She accused me of trying to control everything and said I wasn't being supportive.
It must be really hurtful to feel misunderstood like that. How are you feeling about it now?
I feel terrible. I love her and want to be there for her, but now it seems I've done the opposite.
Remember, it's not always easy to navigate these situations. Has this tension changed how you feel about attending the wedding?
A bit, yeah. I was looking forward to being part of it, but now it feels awkward.
It's understandable to feel conflicted. Being part of her big day is important, but so is your peace of mind.
Exactly. I just worry that our relationship might not be the same after this.
Are there moments from the past where you've overcome conflicts together?
Yes, there were times we've disagreed but always managed to mend things eventually.
That's promising. Perhaps this can be mended over time too. Do you think talking to her calmly might help?
Maybe. I guess I need to find the right time and words to explain my intentions.
That sounds like a thoughtful approach. Taking time to sort out your feelings first could also be beneficial.
Yes, I think writing about it in my journal could help me process everything.

supporter: Hi Jane! Of course, I'm here for you. What's on your mind?

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hey! How are you?
seeker: Hi, I am having a really hard time. I just found out that my boyfriend cheated on me a year ago.
supporter: Have you confronted him about it yet?
seeker: Yes, I told him that my best friend confessed it to me. It was my best friend and him. I was so shocked.
supporter: Have you broken up yet?
seeker: No, I am so mad but I don't want to break up with him. I told my best friends that I never want to see her again though. My boyfriend and I have plans to get engaged this month. I am furious at him though.
supporter: I think you should postpone the engagement as infidelity during marriage is far more painful
supporter: You are strong if you are able to forgive him though because I know I wouldn't 
seeker: I have never been so blind sided. Maybe I should reconsider! I have had a guy after me for at least the last year but I never cheated! I really wanted to though.
supporter: No you should never cheat, because you would be on the same wavelength as your boyfriend. Instead, if you like the other man then you should go where your feelings take you :)
seeker: I am thinking that you are right. I feel like my whole world is upside down and I have wasted all this time with the wrong guy and the wrong best friend. I also wonder who else he might have cheated on my with. 
supporter: Yeah, that might be true, a relationship isn't healthy if you are cheated on
seeker: I am so grossed out because I am a germaphobe to begin with. I have not slept with any other person in my whole life so I feel like I am ruined. I want to throw up when I think of him cheating on me. I want to get married and I have a timeline so I am also really confused on what to do if I dump him.
supporter: To dump him is the best thing to do in my opinion. But always go where your heart is, because you won't be happy if you don't. If you do though, there are plenty men out there, and one of them is chasing you
seeker: Yeah, the guy who liked me was super rich too! My boyfriend is telling me that he wants my best friend to still be in the wedding party too. She was suppose to be my maid of honor, no less.
supporter: Yeah, but don't go with him because of he money though, genuinely get to know him first
seeker: I have compartmentalized my life and never thought of looking around at my other options. You are making really good points. I need to just stop and really look at my options. I never realized that I have options, it's not like i am even engaged yet.
supporter: Yeah, you have a lot of options at this stage, so always do what your heart is telling you at the end of the day
seeker: It feels good sharing how I feel with you because you don't have a dog in the fight so to speak.
supporter: yeah, lool something like that ;). Glad your better
seeker: I never listen to my heart and think that is a great place to start. I always have a plan and go with that but you are making a lot of sense. Thank you for your time today.

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: My friend Lisa borrowed money from me but she won't return it now
supporter: I am sorry about that. It is always hard when we trust someone and they let us down. is that waht you are feeling? Disappointment in your friend?
seeker: Yes,i am very dissapointed because i trusted her completely.
supporter: I understand. I have been through a similar situation.
supporter: Was it a large amount of money?
seeker: What did you do to come out of the tricky situation?
seeker: Yes,it was for me,a total of $10000
supporter: Oh, That is a very large amount of money. I can understand your being upset with them
supporter: Have you talked to them about the money and returning it?
seeker: Yes,i am very very upset.What would you do in my position?
seeker: Yes,she just sounded non-comittal,saying that she will return it when she can
supporter: I see. It is a financially difficult time for us all. I am wondering if your friend might be upset and embarrassed that they can not pay you back immediately? Have you asked her if she could even afford some sort of small payments?
seeker: Yes,i asked her how we could restructure the payment in her favor because i understand how difficult it is for everyone right now but she did not answer
supporter: Were you speaking on the phone or in person? Is this a financial burden for you?
supporter: Would you consider this person a good friend? Would you be sad if they were not in your life anymore?
seeker: We were speaking on phone because i wanted to set up a physical meeting where we could discuss the logistics
seeker: Yes,it is a financial burden because this is money i was saving for a venture
supporter: That is very difficult. It is hard to judge things on the phone. 
seeker: Yes,this is a really close friend from way back and i would be devastated to lose the friendship
seeker: It is difficult to judge on the phone yes,which is why i wanted a physical meeting but she snapped at me and said that she will just pay me when she can
supporter: I see. I am very sorry about that! it is very difficult when a friend betrays your trust like that. 
seeker: Yes,very difficult
supporter: It sounds like you are doing what you can. It is very nice of you to have been this patient.
seeker: How do you suggest i shoulp proceed?
supporter: Is the friendship more important than the money? That is what it came down to for me.
seeker: And you chose what?
supporter: If you can not get her to meet with you, perhaps it might be time to seek advice from a lawyer? That is providing that you are willing to possibly lose a friend. 
seeker: Thank you very much for the advice
supporter: you are welcome. Good luck! I hope you find resolution and find a way to save your friendship!","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-10-05","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hey, do you have a moment? I could use some support right now.
supporter: Of course, Jane. What's going on?
seeker: I just got hit with an unexpected bill, and it's really stressing me out.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. Financial stress can be so overwhelming. Do you want to talk more about the bill?
seeker: Yeah, it's for my car insurance. I thought I had paid it, but apparently, there was some sort of oversight, and now I owe more than I expected.
supporter: That sounds frustrating, especially when you're already stretched thin. How are you handling it so far?
seeker: Honestly, not well. I'm feeling pretty anxious about it because money has been tight lately, especially since the whole situation with my friend.
supporter: I remember you mentioned that. It must be tough still dealing with those effects. How does that add to your current stress?
seeker: It just feels like a never-ending cycle. Losing that friendship was hard, and now this bill feels like another setback.
supporter: That's completely understandable. It's like everything piles up at once. How are you coping with these feelings?
seeker: I've been trying to budget more strictly and cut unnecessary expenses, but unexpected things keep popping up.
supporter: That can make it feel like you're running in place, right? Are there any specific concerns you're dwelling on?
seeker: I'm worried I'll fall behind on other payments. I hate feeling this insecure financially. I just want to feel stable again.
supporter: It's such a difficult spot to be in. Maybe talking to someone about financial strategies or planning could help?
seeker: That's a good idea. I haven't really considered reaching out for advice yet. I'm always thinking I have to handle it alone.
supporter: It's okay to ask for help, Jane. You've been doing so much on your own. Sometimes, a fresh perspective makes all the difference.
seeker: I appreciate you saying that. I'll look into finding someone who can help with budgeting strategies.
supporter: I'm glad to hear that. You're handling this situation with a lot of grace, even if it doesn't feel like it right now.
seeker: Thanks. It helps to talk about it. I'm feeling a little more at ease just expressing what's been on my mind.
supporter: Anytime, Jane. I'm here for you whenever you need to talk.
seeker: I really appreciate it. I'll keep you updated on how things go with the financial advice.
supporter: Please do. Remember, you're not alone in this. You have people who care about you.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-10-20","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hey Jane, how are things going for you today?
seeker: Hi, I'm okay, I guess. I got a new journal today to help me figure things out.
supporter: That sounds like a positive step. What inspired you to start journaling?
seeker: Well, things have been pretty overwhelming lately with everything going on. I thought it might help me process my thoughts and emotions better.
supporter: It's great that you're taking proactive steps to manage your stress. Would you like to share more about what's been on your mind?
seeker: Sure. I've been really stressed about this money issue with my friend, or former friend now, and the unexpected bills that keep coming up.
supporter: That sounds really tough. Financial stress combined with losing a friend can be a lot to handle. How are you managing everything?
seeker: It's hard. I feel anxious most of the time. I'm constantly worried about my finances and how to make ends meet, especially with that insurance bill.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. It sounds like you're carrying a lot on your shoulders. Have you been able to find any moments of peace or relaxation lately?
seeker: Not really. I keep trying to focus on work to distract myself, but it's not really working out.
supporter: It must be difficult to juggle work with all these thoughts in your mind. Do you feel like journaling might help untangle some of them?
seeker: Yeah, I hope so. I haven't written in it yet, but I plan to start tonight. Maybe it will help clarify my feelings and guide me to some solutions.
supporter: Starting is often the hardest part, but it sounds like you're on the right track. Taking time for yourself can be really healing. What do you hope to gain from journaling?
seeker: I just hope to understand my emotions better and maybe find new perspectives on my situation. I'm also hoping to find some sense of control over things again.
supporter: That's a wonderful goal. Gaining insight into your emotions can provide clarity. Remember that you're not alone in this. I'm here to listen whenever you need to talk.
seeker: Thank you. It really helps to know that someone is here to listen.
supporter: Anytime, Jane. I'm glad you reached out today. Keep me updated on how the journaling goes, okay?
seeker: I will. Thanks for the support. It means a lot.
supporter: You're welcome. You're doing the best you can, and I'm proud of you for taking steps towards self-care. Take care and talk soon!","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-10-28","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

seeker: Hey, it's been tough, honestly. I've been dealing with a lot of stress and barely sleeping.
supporter: I'm so sorry to hear that. Stress and insomnia can really take a toll. What's been weighing on you the most?
seeker: It's a mix of things... Financial issues, work, and I guess, the whole fallout with Lisa.
supporter: Losing a friend over money is really difficult. Do you want to talk more about what's been going on with work as well?
seeker: Yeah, I had a poor performance review last week, and it shook my confidence. It's hard to focus when my mind is elsewhere.
supporter: That sounds really challenging, especially when you're already feeling anxious. Have you noticed any patterns or triggers for the stress?
seeker: I think it's the feeling of everything piling up at once. Every little thing just feels like too much now.
supporter: When it all becomes overwhelming, it's so important to prioritize taking care of yourself. Have you been able to use your journal to help manage the stress?
seeker: Yes, I try to write in it every night. It does help to put my thoughts on paper, but sometimes the anxiety is just too strong.
supporter: It's good that you're using your journal as a tool. It's natural to still feel overwhelmed, especially given everything you're handling right now.
seeker: Thanks. I know you’re right, but sometimes I just feel so alone in this.
supporter: You’re definitely not alone, Jane. I'm here for you, and it’s okay to reach out whenever you need someone to listen.
seeker: I really appreciate that. It’s comforting to have someone to talk to.
supporter: Do you have any plans to tackle the financial stress, or is there someone who could help you navigate that?
seeker: I’ve been looking into budgeting more strictly, but it’s tough. I think I just feel angry and sad about how things ended with Lisa.
supporter: It's understandable to feel that guilt, but you're doing your best under challenging circumstances. It's important to be gentle with yourself.
seeker: Yeah, I know logically I did what I could, but emotionally it’s hard to let go.
supporter: Emotions can be tough to navigate, but it’s a process. Small steps are still progress. Have you been able to find moments of peace or relaxation?
seeker: I try to meditate a bit or take a walk when I can. It helps, even if just a little.
supporter: That's great! Even small moments of peace can accumulate and make a difference over time. You're doing really well to manage through this.
seeker: Thank you. It means a lot to hear that, especially when I feel like I'm drowning.
supporter: Always happy to remind you. You’re stronger than you realize, and it takes courage to face these challenges.
seeker: I hope things will start to turn around soon. I'm trying to keep faith.
supporter: Holding onto hope is incredibly powerful. And remember, you’re not alone - I’m here cheering you on every step of the way.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-11-15","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

seeker: Hi, it's been a bit rough lately. My car broke down and the repair costs are just... more than I can handle right now.
supporter: Oh no, I'm so sorry to hear that, Jane. That must be incredibly stressful, especially with everything else you've had to deal with recently.
seeker: It really is. I've been trying to manage, but the financial stress keeps piling up. I still haven't resolved the money issue with my friend, and now this... It's overwhelming.
supporter: I can only imagine how difficult that must be. You've been doing your best under such challenging circumstances. It's okay to feel overwhelmed.
seeker: Thank you. Sometimes it feels like I'm just not able to catch a break. I've been trying to keep track of everything with my journal, but it feels like every day brings something new.
supporter: Journaling is a great tool, and it's a good step that you're using it to process your thoughts and feelings. It shows how you're trying to find ways to cope.
seeker: Yeah, I thought it might help calm my anxieties. But with my job performance not being where it's supposed to be, and money problems, I just feel stuck.
supporter: Feeling stuck is definitely tough. It's important to remember that it's not a reflection of your abilities or worth. You're dealing with a lot, and your efforts are meaningful.
seeker: Thanks. Sometimes I just worry that I'm not living up to expectations, especially at work. The fear of being seen as incompetent is always there.
supporter: I understand. Work pressure can be intense, and when combined with personal challenges, it's a lot to balance. Have you been able to talk to anyone at work about how you're feeling?
seeker: Not yet. I'm hesitant because I don't want it to seem like I'm making excuses. I really want to prove myself and get back on track.
supporter: That makes sense. It might help to reach out for support when you're ready, even just to get some feedback. Sometimes, opening up can bring understanding and solutions you couldn't see before.
seeker: You're right. I'll think about that. Maybe just having a conversation could help put things into perspective.
supporter: Absolutely, even small steps can lead to positive changes. Remember, you're doing the best you can, and it's okay to seek help when you need it.
seeker: I will try to remember that. It's helpful to talk about it and just get it off my chest a bit.
supporter: I'm glad you reached out, Jane. It's important to have a space where you feel heard. If you ever need to talk or get things off your mind, I'm here.
seeker: Thank you so much. It really means a lot to have someone who listens and understands.
supporter: You're welcome. Remember, one step at a time, and be gentle with yourself. You're not alone in this, and there are brighter days ahead.
seeker: I'll keep that in mind. Thanks again for your support.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-12-10","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hey! How are you?
seeker: Hi, I am having a really hard time. I just found out that my boyfriend cheated on me a year ago.
supporter: Have you confronted him about it yet?
seeker: Yes, I told him that my best friend confessed it to me. It was my best friend and him. I was so shocked.
supporter: Have you broken up yet?
seeker: No, I am so mad but I don't want to break up with him. I told my best friends that I never want to see her again though. My boyfriend and I have plans to get engaged this month. I am furious at him though.
supporter: I think you should postpone the engagement as infidelity during marriage is far more painful
supporter: You are strong if you are able to forgive him though because I know I wouldn't 
seeker: I have never been so blind sided. Maybe I should reconsider! I have had a guy after me for at least the last year but I never cheated! I really wanted to though.
supporter: No you should never cheat, because you would be on the same wavelength as your boyfriend. Instead, if you like the other man then you should go where your feelings take you :)
seeker: I am thinking that you are right. I feel like my whole world is upside down and I have wasted all this time with the wrong guy and the wrong best friend. I also wonder who else he might have cheated on my with. 
supporter: Yeah, that might be true, a relationship isn't healthy if you are cheated on
seeker: I am so grossed out because I am a germaphobe to begin with. I have not slept with any other person in my whole life so I feel like I am ruined. I want to throw up when I think of him cheating on me. I want to get married and I have a timeline so I am also really confused on what to do if I dump him.
supporter: To dump him is the best thing to do in my opinion. But always go where your heart is, because you won't be happy if you don't. If you do though, there are plenty men out there, and one of them is chasing you
seeker: Yeah, the guy who liked me was super rich too! My boyfriend is telling me that he wants my best friend to still be in the wedding party too. She was suppose to be my maid of honor, no less.
supporter: Yeah, but don't go with him because of he money though, genuinely get to know him first
seeker: I have compartmentalized my life and never thought of looking around at my other options. You are making really good points. I need to just stop and really look at my options. I never realized that I have options, it's not like i am even engaged yet.
supporter: Yeah, you have a lot of options at this stage, so always do what your heart is telling you at the end of the day
seeker: It feels good sharing how I feel with you because you don't have a dog in the fight so to speak.
supporter: yeah, lool something like that ;). Glad your better
seeker: I never listen to my heart and think that is a great place to start. I always have a plan and go with that but you are making a lot of sense. Thank you for your time today.
supporter: Your welcome ;)
seeker: Have a great day and I might be back soon to give an update.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-09-01","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: I am worried about being perfect on my job.  I don't want to lose my job.
supporter: I hear you are trying to be perfect on your job because you are worried about losing your job.  How long have you been at your job?
seeker: I have been working for about 4 months, but I just am not as fast at it as everyone else.  I'm trying so hard working late and everything but it's never enough.
supporter: That can be hard when you are working so hard to try to do your best.  Can you consult with a supervisor or co-workers to get some help?
seeker: Maybe I could ask my friend and co-worker for some tips.  I'm a little embarrassed to do so, but don't know where to turn. I don't want to get fired.
supporter: Asking for help isn't always a bad thing.  I asked for help at my last job and they gave me someone to help out.  I was so relieved.
seeker: That's true maybe it could turn out for the better.  But what if they see me as incompetant?
supporter: I can see that you have worry of being seen incompetent but as long as you are doing your best, they have to see the efforts you are making as positive.
seeker: That's a good way to put it.
supporter: Sometimes deep breaths can help keep you calm when approaching others in an anxiety provoking situation.
seeker: I will have to try that.  That might help.
supporter: Have you thought of doing additional work related trainings?  Sometimes they can give suggestions to improve work abilities.
seeker: That sounds great.  Do you think my work would be supportive?
supporter: Work can often pay for trainings or offer suggestions what may improve work strategies.
seeker: Wow, I hope I can take advantage of that.  I will have to check into that.  Who should I approach at work?
supporter: You could ask your immediate supervisor or sometimes Human resources for support.
seeker: I can do that.  I think I'll reach out tomorrow to Human Resources for some help.
supporter: That sounds like a good plan to reach out for support.  Is there anything else I can help with?
seeker: No that should be all.  I am feeling more confident in strategies to use to help me.  Thanks
supporter: You are very welcome.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-11-01","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: My friend Lisa borrowed money from me but she won't return it now
supporter: I am sorry about that. It is always hard when we trust someone and they let us down. is that waht you are feeling? Disappointment in your friend?
seeker: Yes,i am very dissapointed because i trusted her completely.
supporter: I understand. I have been through a similar situation.
supporter: Was it a large amount of money?
seeker: What did you do to come out of the tricky situation?
seeker: Yes,it was for me,a total of $10000
supporter: Oh, That is a very large amount of money. I can understand your being upset with them
supporter: Have you talked to them about the money and returning it?
seeker: Yes,i am very very upset.What would you do in my position?
seeker: Yes,she just sounded non-comittal,saying that she will return it when she can
supporter: I see. It is a financially difficult time for us all. I am wondering if your friend might be upset and embarrassed that they can not pay you back immediately? Have you asked her if she could even afford some sort of small payments?
seeker: Yes,i asked her how we could restructure the payment in her favor because i understand how difficult it is for everyone right now but she did not answer
supporter: Were you speaking on the phone or in person? Is this a financial burden for you?
supporter: Would you consider this person a good friend? Would you be sad if they were not in your life anymore?
seeker: We were speaking on phone because i wanted to set up a physical meeting where we could discuss the logistics
seeker: Yes,it is a financial burden because this is money i was saving for a venture
supporter: That is very difficult. It is hard to judge things on the phone. 
seeker: Yes,this is a really close friend from way back and i would be devastated to lose the friendship
seeker: It is difficult to judge on the phone yes,which is why i wanted a physical meeting but she snapped at me and said that she will just pay me when she can
supporter: I see. I am very sorry about that! it is very difficult when a friend betrays your trust like that. 
seeker: Yes,very difficult
supporter: It sounds like you are doing what you can. It is very nice of you to have been this patient.
seeker: How do you suggest i shoulp proceed?
supporter: Is the friendship more important than the money? That is what it came down to for me.
seeker: And you chose what?
supporter: If you can not get her to meet with you, perhaps it might be time to seek advice from a lawyer? That is providing that you are willing to possibly lose a friend. 
seeker: Thank you very much for the advice
supporter: you are welcome. Good luck! I hope you find resolution and find a way to save your friendship!","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-10-05","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hey Jane, how have you been holding up lately?
seeker: Hi. Not too great, to be honest. It's been a rough couple of weeks.
supporter: I'm really sorry to hear that. Would you like to talk about what's been going on?
seeker: Well, do you remember Lisa? My friend I mentioned before?
supporter: Yes, I remember you talking about them. What's up with Lisa?
seeker: So, we've hit this weird and stressful snag. I lent her some money months ago and she hasn’t paid me back yet.
supporter: That definitely sounds stressful. How is it affecting your relationship with Lisa?
seeker: She's completely cut off communication with me. No calls, texts, nothing.
supporter: That must be really hard on you, especially since she was such a close friend.
seeker: It feels like losing a part of my life. We used to hang out all the time and now it's just silence.
supporter: It sounds like you're mourning the loss of that friendship. Have you had a chance to reach out or communicate with her recently?
seeker: I’ve tried. Sent a couple of messages, but they’ve gone unanswered.
supporter: It must feel really disappointing not to hear back. What do you miss most about your friendship with Lisa?
seeker: We used to bounce ideas off each other, and she was the first person I'd call when something great happened at work.
supporter: It's understandable to miss those shared moments and support. How are you managing everything else alongside this?
seeker: It's made focusing on work tough. I feel a bit isolated, honestly.
supporter: I'm so sorry you're feeling this way. Feeling isolated can really weigh on you. Is there anyone else you feel comfortable confiding in?
seeker: I haven't really opened up to anyone else about this. It's been hard admitting to myself how deep this issue has affected me.
supporter: It takes a lot of courage to open up. It's important to take time for yourself and process everything. Is there anything you can do to help ease your mind a bit right now?
seeker: Maybe get back into some hobbies. I used to enjoy painting but haven't done it in a while.
supporter: That sounds like a wonderful idea. Engaging in something creative can be really therapeutic. Would you like support picking it back up?
seeker: I think that would help. Just getting started again might lift this weight a little.
supporter: I'm here to support you with this. Whenever you're ready, you can share your progress, and I’d love to hear how it goes.

turns.content: Hey, can I vent about something?
Of course, Jane. What's on your mind?
I just found out I missed out on the overseas promotion I was offered a while back.
Oh no, that's really disappointing, especially after having been offered it. How are you feeling about it?
Honestly, I feel a bit betrayed. No one even told me; I just found out through the grapevine.
That sounds really tough, Jane. It's hard to be left out of the loop like that. How are you coping with all these emotions?
I'm trying to process it, but it's hard not to feel like it's a reflection of my value at work.
It's understandable to feel that way. Your work and contributions are valuable, even if it doesn't feel like it right now. Do you want to talk more about what led to this?
I think it's a combination of things. There was so much going on—my anxiety, all the financial stress, and then this on top of it.
It's a lot to deal with, for sure. It reminds me of when you were considering the promotion and feeling overwhelmed. Do you think those feelings had an impact?

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hey there, do you have a moment to chat?
supporter: Of course, Jane. What's on your mind?
seeker: I attended a social event recently, and it unearthed some emotions I thought I had tucked away.
supporter: It sounds like it was quite an experience. What happened that brought these feelings to the surface?
seeker: I met someone there who reminded me of my past relationships, particularly the one that ended in a mess due to infidelity.
supporter: That must have been tough to be reminded of. How did it feel encountering someone who brought those memories back?
seeker: It was like reliving a bit of that heartache. I was both fascinated and apprehensive.
supporter: That's understandable. Did this interaction lead you to reflect on your past relationship?
seeker: Yes. I wondered if I've truly moved on or just buried the feelings. And with everything else, the stress seems unending.
supporter: Between work, financial pressures, and this emotional trigger, it sounds like you're carrying a heavy load.
seeker: Exactly. I've been thinking about switching jobs, but the fear of instability holds me back.
supporter: It's a significant decision. Finding a balance between what you want and need is crucial.
seeker: And my sister's engagement has been on my mind too. I'm genuinely happy for her, but I can't help feeling a little left behind.
supporter: It's okay to feel those mixed emotions. How are you and Eliza doing since you mended things?
seeker: We're in a good place now. She really understood where I was coming from after we talked things out.
supporter: That's wonderful to hear. Having her support must mean a lot.
seeker: It definitely does. I just wish I felt more settled with everything else. All these thoughts keep me up at night.
supporter: Insomnia can really take a toll. How have you been coping with the stress?
seeker: I've been journaling to process my thoughts, but it's been a rollercoaster.
supporter: Writing can be therapeutic, but it sounds like there's more weighing on you.
seeker: Yeah, all of it combined just overwhelms me sometimes.
supporter: Jane, remember it's okay to seek help. Talking to someone professionally might help make things more manageable.
seeker: You might be right. It feels reassuring to know there are options out there.
supporter: Absolutely. You're not alone in this, and taking steps to care for yourself is important.
seeker: Thanks. I appreciate knowing there's someone who understands.
supporter: Anytime, Jane. You're doing the best you can, and that's enough.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-04-05","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hey, I'm feeling a bit overwhelmed today.
supporter: Hi Jane, I'm here for you. What's on your mind?
seeker: My sister Eliza just announced her engagement.
supporter: Oh wow, that must be a big piece of news for the family. How are you processing it?
seeker: I'm happy for her, truly, but it also makes me reflect on where I am in my life.
supporter: It's completely natural to have mixed feelings. Have you been able to talk to Eliza about how you're feeling?
seeker: Not yet. I don’t want to dampen her excitement with my own worries.
supporter: That's considerate of you. How has this news been affecting you emotionally?
seeker: I feel lonely, to be honest. Recently, things haven't been great for me...work stress, financial issues...it's cumulative.
supporter: That sounds really challenging. You've been through a lot lately. Remember, it's okay to feel this way.
seeker: There’s also the lingering anxiety from my last breakup, and then seeing Eliza so happy makes me question my own happiness.
supporter: Breakups can be incredibly tough, and comparing situations is a natural response. But your journey is unique and just as important.
seeker: Thanks for saying that. I guess I need to focus on myself more, but it's hard with all the stress.
supporter: It seems like a lot is demanding your attention. Maybe you could lean into that journaling habit you started?
seeker: That's a good idea. I haven’t been consistent, but I think it helps when I do it.
supporter: Starting small is perfectly fine. You're doing your best and that's what matters. Have you considered talking to a professional about everything you've been facing?
seeker: I've thought about it. It might be time to reach out for more help. Just to sort through everything.
supporter: I think that could be really beneficial. You're taking important steps by recognizing where you are. You're not alone in this.
seeker: Thanks, I appreciate that. Just expressing these feelings openly has been a relief.
supporter: I'm glad to hear that. I'm always here to listen. Take care of yourself, Jane.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-01-15","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hey! How are you?
seeker: Hi, I am having a really hard time. I just found out that my boyfriend cheated on me a year ago.
supporter: Have you confronted him about it yet?
seeker: Yes, I told him that my best friend confessed it to me. It was my best friend and him. I was so shocked.
supporter: Have you broken up yet?
seeker: No, I am so mad but I don't want to break up with him. I told my best friends that I never want to see her again though. My boyfriend and I have plans to get engaged this month. I am furious at him though.
supporter: I think you should postpone the engagement as infidelity during marriage is far more painful
supporter: You are strong if you are able to forgive him though because I know I wouldn't 
seeker: I have never been so blind sided. Maybe I should reconsider! I have had a guy after me for at least the last year but I never cheated! I really wanted to though.
supporter: No you should never cheat, because you would be on the same wavelength as your boyfriend. Instead, if you like the other man then you should go where your feelings take you :)
seeker: I am thinking that you are right. I feel like my whole world is upside down and I have wasted all this time with the wrong guy and the wrong best friend. I also wonder who else he might have cheated on my with. 
supporter: Yeah, that might be true, a relationship isn't healthy if you are cheated on
seeker: I am so grossed out because I am a germaphobe to begin with. I have not slept with any other person in my whole life so I feel like I am ruined. I want to throw up when I think of him cheating on me. I want to get married and I have a timeline so I am also really confused on what to do if I dump him.
supporter: To dump him is the best thing to do in my opinion. But always go where your heart is, because you won't be happy if you don't. If you do though, there are plenty men out there, and one of them is chasing you
seeker: Yeah, the guy who liked me was super rich too! My boyfriend is telling me that he wants my best friend to still be in the wedding party too. She was suppose to be my maid of honor, no less.
supporter: Yeah, but don't go with him because of he money though, genuinely get to know him first
seeker: I have compartmentalized my life and never thought of looking around at my other options. You are making really good points. I need to just stop and really look at my options. I never realized that I have options, it's not like i am even engaged yet.
supporter: Yeah, you have a lot of options at this stage, so always do what your heart is telling you at the end of the day
seeker: It feels good sharing how I feel with you because you don't have a dog in the fight so to speak.
supporter: yeah, lool something like that ;). Glad your better
seeker: I never listen to my heart and think that is a great place to start. I always have a plan and go with that but you are making a lot of sense. Thank you for your time today.
supporter: Your welcome ;)
seeker: Have a great day and I might be back soon to give an update.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-09-01","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

supporter: I hear you are trying to be perfect on your job because you are worried about losing your job.  How long have you been at your job?

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: My friend Lisa borrowed money from me but she won't return it now
supporter: I am sorry about that. It is always hard when we trust someone and they let us down. is that waht you are feeling? Disappointment in your friend?
seeker: Yes,i am very dissapointed because i trusted her completely.
supporter: I understand. I have been through a similar situation.
supporter: Was it a large amount of money?
seeker: What did you do to come out of the tricky situation?
seeker: Yes,it was for me,a total of $10000
supporter: Oh, That is a very large amount of money. I can understand your being upset with them
supporter: Have you talked to them about the money and returning it?
seeker: Yes,i am very very upset.What would you do in my position?
seeker: Yes,she just sounded non-comittal,saying that she will return it when she can
supporter: I see. It is a financially difficult time for us all. I am wondering if your friend might be upset and embarrassed that they can not pay you back immediately? Have you asked her if she could even afford some sort of small payments?

supporter: Were you speaking on the phone or in person? Is this a financial burden for you?
supporter: Would you consider this person a good friend? Would you be sad if they were not in your life anymore?
seeker: We were speaking on phone because i wanted to set up a physical meeting where we could discuss the logistics
seeker: Yes,it is a financial burden because this is money i was saving for a venture
supporter: That is very difficult. It is hard to judge things on the phone. 
seeker: Yes,this is a really close friend from way back and i would be devastated to lose the friendship

seeker: Yes,very difficult

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hey Jane, how have you been holding up lately?
seeker: Hi. Not too great, to be honest. It's been a rough couple of weeks.
supporter: I'm really sorry to hear that. Would you like to talk about what's been going on?
seeker: Well, do you remember Lisa? My friend I mentioned before?
supporter: Yes, I remember you talking about them. What's up with Lisa?
seeker: So, we've hit this weird and stressful snag. I lent her some money months ago and she hasn’t paid me back yet.
supporter: That definitely sounds stressful. How is it affecting your relationship with Lisa?
seeker: She's completely cut off communication with me. No calls, texts, nothing.
supporter: That must be really hard on you, especially since she was such a close friend.
seeker: It feels like losing a part of my life. We used to hang out all the time and now it's just silence.
supporter: It sounds like you're mourning the loss of that friendship. Have you had a chance to reach out or communicate with her recently?
seeker: I’ve tried. Sent a couple of messages, but they’ve gone unanswered.
supporter: It must feel really disappointing not to hear back. What do you miss most about your friendship with Lisa?
seeker: We used to bounce ideas off each other, and she was the first person I'd call when something great happened at work.
supporter: It's understandable to miss those shared moments and support. How are you managing everything else alongside this?
seeker: It's made focusing on work tough. I feel a bit isolated, honestly.
supporter: I'm so sorry you're feeling this way. Feeling isolated can really weigh on you. Is there anyone else you feel comfortable confiding in?
seeker: I haven't really opened up to anyone else about this. It's been hard admitting to myself how deep this issue has affected me.
supporter: It takes a lot of courage to open up. It's important to take time for yourself and process everything. Is there anything you can do to help ease your mind a bit right now?
seeker: Maybe get back into some hobbies. I used to enjoy painting but haven't done it in a while.
supporter: That sounds like a wonderful idea. Engaging in something creative can be really therapeutic. Would you like support picking it back up?

supporter: I'm here to support you with this. Whenever you're ready, you can share your progress, and I’d love to hear how it goes.

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hey, feeling a bit all over the place today. Mind if I share?
supporter: Of course, Jane. I'm here to listen. What's been going on?
seeker: Well, you know how Eliza and I had that big fight about her wedding?
supporter: Yes, you’ve mentioned feeling misunderstood during that time. How are things between you two now?
seeker: We actually had a really deep conversation a few days ago. Lots of tears but good ones, I think.
supporter: That sounds intense but potentially healing. How did that feel for you?
seeker: It was a mix of relief and lingering sadness. I’m happy we cleared the air, but all those pent-up emotions were exhausting.
supporter: It makes sense to feel drained after such a heart-to-heart. It's brave of you both to confront those emotions together.
seeker: Thanks. I just wish it didn't have to get so messy before getting better.
supporter: Relationships can be messy, but the reconciling part is important. How’s your perspective on everything now?
seeker: I feel closer to her actually. We both admitted how much the wedding planning has stressed us out.
supporter: That’s insightful. Acknowledging shared stress can bring people together. How’s the wedding planning going now?
seeker: Better. We’ve agreed to communicate openly about decisions. It feels more like a partnership now, rather than me just helping her.
supporter: That’s great to hear, Jane. Open communication is key in any relationship.
seeker: Yeah, I've also started journaling again. It helps sort through these complicated feelings.
supporter: Journaling is a great tool. How does writing about your thoughts and emotions help you?
seeker: It gives me clarity. Putting pen to paper makes everything feel less overwhelming and more manageable.
supporter: I’m glad it’s helping you. Have you noticed any other changes since you reconciled with Eliza?
seeker: I feel a bit lighter emotionally. Mending the rift with her feels like a burden lifted.
supporter: That’s a beautiful way to put it. Rebuilding that connection must feel rewarding.
seeker: It does. I’m also trying to be more proactive about addressing my financial stress instead of letting it control me.
supporter: That’s a positive step forward. You've been through a lot, and it’s important to take care of yourself too.
seeker: Trying my best. It’s a work in progress, you know? Balancing everything is tough.
supporter: Absolutely. You’re making great progress, even if it doesn’t always feel that way. I’m here whenever you need to talk.
seeker: Thank you, that means a lot. I’ll keep leaning on you if that's okay.
supporter: Always, Jane. Your journey is important, and I’m here to support you along the way.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-03-20","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hi, I really need to talk.
supporter: Of course, Jane. I'm here for you. What's on your mind?
seeker: It's about Jack. He tried reaching out to me again, and it really threw me off.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that, Jane. How did you feel when he contacted you?
seeker: Honestly, I felt a wave of anxiety and a bit of anger. I thought I was moving on, you know?
supporter: That sounds really tough. It's understandable to have those feelings, especially when someone from your past re-emerges unexpectedly.
seeker: Yeah, it's like all those feelings I had during our breakup came rushing back.
supporter: Breakups can leave a lasting impact, especially if things ended with unresolved issues. What worries you the most about Jack reaching out?
seeker: I guess I'm afraid of falling back into habits that were bad for me, like constantly questioning myself. We had a pretty toxic dynamic at times.
supporter: It's important that you're aware of the impact he had on you. It sounds like you're protecting yourself, which is a good step.
seeker: I'm trying. But it's hard when I think of all the other stressors in my life, like work and money. Everything feels so overwhelming.
supporter: It must be really challenging juggling all these pressures at once. Have you found anything that helps you manage when things get overwhelming?
seeker: Writing in my journal sometimes helps, but lately, I find it hard to focus or even sleep well.
supporter: Journaling is a great tool, and it's understandable that sleep and focus might be affected by anxiety. Do you have any relaxation techniques that help at night?
seeker: I try breathing exercises, but my mind races a lot. Maybe I need to establish a better nighttime routine.
supporter: That sounds like a good idea. A consistent routine can sometimes make a difference. Have you considered reaching out for professional help to guide you through this?
seeker: I have thought about therapy, but I'm worried about the cost, especially with my financial situation.
supporter: That's a valid concern. Some therapists offer sliding scales or there may be community resources available. It might be worth exploring if it can help you find balance.
seeker: I'll look into it. Just talking to you has helped a bit already.
supporter: I'm really glad to hear that. I'm always here whenever you need to talk. Take it one step at a time, Jane.
seeker: Thank you. It feels good to know I'm not alone in this.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-05-01","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

seeker: Hi, I'm okay, I guess. I got a new journal today to help me figure things out.

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hi, just needed someone to talk to.
supporter: Hi Jane! Of course, I'm here for you. What's on your mind?
seeker: I had my performance review at work today... and it wasn't great.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. It sounds like it must be really tough to hear. How are you feeling about it?
seeker: I'm feeling anxious and a bit of self-doubt creeping in. I thought I was handling everything okay.
supporter: It's completely understandable to feel that way. It seems like there's been a lot on your plate recently. Would you like to talk more about it?
seeker: I guess everything's just been snowballing since the thing with Lisa. I still can't believe how it all fell apart.
supporter: Losing a friend, especially over something like money, can feel really isolating. How has it been affecting you lately?
seeker: It's made focusing on work harder. And getting hit with that unexpected bill last month didn't help. Everything feels out of control.
supporter: It sounds like you're dealing with a lot of financial and emotional stress right now. It's a lot for anyone to handle. How have you been coping with it all?
seeker: I started writing in a journal. It helps sometimes, but the stress keeps piling up. I thought it would get better by now.
supporter: Journaling can be a great outlet. It's important to give yourself grace with everything happening. You're doing your best in a really challenging time.
seeker: Thank you. I keep telling myself that, but it's hard to believe it sometimes. I just wish things would turn around.
supporter: It makes sense to want things to improve quickly. Progress can be slow, but you're taking steps in the right direction by reaching out and processing everything going on.
seeker: Yeah, it helps to talk about it. I suppose I need to take it one day at a time.
supporter: Absolutely. It's like building a path through all these challenges— day by day, step by step. You have the strength to navigate this, even if it doesn't feel like it sometimes.
seeker: I really appreciate your support. It makes things feel a bit less overwhelming.
supporter: I'm glad to be here for you. Remember, you're not alone in this. We can keep talking anytime you need.
seeker: Thanks a lot. I might take you up on that.
supporter: Anytime, Jane. Take care of yourself, and reach out whenever you need to.
seeker: Will do. Take care, too.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-11-05","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

supporter: That sounds really challenging, especially when you're already feeling anxious. Have you noticed any patterns or triggers for the stress?

turns.content: Hi Jimmy, how have you been feeling lately?
Hey, it's been a bit of a rollercoaster. I'm trying something new with mindfulness and meditation.
That's interesting! What made you decide to explore mindfulness and meditation?
I just felt really overwhelmed after everything that happened recently. My anxiety has been through the roof.
I can imagine. It sounds like you've been through a lot. How have the mindfulness exercises been for you so far?
It's still new, but I think it's helping a bit. I can, at least, find moments of calm when I focus on it.
That's great to hear, even small moments of relief can be a huge step forward. Have you found any particular techniques that work well for you?
Guided meditations seem to work best, especially those focusing on anxiety. It's like having a support system even when alone.
It sounds like a very constructive approach. Have your interactions with Bob from the AA meetings been helpful as well?
Yeah, Bob's been really supportive. It feels good to have someone who truly gets it.
That's fantastic, having someone to share and talk to can make a huge difference. How have things been at work since last we talked?
Work has been tense. Got a warning over attendance, which just adds to the anxiety, you know?
That sounds really tough, especially when you're dealing with so much. Are you finding any ways to manage the stress related to work?
I'm trying to focus on what's directly in front of me and not let my mind wander. But at the same time, those past arguments with my manager still haunt me.
It's understandable. Past conflicts can linger, but it's great that you're focusing on the present tasks. Maybe addressing these feelings with a professional could also be beneficial?
You might be right, seeking professional advice could help make sense of this tangled mess.
Absolutely, a therapist could offer strategies specifically tailored for you. How do you feel about that idea?
It feels daunting, opening up to someone new, but necessary if I want to move forward.

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hi Jimmy, how are you holding up today?
seeker: Hey. Honestly, not too well. I had a bit of a slip up recently.
supporter: I'm really sorry to hear that, Jimmy. Do you feel like talking about what happened?
seeker: Yeah, I guess it's better to talk about it. I was at a family gathering and it just got overwhelming... and I ended up drinking.
supporter: Family gatherings can definitely be tough. What do you think made it overwhelming for you?
seeker: It was just a lot, you know? Everyone kept asking about my job, and there was a lot of pressure to 'act normal.' I tried to keep it together, but it felt like suffocating.
supporter: It sounds like there was a lot of unwanted pressure and it became too much. It’s understandable, given everything you've been dealing with. What did you do after realizing you had relapsed?
seeker: Honestly, I felt ashamed. But I reached out to Bob, my new friend from the AA meetings, and they were pretty supportive about it.
supporter: That's great that Bob was there for you. How are you feeling after talking with Bob?
seeker: A bit better. They reminded me that recovery isn't about being perfect; it's about trying to improve one step at a time.
supporter: That's a really healthy perspective. It's important to be gentle with yourself through this process. How else can I support you right now?
seeker: I'm just trying to figure out how to communicate better with my manager and deal with work stress. Bob suggested a couple of strategies.
supporter: That's a good step. Improving that relationship could lessen some of your stress. Do you feel like talking about those strategies?
seeker: Bob mentioned setting clearer boundaries and maybe considering mediation if things don't improve. It's nerve-racking, but I know I have to do something.
supporter: Those sound like constructive steps forward. It’s about finding what works best for you. Do you have anything else in mind that might help ease the stress?
seeker: I've also thought about re-evaluating my workload to manage it better. Maybe take some time to plan rather than just react.
supporter: Planning sounds like a promising approach. It might give you more control over the situation. Remember, you're making progress, even on the hard days.
seeker: Thanks. I needed to hear that. It's easy to get lost in the mistakes and forget about the progress.
supporter: We all need reminders sometimes. You're not alone in this, Jimmy. Anytime you want to talk, I'm here.
seeker: I appreciate that. I think I'll take things one day at a time and reach out whenever I feel stuck or overwhelmed.
supporter: That sounds like a solid plan. Don't hesitate to lean on your friends, your AA support group, or me. We believe in you.
seeker: I will. Thanks again. It really helps to have someone to talk to who understands.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-11-25","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Yo
supporter: Hi, how are you doing?
seeker: I am decent. I am here because my friend talks way too much on the phone, and it frustrates me.
seeker: They never want to hang up, and the talk can literally go on for hours.
supporter: It sounds like it would be quite frustrating for your friend to talk way too much on the phone. 
seeker: No, he loves it! I'm the one who hates it.
supporter: My goodness! How do they respond when you ask to end the conversation?
seeker: I tell him, but he just doesn't get it. Or, he says he understands, but then just goes back to talking!
seeker: Or, he may finally end the talk, but the next time we talk, he will just do it all over again!
supporter: I wonder what it would be like for him if you hung up the phone even after he said he still wanted to talk.
supporter: Wow--that does sound annoying that he will repeat the same pattern the next time.
seeker: He will literally talk up to 10 minutes without letting you have a word in. As far as that advice, I have hung up, but he gets extremely offended easily.
supporter: That sounds really difficult if he gets offended so easily. I find it hard to talk to some of those kinds of friends.
seeker: I'm at my wits end. I tell him all the time. "You talk too much. You gotta stop talking at me. You gotta give the other person a turn. You gotta respect other's time."
supporter: What do you get out of the friendship with this other person?
seeker: Well, I've been friends with him for a long time. He's funny and can have interesting perspectives on things. Also, we have done a lot together in the past.
supporter: That sounds like a lot that the two of you have been through. Were there other times that your friends was more equally responsive or attuned to you in conversations?
seeker: Oh, yes, I have other friends in conversations who can take turns and understand the concept of time just fine.
seeker: I just don't know what to do about this guy in particular. I still want to be his friend, but he just doesn't change.
supporter: I wonder if there is anything nice you could do for yourself when you are talking to him that would make it easier to talk to him.
seeker: Do you think I should just have a timer that goes off at 1 minute and let it beep in his face if he goes on for too long to train him like a monkey?
supporter: I can see that you are feeling upset and angry when he talks so much and that is totally understandable. 
seeker: I just need a method. Talking to him is just not working.
seeker: He is hard to condition.
supporter: Would it hurt his feelings to use a timer like that? It may for some other people. 
seeker: Yea, but I might be able to slip some humour in there to take the edge off because it is so silly.
supporter: Humor is really helpful for a lot of people. 
seeker: Any other ideas?
supporter: Sometimes, people draw or do something else distracting with their hands when talking to someone who dominates the conversation.
seeker: So your option is to start just doing something else when he is talking? He might get the message in a subtle way?
supporter: Sometimes that is a less offensive way to retrain someone who is being obnoxious or dominant and yet who is easily offended. And, it can help preserve your sense of being grounded.
supporter: The strategy works well for me with some of my family members who seem like they will never change. But, with distraction, I enjoy them all the more.
seeker: This is true, and it isn't bade advice. Haha! That is funny. Yes, maybe I should find something to carry around with me that I can enjoy.
seeker: I don't really like to draw...
supporter: Is there anything else that you like to do that would be distracting while also letting you somewhat participate in the conversation?
seeker: Yes, perhaps I should just use the internet when he starts talking too much. 
seeker: I have a phone.
supporter: That sounds really helpful. Sometimes people also play phone games or with a fidget spinner. I like your idea of looking on the internet.
seeker: This solves the problem in person, but it doesn't solve the talks over the phone, but it has been 15 minutes now and this has been helpful enough. Thank you for your solutions. You have been very supportive and kind to me
seeker: I don't want to take up any more of your time. It has been a good conversation. 
supporter: You are very welcome. I wish you all the best!
seeker: Goodbye. You as well.
supporter: Bye!","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-07-15","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hello
seeker: Hi there I was hoping you can help me.
supporter: Sure. What can I help you with?
seeker: Well you see I am heartbroken and I can't seem to move on from a previous relationship, and its been over two years. Do you have any advice?
supporter: I’m understand how hard ending a relationship can be. 
supporter: What do you find is the hardest thing for you each day. That is, where do you find it hardest to move on?
seeker: Well I would say mentally because I frequently think about her and constantly have memories throughout the day. Also when i hear a certain song or see a restaurant it makes me think of her.
supporter: Memories are a blessing and a curse. Are the memories and thought you are  having positive or negative? 
seeker: They are a mix of both because at one point they were positive and now when I think about it, it brings me down in a negative way.
seeker: What have you done in the past to help you move on from a break up?
supporter: It’s hard when we have various emotions. These memories being more negative are hard to cope with. In my experience, if I rethink memories regarding relationships which tend to bring me down in way that is a learning experience, I feel more empowered. 
seeker: Yeah I agree that's what I have been doing too, and it's nice to know that you do the same.
supporter: In my past I have been able to try and look at each  relationship as a chance to grow. To figure out what worked with that person and what didn’t. I have them used this as a tool for the future. 
seeker: That's a good way to look at it.
supporter: You are making good steps to rethink the situations. Is there anything else contributing to the heat rack you still feel?
supporter: Heartbreak 
seeker: Well I have also not met anyone since and fear that I will not fall in love again.
supporter: That is difficult. I understand how it feels to be lonely. Something I’ve done when I’ve felt that way was to learn to fall in love with myself. I like to do self care and make time for things I might not have time for if I were in a relationship. 
seeker: hmm interesting I have never thought about falling in love with myself..maybe I will give it a try. Thanks.
supporter: It’s so important to love yourself. Self love breeds confidence and confidence is not only attractive, but powerful in so many ways  
seeker: I appreciate the feedback and support, you have helped me take the next step to move on with my life.
supporter: I’m glad I could help. You will overcome this. 
seeker: Thank you and hope to talk to you again. Have a good night.
supporter: You too. ","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-08-15","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hi there, how are you doing?
seeker: IM HANGING IN THERE HOW ARE YOU?
supporter: I am okay. What would you like to talk to me about?
seeker: Well, i have a problem with drinking alcoholI am so scared my job will find out
supporter: Do you drink when you are at work?
seeker: I have started calling in atleast twice as week.
seeker: I have started drinking at work close to the end of my shift in the bathroom
supporter: That does sound like it might be a big problem. How are  your employers reacting? 
supporter: It sounds like you have a big problem that needs professional help, would you agree? 
seeker: They have not mentioned anything to me yet. 
supporter: I think it is likely to have been noticed though, at least. 
seeker: Yes I agree it sounds like a really big problem, but what should i do?
supporter: I think the best thing would be to be really honest with your employers and ask if you can have time off for professional help. 
seeker: That is a good idea
supporter: Are you employers likely to be sympathetic?
seeker: my main concern, that makes me fearful is being fired, and being the talk of the workplace
supporter: Ah people do love to idly gossip don't they? I've been through that myself. I know it's hard to ignore them but it's best to try. 
seeker: My employer is an well known organization that employees over 3,000 people.
supporter: I do not know if they can fire you if you have a legitimate medical problem though.
supporter: Well you could always shame them if they unfairly fired you. 
seeker: Very good to know that I will look into it. It did not start overnight and I don't expect it to end overnight
seeker: lol, yes that is true.
seeker: Thank you so much for your time. 
supporter: Large corporations are always over concerned about their images. (we have to talk for fifteen minutes :))
seeker: oh ok I thought it was just for 10 lines, lol
seeker: but none the less, there are people really going through that scenario I just portrayex

supporter: To be honest, and I mean this sincerely, I've been through it :( 
seeker: I believe rehabilitative therapy would be best
supporter: It can be very expensive though. In my country you can get it for free but there's a long waiting list. 
seeker: I have hads  a few drinks often but never abused it. thankfully. 
seeker: Well here you might can get help for free, but it does have to be paid back
supporter: Heh be grateful :)

seeker: Yes Im in the United States (Alabama) 
seeker: I heard of the UK so many times but truthfully I know nothing about it
supporter: Ah you are a long way away from me. I hope that you do manage to sort out your problems though and definitely do talk to your employers
supporter: Ah it's quite nice here. We pay for healthcare out of our taxes so it's free at source.

supporter: Gossipy people are the worst. Just remind yourself that they all have skeletons in their closets too 
seeker: great advice
supporter: Well anyway, I hope I have been able to offer your  some useful advice. I wish you all of the very best in the future.
seeker: I think also the best thing to do is to talk to great people like you
supporter: (can you press quit first and do the survey as I am not able to do it from my side)
supporter: Well thanks :) ","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-09-01","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hey Jimmy, it's good to hear from you. How's everything on your end?
seeker: Hey, not too great to be honest. I tried opening up to my friends at the gathering I hosted, but it didn't go as I hoped.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that, Jimmy. It sounds frustrating. Do you want to talk more about what happened?
seeker: Yeah, I felt like I was finally ready to share some personal stuff, and it seemed like nobody wanted to listen or take it seriously.
supporter: That must have been really tough, especially when you were putting yourself out there. How did you end up feeling after that?
seeker: I felt pretty down. It was like my feelings didn't matter to them, and it made me question if they really care about me.
supporter: It's completely understandable to feel that way. It sounds like you were looking for some support from your friends.
seeker: Exactly. I just wanted someone to hear me out and maybe offer some advice or comfort.
supporter: Feeling dismissed by friends could be really disheartening. Have you experienced anything like this before with them?
seeker: Not really. That's why it was kind of a shock. I just didn't expect it from them.

turns.content: Hey Jimmy, how have you been doing lately?
Hey, I'm okay, I guess. I've started journaling daily. Thought it might help me make sense of everything.
That's a great step. Writing things down can help untangle what's going on inside. How's it been for you so far?
It's been... enlightening, but also a bit heavy. I didn't realize how many emotions I've been bottling up.
I can imagine. Opening that bottle can be tough. Have you discovered anything about yourself through journaling?
Yeah, I've noticed a pattern of avoiding conversations that make me uncomfortable. I guess I've been doing that a lot.
Recognizing those patterns is a big first step. It shows you're gaining clarity. Have any specific situations come to mind?
Well, my recent move to Sydney was partly because I felt trapped by my past here in Canberra. Wanted a fresh start, but I miss some things too.

MS.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hey Jimmy, how are you doing today?
seeker: Hey, I'm feeling a bit off. I took a walk around my old workplace in Canberra and it brought back a lot of memories.
supporter: That sounds intense. What kind of memories did it bring up for you?
seeker: A mix of good and bad, honestly. I miss the routine, but I also remember the stress and how overwhelmed I felt back then.
supporter: It makes sense to have mixed feelings. Have you been thinking about your decision to move to Sydney at all?
seeker: Yeah, it’s been on my mind. Part of me wonders if I'm making the right decision, leaving it all behind.
supporter: It's natural to have doubts, especially with such a big change. What do you hope to gain from moving?
seeker: A fresh start, I suppose. I want to leave behind the stress and the drinking issues I faced here.
supporter: That sounds like a healthy goal. How have you been coping with those challenges recently?
seeker: I’ve been trying meditation and mindfulness. It's helping, but I still slip up every now and then.
supporter: You've been working hard to improve, and that's commendable. Do you feel the change of scenery might help with your healing?
seeker: I think so. I need a place where I can focus on becoming the best version of myself without constant reminders of the past.
supporter: That sounds like a positive step. How has the idea of relocating affected your daily routine currently?
seeker: It’s been a bit unsettling. I've been trying to wrap things up here, but it's hard to leave things behind.
supporter: I guess it’s a mix of excitement and anxiety. Have you talked to anyone else about how you’re feeling?
seeker: I mentioned it briefly to my AA friend. They understand where I’m coming from, but I still feel quite alone in this.
supporter: I'm glad you have someone to relate to, but it's also important to reach out to others, like your therapist, if you need more support.
seeker: You’re right. I've been meaning to, but sometimes I just don’t know where to start explaining how I feel.
supporter: That can be tough. Maybe starting with how it feels to revisit old places and planning your move could be a good entry point.
seeker: That’s a good idea. I just hope moving will give me the perspective and space I need to heal.
supporter: It sounds like you’re on the right path by acknowledging these feelings. Remember, it’s okay to seek help along the way.
seeker: Thanks, I really appreciate your support. I'll try to keep taking these steps forward.
supporter: Anytime, Jimmy. You’re doing great just by being open to change and growth.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-03-20","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hi George, I hope you're free to chat for a bit?
supporter: Hey Jimmy, of course! What's going on?
seeker: I've been having a rough patch emotionally. Yesterday, I wrote a letter to my ex-girlfriend. It brought back a lot of memories.
supporter: That sounds heavy. What prompted you to write the letter?
seeker: We talked recently, and it stirred up old feelings. I felt I needed to get everything off my chest for some closure.
supporter: I can understand why that would be important to you. How did it feel writing it all out?
seeker: It was cathartic, actually. But at the same time, it made me reflect on a lot of what-ifs and missed opportunities.
supporter: It’s natural to reflect on those things, especially when so much has changed since. Did it help clarify your feelings at all?
seeker: I think so. I've been feeling a mixture of relief and sadness. Like a chapter is finally concluding.
supporter: Endings can definitely feel bittersweet. Have you been able to talk to anyone else about this?
seeker: Not yet. You're the first person I reached out to. I thought about talking to Jane, my therapist, but I haven’t made the appointment yet.
supporter: I'm glad you reached out. It sounds like it might be a good idea to schedule that session with Jane.
seeker: Yeah, that's probably a good idea. I worry that if I don't address these emotions, they might affect other parts of my life.
supporter: That's a valid concern. You've been working hard on moving forward, and processing these emotions can only help with that.
seeker: Thanks, George. It’s just tough navigating these waters. But talking about it definitely eases some of the burden.
supporter: I’m happy to be here for you, Jimmy. Remember, it’s okay to take one step at a time. Have you considered how you'll spend the next few days?
seeker: I think I'll try to keep busy. Maybe focus more on my new job in Sydney and make plans to meet with friends here.
supporter: Sounds like a solid plan. Keeping active can help manage those feelings of sadness. And it sounds like you do have a support network you're building there.
seeker: Yeah, I’m trying. It’s challenging starting fresh, but it’s comforting to know I’m not alone in this journey.
supporter: You’re doing great, Jimmy. Just keep reaching out when you need an ear, okay?
